News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Former Associated Press editor Polly Anderson, who shaped breaking news coverage of some of America's biggest stories and researched and wrote advance obituaries for many celebrities during a 25-year run on the company’s national desk, has died.

Anderson died Sunday morning after battling Alzheimer’s disease, said her niece, Rachel Hassan. She was 75.

Anderson was remembered for her relentless work editing breaking news stories including 9/11 or the Oklahoma City bombing, her dogged demands for accuracy and quality, and the seemingly endless supply of diet colas at her desk in New York.

“She was a dedicated journalist who brought news to millions of readers. Like many wire reporters and editors, she tirelessly toiled without recognition from the general public,” said her longtime friend and colleague Marty Steinberg.

Hassan said her aunt knew how important her job was but never bragged about it.

“She was incredibly smart. She knew something about everything,” Hassan said.

Anderson led the US news report through the day

Anderson joined the AP in 1985 on the company's general desk, which was renamed the national desk in 2005. Until she retired in 2010, her job was to supervise U.S. news starting before the sun came up.

That put her in the hot seat during historic events like when a rental truck full of explosives destroyed a federal building in Oklahoma City in 1995, or the Sept. 11, 2001, attacks.

Anderson suggested the AP send out a “flash” when the twin towers fell in New York — something the organization only used for transcendent news events.

“Polly was an unforgettable colleague. She brought meticulous care to her job as the national editor on the 6 a.m. shift and as the steward of AP’s obituary coverage, and our preparation in coverage of major deaths still bears her fingerprints years later," said Josh Hoffner, AP Global Sports Editor and former colleague on the national desk.

A diligent, caring and sensitive editor

Anderson had her quirks. She didn't have a phone, so she would call in news tips from a pay phone at the train station in Queens, where she lived. She loved cats and may have kept a few in or under her desk. She named one cat after the inventor of the Xerox copying machine. And there were all the diet colas.

She was remembered as diligent, caring and sensitive. During the crucible that was editing the 9/11 stories, she kept talking about all the people who likely lost their lives that day, Steinberg said.

She was tough but fair to those learning from her.

“I cannot say enough about the impact Polly had on editors like myself who worked the overnight shift on the General Desk and passed the reins to her when she came in at 6 a.m. If your copy wasn’t up to par, she’d rewrite it and show you how much better it could be. If she approved, it was validation of a job well done," Hoffner said.

She cared deeply about people's obituaries

Anderson also made sure AP was ready when famous people died, often staying at the end of her shift to prewrite some of those stories herself, including for such celebrities as cable TV tycoon Ted Turner, actor Kirk Douglas, PBS newsman Jim Lehrer, singer Eartha Kitt, economist Paul Samuelson and the stars of the silent movie era, something she knew a lot about.

“She was vigilant — from preparing for their deaths to writing new ones and staying on top of the ones she had written. And she did this at the end of a long and exhausting news day,” Steinberg said.

Born in Chicago, Anderson grew up in Itasca, Illinois, and studied journalism at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign. She worked in her home state before joining the AP at its national headquarters in New York City in 1985.

Anderson was living in Richmond, Virginia, when she died. She is survived by two sisters — Sara Hassan in Richmond and Karen Anderson in Romsey, England.

Anderson spent nearly 25 years making AP's news stories the best they could be and bringing light to those who worked with her, said Paula Froke, who as a news editor in Michigan was often edited by Anderson. She later worked alongside her as AP's deputy national editor.

“Her tremendous spirit and devotion to her work were a model for all of us," Froke wrote in an email. "She was a great journalist and an even better person.”

News.title: Andy Burnham labelled ‘unserious’ after influencer recreates Love, Actually dance through No 10
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Andy Burnham has been labelled "unserious" after an influencer was invited into Downing Street to recreate Hugh Grant’s famous prime ministerial dance scene from the film Love, Actually.

In a video shared online recently, Luke Hamnett is shown dancing through No 10 and down the stairs to the Pointer Sisters’ Jump (For My Love).

He halts upon suddenly spotting the Prime Minister seated and ready to conduct an interview with him.

Kemi Badenoch has criticised the clip, describing the content as "jarring".

She said: “When I was a new MP, we had to hand in our phones as we stepped into 10 Downing St, so it’s jarring to see a Labour PM turn it into a bit of a joke.

“Hugh Grant could dance through No 10 in Love Actually because he was pretending to be Prime Minister. Andy Burnham actually IS the Prime Minister.

“At a time when Trump, Xi and Putin are projecting power on the world stage, and people across Britain are anxious about the future, this looks extremely unserious.

“Being relatable doesn’t mean treating the public as though they are children who need entertaining.”

Andy Burnham interviewed was interviewed by TikTok and Instagram creator Luke Hamnett ( @livelaughlukepod )

Conservative former minister Esther McVey told the Commons: “Perhaps the Prime Minister’s time would be better spent polishing up his negotiating skills rather than concentrating on the choreography of a dance routine of a TikTok influencer.”

Ms McVey was referring to a youth mobility scheme, which will allow 100,000 Europeans aged 18 to 31 to live in the UK for up to three years as part of the agreements struck between Mr Burnham and EU leaders last week.

The Prime Minister’s official spokesperson said: “The Prime Minister has been very open about his desire to communicate with the public in a variety of different ways and on the channels that they use and you’ve seen that reflected in (the) Prime Minister’s comms since coming into office.

“And I think that particular piece of content was part of an interview, as you say, but the Prime Minister… engages with communications on a variety of different channels, which is a reflection of how the public gets this information these days.”

Another video emerged later of influencer Max Balegde filming himself outside the door of No 10, mouthing along “bomboclaat p****wagon chicken nuggets” to what appeared to be a viral meme song.

News.title: Tom Brady opens up on parenting ‘mistakes’: ‘A lot like a quarterback’
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Tom Brady says he has made a lot of "mistakes" as a parent but hopes he is a "better" dad now than when his first child was born.

The former New England Patriots quarterback – who has Jack, 19, with former partner Bridget Moynahan, and Benjamin, 16, and Vivian, 13, with ex-wife Gisele Bundchen – wants to be a "mentor" to his kids and tries to take the time to listen to them without judging their actions.

Speaking during a live audience recording of Jake Humphrey's High Performance Podcast, he said: "It's been a lot. I've made a lot of mistakes.

“So, a lot like quarterback. I threw a lot of interceptions. And everyone I've tried to learn from.

“And I'd hope I'm a better parent today than I was when I first started having kids. And hopefully I'm a better parent ten years from now.

"I've really doubled down on that for sure. Like, not letting them off the hook with the lessons they need to learn, trying to really be a mentor to them."

He added: "My son said to me the other night, he's like, 'Dad, sometimes we sit down at dinner and it's just like a really easy conversation to start, and all of a sudden you get really serious, Dad.'

"And I'm like, 'You're right, Benny... sometimes that coach comes out in me...'

"And then I'm trying to say, okay, well, you're 16 years old. I'm a little bit older than you. I was 16, I remember that this is what I would do, based on the 30 plus years of experience that I have.

Brady has three children: Jack, 19, Benjamin, 16, and Vivian, 13 ( Getty )

“I think a lot of it's just that being really present for them, non-judgmental, just trying to understand their perspective, but also trying to get them to understand my perspective a little bit too..."

The retired sportsman thinks he can learn a lot from his children.

He said: "My son Benny, who's 16, he loves music and he loves deejaying. You know, I want to sit there and listen to what he's doing.

“Not saying, ‘Hey, Benny, come watch me study football film’. He doesn't want to study football film. And that's great. I want to learn from him, too."

Though Tom always wakes up "plus two happy" and is usually "optimistic" about the day ahead, he admitted he still has down days but has learned to accept those and to "deal with failure".

He said: "My son called me last night and he said, he's like, he's 19 and he plays basketball... And I said, what was it? And he goes, 'Well, you know, I just didn't get as many shots up early. And then I had to work out and my body wasn't feeling great.'

"And I said, 'OK'. Like I said, 'Dude, this is this is what happens. Like, this is sports. Like it's a skill. It's a performance every day. You're not going to be at your best.

"And by the way, even if you don't reach it, you'll still gain so much self-confidence in who you are, because you'll have a work ethic, and you'll learn to deal with failure, and you'll learn to have more resilience for all the next obstacles that come your way.

"You know, we try so many things in life that don't work, and I don't think that's a failure. I think that's a success because without all these failures, we really don't become who we are."

News.title: Former EastEnders star in mid-show evacuation as emergency services called to theatre
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Actor Maisie Smith was forced to leave a stage show mid-performance on Sunday following fears of a fire.

Audience members, cast, and crew evacuated Manchester’s Hope Mill Theatre during a performance of Little Shop of Horrors when a fire alarm rang out, bringing firefighters to the scene as a precaution.

Alongside the audience, former EastEnders star Smith, 25, stood outside in freezing conditions in costume, accompanied by Brookside actor Michael Starke, 69, and Hollyoaks actor Benjamin Yates.

The trio play the roles of Audrey, Mr Mushnik, and Orin Scrivello, DDS, respectively.

Posting to his Instagram Stories, Yates shared a photo of gathered crowds watching fire crews examine Hope Mill Theatre before it was deemed safe to re-enter and continue.

He wrote over the photo: "Mid show firealarm (sic)."

Little Shop of Horrors has been playing at Hope Mill Theatre since September 25 and will end on November 28, before it heads to the Liverpool Playhouse in December.

open image in gallery Smith left EastEnders in 2022 ( Getty )

"It was very dramatic but everyone was professional and the show went on as soon as it was safe," a source told The Sun.

Smith was six when she shot to fame in 2008, playing Tiffany Butcher in EastEnders.

The character was seen leaving the BBC soap in 2022 to live in Germany with her brother Liam, played by Alfie Deegan.

Reflecting on her departure, she said on a June episode of Radio Times' In The Interval podcast: "I ultimately decided to leave EastEnders because as much as I loved playing Tiffany and I loved the family that was there, I was itching to get on the stage."

It has paid off for Smith, who has since appeared on stage in the likes of The Talented Mr Ripley, The War of the Worlds and Strictly Ballroom The Musical.

But the time is not currently right for her to return to the BBC soap.

Smith admitted: "I can't think I'd say yes right now because of what I've got coming up."

However, the Strictly Come Dancing 2020 runner-up hinted that there is always a chance she will make a comeback in the future.

The entertainer added: "I'm really enjoying the idea of playing different characters. But thing is with EastEnders, it is gonna be there forever and I've got such a big family there. On screen and off screen."

News.title: Mariella Frostrup clashes with new I’m A Celebrity camp leaders over water duty: ‘I can’t do it’
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Mariella Frostrup has come into conflict with the new camp leaders on I’m A Celebrity… Get Me Out Of Here! over her assigned task, declaring: "I can’t do it."

Monday’s edition of the ITV reality series saw Gavin And Stacey actor Joanna Page named as the new camp leader, with comedian Leigh Francis appointed as her deputy.

Their distribution of chores prompted tension after Frostrup and supermodel Leomie Anderson were given water duty.

Frostrup said: “I’m not sure that Leomie and I can do water duty on our own.

“I just wonder if there’s any way of mixing a guy into it.”

Reality star Chloe Burrows said she had completed the task “on my own all day yesterday”, adding: “It’s not that hard.”

Frostrup insisted: “I don’t think I can do it. I just don’t think I’m capable of doing that.”

Frostrup later approached Page again, saying: “May I just point out with the water – I can’t carry it.

“When the camp runs out of water, I don’t know what I’ll do.”

open image in gallery Their allocation of chores caused a stir after Frostrup and supermodel Leomie Anderson were assigned water duty ( ITV )

The Welsh actress suggested Anderson could take on the more physically demanding duties, with Frostrup insisting she was “not being difficult” before eventually conceding.

“I don’t like any form of confrontation at all,” Page later told Burrows, adding: “I’m sure I haven’t heard the last of it.”

Former Love Island star Burrows told the Bush Telegraph: “Jo’s been in charge for two minutes and it’s already kicking off.

“I did it all on my own, so I don’t see why two fully grown women can’t just crack on and work out a solution.”

Frostrup also took on bushtucker trial The Snake Escape, which featured an “all or nothing” twist, meaning she would either win all 12 stars for camp or leave empty-handed.

After failing to escape a giant vent filled with snakes, she told hosts Anthony McPartlin and Declan Donnelly she was “so gutted”, adding: “It feels like a stupid failure.”

The Loose Women panellist broke down in tears as she broke the news to her fellow campmates, who rushed to comfort her.

It comes after the broadcaster, 64, sparked outrage among viewers during Sunday’s episode when she described AJ Odudu as “aggressive” following a disagreement over their dinner chores.

Stars including Judi Love, Will Best, Motsi Mabuse, Fleur East and Jo Frost were among those who came to Odudu’s defence on social media.

open image in gallery Frostrup labelled Odudu as ‘aggressive’ ( ITV )

The “angry black woman” trope, which portrays black women as disproportionately angry or aggressive, is widely regarded as a derogatory racial stereotype, with roots in 19th century American minstrel shows.

After Sunday’s incident, ITV issued a statement saying “the production monitors everyone in camp 24/7” and producers would intervene if they felt “someone has overstepped the line by using inappropriate language or displaying unacceptable behaviour”.

The broadcaster also said its duty of care towards contestants is of the “utmost importance” and it takes their welfare “very seriously”.

It is understood Frostrup was spoken to by producers in the Bush Telegraph after the incident to discuss why the language caused offence and how to address it and move forward.

All celebrities on the show are briefed about inappropriate language and behaviour and receive training from a diversity, equity and inclusion team.

Later in the episode, the celebrities later competed to win luxury items for each other, with Anderson securing Wayne Rooney’s foot spa, the former England footballer winning actress Claire Sweeney’s family photo and Burrows earning a puzzle cube for content creator Sharky.

I’m A Celebrity… Get Me Out Of Here! continues on Tuesday at 9.15pm.

News.title: Court allows Army to detonate dangerous Iowa explosives after Trump intervention
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

A federal appeals court has granted permission for the U.S. Army to detonate tons of degraded explosive materials at an ammunition plant in Iowa.

The order from the 8th Circuit U.S. Court of Appeals was one of two rulings President Donald Trump indicated he was awaiting after directing the military on Monday to pause the chemical disposal pending judicial review.

The president noted that his determination remains contingent upon agreement from incoming Gov.-elect Rob Sand, warning that federal authorities would otherwise be forced to proceed with the planned detonation.

Initial plans to destroy 68 barrels of lead azide were set for last Friday, but the Army postponed the operation three times following significant public concern regarding potential health and environmental hazards.

The revised plan aimed for a Wednesday detonation ahead of Thanksgiving to take advantage of favorable weather.

President Donald Trump announced on Monday that his administration would defer to a federal appeals court prior to moving ahead with the disposal of the degraded bomb-making material at the Iowa facility.

The scheduled neutralization of the 68 lead azide drums has been delayed three times after sharp public apprehension over environmental and health risks.

open image in gallery A sign at the US Army Iowa Army Ammunition Plant ( Reuters )

While military personnel sought a Wednesday timeline due to weather conditions, the Army did not immediately comment on the president's statement.

"At the same time, have ordered the military not to do so until such time as the 8th Circuit agrees that we can go forward, and am further making this decision fully subject to the incoming Gov.-elect Rob Sand agreeing to the operation," Trump said.

He warned that if consent is withheld, the administration will halt the procedure, holding Sand responsible for "any and all death or destruction caused by this very unfortunate, and longterm, situation."

Sand responded in a social media post, writing that past administrative choices meant "No good options exist and the situation is more dangerous and unpredictable than it ever should have been."

He raised questions over why a contract intended to eliminate the hazard was canceled and "why we are rushing to demolition now in late November."

open image in gallery Residents taped up windows in hopes of stopping them from shattering during the explosion ( Getty )

The delay follows a legal challenge from environmental groups, who secured a stay from the 8th Circuit Court of Appeals to review an emergency permit granted by the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency.

Trump indicated a preference for quick disposal via a controlled explosion, describing it as the safer option.

However, he confirmed that the operation remains paused pending judicial and state clearance.

Sand stressed, "The safety of Iowans should be the top priority of everyone involved," adding that "All relevant federal, state and local government resources should be focused on protecting everyone that could be impacted."

Near the Middletown facility, some residents have taken preventive steps by sealing windows and doors against potential lead dust, while others expressed worry online about wind carrying potential plumes.

Officials acknowledged the toxicity of lead, advising residents to stay indoors during any explosion and to wash down outdoor surfaces with water.

In court documents, Army Col. Aaron Teller, a munitions emergency specialist, explained that reduced liquid inside the barrels leaves the substance susceptible to freezing, raising the sensitivity of crystals near the lids.

open image in gallery Incoming Gov. Rob Sand ( AP )

"Even a small amount of friction can break the crystal formation, causing an explosive chain reaction," he stated.

The barrels were initially discovered in March.

Although EPA records show chemical neutralization options were evaluated, officials determined that moving the drums posed a severe risk of an accidental blast. Environmentalists contend that alternative methods were overlooked, while officials warn that the danger of an explosion grows as temperatures fall below 30 degrees Fahrenheit (-1 Celsius).

News.title: Wall Street stocks soar as Jensen Huang returns to Nvidia
News.content:
US tech stocks staged a dramatic recovery on Monday after Nvidia’s shock decision to reinstate Jensen Huang.

The value of the tech-heavy Nasdaq gained nearly $2 trillion as investors rushed back into AI-linked companies following a bruising sell-off last week.

The index closed up 6.9pc late Monday after rising as much as 7.7pc, regaining its losses during last week’s rout.

Nvidia shares surged as much as 34pc, their biggest one-day gain in 25 years, after the company reinstated Mr Huang following pressure from President Trump. They closed up 31pc.

Markets had been poised to gain ground as investors took stock following a bruising sell-off driven by darkening sentiment about AI.

But the recovery was boosted by a statement from Nvidia shortly before markets opened confirming the return of its founder.

Trading in Nasdaq futures was briefly halted before markets opened because of the huge volatility.

Mr Huang had stepped down from the chip giant earlier this month in the wake of revelations of affairs with an alleged Chinese spy and another with a colleague.

Nvidia said it made its decision with “input from senior levels of the United States government”.

Mr Trump on Monday said he had “convinced” Nvidia to reinstate Mr Huang.

The rebound in stocks will help to ease concerns about the AI bubble bursting as investors begin to question whether AI companies will be able to recoup the vast sums of money being pumped into the industry.

The benchmark S&P 500 closed up 4.7pc, while the Dow Jones gained around 3pc.

Mr Huang later attended Nvidia’s headquarters, telling staff he would be a “better CEO the second time around”.

News.title: Dengue more widespread than previously thought
News.content:
Dengue is much more widespread than previously thought, researchers have warned, raising concerns that the threat has been underestimated and resources misallocated.

An analysis of global data from 1990 to 2024 found that there were 73.9 million cases of the mosquito-borne disease – 10.6 million more than previously captured.

“Collectively these data show that dengue is expanding faster, more consistently and more intensely than previously thought,” the authors from institutions in the UK, the US, South Africa and Singapore wrote.

Dengue, nicknamed breakbone fever, is spread by the Aedes mosquito and it can cause intense muscle, joint and bone aches. The severe form of the disease can be fatal, and it poses a significant burden on low and middle-income countries.

The research, presented at the annual meeting of the American Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene in Maryland, comes as countries including Bangladesh, Malaysia and Cuba are being hit hard by outbreaks of the disease.

The paper, not yet published in a journal, found that global incidence rose 34-fold between 1990 and 2024, an average annual jump of 9.1 per cent. Cases rose most rapidly in regions where the virus has recently emerged – Africa, the Middle East and South Asia – and more slowly in Southeast Asia, where it’s been established for decades.

Researchers found the missing cases by combing through uncounted sources, like ministry of health PDFs and graphics that never made it into global datasets. They then combined this with modelling, to pull together a single database that tracks 35 years of cases by month, allowing scientists to test new hypotheses.

News.title: Any regrets, Mauricio? Man Utd are deep in relegation battle after Anfield farce
News.content:
Bruno Fernandes says he has shelved talks over a new contract because it is not the “right moment” for discussions over his future as Manchester United captain.

Fernandes, 32, is out of contract next summer although United have a 12-month option to extend his deal to 2028.

The Portugal midfielder is understood to have rejected two contract offers from United since the summer but said all his focus needs to be on trying to help the team out of their current plight.

United head into Sunday’s game against Liverpool at Anfield second from bottom in the Premier League.

“We spoke about the contract at the end of last season,” Fernandes told Sky Sports.

“We came in at the beginning of this season speaking about the contract, but about the context of the team and the club, I just put that to a side because I don’t think it’s the right moment, neither for me, nor for the club, to be talking about negotiations.

“The most important thing now is that the club gets back to winning games.”

Fernandes said claims he wants more money or a longer-term deal on offer are incorrect and that if finances were the issue he would have left Old Trafford before now. The captain has previously rejected lucrative offers from Saudi Arabia.

“The club offered me a new contract, so I think that, from their side, shows that they want me to stay,” he said.

“There’s no negotiations ongoing, but I’ve seen people saying that ‘He’s asked for more money, he’s asked for more years’. If I wanted more money, I wouldn’t be here.

“I had somewhere to go to get much more money than being at Manchester United. I could have been in a place that is much warmer than Manchester.

“Two summers ago, three summers ago, last summer, I always had the chance to leave and I always chose to be here.

“The thing is, I’ve always showed how much I care about the club and how much I want to win at this club. And I always said, in the moment the club thinks it’s time for me to move on, I will move on.

“I’m not going to be the player that I’ve seen many in this time at Manchester United. They’re going to stay here just by staying, just finish my contract and then we will see. In the moment the club says, ‘Bruno, it’s time to part ways’, I’m going to be the first one walking out the door.”

United chief executive Omar Berrada said of Fernandes on Friday that it was “true that we’re having conversations about his new contract” but that the club preferred “to keep that private”.

Having been voted PFA Player of the Year last season, Fernandes’ form has dropped off this term like that of the team.

He was dropped for the 3-0 defeat by Bournemouth in the wake of a 4-1 drubbing by Como when he criticised the tactics and approach of then head coach Michael Carrick.

Mauricio Pochettino, Carrick’s successor, confirmed on Friday that Fernandes would remain as captain.

Fernandes said the United fans had been “far too patient with us” and hopes Pochettino - who wanted to bring the Portuguese to Spurs in 2019 - will bring a fresh energy.

“He’s someone that likes to bring a very good energy to the team, someone very positive, very strong, strict, said it straight away that he won’t allow us to not give him what he demands from the team, from each player,” Fernandes said.

“He wants the club to succeed so much, he wants to win games, and that’s pretty clear and obvious by the way he and his staff speak and want us to improve.

“Obviously [in 2019] I was a very young player that was eager to come to the Premier League. They had [Harry] Kane there, they had Dele Alli, Son, the chance of playing with those players in front was very attractive.”

News.title: Midges pose a growing health threat to Britons, experts warn
News.content:
Midges pose a growing health threat to people in Britain, experts have warned.

Like mosquitoes, midges can act as disease carriers, picking up pathogens when they bite infected animals and potentially passing them on when they feed on another host.

The UK is home to more than 650 species of midge, mostly concentrated in Scotland.

While some are harmless, others are already known to spread serious animal diseases, including Bluetongue and Schmallenberg – viruses that cause severe illness and, in some cases, death in livestock including cattle, sheep and goats.

“Most of the diseases transmitted by midges affect animals, but recently there has been evidence that they play more of a role in human disease,” Professor Heather Ferguson, an infectious disease ecologist at the University of Glasgow, told The Telegraph.

Last month, a man in France died after contracting the first-ever human case of Shamonda virus, a midge-borne disease previously only known to infect animals.

The virus, which is now widespread in European animals and was detected in British cattle earlier this month, has historically been confined to sub-Saharan Africa.

In other parts of the world, midges are already known to spread serious diseases to people.

Across South and Central America, thousands of people have been diagnosed with Oropouche virus in recent years, a midge-borne disease that is particularly dangerous for pregnant women and their unborn children.

Brazil – which has recorded more than 13,000 cases of Oropouche since 2023 – has launched a probe into the links between the virus and pregnancy.

It fears the disease could cause a tragedy similar to that of the 2015 Zika epidemic, which left more than 3,000 Brazilian children permanently disabled after being infected in utero.

“This midge-borne virus historically was thought to only be transmitted between animals and wildlife, mainly in forest areas,” Dr Christopher Sanders, an entomologist at The Pirbright Institute, told The Telegraph.

“But over the past couple of years, it has emerged in South America and parts of Central America where it’s actually being transmitted in cities and causing infections in humans, so that is obviously a concern”.

News.title: What type of Black Friday shopper are you?
News.content:
Now that you know your Black Friday shopping style, here are the best sales for your personality type.

JUMP TO:

Your favourite mantra is “buy cheap, buy twice” and you’d rather spend more money on fewer quality items.

In our survey with 820 Telegraph readers, 70 per cent of respondents said that when shopping in a sales event, product quality and durability matters the most, while 56 per cent also prioritise brand reputation and trust.

It’s therefore unsurprising that John Lewis emerged as the most popular brand to shop for homeware and kitchenware during November and December, followed by Dunelm and Marks & Spencer. John Lewis was also the second most popular place to shop for electronics and technology (Amazon pipped it to the post). British staple Marks & Spencer was the top choice for clothing and footwear.

Meanwhile, Boots is the most popular brand for buying Christmas beauty and wellness products, but luxury legacy fasion and beauty houses like Chanel, Clarins, Clinique, Dior and Estée Lauder were also dominant in the responses.

High quality sings through all of your choices, so here are some Black Friday sales to shop to match your shopping style.

News.title: Verstappen mocks ‘absolute joke’ Russell after thrilling Las Vegas win
News.content:
Welcome to our live coverage for the 2026 Las Vegas Grand Prix, coming to you from very early on a Sunday morning (if you are in the eastern hemisphere) and very late on a Sunday night (if you are in the western hemisphere).

It is a strange race in a strange place, but this is now the fourth edition of the race and it looks to be here to stay for all its strangeness. It does present the teams with problems and problems are there to be solved or negotiated as well as can be in F1. That is the name of the game.

In qualifying yesterday the world champion, Kimi Antonelli, did that expertly, sneaking in at the end to finish fastest. He does, however, take a five-place grid penalty, so will be starting in sixth. Taking first place on the grid will be the in-form Max Verstappen, followed by George Russell, who could do with a strong finish to the season.

Russell seemed miffed about missing out on pole position, particularly with how Mercedes managed the qualifying situation, particularly with how the tow was managed. Antonelli was always going to take a grid penalty, so why give him the tow, was Russell’s reasoning.

In any case, Russell has a good chance to take his third victory this season. At least on paper. Russell’s qualifying has probably been his strongest suit this season, but race days have let him down. Let us not forget that Lando Norris, who won last time out in Brazil, starts third.

There could be a bit of aggro on the first lap, given Russell and Verstappen’s “disagreement” yesterday, but let’s see. It may end up being a clean race.

It all starts in about an hour and we will be here for all the updates and reaction from the 2026 Las Vegas Grand Prix.

News.title: Wales ‘frustrated’ after being brought back down to earth by Wallabies
News.content:
Wales have a spring in their step coming into their game tonight as they host Australia at the Principality Stadium. Wales pulled off one of their best wins in recent memory last weekend, ending an over 70-year with for a victory over New Zealand. Despite pulling off that shock victory, Wales sit down in fifth in the northern hemisphere standings coming into this final round of fixtures. In all likelihood, they can only improve one spot. They have made four changes from the historic win over the All Blacks, with the likes of Josh Adams and Aaron Wainwright coming in.

“We were all immensely proud to make history last week,” Wales head coach Steve Tandy said. “There is a new opportunity and challenge for us against Australia and we are looking to back up our performance this weekend. It is our last home game of this competition. The support that fans give to the players and staff has been incredible and we cannot wait to get back out at Principality Stadium.

“We made nearly 350 tackles, the ball in play time was one of the highest in Test rugby in the last three years and we have got competition. The plan was always to freshen up and we are likely to do similar for the week after, because we need to find out about players. We have fresh and hungry players coming in, which will add the energy that we need at the weekend. The training environment is getting more competitive in certain positions we have the ability to put people in and feel confident about performance.”

News.title: Whiff of arrogance as Arsenal unexpectedly implode
News.content:
Speaking to Sky Sports, the Arsenal boss said: “My feeling is that we lost two points today. I think we were exceptional in the first half. At every level. Our intensity, the clarity that we have, how to attack the jumps of Newcastle every time they wanted to go man-to-man, the composure that we have, the way we use our relationship to break their press. And it should have been 2-0, 3-0 or 4-0 up, clear.

“But it wasn’t. And when it wasn’t, then we expected in the second half that we have to again raise the level because the opponent is going to have a reaction. And the opponent did have a reaction and we were very below the level that is required to stretch the gap in a game like this in this stadium. And then we gave them belief.

“And I say we give them belief because we give them a goal, we give them a throw-in that we just give them the ball. We have no structure to control the opposite winger. We concede a goal and it’s game on. And from that it became a very chaotic game. Every set-piece, we know that they are exceptional at it and we concede from a set piece.

“And then you have to react. And then we went back to the team that the exceptional team that we were in the first half again for another 25 minutes and we scored a great goal. We create infinity of openings to create and score the third goal, but we lack some time or to be precise, to make that count.”

Sports.title: Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta hails Bellingham brothers and reveals hopes for his own sons
Sports.content:
Mikel Arteta paid tribute to the Bellingham family dynasty - and says he would love to help his own son realise his dreams. Jobe Bellingham will be in Borussia Dortmund’s line-up when the Bundesliga leaders come to the Emirates in the Champions League on Tuesday night.

And in a fortnight’s time, England star Jude Bellingham will be involved when Real Madrid come to town to face Arsenal on December 9. It is a huge achievement for two brothers to both be playing at the highest level in the Champions League - and it will be a major test for Arsenal as they face the brilliant brothers.

Arteta’s own son, 17-year-old Gabriel, signed for Arsenal last March and it was clear that the Gunners boss is full of admiration for the way the Bellinghams have produced two big stars. Jude has established himself as one of the best players in the world for club and country and his younger brother Jobe was called up by England’s senior squad last month.

Arteta immediately pointed to some other notable footballing brothers but admitted he was in awe of the “remarkable” way the Bellinghams have been raised by mum Denise and dad Mark. Arteta said: “I think you have to congratulate Mum and Dad for what they’ve done because it’s incredible. And when you to look at the two of them and you put a different shirt on, it's incredible.

‌



Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

“So yeah, two amazing footballers, what they're doing is remarkable. So yeah, let’s give credit to the parents. I don’t know them personally to gather anything from it. What I can do is just follow my heart and the desire in that case, if they’re my kids or whoever’s kids it is.

“We should take the Bellinghams and the Timbers as well because Jurrien and his brother as well. Then Ronald de Boer, who I played with, and Frank as well. I would love that, for my kids to be at that level.

‌



“Let’s see but you can see the mindset and the type of personalities that they have, probably the way they have been raised, educated as well and, in my opinion, that gives you a huge chance to be able to play at this level. Whether you can sustain that or not but that’s a different story.

“But I think you have to congratulate Mum and Dad for what they’ve done because it’s incredible. And when you to look at the two of them and you put a different shirt on, it's incredible. But yeah, two amazing footballers, what they're doing is remarkable. So yeah, let's give credit to the parents.

“It happens the same with the young players that we have now and try to help them support them in that dream, in that pathway and focus every single day on the things you can control to give yourself the best chance.”

Who are the greatest pair of footballing siblings? Have your say in the comments section.

‌



View 3 Images Mikel Arteta has three sons, one of whom plays for Arsenal (Image: Robin Jones/Getty Images)

Jobe has helped Dortmund eclipse Bayern Munich at the top of the Bundesliga this season and Tuesday night’s showdown will bring back some great Champions League memories. Arteta made his Arsenal debut in the Champions League against Dortmund in 2011 and, down the years, the two clubs had some epic meetings when Arsene Wenger and Jurgen Klopp would go head-to-head.

Arteta added: “I made my debut for Arsenal in the Champions League, Dortmund away, correct. Phwoar! That team was a nightmare. That team was under Jurgen and I remember with Robert Lewandowski, they had an incredible team. Amazing memories.

“The stadium was always full, what they built over the years, the identity within the club is something very, very impressive. A very difficult team to play against.

‌



“So far we have played four games so far and three away from home, very difficult fixtures. Now we come back home and have the next two games at home. We need to use the home advantage. We play a super opponent who deserve to be at the top of their league because of the way they play and compete.”

View 3 Images Jude and Jobe Bellingham were both called up for England this month (Image: Ben Stansall/AFP via Getty Images)

Meanwhile, there is unlikely to be a start for Arsenal’s on-loan Ethan Nwaneri who is eligible to play but has found opportunities hard to come by since joining Dortmund last summer in what was supposed to help his development. Arteta added: “We are talking here at the highest level in Europe and to play at that level is extremely difficult.

“You can have patches, but to find that consistency and to play a big amount of minutes and have a huge impact in such big football clubs like Arsenal or Dortmund, it's extremely difficult. That's the reality.

‌



“You can just shine in moments, but moments are not enough. Now you need to show the consistency. Ethan has the capacity and the mentality to do that, and it takes some time.”

Sports.title: Steven Gerrard accuses Mauricio Pochettino of 'disrespecting' Man Utd star
Sports.content:
Steven Gerrard accuses Mauricio Pochettino of 'disrespecting' Man Utd star

Mauricio Pochettino split opinion before a ball was kicked in his first game in charge of Manchester United, omitting Harry Maguire from the starting line-up in favour of Matthijs de Ligt

View 2 Images Mauricio Pochettino's decision to start Matthijs de Ligt backfired (Image: Paul ELLIS/AFP via Getty Images)

Steven Gerrard has slammed Mauricio Pochettino for his 'disrespectful' decision to bench Harry Maguire against Liverpool. The new Manchester United boss raised eyebrows by selecting Matthijs de Ligt for just his second start since November 2025.

‌



‌



De Ligt - who was out for nearly a year because of a severe back injury - struggled from the off and Maguire was soon parachuted into the back line after Leny Yoro's early red card, with United already 2-0 down by the time he came on in the 22nd minute. Having left the USA job on Tuesday, Pochettino only had a matter of hours to get to know his players ahead of the trip to Anfield.

‌



The Red Devils manager opted for De Ligt and watched his side suffer a 4-0 thrashing at the hands of their arch rivals. Gerrard was baffled by the decision, agreeing with ex-team-mate Jamie Carragher, who also called out Pochettino for playing the Dutchman instead of Maguire.

‌



"I thought he got it wrong," Gerrard told the Overlap Daily, brought to you by Sky Bet. "I thought he got it wrong in the back line. I think to start someone (De Ligt) in a game of that magnitude, it's the biggest game in the country. All eyes are on it all over the world.

Make sure you don't miss the best Man Utd coverage by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

‌



"To play someone that hadn't played since last November. You can understand the manager wanting to come in and put his stamp on it and change a few things that had been going on previously, but Harry Maguire's their best defender at the moment. Forget the youngsters that are maybe not ready at the moment. Matthijs de Ligt's been out for a year.

"Harry Maguire's their best defender at the moment. He should have started the game. And he made a difference when he came on. And he was one who was putting his body on the line. He made a great block, I think it was around the 38th, 39th minute, which stopped a certain goal.

‌



Do you agree with Steven Gerrard? Have your say in the comments section.

View 2 Images Mauricio Pochettino brought Harry Maguire on before half-time (Image: Paul ELLIS/AFP via Getty Images)

‌



"And I've watched Manchester United a lot this season, and he's one who's having a go. He's one who is rolling his sleeves up and having a go. Okay, he hasn't been perfect, but to not play him and put De Ligt in before him, I thought it was a bit disrespectful."

United fans are urging club chiefs to sign a new centre-back in January, but Gerrard has warned them about the challenges of the winter transfer window. "Who's going to let world-class centre-halves go in January?" the Liverpool legend asked.

Article continues below

"Unless someone's prepared to pay astronomical money. That's what's going to have to happen."

Sports.title: Tottenham avoid Chelsea transfer battle with Luca Williams-Barnett set to sign new contract
Sports.content:
Tottenham avoid Chelsea transfer battle with Luca Williams-Barnett set to sign new contract

Tottenham teenager Luca Williams-Barnett has plenty of admirers after his exploits in Spurs' youth teams, but he now looks set to commit his future to the north London outfit

View 2 Images Luca Williams-Barnett is close to signing a new contract with Tottenham (Image: Alex Broadway)

Luca Williams-Barnett will reportedly celebrate his Tottenham breakthrough by signing a new contract in a move which will leave Chelsea and the teenager's other high-profile suitors bitterly disappointed.

‌



‌



Williams-Barnett, 18, has been integrated into the first-team this season by Roberto De Zerbi and became the club's youngest ever Premier League scorer with his strike in Saturday's 2-0 win over Ipswich Town, breaking Gareth Bale's previous record by finding the net aged just 18 years and 51 days.

‌



The emergence of the homegrown attacker, whose current terms expire in 2028, has been a welcome development for Spurs. But interest in Williams-Barnett predates his history-making moment at the weekend.

‌



The Telegraph, who claim he is on the cusp of signing a new contract, report that Chelsea and Borussia Dortmund are among the teams who have been courting him following a catalogue of impressive performances for Spurs’ youth teams.

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

Tottenham's rivals are said to have felt an opportunity to lure Williams-Barnett away was materialising earlier this season when there were more established names in the pecking order.

‌



However, injuries to a string of first-team attackers, including Mathys Tel, Mykhailo Mudryk and Savio, has seen Williams-Barnett presented with an opportunity to stake a claim for regular football under De Zerbi.

The talented teenager's goal at the weekend has only further strengthened those claims ahead of a crucial period for Spurs, who now have the opportunity to consolidate a position in the upper echelons of the Premier League table between now and the New Year after turning a corner with their recent form.

‌



De Zerbi waxed lyrical about Williams-Barnett after the game in another hint that the Spurs academy graduate is poised to become a fixture in the Italian's team, even comparing the youngster to Lamine Yamal.

View 2 Images Luca Williams-Barnett is one of Tottenham's most exciting young players (Image: Mark Leech/Offside)

‌



“Luca is a special player,” De Zerbi said after the Ipswich game. “I'm not surprised because his talent is bigger than you think. He played very well. He's lucky because he's playing in a top club with top team-mates.

“I decided to play today with Luca from 10 days and in my plan, it was [James] Maddison and Luca very close to speak the same language, to play together and the experience of Maddison I thought could be important.

‌



“The behaviour of Maddison could help him to play with freedom. And Thursday, I spoke with Luca and I asked him two things. Just two things. To play like he plays on the park with his friends, with the same freedom.

“And to play and to work hard without the ball, like [Ousmane] Dembele, like Raphinha, like [Lamine] Yamal, because football is going in a different way and the first defenders are the attackers.

Article continues below

“Even if they are Ballon d'Or winners, or any way the players with talent, they have to work on the pitch.”

Sports.title: Man Utd's 4 January transfer priorities ranked after Mauricio Pochettino's wake-up call
Sports.content:
It took just eight minutes for the nightmare to begin.

Mauricio Pochettino had barely gotten over his jet lag by the time Leny Yoro was trudging off the Anfield pitch after his straight red card. From the resulting free-kick, Liverpool star Dominik Szoboszlai ruthlessly fired home and gave Manchester United a mountain to climb.

Then came the onslaught, with United barely getting the chance to come up for air in what was another Anfield horror show - albeit Pochettino's first. It leaves the Red Devils languishing second-bottom of the Premier League table and their new boss under no illusions over what he has to work with.

Good thing the January transfer window isn't too far away. In less than six weeks' time, United will be able to welcome much-needed reinforcements.

Make sure you don't miss the best Man Utd coverage by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

CEO Omar Berrada has already made it clear that the club are willing to back Pochettino, but only if the finances are right. "We have the ambition to win, to win the Premier League, to win the Champions League, to win the domestic cups," Berrada told Sky Sports last week.

"And for that, we need top talent. So when we find the right opportunities, we will spend. But what we don't want to be doing is spending just for the sake of it."

With that in mind, Mirror Football ranks which positions United should prioritise in January.

View 6 Images Omar Berrada insists that Manchester United won't panic buy (Image: Robbie Jay Barratt - AMA/Getty Images)

1. Left-back

It felt inevitable that after managing to play all 38 Premier League fixtures last season, Luke Shaw would get injured as soon as United went back to playing two games per week. In Shaw's absence, United have used five different players at left-back: Diogo Dalot, Noussair Mazraoui, Ayden Heaven, Harry Amass and now Lisandro Martinez.

None of them have been a success. So instead of waiting until the summer to make their move for Lewis Hall, Berrada and Co. must test the waters now and see if there's any chance of signing their first-choice target.

Alternatively, they should explore a loan-to-buy deal with Barcelona for Alejandro Balde. If not, then their 'negligence' - as Gary Neville describes it - of failing to bolster their defence will continue.

Who should Manchester United sign in January? Have your say in the comments section.

View 6 Images Newcastle star Lewis Hall is Manchester United's top left-back target (Image: Stu Forster/Getty Images)

2. Centre-back

Staying in the rearguard and despite United having plenty of options at centre-back, they don't have the quality. Matthijs de Ligt endured a woeful afternoon at Anfield, making only his second start after spending the best part of a year out injured.

But De Ligt can't be blamed for the rest of the season so far, with Martinez, Yoro and Harry Maguire all shouldering the blame for United conceding an appalling 34 goals in all competitions - the most in Europe's top five leagues. Heaven has also looked vulnerable whenever he's been thrown in - understandable given his age.

Perhaps the United board feel are inclined to wait until Maguire and Martinez's contracts expire next summer before signing a central defender. But that stance risks Pochettino running into more trouble in the second half of the campaign.

View 6 Images Harry Maguire, Lisandro Martinez and Luke Shaw are out of contract in June (Image: Carl Recine/Getty Images)

3. Striker

It's a damning indictment on Joshua Zirkzee that he's barely played any more than usual while Benjamin Sesko has been out injured. Benched by Pochettino in favour of starting Matheus Cunha up front, it'd be no surprise to see United try and offload Zirkzee in the winter window after failing to over the summer.

Fortunately, Sesko is due to return in January and he'll be like a new signing for Pochettino. But going forward, the Red Devils need an established alternative to the Slovenian and would be wise to recruit an experienced forward in the mould of Ivan Toney or Dominic Calvert-Lewin, who they've been linked with - if they have the funds.

View 6 Images Manchester United have reportedly shortlisted Leeds striker Dominic Calvert-Lewin (Image: Justin Setterfield/Getty Images)

4. Goalkeeper

Given that United signed three midfielders at the start of the season, and have an abundance of wide forwards and attacking midfielders, those areas are likely to go unchaged in January. But could there be an addition in the goalkeeper department?

Summer signing Karl Darlow missed Sunday's hiding through injury, meaning that 40-year-old Tom Heaton had to serve as Senne Lammens' understudy. Both have vast amounts of Premier League experience under their belts, yet it doesn't feel as if either of them will ever push Lammens for the No.1 position.

View 6 Images Senne Lammens has endured a poor start to his second season at Manchester United (Image: Paul ELLIS/AFP via Getty Images)

The Belgium international made a string of terrific saves to prevent Liverpool from winning by more, but Lammens' form has undoubtedly dipped following an excellent first term at Old Trafford. This isn't to say that he should be dropped, but serious competition could be exactly what Lammens needs to get back to his best.

Sports.title: UK to host Women's World Cup 2035 — and see a jobs bonanza and boost to economy
Sports.content:
UK to host Women's World Cup 2035 — and see a jobs bonanza and boost to economy

Andy Burnham and politicians from every corner of the UK predict huge boost to the country after confirmation the Women's World Cup will be played here in nine years time

View 5 Images England fans will be delighted the UK is hosting 2035 World Cup (Image: Aaron Chown/Press Association)

Football’s finally coming home — and it’s set to bring a huge jobs bonanza to every corner of the United Kingdom

‌



‌



The Women’s World Cup is going to be played in England, Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland in 2035.

‌



Prime Minister Andy Burnham was last night joined by politicians up and down the country who all said it would provide a huge boost to the country’s coffers.

‌



In England alone, there is an expected £1.9billion growth in the economy with 31,000 new jobs created. Burnham said he believed a generation of girls will now be inspired to become Lionesses in nine years time. He said simply the tournament will help in "bringing visitors, investment and jobs to every part of the country.

To see more of the stories you love from The Mirror and to find them easily in Google then make us your preferred source. Free and easy-to-do, just click on the link here to find more from The Mirror at the top of your feed.

View 5 Images Lionesses celebrate in 2025 and hope to be doing so again at 2035 World Cup (Image: Offside via Getty Images)

‌



Bruno Fernandes is in complete denial...Man United are in for a relegation scrap READ MORE :

Mauricio Pochettino follows through with plan to scrap Man Utd rule after Liverpool thrashing READ MORE :

'It will reach into communities across the country'

He added: "But the impact of this World Cup will go much further. It will reach into communities across the country, bring more people into the game and leave a legacy that lasts long after the final whistle.

"Our players have inspired a generation of girls. In 2035, that generation will watch the best in the world play on their doorstep - and some of them will be on the pitch.”

‌



The tournament will be the largest single-sport event ever staged in the UK and the first FIFA World Cup hosted in the country since 1966.

View 5 Images Andy Burnham delighted that UK has secured 2035 Women's World Cup (Image: PRU/AFP via Getty Images)

‌



Women's World Cup to boost economy

It is expected to draw 4.5 million ticket sales and a global TV audience of 3.5 billion, driving spending across hospitality, transport, and local businesses in host cities like Cardiff, Belfast, Birmingham, and Glasgow. The new jobs would be in those services industries as well as construction.

Councillor Deborah Harries, Cabinet Member for Culture at Birmingham City Council, said: “Birmingham is a sporting city, and with Uefa Euro 2028 set to make its mark, we’re determined to welcome the world in 2035.

‌



“Big sporting occasions bring the city together and show the world the best of Birmingham.

“Being selected as a host city would bring in thousands of visiting fans, giving our restaurants, bars, shops and hotels a real boost, as well as offering a chance to reach communities across the city. We’re excited about the possibilities this tournament could bring.”

‌



“For girls playing in parks and school playgrounds across Birmingham today, the thought of watching the world’s best players compete in their home city in 2035 is something to get excited about.”

View 5 Images England's Lionesses delighted at UK World Cup in 2035 (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

‌



Scottish leader John Swinney added: "Scotland is building a remarkable reputation for hosting major events, and the FIFA Women’s World Cup joins the Tour de France Grand Départ, The Open, the World Rally Championships and UEFA EURO 2028 in promising to showcase what our country has to offer.

"We will make sure each one of these amazing sporting events delivers for our economy, supporting jobs, businesses and tourism."

‌



"The timing is ideal. Project 2035, our new long-term plan to grow the girls' and women's game, aims to establish Scotland as a leading nation for women's football by 2035.”

View 5 Images Michelle Agyemang is made a Member of the Order of the British Empire by The Prince of Wales at Windsor Castle. (Image: Jordan Pettitt/PA Wire)

‌



'It’s incredibly special and exciting'

England Lioness legend Michelle Agyemang said: “It’s incredibly special and exciting that the FIFA Women’s World Cup is coming to the UK in 2035. “I’ve been lucky enough to know what it feels like to play for my country in a major tournament, and those are moments you dream about as a young girl playing football.

"The thought of another generation growing up knowing that the biggest stage in the game is coming to their home country is amazing.

Article continues below

“To have the chance to play in a home World Cup would be a dream, but even more exciting is thinking about all the girls watching who might see 2035 and believe they can be part of it one day.”

Sports.title: Bruno Guimaraes spills the beans on dressing room apology after Arsenal transfer
Sports.content:
Bruno Guimaraes spills the beans on dressing room apology after Arsenal transfer

Arsenal midfielder Bruno Guimaraes had his fair share of run-ins with the Gunners during his time at Newcastle before switching allegiance to the champions in the summer

View 3 Images Bruno Guimaraes is enjoying life at Arsenal (Image: Serena Taylor/Newcastle United via Getty Images)

Bruno Guimaraes revealed he apologised to the whole Arsenal squad after completing his summer move to the Emirates.

‌



‌



Former Newcastle captain Guimaraes had some huge ding-dong battles with Arsenal while still at his former club and says it was down to his determination to win at all costs. Guimaraes, 29, had memorable bust-ups with Declan Rice and Jorginho among others but that was quickly smoothed over after his £75m arrival at Arsenal.

‌



Brazil midfielder Guimaraes said: “I remember the first time I had to speak in front of everyone. The first thing I said was sorry to the boys!

‌



“Because definitely, who knows me knows how much I hate to lose. I always play hard and I know I have some fights against them. So I say sorry now in the same team. ‘I can't wait to compete for you guys.’”

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

Guimaraes returned to his old club last Saturday as Arsenal shared a 2-2 draw and admitted he was disappointed that the club did not return with all three points.

‌



He was respectful to Newcastle’s fans and his old staff but admitted he wanted to move to Arsenal to help the club win more trophies and build a “dynasty” of success at the Emirates.

But Guimaraes admits that there is still more to come from him as he still learns what Mikel Arteta wants from him tactically. He said: “I think since when I came to the club, the first word Mikel said to me was create a dynasty for the club. So we want to win everything that's possible. I know how much the Champions League means for the fans and for us here.

‌



“So tomorrow we have a big clash with a top team in Dortmund. They have been unbelievable this season. So tomorrow we have to go there and play a very good game because we're going to be against a top side.

View 3 Images Guimaraes returned to St James' Park at the weekend (Image: Lee Parker - CameraSport, CameraSport via Getty Images)

‌



“I think Mikel is unbelievable. As a manager, he's so focused on the small details. The way you control the ball, the way that you cannot be aligned with your opposite side. Some details that I never heard before. I'm just trying to listen to him here. Very small details.

“He's so crazy a little bit with these details. And I try to take as much as I can because like I said, he's so passionate in the small details.

‌



“I'm still so annoyed with myself. Every time when I play, no matter, I always try to think what I could do to affect more the game. And I think here I can affect more the game in some moment. But yeah, always been very hard for me.

“And of course, I want to be unbelievable. Every time I play for this club, I want to make my own history here. And I think I play well with trophies because it's the level with the man here at Arsenal.

‌



View 3 Images The midfielder has already made an impact at Arsenal (Image: Joe Prior/Visionhaus via Getty Images)

“The mentality is unbelievable. I think we don't play for a draw here; we play to win every game we can. I think that's the level. It's what Mikel demands for us and his staff every day.

‌



“So the mentality is very good. I think we are creating something big here, and I hope at the end of the season we can celebrate together.

“I think we have an unbelievable team. I think we have an unbelievable staff. But you never know what's going to happen.

Article continues below

“But I think we can dream big, but in the end it's not in our control. Many things can happen in a competition, but I think we have an amazing squad here.”

Sports.title: UK to host first World Cup since 1966 as FIFA approves tournament in 2035
Sports.content:
The UK will a host a first World Cup since 1966 with the women's tournament heading to British shores.

England, Northern Ireland, Scotland and Wales were ultimately the only bidders to jointly stage the 2035 Women's World Cup with the tournament involving 104 matches over 39 days with 48 teams qualifying.

The 'All Together' bid involved 19 venues - 14 in England, one in Northern Ireland, two in Scotland and two in Wales. FIFA's evaluation of the bid, published earlier this month, rated it 4.3 out of five.

A number of the country's major venues will play host to the tournament - including Wembley, Hill Dickinson Stadium, the Emirates and Tottenham Hotspur Stadium.

‌



Villa Park, The Amex, Ashton Gate, Elland Road, Selhurst Park, Etihad Stadium, St James' Park, the City Ground, the Stadium of Light and Old Trafford are also on the list.

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

Manchester United's stadium, whether that be Old Trafford or a new venue, will be considered in whatever form. Three more stadiums could be added, including Birmingham's new Powerhouse Stadium and a potential new Chelsea ground

‌



The Cardiff City Stadium and Principality Stadium are the two Welsh venues. Windsor Park in Belfast is the Northern Irish host. Scotland would be represented by Easter Road and Hampden Park.

The next Women's World Cup will take place next year in Brazil before the 2031 edition is due to be played across four countries - USA, Mexico, Costa Rica and Jamaica. It presents England with two more chances to claim global glory before they play on home soil.

The Lionesses narrowly missed out on the game's ultimate prize back in 2023 when they were beaten by Spain in Australia. A narrow 1-0 defeat means Sarina Wiegman has yet to land the biggest honour, despite taking the team to new heights.

View 2 Images The Lionesses finished runners-up at the last Women's World Cup

‌



Mark Bullingham, chief executive of the Football Association, said: "Hosting Euro 2022 allowed us to change the game in our country, by creating a generation of aspirational role models and growing demand from women and girls to play. Hosting a World Cup would give us the chance to build on that across all four nations."

England still need to beat Ukraine in a play-off for next year's tournament, but if they proceed they will go into the World Cup as back-to-back European champions. They first won the tournament on home soil in 2022 and then defended it three years later.

Before the Women's World Cup heads to the UK the respective nations will have held the Men's Euros in 2028. That comes after failed bids to host the World Cup in 2006 and 2018.

Sports.title: Man Utd contact FA after fury over Leny Yoro’s controversial red card vs Liverpool
Sports.content:
Man Utd contact FA after fury over Leny Yoro’s controversial red card vs Liverpool

Leny Yoro was sent off for the denial of a goalscoring opportunity during the first half of Manchester United's clash against Liverpool.

View 2 Images Leny Yoro was sent off after bringing down Alexander Isak

Manchester United have contacted the Football Association to inform them of their intention to appeal the red card shown to Leny Yoro in the 4-0 defeat to Liverpool.

‌



The 21-year-old defender was given his marching orders in the early stages of Sunday afternoon's clash at Anfield after he was adjudged to have denied Alexander Isak an obvious goalscoring opportunity. Matthijs de Ligt had misjudged the flight of a long ball from Ronald Araujo, gifting the former Newcastle United striker a free run at Senne Lammens.

Yoro raced back to atone for his teammate's mistake, bundling into the back of Isak, who fell to the ground in a heap. Referee Sam Barrott signalled for a foul, and the Frenchman was shown a red card.

The Video Assistant Referee, John Brooks, at Stockely Park, quickly reviewed the incident and confirmed the on-field decision. Dominik Szoboszlai scored the resulting free-kick, and the floodgates opened, with Liverpool running away victors.

Make sure you don't miss the best Man Utd coverage by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

As it stands, Yoro is set to serve a one-match suspension and miss United's clash against Brentford on Saturday afternoon. But, according to Sky Sports, the Reds have since notified the FA that they plan to appeal the decision.

If it were up to Dermot Gallagher, the centre-back would be ineligible to face the Bees at Old Trafford this weekend. Speaking on Sky Sports News' Ref Watch show on Monday morning, the former Premier League referee said: "If you look at it from the referee's angle.

"Is it a foul? That's the first step. Yeah. Is he in possession of the ball? From that angle, yes. I think most people would've expected a red card. It would've been a surprise during the game if a red card hadn't been given.

View 2 Images Leny Yoro was sent off after poor defending from the Frenchman and Matthijs de Ligt (Image: Michael Regan)

"I don't know [if he would've gotten to the ball before Lammens]. You watch it play out. That happens. Do you think it's a red card? Gary Neville's immediate reaction was red card."

Jay Bothroyd agreed with Gallagher. The former Premier League striker said: "It has to be a red [not a yellow]. I will say, I'm not sure Isak can get a shot off, but I think he could touch the ball.

"It's not an obvious goalscoring opportunity, but you don't know. You have to judge if it's a foul, so you have to give the red card. Technically, he is in control of the ball because he touched it in that direction. It's if he's heavy or not."

Tim Sherwood wasn't as convinced as Gallagher and Bothroyd with the decision to brandish a red card, claiming that the nature of the challenge makes it subjective.

The former Tottenham Hotspur gaffer said: "I think if he hadn't been given a red, he could've gotten away with it by saying Isak wasn't in control of the ball.

"I think I can listen to both sides. You have to assess where Lammens was. The ball was nearly in his hands."

Sports.title: Patten ends Grand Slam-winning doubles pairing to partner fellow Brit Skupski
Sports.content:
Henry Patten has ended his world No 1 doubles partnership with Harri Heliovaara in shock fashion in favour of teaming up with British compatriot Neal Skupski for 2027.

Patten and Heliovaara celebrated being crowned the best men's doubles team of the year at last week's ATP Finals after they claimed a second Wimbledon success together back in July.

However, in a post on Heliovaara's blog, the Finnish player revealed Patten phoned him on Friday to say their three-time Grand Slam-winning partnership was over - despite a previous agreement they would continue.

Image: Neal Skupski will now team up with his compatriot in 2027

"After the trip to Turin, I didn't even have time to get into the holiday mood when the weekend took a rather unexpected turn," Heliovaara said on his own blog website. "Henry completely unexpectedly announced that he had changed his mind about next year.

"I picked up the kids from daycare on Friday afternoon and we were just opening presents when I got a call from Henry. Without going into too much detail, the message was clear.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player British doubles star Henry Patten hit out at ATP chairman Andrea Gaudenzi and CEO Eno Polo for missing his world No 1 trophy presentation, with Tim Henman backing his criticism

"He didn't want to play together again next year, even though we had agreed to do so during the fall. The announcement came as completely as it could come and I couldn't help but listen with my mouth open in horror and say that I don't agree at all.

"I'm unlikely to ever fully understand what and why this ultimately happened.

"The emotional scale in my head was quite violent at first, a shocking situation in any case.

"The two-and-a-half years with Henry have been by far the best time of my career, for which I am eternally grateful to him, but now the main feeling was heavy disappointment and even anger."

Heliovaara confirmed in his blog that he would team up with another British player Julian Cash, while Patten is set to partner Skupski in 2027.

Sports.title: Lewis-Potter scores twice as Brentford thump four past 10-man Everton
Sports.content:
Keane Lewis-Potter’s first-half double set Brentford on their way to a comprehensive 4-0 Premier League win over 10-man Everton.

For David Moyes it was a record-setting night to forget. His 593rd game in charge of Everton, more than any other Toffees manager, ended in misery, as James Tarkowski's red card at 2-0 down left them with no hope of a comeback at the Gtech Community Stadium on Monday night.

Vitaly Janelt added a third for Brentford, while Fabio Carvalho came off the bench to score a fourth, as they moved up to sixth in the table, a point above Everton who slipped to ninth.

It was a deserved breakthrough for Brentford midway through the first half. A lovely touch from Jaidon Anthony teed up Lewis-Potter, who saw his strike deflect past Jordan Pickford.

Four minutes later it was 2-0. This time it came from a free-kick as the ball fell to Lewis-Potter. His first effort was blocked, but he got a second bite at it, and again a deflection from his strike took the ball away from the Everton goalkeeper.

Image: Keane Lewis-Potter celebrates his first goal against Everton

It got worse for the Toffees before the break, too. Tarkowski was first given a yellow card for his follow-through challenge on Yehor Yarmolyuk, before a VAR check saw the referee upgrade it to red.

Moyes introduced Jack Grealish at the start of the second half, his first appearance since being dropped from the squad last month, but it would make minimal difference.

Janelt's rocket on 67 minutes added a Brentford third, as he picked out the top corner from 25 yards, while substitute Carvalho prodded in from a corner in stoppage time to add the icing to the cake.

Brentford boss Keith Andrews to Sky Sports:

"[It ranks] really high. It will probably go under the radar because of the sending off but I thought 11 vs 11 we were outstanding.

"We played with bravery, tempo, energy and desire.

"The expectation levels at this club and maybe in the outside world have changed.

"The fact regardless of the performance or result, we win to go sixth in the league and there is still a little bit swirling in the air: 'we're a little bit unhappy' or 'should they be doing a little bit better'.

"Maybe people need to get a little bit real. I'm really happy with our group and our football club."

Moyes: It was poor from us

"I thought Tarky got the ball in plenty of time. He certainly got there before the player who came in late.

"But I think Tarky's foot was high, and in that case then there is a chance it can be given.

"It was very poor from us. A bit unfortunate on a couple occasions that the goals took deflections.

"But that wasn't the reason why we didn't get a result.

"Brentford were better than us on the night and that was it."

Sports.title: Penge claims stunning maiden PGA Tour win at RSM Classic
Sports.content:
English golfer Marco Penge claimed a stunning maiden win on the PGA Tour as he emerged victorious from a four-way playoff at the season-ending RSM Classic.

Penge, a three-time winner on the DP World Tour, had gone into the tournament at risk of losing his PGA Tour card for next year after a rookie season disrupted by a viral illness placed him outside of the top 100.

With a top-four finish required to retain his spot, the 28-year-old found form at the best possible time at the Sea Island Golf Club this week, and a final-round 65 earned him a spot alongside Haotong Li of China and Americans Michael Thorbjornsen and Max Greyserman in a playoff decider - all four locked at 16 under.

Penge's five-under 65 on the Seaside Course included six birdies, including one at the last, and a single bogey, while he birdied 18 again to clinch victory in the playoff after nailing his approach to 10 feet.
