Sports.title: Are Man Utd genuinely in a relegation battle?
Sports.content:
What started as a blip has become a problem far more systemic for Man Utd.

"If the name wasn't Man Utd and you're watching their performances, you'd say they are a team in a relegation fight. They're conceding lots of goals, a comedy of errors, red cards - they've won one game all season," said Sky Sports' Jamie Carragher.

Only Ipswich beaten in 11 attempts, the worst defence in Europe - and a 4-0 hammering at Liverpool on Sunday to wipe the gloss off Mauricio Pochettino's arrival within 12 first-half minutes.

Carragher added: "This Manchester United back four can't cope with pace. They're a million miles off it in terms of coming up against what they are in the Premier League."

The unthinkable is beginning to become thinkable. Are United in an actual relegation battle now?

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports' Kaveh Solhekol looks at what it could cost Man Utd if they were to be relegated from the Premier League.

"They're in a relegation fight right now because of where they are in the table," said Carragher after a fifth defeat of the season left them with their lowest points tally at this stage of a season since 1972. "You can't say anything else when you look at their record this season.

"We don't believe it will happen over a 38-game season, but they haven't had the most difficult of starts. They've played a lot of promoted teams; they haven't played the best team in the league, Arsenal, yet.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Watch free match highlights of Mauricio Pochettino's first game in charge of Man Utd, a 4-0 thrashing at Liverpool

"I don't think they'll go down, but this idea that they haven't got a scrap on their hands, they have."

It seems unfathomable. But should it? The numbers don't give Pochettino any grounds for optimism. Only 26 teams - barely one a season - have picked up eight points or fewer from their opening 11 games in the history of the Premier League and only 13 of those, exactly half, avoided the drop.

Of course, most of those were not clubs anywhere near the size and stature of Manchester United. But even the Opta supercomputer, which provides far more contextualised feedback, is losing faith and gives them a 24 per cent chance of going down - though it does still back them to stumble to safety and finish 16th.

"You wonder how low it can get," said Gary Neville after Sunday's defeat. "It's embarrassing. I don't believe they're in a relegation fight, they'll get out of this, but this is the worst Man Utd have been in 53 years. The worst defensive team in Europe, second-bottom in the league, they've never started this badly.

"Mauricio Pochettino's options aren't great."

That may be putting it lightly. As well as the worst defence in Europe's top-five leagues across all competitions, United also have the third-worst performing attack in the Premier League, falling below their xG tally by 4.2 goals already.

In an immediately infamous tweet in 2014, then-boss David Moyes was quoted as saying United "must improve in a number of areas, including passing, creating chances and defending".

Pochettino is unlikely to admit it publicly, but behind closed doors must have similarly widespread concerns even at this early stage. United have not found themselves in the bottom two after 11 games in 40 years.

Sir Alex Ferguson was brought in as their eventual saviour that winter, but turning the tide on this United side is a significantly bigger ask.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player On the Premier League Show, Adam Binnie breaks down Manchester United's points tally this season compared to Tottenham's in 2025/26 and the big possibility of a potential relegation.

Are there personnel at his disposal who could improve matters? Potentially. Neville did pinpoint a back four of Luke Shaw, Harry Maguire, Lisandro Martinez and Diego Dalot who could at least get United out of their defensive slump.

"It's a poor back four, but it's their best back four. It could compete," he added. "But the one that started today and finished against Villa a few weeks ago, that'll get you relegated."

There is good news and bad news. Neville's quartet are unbeaten in every game they have started together since the start of 2023/24 - and can boast a 70-per-cent win ratio. Unfortunately for Pochettino, that only amounts to 10 games across more than three seasons, owing largely to availability.

But that still does not solve the problem of their limp attack. Of the 22 players to have attempted a shot for the club this season, 19 have under-performed their xG, and the three who have not, Benjamin Sesko, Joshua Zirkzee and Youri Tielemans, have scored only a solitary goal apiece.

There remain huge question marks over the Man Utd dressing room, its commitment and a lack of leadership which permeated into the public sphere in the final weeks of Michael Carrick's reign. Though Pochettino's players have shown they can perform when they want to. Carrick himself knows that better than anyone.

But his successor barely has time to address it over the next few weeks, with only one free midweek between now and the end of 2026 - and even then he has a trip to the Emirates, live on Sky Sports on December 20, to face at the end of his first uninterrupted week on the training pitch.

By that point United will be almost half-way through the Premier League season - and alarm bells will be ringing even louder if they still find themselves in the quagmire, especially with rock bottom Crystal Palace and promoted Coventry to come before then.

But might even that prove problematic for Pochettino?

"If you look at the strength of the Premier League this season, in terms of what we would call the teams you'd expect to be mid-table or near the bottom - it's probably as strong as it's ever been," said Carragher.

"There's no poor teams. There's not many great teams, but there's no poor teams.

"And that's a problem for Man Utd."

Sports.title: Has Verstappen feud reignited at wrong time for Russell?
Sports.content:
The reignition of the long-running feud between George Russell and Max Verstappen has added an entertaining twist to the end of the 2026 Formula 1 season, but it may not be what the Mercedes driver needed at this moment.

Russell and Verstappen clashed during final practice at the Las Vegas Grand Prix when the Red Bull driver, slightly cheekily, snatched track position from his Mercedes rival as they both prepared for push laps.

Irked by Verstappen's actions, which he later said he felt breached a gentleman's agreement the drivers share, Russell attempted to reclaim track position from the weaving Red Bull, with the pair making slight contact.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player George Russell and Max Verstappen collided with one another during final practice at the Las Vegas Grand Prix

The stewards summoned the two drivers following the session as they conducted an investigation, before handing Verstappen a warning.

The incident came less than a month on from Verstappen being involved a similar incident with Racing Bulls driver Liam Lawson during practice at the Mexico City Grand Prix, which resulted in both drivers being given one-place grid penalties.

Speaking to Sky Italy later that evening, Russell said: "There's nothing in the rules to say you cannot overtake someone who is starting a lap but when you do this, you are screwing this person over and he does this week in, week out with many drivers and everybody accepts it.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player George Russell reacted to the collision with Max Verstappen in final practice at the Las Vegas Grand Prix, accusing the Red Bull driver of of 'screwing' his rivals over

"I'm not just going to accept somebody to screw me over like this and walk around like they're bigger and better than everyone else. Somebody's got to stand up to that guy."

Russell's comments came after the result of qualifying in Las Vegas dictated that the pair would start together on the front row, with Verstappen ahead in pole position.

That setup a Saturday night showdown, in which the pair engaged in a thrilling battle for the lead for much of the race, before Russell dropped behind Kimi Antonelli in the latter stages and then drove into a barrier attempting to pass his Mercedes team-mate.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player George Russell hits the barrier after a lock-up when trying to overtake team-mate Kimi Antonelli at the Las Vegas Grand Prix, much to the delight of rival Max Verstappen

Verstappen reacted on team radio with apparent glee having seen Russell's error in his mirrors, and then, after closing out a superb victory, further stuck the boot into the British driver during the post-race press conference for the top three.

The four-time world champion said: "The thing is, he speaks a lot next to the track. And honestly, for me, it doesn't really bother me because he's so far below my level that it doesn't really make any sense for me anyway to try and challenge that. So, it doesn't bother me.

"And today, karma is a b****. It was honestly fantastic when I looked in my mirror and I saw what was happening [when Russell crashed]. I was like, 'fantastic, my day is only getting better.' And of course, when I then crossed the line in first, my day was complete."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Max Verstappen had a choice few words for long-time foe George Russell after winning the Las Vegas Grand Prix

A history of the Russell-Verstappen feud

With less than five months separating them in age, Russell and Verstappen have been racing each other in karting since they were children.

While Mercedes team principal Toto Wolff reflected in Las Vegas that the feud may have stretched back to those days, the first notable F1 flashpoint between the pair came in the 2023 Azerbaijan Sprint when they made contact through several corners on the opening lap.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Max Verstappen and George Russell share an angry exchange after the two made contact on the first lap of the Sprint at the Azerbaijan Grand Prix

In a post-race exchange broadcast to the world, Verstappen barked at Russell to "expect next time the same" and swore at the Mercedes driver as he walked away. He would later refer to Russell as "princess George" in an interview with the Dutch media.

A spectacular fall out between the pair then occurred towards the end of the 2024 season, after Verstappen felt Russell had played an unreasonably key role in the Red Bull driver being given a grid penalty that cost him pole for the Qatar Grand Prix.

Verstappen said in Qatar that he had "lost all respect" for Russell, who then responded with a remarkable explosive verbal attack on the Dutchman the following week at the season-ending Abu Dhabi Grand Prix.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Craig Slater took a closer look at how the Qatar penalty fallout escalated between George Russell and Max Verstappen after George labelled the Red Bull driver as a 'bully'

Russell said Verstappen had threatened to put him "in the wall" in Qatar, and said that "people have been bullied by Max for years". Verstappen questioned the accuracy of Russell's claims and labelled him a "loser" and "backstabber".

The pair clashed once more on track at the 2025 Spanish Grand Prix when Verstappen, enraged at his own team for instructing him to let Russell through to avoid receiving a penalty, appeared to wave the Mercedes past before lunging into the side of it.

Verstappen was penalised by the stewards, later admitted the move was "not right" and apologised to his team, but did not personally address Russell.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Red Bull's Max Verstappen controversially collided with George Russell towards the end of the Spanish Grand Prix - earning himself a 10-second penalty

Less talked about than the pair's clashes is a potential further tension added by Russell's boss Wolff having very publicly tried to sign Verstappen from Red Bull. Russell told Sky Sports F1 in June 2025 that his own contract extension was being delayed by Mercedes' attempts to sign Verstappen.

More 2026 pain for Russell?

The previous clashes between the pair came when Russell was in a position of strength at Mercedes, given he had performed hugely impressively during his first four seasons with the team from 2022 to 2025.

Russell had expressed belief on many occasions over the years that if Mercedes delivered a title-winning car, he was ready to grab the opportunity, and few doubted him.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player A look back at some of F1's newly-crowed champion Kimi Antonelli's best moments of the season

However, when they finally produced such a car following the major regulation changes ahead of the 2026 season, it was his far less-experienced team-mate Antonelli who snatched away what Russell thought was going to be his title.

Russell has been tormented by his struggles throughout the season, repeatedly expressing uncertainty over what was causing his deficit to Antonelli before eventually appearing to decide that he must alter his driving style to be able to match the 20-year-old Italian in the sport's latest machinery.

If there was any doubt over how painful the season had been, it was crystalised by Wolff's decision to allow the Brit to leave the track in Mexico almost immediately after the race when Antonelli sealed the title, which the Austrian said was because he found Russell "distraught".

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player With Mercedes team-mate Kimi Antonelli having won the world title at the last race, George Russell reflects on what's been a tough season for him

It was one thing Russell 'standing up' to Verstappen when he could claim that given a strong car, he would rival the Dutchman, but the way the 2026 season has played out has left Russell vulnerable, a reality which Verstappen attempted to exploit with his "not on my level" remarks.

Not only has Russell been comprehensively outperformed by Antonelli, but he has now fallen to fifth in the drivers' standings, with Verstappen's four wins in the last six races having put him firmly on course for second place.

While Mercedes have proven in the past that they will allow both their drivers to fight for championships, there is no doubt that Antonelli has made himself the team's clear top dog for the tie being.

What will happen next?

Given both championships have already been decided, the Russell-Verstappen feud is going to attract huge attention at the final two rounds of the season in Qatar and Abu Dhabi.

The best-case scenario for Russell across the season-ending triple header was to put together some strong results and enter the winter with some moment to take into 2027.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Craig Slater gives his verdict on the Las Vegas GP where Max Verstappen claimed victory after multiple lead changes and Ferrari come together raising more dilemmas for Fred Vasseur

Verstappen, who has finished on the podium at nine successive races, and his own team-mate Antonelli, were always likely to be the biggest obstacles to that.

While Verstappen insisted in Las Vegas that he wasn't motivated by Russell's remarks, his comments on radio and after the race suggested there was some extra fire in his belly, which may well remain there in the Middle East.

The sporting challenge of claiming a victory may have stiffened, but Russell has also heightened his emotional load by putt himself back in the spotlight at a time where the relative calm offered by the titles having been decided may have been welcomed.

The drivers have in recent years established a tradition of all going for dinner one night at the final round in Abu Dhabi, where Verstappen famously offered Russell a seat next to him just days after their war of words in 2024.

Sports.title: Metcalf denies poking DeJean in the eyes as NFL rules out suspension
Sports.content:
Pittsburgh Steelers wide receiver DK Metcalf will not be suspended by the NFL for appearing to poke Philadelphia Eagles defensive back Cooper DeJean in the eyes but he could still be fined, according to sources.

Metcalf denied that he intentionally stuck his fingers in the Eagles defender's facemask when addressing the media on Monday.

Having been ejected from a game for the third time in his career during the second half of the Steelers' 19-16 loss on Sunday, Metcalf initially said that he "couldn't remember" the incident, before backtracking and saying that he was trying to send a message to DeJean to "stop pushing me".

Metcalf had caught only one pass for two yards before being sent to the locker room after being flagged twice for personal fouls following a couple of confrontations with DeJean.

Image: Players and officials try to stop DK Metcalf (R) and Cooper DeJean (L) fom fighting during the Steelers-Eagles game on Sunday

The NFL will review Metcalf's actions during the game for potential fines as part of its standard disciplinary review process, ESPN and NFL Network reported, but he escapes a suspension.

The 28-year-old was banned for two games last season for swiping at a fan in Detroit and was shown the door twice earlier in his career while playing for the Seattle Seahawks.

Asked why this keeps happening, Metcalf told reporters: "I think you got to ask the people that seem to do that to me".

Metcalf noted that opponents trying to get under his skin is nothing new, saying that San Francisco 49ers players attempted to do that regularly during the Seahawks' frequent meetings with their NFC West rivals.

The two-time Pro Bowler, who is on pace for career lows in receptions and yards receiving this season, declined to blame the heated interaction on frustration, pointing out that the Steelers are "winning", though Pittsburgh (6-4) has dropped two straight after losing in Philadelphia.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the Pittsburgh Steelers against the Philadelphia Eagles from Week 11 of the NFL season.

Steelers coach Mike McCarthy called Metcalf's actions "unacceptable" but said he needed more information before deciding whether to take any action.

Metcalf did not appear to be worried about being disciplined by the Steelers or the NFL. "You've got to ask [Pittsburgh general manager] Omar [Khan] that, or anybody else other than DeKaylin," Metcalf said, using his given name.

The highest-paid wide receiver in team history also added that the Steelers need to "score points when we get the ball and not stall on third down or get a turnover on downs, stay on the field so our defense can stay off the field".

Pittsburgh remain firmly in playoff position as Thanksgiving looms but face a daunting stretch over the next three weeks that includes a pair of meeting with first-placed teams in their division - the Denver Broncos (8-2) and Jacksonville Jaguars (7-3), as well as a key clash with fellow AFC wildcard contenders the Houston Texans (4-6).

Sports.title: Aston Villa's Champions League clash with Galatasaray plunged into chaos as Turkish police hunt for a fugitive LION spotted 10 miles from the stadium
Sports.content:
Aston Villa's Champions League clash with Galatasaray plunged into chaos as Turkish police hunt for a fugitive LION spotted 10 miles from the stadium

A lion has been spotted about ten miles from the stadium where Aston Villa are due to face Galatasaray in the Champions League on Tuesday.

In a bizarre development, Turkish security and wildlife personnel were on Monday searching for the animal​, believed to be roaming loose ‌in woodland north of Istanbul.

Around 70 people, including police and other emergency personnel, have been involved in the search, with seven drones deployed. The animal was first sighted in Istanbul's Sariyer district, which is also where Galatasaray's RAMS Park is located.

According to local reports, personnel at a police station in ​the Zekeriyakoy area, north of the ​European side of Istanbul, reported seeing 'an animal ⁠resembling a lion' on surveillance cameras at ​around 9pm local time on Sunday (6pm GMT).

Extensive security measures have been put in place around the forested area where the animal is believed to be located and nearby villas. Access to and from the area is being controlled, while residents have been warned to remain cautious.

'The area where the lion is located has been identified, and every effort is being made to capture it alive,' the Istanbul Governor's Office said in a statement.

A lion has been spotted 10 miles from where Aston Villa are set to play in the Champions League on Tuesday

The Istanbul Governor's Office said 'every effort' is being made to capture the lion alive

Reaction to the lion's escape bordered on the surreal, with one outlet interviewing a person in a lion suit, wearing a Galatasaray shirt, about it. Galatasaray are nicknamed the Lions while Villa have a lion on their badge.

Gala defender Abdulkerim Bardakci was even asked about the matter, and replied: 'I want to say something because the whole country is talking about this right now. There's only one lion I keep at home, and that's my son.'

Daily Mail Sport has contacted UEFA for an update.

There were even suggestions in Turkey that Villa had cancelled their training session at RAMS Park because of the lion, but Villa did their preparation at Bodymoor Heath for a very different reason – the state of the RAMS Park pitch.

European football chiefs are confident the playing surface will pose no risk to Aston Villa after conducting thorough inspections.

The Turkish giants have commissioned intensive work on the pitch and moved their most recent league game, against Samsunspor, to the stadium of rivals Istanbul Basaksehir.

Yet it is thought conditions will be some way from perfect and though Villa boss Unai Emery played it down, he will be anxious about injuries. 'We have to think that if there was a risk of injury, we wouldn't be playing on it,' he said. 'The pitch will be better or worse, for both teams.'

Villa defender Ian Maatsen said: 'We don't know anything about the pitch. They say it's in a little bit of a bad condition but that's no excuse. We have to see how the pitch is. We are ready.'

Galatasaray coach Okan Buruk added: 'It was dug up again, another hybrid treatment was applied, and seeds were planted. There is also sand mixed into the pitch to help.'

Villa, who have been followed abroad by Prince William this season, will take on Galatasaray

Villa aim for last-16 spot

Aston Villa shocked Europe by marching straight into the last 16 in the Champions League two seasons ago but a win over Galatasaray will put them on course to repeat it.

Unai Emery’s side have nine points from a possible 12 in the league phase and victory in Istanbul will give them one foot in the knockout rounds.

Daily Mail Sport looks at what Villa can expect from one of the toughest tests on the European calendar.

Villa hold their breath

European football chiefs are confident Galatasaray’s pitch will pose no risk to Aston Villa after conducting thorough inspections of the playing surface at RAMS Park.

The Turkish giants have commissioned intensive work on the pitch and moved their most recent league game, against Samsunspor, to the stadium of rivals Istanbul Basaksehir.

Yet it is thought conditions will be some way from perfect and though Villa boss Unai Emery played it down, he will be anxious about injuries.

Villa defender Ian Maatsen said: ‘We don't know anything about the pitch. They say it's in a little bit of a bad condition but that's no excuse. We have to see how the pitch is. We are ready.’

Galatasaray coach Okan Buruk added: ‘It was dug up again, another hybrid treatment was applied, and seeds were planted. There is also sand mixed into the pitch to help.’

Villa are back in their happy place. This city hosted their 3-0 win over Freiburg in the Europa League Final last May, though that game happened at Tupras Stadium, home of Besiktas.

Repeat that result here and Villa will be eyeing a top-eight finish – which they also achieved two years ago. That would allow them to skip the play-off round early next year and head straight into the last 16.

European football chiefs are confident Galatasaray’s pitch will pose no risk to Aston Villa (Source: X/Forza Cimbom)

Will Garnacho’s chance ever come?

Five months into his loan spell from Chelsea, Alejandro Garnacho is still waiting for his first competitive start for Aston Villa.

When the Argentine moved to Villa Park, it was suggested that turning the temporary move into a £43million permanent deal would be a relative formality. Right now, that feels nearly impossible. Garnacho has featured for only 95 minutes this term and if Emery really did want the 22-year-old last summer, he has a funny way of showing it.

Indeed, Daily Mail Sport understands that even during Garnacho’s early days at the club, some Villa players were starting to wonder whether he would ever play regularly for Emery.

What next? There is believed to be no recall clause in the loan deal with Chelsea yet as Garnacho has only represented Villa this term, the clubs could agree to cancel the arrangement in January.

Born in Madrid, Garnacho was part of the youth system at Atletico before joining Manchester United. With four Argentines in the Atletico squad, plus another in boss Diego Simeone, that might be worth keeping an eye on.

Yet it is thought that neither Galatasaray nor Fenerbahce, who were monitoring Garnacho last summer, are in the market for a high-wage signing in January. That would close off one potential escape route.

January plans

Thanks to the sales of Morgan Rogers, Ezri Konsa and Youri Tielemans that brought in nearly £200million, Villa were able to spend heavily in the summer.

To invest again in the winter, they will probably need to attract offers for some fringe players. As well as Garnacho, Tammy Abraham and Lamare Bogarde have been overlooked by Emery recently. Abraham has fallen behind Brian Madjo in the pecking order, though the 17-year-old was not included in the Champions League squad, while Bogarde’s only starts have been in the Carabao Cup, which is always low on Emery’s priority list. Selling Bogarde would also deliver pure profit – crucial for a club forever fighting to stay in line with Premier League and UEFA spending rules.

There were always going to be bumps in the road this season for Villa, and there will likely be more. In last Saturday’s dispiriting 0-0 draw with Sunderland, there were only two players – Emi Buendia and Pau Torres – in the starting XI who were also in the line-up for the Europa League Final. Replacing the six who departed will take time.

In their commendable attempts to bring down the average age of the squad, Villa find themselves with a surplus of attackers but no midfield controller since the departure of Tielemans, and they also look vulnerable in central defence.

Tyrone Mings turns 34 in March and Victor Lindelof was 32 in July while Taylor Harwood-Bellis must find his feet quickly in one of the most demanding competitions in the world. It is tough without Konsa.

Elsewhere, there are possibly too many options. George Hemmings and then Alysson have forced their way into the side at different times this season, meaning fewer opportunities for Ibrahim Mbaye, who cost nearly £50million from Paris Saint-Germain last summer. Johan Manzambi has played regularly and with John McGinn and Buendia also in the mix, a player like Garnacho has a near-impossible task to convince Emery.

Alejandro Garnacho is still waiting for his first competitive start for Aston Villa - five months after joining from Chelsea

Batrakov aims to shine

Scouts from across Europe have been watching Galatasaray’s matches this season and Aleksey Batrakov is usually the reason why.

The 21-year-old Russian playmaker has six goals – including four in the Champions League – and four assists since his £21million move from Lokomotiv Moscow and is one of the breakout stars of the world game.

He caught the eye of Paris Saint-Germain while playing for Lokomotiv and Barcelona boss Hansi Flick has praised him.

The last Russian to play in the Premier League was Pavel Pogrebnyak, whose last game for Reading was against West Ham in May 2013.

Given the current geopolitical situation, Pogrebnyak will surely hold that record for some time to come.

Sports.title: Brentford 4-0 Everton: David Moyes' record-breaking night ends in misery as James Tarkowski sees red and rampant Bees boost European hopes
Sports.content:
Brentford 4-0 Everton: David Moyes' record-breaking night ends in misery as James Tarkowski sees red and rampant Bees boost European hopes

David Moyes’ record-breaking night as Everton manager could not have been more miserable.

In his 593rd game as Toffees boss, Moyes broke Harry Catterick’s 75-year record for most games in the dugout.

But that was about the only positive he could take away from the Gtech Community Stadium, as high-flying Brentford battered ten-man Everton on an evening to forget for the 63-year-old Scotsman.

Daily Mail Sport's Bobby Manzi was at the Gtech Community Stadium on a torrid night for the Toffees...

The Bees can mix it with big boys

Brentford, having missed out on European football on goal difference last season, are showing all the signs of being there or thereabouts again.

They climbed to sixth, leapfrogging Leeds — who have had far more praise lavished on them this season than Keith Andrews’ reliable side.

Brentford are disciplined with plenty of attacking flair, even with frontman and top goalscorer Igor Thiago suspended.

In his 593rd game as Toffees boss, Moyes broke Harry Catterick’s 75-year record

Brentford, having missed out on European football on goal difference last season, are showing all the signs of being there or thereabouts again

The Premier League lacks quality this season, but Brentford are consistent, losing just twice.

This well-oiled Andrews machine must take advantage of the floundering elite, with Manchester United, Chelsea and Tottenham all struggling, and finally secure Europe.

‘We set out this season looking to be better than last season, and if that happens, we will be flying to different destinations next season,’ Andrews said of their European hopes.’

‘We've got a very competitive squad that strives to get better. If we continue with that mindset, we'll hopefully be in a good place.

‘I enjoyed us,’ he added about the performance. ‘I thought we were very good. We played with real bravery, courage and energy.’

Brentford limited Everton to just three touches in the penalty area in the first half. They grabbed the game by the scruff of the neck and pinned their opponents back.

Jaidon Anthony was superb on the flank, providing two assists. Midfielder Vitaly Janelt capped off a brilliant display with a wonder strike from 25 yards, finding the top corner with his left foot.

It was a surprise to see Kevin Schade benched but this team is so cohesive, with more focus on the unit than any individual stars, that victory was light work for them.

It was a surprise to see Kevin Schade (above) benched but this team is so cohesive, with more focus on the unit than any individual stars, that victory was light work for them

MATCH FACTS Brentford: Kelleher 7; Kayode 7, Ajer 7, van den Berg 7, Lewis-Potter 9 (Diouf 74min, 6); Yarmolyuk 8 (Jensen 74, 7), Janelt 8 (Sangare 82); Ouattara 6 (Schade 66, 6), Damsgaard 7, Anthony 8 (Carvalho 81, 7); Wilson 7. Manager: Keith Andrews 8. Everton: Pickford 5; O’Brien 5, Tarkowski 4, Branthwaite 5, Mykolenko 5; Armstrong 5, Garner 6 (Norgaard 85); Rohl 5 (Keane 69, 6), Dewsbury-Hall 5 (Hackney 69, 6), George 5 (Grealish 66, 5); Barry 4 (Johnson 69, 5). Manager: David Moyes 4. Yellow cards: Mykolenko. Red cards: Tarkowski 40. Referee: Craig Pawson 6. Attendance: 18,877.

Both of Keane Lewis-Potter’s goals had an element of fortune attached. But teams earn that luck when they manage ten shots in their opponents’ penalty area in just 45 minutes.

Lewis Potter starred at left-back, registering seven shots — the most of any player — and the joint-most touches in the opposition box. He was a menace and integral to every Brentford attack.

Tarkowski's moment of madness

James Tarkowski endured a depressing return to his former club when he was shown the first Premier League red card of his career.

It will split opinion, but in this day and age it is a clear red card. Although the Everton defender won the ball, his studs connected with Yehor Yarmolyuk’s shin on follow-through. The speed and intensity of the tackle endangered his opponent. He had to go.

Referee Craig Pawson brandished a yellow, but a quick trip to the monitor saw it upgraded. Tarkowski ran down the tunnel before Pawson could even get the red card out of his pocket.

The home support enjoyed it, having taunted their former player throughout the first half.

To compound Everton’s misery, the first game of Tarkowski three-match ban is next weekend’s Merseyside derby.

Although Tarkowski won the ball, his studs connected with Yarmolyuk’s shin on follow-through

A deflated Moyes had few complaints. ‘My feeling at the time was it wasn’t a red because James easily got to the ball before the Brentford player,’ the Everton boss said.

‘But after I saw it again, Tarky's boot is a bit higher than I'd like, so I can understand why the decision went against us.

‘We didn’t play well. Brentford did and credit to them. A bit unfortunate with the goals, it made it look even worse than it was.’

Toffees' torrid slide

Everton were unbeaten in four games at Brentford before this and their defeat came in the form of the sublime and the ridiculous.

The first goal was all about Anthony undoing Everton on the left before Lewis-Potter was given far too much space to get his shot away. The deflection was unfortunate, but the defending was poor to begin with.

Tarkowski blocked an initial effort from Lewis-Potter for the second goal but the ball fell straight back to him, and Jake O’Brien helped his second attempt past Jordan Pickford. Once again, Everton should have done better and cleared the initial free-kick.

Portuguese forward Fabio Carvalho could not believe his luck when he added a late fourth, tapping in as Mathias Jensen’s corner flew straight past the congested pack at the near post.

Sports.title: Jack Grealish plays for Everton for the first time since being axed for skipping training without permission in 'breach of club discipline' - as winger comes off the bench during loss at Brentford
Sports.content:
Jack Grealish plays for Everton for the first time since being axed for skipping training without permission in 'breach of club discipline' - as winger comes off the bench during loss at Brentford

Jack Grealish returned to the Everton squad for the first time since being made unavailable for selection due to a breach of club discipline, and came off the bench at half-time against Brentford on Monday.

The Manchester City loanee was punished by the club for failing to report to training sessions and missed several matches. He had not featured for four games: one because of illness, then a 'breach of club discipline' and a lack of fitness thereafter.

He last featured on October 17, over a month ago, but returned to the match day squad to take on Brentford on Monday night – named on the substitutes' bench. He was introduced at half-time for Tyrique George, with the Toffees 2-0 down and down to 10 men after James Tarkowski's red card. They would ultimately lose 4-0.

Manager David Moyes said ahead of the game: 'He has served his punishment and we will treat him as we were treating him before.

'We will get on with things. The team is going really well at the moment and what I don't want to do is turn it into a Jack story because it shouldn't be.'

Pushed if that suggests he will not play on Monday night, Moyes replied: 'He could easily. He is back in the squad, he is a good player. Who knows?'

Jack Grealish (right) returned to Everton action on Monday for the first time since being punished for missing training

He was named on the bench against Brentford, coming on for Tyrique George at half-time

Everton had won their last three games and went into Monday's match sixth in the table. The result, though, was a blow as they dropped to ninth.

Asked what Grealish can offer, Moyes added: 'Jack can offer us a lot. I want more from him, I want him to show more than he has done. I want him to give me more assists, goals.

'But there's lots of things about him which we need and he's good at retaining the ball, giving us good possession, carrying. So we hope that he can get back to those levels and give us what we need.

'I think this time last year he was probably sitting on five or six assists so we're hoping to get that.'

Grealish's social media apology came after he featured in a behind-closed-doors match during the international break.

'Nice to be back out there with the boys today after a few good days training!' Grealish wrote. 'I want to apologise to the fans (and) everyone at the club for not being able to help the team the last few weeks.

'I love playing for this club (and) can't wait to be back playing in front of you guys in an Everton shirt.

'See you all soon (blue heart emoji)'.

Sports.title: Jude Bellingham and Real Madrid in advanced talks over new five-year deal - with England superstar set to become one of Europe's HIGHEST earners on par with £500,000-a-week team-mate Vinicius Junior
Sports.content:
Jude Bellingham and Real Madrid are advancing in talks over a new contract that will make him one of the best paid players in Europe.

Madrid have been eager to tie down the in-form England midfielder beyond his current contract, understood to be worth around £12.5million a year after tax, which runs until 2029, in recognition of his performances.

Talks were initiated in September over an extension until 2031 and have been progressing well since with sources at Madrid confident they are close to reaching a conclusion.

Bellingham is expected to be handed improved terms to put him on par with team-mate Vinicius Jr, who agreed a new deal last summer reputedly on around £500,000 a week after tax.

Kylian Mbappe remains the best paid player at the club while talks are also advancing over a new contract for Fede Valverde. Real have also recently renewed the contracts of Turkish winger Arda Guler and France international Aurelien Tchouameni on deals until 2032.

Jude Bellingham and Real Madrid are advancing in talks over a contract extension until 2031

The new deal at Madrid will make England's superstar one of the highest earners in Europe - on par with Vinicius Junior's £500,000-a-week contract (Pictured left at his unveiling in 2023)

The contract for Bellingham will be just reward for the 23-year-old who has flourished under coach Jose Mourinho who recently described the former Birmingham City academy graduate as ‘one of a kind’.

Bellingham, who has scored six goals this season, could be rested for Madrid’s Champions League tie with PSV Eindhoven tonight but was still the topic of conversation as goalkeeper Thibaut Courtois praised his influence on the team on Monday.

‘Jude is someone who really wants to win,’ said Courtois. ‘That's why on the field he swears a lot! He's really a winner, and when he's not happy, he will make it known. He's also a leader on the field. He's a great player, a great mentality. You need those kind of people like that in your team that go for everything.

‘Jude is a young guy but when you see him, it feels like he's a few years older.

‘It seems like he has an engine to play 200 minutes. He keeps on going, running with the ball, it's really hard to dispossess him. And on the outside he just works hard, he goes to the gym. With a good Jude, we play better.’

Sports.title: The Women's World Cup is coming home... but 2035 cannot be treated as a fix for the game's problems, writes TARA ANSON-WALSH
Sports.content:
The United Kingdom will host the 2035 Women's World Cup, the first football World Cup to be staged on these shores since 1966, it was announced to much fanfare on Monday.

Yet while the countdown can now officially begin, the biggest challenges facing the women's game cannot be kicked eight-and-a-half years down the road.

Over in Zurich, FIFA president Gianni Infantino undertook his usual long-winded and self-serving monologue which precedes these ceremonies, in which he heralded the 'incredible growth' of the Women's World Cup, describing a time when they 'didn't exist'.

'We all remember the last Women's World Cup,' the embattled 56-year-old Italian said, calling it 'a huge success'.

The irony, of course, is that the last Women's World Cup in Australia and New Zealand is remembered by many for all the wrong reasons, with newspaper back pages peppered with images of Spain captain Jenni Hermoso's kiss with the former president of Spain's FA, Luis Rubiales, for days after the final.

Rubiales was later convicted of sexual assault for the incident, which triggered widespread protests across the country and overshadowed Spain's terrific 1-0 triumph over England in Sydney.

Gianni Infantino undertook his usual long-winded and self-serving monologue which precedes these ceremonies, in which he heralded the 'incredible growth' of the Women's World Cup

Rubiales was later convicted of sexual assault for the incident, which triggered widespread protests across the country and overshadowed Spain's terrific 1-0 triumph over England

There is an added layer of irony in that Infantino had, two days before the 2023 final, angered many women worldwide with yet another controversial speech in which he told them: 'You have the power to change', but that they had to 'convince us men what we have to do'.

Alongside this patronising statement, Infantino also insisted that equal pay at the World Cup 'would not solve anything'.

Three years later, Infantino is unfortunately still at the helm, while UEFA's attempts to unseat him following his controversial bid to sell off the World Cup now look to have failed spectacularly, with the football despot increasingly likely to secure a fourth term.

What the social and political landscape will look like by the time this women's footballing bonanza arrives on these shores in 2035 remains unclear. What is clear, however, is that the game's continued progress will require more than the record attendances and soaring commercial revenues the FA are predicting.

It will require the figures who have too often held it back to finally step aside, and that process should begin with the likes of Infantino being shown the door.

It will require those at the top of English football to put their heads together and work out how to stem falling attendances in the league. The average attendance across the first eight WSL matchweeks of 2024-25 was 8,173. Last season it was 7,472. This season, it is tracking at around 5,677.

And third, it will require somewhere other than Wembley to stage the final.

Wembley was, of course, the scene of Chloe Kelly's moment of madness, yet by the time the 2035 Women's World Cup comes around it will also have hosted the men's finals of Euro 2024 and 2028.

The FA paid off its debt on the national stadium in 2024, 17 years after its reopening, and is no longer obligated to host major events there to service repayments.

The rules have been left open for another venue to emerge to host the final, such as Man United's proposed new 100,000 stadium

While under current FIFA regulations, Wembley is the only one of the proposed 22 stadiums that meets the requirements to host a final, the rules have been left open enough for another venue to emerge should a suitable stadium be completed before 2035.

Step up Sir Jim Ratcliffe, although please refer back to point one in this regard – the Manchester United co-owner who famously asked former captain Katie Zelem 'what do you do here?' while touring the club's women's facilities.

United's proposed new 100,000-seater stadium was included in the 2035 bid and could yet come under consideration from FIFA.

While there are still many hurdles to clear before then, hosting a tournament final in Manchester would undoubtedly be huge for the women's game, not least given the optics of a bid built around being 'all together', described as 'a rallying cry to unite people through football'.

London should not be the epicentre of the tournament, not if the intention is to spread the women's game across the United Kingdom rather than concentrate it in the capital, where Arsenal's attendances continue to dwarf those of every other WSL club.

In other words, the women's game in this country cannot be put on hold until 2035.

It cannot afford to wait eight-and-a-half years for this World Cup to come and rescue it. Time to get cracking.

Sports.title: Man United's January transfer budget will be less than £50m with Mauricio Pochettino expected to make only TWO signings - despite needing to bolster their attack and defence
Sports.content:
Man United's January transfer budget will be less than £50m with Mauricio Pochettino expected to make only TWO signings - despite needing to bolster their attack and defence

Mauricio Pochettino will have less than £50million to buy Manchester United out of trouble in the January transfer window.

Pochettino admitted that United are in a relegation battle after a painful 4-0 defeat to Liverpool in his first game in charge left the club second from bottom of the Premier League.

It’s understood the Argentine will have a limited budget well under £50million with United’s hands tied by the league’s new financial rules. Pochettino is only expected to make two new signings in January, even if one of them is a loan deal.

Sources have not ruled out the possibility of United gambling if there is a genuine threat of the club being relegated for the first time in 53 years, but they would still have to spend responsibly.

The defeat to Liverpool underlined the need for Pochettino to strengthen in central defence, with Brentford’s Nathan Collins emerging as a strong candidate ahead of Calvin Bassey, who is expected to sign a new contract with Fulham, and Everton’s Jarrad Branthwaite who is valued at over £70million.

United also want a left-back after failing to sign cover for Luke Shaw in the summer when they were linked with Barcelona’s Alejandro Balde and Rayan Ait-Nouri of Manchester City. Both those players could be potential targets again.

Mauricio Pochettino will have less than £50million to try and fix Manchester United in January

Pochettino is only expected to make two new signings in January - pictured: Chief executive Omar Berrada (left) and director of football Jason Wilcox (centre)

Pochettino would also like a new striker after Benjamin Sesko’s shin injury left him short of firepower until the New Year.

Monaco’s Folarin Balogun, who played under Pochettino for the US national team, Leeds striker Dominic Calvert-Lewin and Ivan Toney, the former Brentford centre-forward now playing for Al-Ahli, have all been linked with a move to Old Trafford.

However, Toney’s £500,000-a-week wages put him out of United’s reach, and Leeds are keen to extend Calvert-Lewin’s contract which is worth £180,000-a-week.

Meanwhile, United are appealing to the FA over Leny Yoro’s controversial red card against Liverpool.

Yoro was sent off in the eighth minute at Anfield for a challenge on Alexander Isak on the edge of the penalty box. The Frenchman was dismissed by referee Sam Barrott, and Dominik Szoboszlai scored Liverpool’s first goal from the free-kick.

However, United insist that Yoro did not deny Isak a clear goalscoring opportunity because goalkeeper Senne Lammens would have reached the ball first.

The club have notified the FA of their intention to appeal in the hope of having Yoro’s one-match ban overturned so he can play against Brentford at Old Trafford on Saturday.

Sports.title: LeBron James' wife Savannah reveals terrifying details of TWO alleged stalkers' break-ins
Sports.content:
LeBron James' wife Savannah reveals terrifying details of TWO alleged stalkers' break-ins

An accused trespasser with luggage in hand attempted to move into LeBron James's Los Angeles mansion, while another claiming to be a family member managed to breach the Philadelphia 76ers superstar's residence, according to court filings obtained by The Daily Mail.

Savannah James, LeBron's wife and mother to his three children, filed two separate restraining order applications in Los Angeles County on Monday after a pair of horrifying break-in attempts at the family's LA homes. It's unclear which residences were infiltrated, but the James clan has one mansion in Brentwood, while a massive compound in Beverly Hills is currently being completed.

One alleged trespasser, identified in the filing as William Norman Rahman, has 'repeatedly targeted the James' home' over the past year, according to one filing.

'Mr. Rahman appears to hold a fixed, delusional belief that he lives at the James residence,' read one filing. 'Acting on that belief, he has used the James family's property address as his own mailing address, had rideshare drivers [Uber] drop him off at the property, and loitered on or near the property with luggage.

'Because he believes our home is his, any member of the James family may encounter him at the residence at any time,' the application continued. 'His conduct is ongoing and has not stopped despite the passage of nearly a year.'

After allegedly ignoring requests to leave the perimeter of the property on November 14, Rahman was approached by police outside the residence and responded by telling officers that it was his address, according to Monday's filing. Officers advised him he was trespassing and would be arrested if he tried to return.

Zhuri (L) and Savannah James, sister and mother of Bronny, watch a summer league game

James is currently building a compound in Beverly Hills after years of living in Brentwood

Previously, according to Savannah's application for the restraining order, Rahman had packages sent to himself at the family's home, prompting the James clan to issue a cease-and-desist letter in February.

Another accused trespasser, Jaliere Zacchaeus McWhite, actually gained access to the James' residence and allegedly believes he is part of the family, according to the application.

'Over just two weeks, he acted on that belief by going to two separate family residences,' read Savannah's restraining order application. 'The second time, he got inside the home. His conduct is getting more serious, earlier police intervention did not stop him, and the family has good reason to fear what he will do next.

'Mr. McWhite's conduct is not random,' the application continued. 'Both times, he went specifically to homes of the James family. On October 23, 2026, he appeared in the front driveway of the family's Tigertail residence, said he was related to the family, acted like a child and said he was 14 years old. These statements show a delusional attachment to the family. That attachment drives his behavior, and it has not gone away.'

The application goes on to describe the lengths McWhite was willing to go to enter the James family home.

'On November 6, 2026, at about 9:00 PM, he climbed onto an adjacent property, crossed onto the James property and went into the residence through the front door,' read the complaint. 'Family members had left that door unlocked moments earlier as they left. Security footage confirms that he was inside the home. In two weeks, his conduct went from showing up uninvited to unlawfully entering the family's home.'

Bryce James is currently a member of the Arizona Wildcats, but hasn't seen much action

Bronny James is now in his third NBA season and his first without having his dad on his team

LeBron did discuss the incident with reporters earlier this month: 'My family is safe and that's the most important. We're still looking into everything.'

James himself was away on a road trip when the incident occurred, as he was in Ohio preparing to play the Cleveland Cavaliers later that night.

With the first-place Sixers off to a 14-3 start, James has been helicoptering between Philadelphia and a residence in New York, while Savannah and their daughter, Zhuri, remain back in LA, where the youngest member of the James family attends school and plays volleyball.

In addition to his Brentwood home, James also owns properties in his native Akron and in Miami's exclusive Coconut Grove.

Currently James's son Bryce is playing basketball at Arizona while the eldest, Bronny, has continued his career with the Lakers.

Neither McWhite nor Rahman have listed attorneys on the LA County court website.

Sports.title: Disgraced NFL star Shawne Merriman sued over $3.5 million in debts... weeks after being told to pay $4m for Playboy model's overdose death
Sports.content:
Disgraced NFL star Shawne Merriman sued over $3.5 million in debts... weeks after being told to pay $4m for Playboy model's overdose death

Former NFL star Shawne Merriman is facing another lawsuit after he and three co-defendants were ordered to pay $4 million by a Los Angeles County judge over the 2017 wrongful death of Playboy model Kimberly Fattorini.

Now, in a 12-count federal memorandum of law obtained by The Daily Mail, the once-feared pass rusher is accused of concealing that looming civil judgement from lender ARI as he obtained millions in debt financing in 2024 and 2025 for his fledgling combat sports circuit, Lights Out XF.

'Merriman personally guaranteed the loans while concealing a pending wrongful death action that subsequently resulted in a $4,000,000 judgment against him arising from the drugging and death of Kimberly Fattorini,' read Thursday's filing from the Southern District of New York.

In September of 2025, a Los Angeles jury found Merriman and three other defendants liable for the 2017 death of Fattorini, a former model who worked on various projects with Playboy. Fattorini's death was initially ruled accidental after coroner tests found alcohol, cocaine and GHB – commonly known as the 'date rape drug' – in her system.

No arrests were ever made in response to Fattorini's death, while Merriman and his co-defendants have denied any wrongdoing. Regardless, an LA judge ordered all four defendants to pay $4million to Fattorini's parents in October as part of the family's civil suit.

One month on from that judgement, Merriman stands accused of fraud, breach of contract, defamation, interference with business relationships, and unjust enrichment by ARI, which also claimed he still owes the firm more than $3.5 million.

Retired NFL star Shawne Merriman is among three defendants ordered to pay the family of a deceased Playboy employee a $4 million judgement after losing a wrongful death civil suit

A Los Angeles jury found Merriman and four other defendants liable for the 2017 death of Kimberly Fattorini (pictured), a former model who worked on various projects with Playboy

According to the latest lawsuit, which was initially filed in May, Merriman personally guaranteed financing but ultimately failed to make a required $300,000 principal payment in September of 2025 – just as he was losing the wrongful death lawsuit.

He has not made any payments to ARI since, according to the company.

Two months later, Merriman allegedly asked ARI for another $500,000 in financing while neglecting to disclose the looming judgement to the lender, according to Thursday's filing, which accuses the former San Diego Chargers star of significant fraud.

'What follows is not a routine default or simple contract dispute, but a deliberate, coordinated, multi-step scheme by Merriman to commit fraud, coercion, misrepresentation, and obstruction – all designed to avoid repayment and accountability,' read the original May lawsuit obtained by The Daily Mail.

The lawsuit claimed Merriman concealed overlapping collateral interests, ruined Lights Out's business and misrepresented the trademarks and related intellectual property as belonging to Wyoming-based Lights Out Holdings LLC. ARI's attorneys allege that a separate Lights Out company in California actually owned those assets.

In January, Merriman's attorneys argued in a Nevada lawsuit that ARI could not exercise governance and warrant rights over the company, but that case was denied in April.

The Daily Mail has sought comment from Merriman's attorneys.

With Merriman allegedly in default, ARI legally removed him from his executive positions atop the MMA circuit and acquired majority control of the company, according to court filings.

ARI attorneys have asked the court for a partial summary judgement recognizing the firm's majority stake in Lights Out and declaring that its intellectual property rights are enforceable. In response, Merriman's attorneys filed a motion of opposition in May.

Shawne Merriman attends Sports Illustrated The Party Brought To You By The Undisputed Group And ABG Entertainment With DaBaby, Black Eyed Peas, And Marshmello in 2020

Of course, his most pressing concern may be the $4 million he and his co-defendants have been asked to pay the Fattorini family after losing the wrongful death lawsuit.

Fattorini's parents originally sued Merriman and others in 2019, claiming she was drugged and possibly sexually assaulted before her overdose death.

A sexual assault test was not conducted and although a coroner found contusions on her body, no photographs of the bruises were taken, according to that 2019 lawsuit filed in Los Angeles County and obtained by The Daily Mail.

That lawsuit also described Merriman arriving at co-defendant Eli Wehbe's house, where Fattorini and other women were socializing. A witness said Merriman was clutching a bottle 'filled with liquid,' according to the complaint, which claimed Fattorini later texted Wehbe to tell him her drink was spiked.

'But Your friend just poor'd half G in my drink,' read the transcript included in the complaint obtained by The Daily Mail.

The lawsuit explains that 'G' stands for 'GHB.'

The group would move on to another apartment, where Fattorini's friend ultimately discovered her lifeless body and called 911.

Paramedics found Fattorini nearly undressed when they arrived, according to the complaint.

'She was half-naked with her jeans unzipped and unbuttoned, as though someone had tried to pull her jeans on to her body before the police or paramedics arrived,' read the complaint. 'Her bra was twisted and her lips were blue. She was also not wearing any underwear despite the fact that she had been going through her menstrual cycle that day and the evening before.'

Merriman was somehow able to leave between the 911 call and when the paramedics arrived, according to the complaint.

'Maass also stated that after moving [Fattorini] to the floor, Merriman stated that he was very concerned about the media attention the incident might create since he was a celebrity, so he told Maass he had to leave. Somehow, under Maass' version of events, Merriman escaped without being seen between the time the 911 call started and the time the paramedics arrived.'

In January, Merriman's attorneys argued in a Nevada filing that ARI could not exercise governance and warrant rights over the company, but that motion was denied in April

One anti-violence organization is pushing Maryland to rescind Merriman's HOF induction

Merriman, now 42, was a first-round pick out of Maryland before winning NFL Defensive Rookie of the Year in 2005. He'd be named to the All-Pro First Team a year later but was busted for violating the NFL's steroid policy in 2006 and ultimately began to battle injury problems.

On Monday, the End Violence Everywhere organization called on Maryland to rescind its induction of Merriman into the Terrapins' athletic Hall of Fame.

'Universities have a responsibility to do more than simply talk about their commitment to protecting students and supporting survivors of violence and abuse. Their actions must reflect those words,' said Cait Alexander, Founder & CEO of EVE, in a statement. 'When an institution chooses to honor someone under these circumstances, it sends a devastating message to survivors that athletic achievement and status are more important than accountability.

'The Fattorinis spent years fighting for justice, and it is heartbreaking that they had to witness the University celebrate someone found liable in connection with their daughter's death. I implore the University to take this as an opportunity to rectify its mistake and show, through action, that its purported values are more than just words.'

The Daily Mail has sought comment with a Maryland athletics spokesman.

Sports.title: Mauricio Pochettino decides on first Man Utd transfer after Liverpool mauling
Sports.content:
Mauricio Pochettino decides on first Man Utd transfer after Liverpool mauling

Manchester United are in desperate need of reinforcements in the January transfer window in order to give new boss Mauricio Pochettino the tools to salvage their season

View 2 Images Mauricio Pochettino will be backed in the January transfer window (Image: Ash Donelon/Manchester United FC)

Mauricio Pochettino and Manchester United will prioritise signing a new striker in the upcoming winter transfer window, it has emerged.

‌



‌



The Red Devils are languishing in the Premier League relegation zone after winning just one of their 11 league matches so far this term, with Pochettino losing his first game at the helm 4-0 on Sunday following another defensive horror show away at arch rivals Liverpool.

‌



Work to enhance United's beleaguered squad is expected to take place in January, with the club keen to back their new head coach after luring him back to England from his post with the United States men's national team.

‌



And while reinforcements in defence are desperately needed, The Times report that a new striker will be the priority in the mid-season transfer window with Benjamin Sesko unlikely to return until 'January at the earliest'.

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

A shin injury has prevented Sesko from playing a significant role this season, with the Slovenia international making just two starts.

‌



Matheus Cunha and Bryan Mbeumo have both been deployed ahead of Joshua Zirkzee as an attacking focal point this term. Zirkzee was introduced at half-time of Sunday's heavy loss at Anfield, though there has been speculation he may be offloaded in January.

While Zirkzee has found goals hard to come by at Old Trafford (11 in 86 appearances) since joining United for £36.5million two years ago, Sesko enjoyed a productive maiden season, scoring 13 goals in 38 games.

‌



A number of strikers have already been linked with United, who have plundered just 14 goals in the Premier League this season, including Folarin Balogun. Pochettino has worked with the former Arsenal striker for the USMNT and Balogun is understood to be keen on a reunion in the Premier League.

View 2 Images Mauricio Pochettino used Joshua Zirkzee in the 4-0 loss against Liverpool but wants more firepower (Image: Robbie Jay Barratt - AMA/Getty Images)

‌



The report adds that moves to strengthen defensively may also likely to be made in January, with United possibly bolstering Pochettino's squad with a left-back. The club considered adding in that area in the summer before deciding against doing so but an injury to Luke Shaw has forced a number of players to deputise in the left-back role unsuccessfully.

Pochettino remains a big advocate of Shaw, who he managed at Southampton in his first managerial post in English football. There have, however, been doubts over the 31-year-old's fitness prior to the Argentine's arrival.

Sports.title: OLI BELL: 'I challenge Matt Chapman to a charity boxing match to raise money for the hospital which saved mother's life'
Sports.content:
Fresh from the ‘walking in a Skelton wonderland’ chants we saw at Haydock on Saturday we head to Newbury this weekend for the latest instalment of the race formerly known as the Hennessy. I’m very sweet on one in here at odds of 10-1 currently and the horse in question is Miami Magic.

He’s a second season novice which is a path well trodden to win this race and crucially benefits from a recent run over hurdles where he showed himself to be In good form by finishing a good second in a big field with the front two pulling clear.

Signed Harry Kane shirt, Arsenal hospitality and trip to Ballydoyle among lots for fundraiser READ MORE :

Jockey disqualified for six months for punching his horse in the neck during race READ MORE :

This is his second start after a wind op which again is an angle many like and given his exploits last season in good company I expect him to go very close for trainer Stuart Edmunds and jockey Charlie Hammond who have had a mighty start to the season.

He’s getting weight from those at the top of the market and for me he is far too big a price. This weekend at Newbury is always well attended with a great atmosphere. I have to say though that in the last couple of seasons you can say that about almost every Newbury fixture.

‌



Ever since Shaun Hinds took over as Cheif Executive in June 2024, there seems to be a really positive feeling at the track again and given its status as one of Britains premier racetracks that is very much welcomed.

I’m sure there will be examples used whereby Newbury can continue to improve and listen to feedback but the point is that in the two years since Hinds started they have been receptive to change, to listening and to trying things out.

I’ve been thoroughly impressed and whilst this weekend is always one I look forward to immensely, given the new found energy at Newbury I’m particularly excited to head there this time around and cheer on Miami Magic.

View 2 Images (Image: PA)

‌



Life-savers

Just away from racing briefly, if I may, I’d like to take this opportunity to publicly thank the doctors and nurses at St George’s Hospital in Tooting who to be blunt, saved my mothers life.

The staff, who come from all over the world were truly extraordinary with their care for her and I know everyone says this during these times but we are so lucky in this country to have that level of care on our doorstep.

I know that there has long been chatter of a charity boxing match involving me and Matt Chapman…. I would happily take him on in the ring and raise money for St George’s Hospital in light of their work during what has been a scary and stressful month or so! What do you say Chapman!!!!?

Sports.title: Signed Harry Kane shirt, Arsenal hospitality and trip to Ballydoyle among lots for fundraiser
Sports.content:
Signed Harry Kane shirt, Arsenal hospitality and trip to Ballydoyle among lots for fundraiser

Other lots include a Willie Mullins gallops morning in the silent auction being organised for racing journalist Marcus Townend who suffered life-changing injuries in 2025

View 3 Images Marcus Townend (left) with Ruby Walsh (Image: HWPA)

A signed Harry Kane England shirt, Arsenal hospitality and a trip to Ballydoyle are among the lots on offer in a fundraiser for well known racing journalist Marcus Townend next month.

‌



‌



Townend, who spent 35 years at the Daily Mail, serving as both racing editor and racing correspondent, and also writing under the moniker "Captain Heath", suffered a life-changing accident in 2025.

‌



He suffered the first of three bleeds to his brain as a result of a fall from his bicycle. The third bleed, which occurred at the end of March this year, following a plate insertion to repair his skull, proved the most damaging, from which he is still recuperating.

‌



Jockey disqualified for six months for punching his horse in the neck during race READ MORE :

In July he was diagnosed with mild haemophilia and despite his amazing determination to communicate clearly, self care and mobilise, he will require ongoing neurological physiotherapy and much care from others to achieve his independent potential.

The HWPA Derby Awards Lunch on December 7, which brings the racing industry together to celebrate the best work of racing journalists, broadcasters, and photographers, as well as honour leading jockeys, trainers, and owners, will include a silent auction for Townend.

The Racing Reporter of the Year in 2019, previously served as President of the Horserace Writers and Photographers Association (HWPA) from 2017 to 2021.

‌



View 3 Images A signed Harry Kane England shirt is among the lots (Image: Getty Images)

The auction will run in the two weeks leading up to the Awards event and Monday December 7. Notable lots include:

‌



A money-can’t-buy trip to Coolmore and Ballydoyle

Willie Mullins gallops morning and stable tour

Grand National Day course walk with National winning jockeys Sam Waley-Cohen and Marcus Armytage

Hospitality at the Emirates Stadium for an Arsenal match

Signed Harry Kane England shirt

Hospitality at racecourses including Aintree, Ascot, Cheltenham, Goodwood, Newbury and York

Numerous gallop mornings at yards all over the country

https://thesilent.auction/e/hw

In addition, businesses and organisations who donate £2,000 or more will be able to add their logo to the Marcus Townend Wall of Supporters, which will form the backdrop to this year’s awards ceremony.

‌



View 3 Images Gallops morning and Willie Mullins stable visit: part of the lots in the Marcus Townend fundraiser (Image: RACINGFOTOS.COM)

David Cleary, President of the Horserace Writers and Photographers Association, said: “Marcus is one of the nicest, kindest and most respected members of the press room and we are all heartbroken that he has suffered such serious injuries.

‌



“The HWPA Derby Awards Lunch was always an event he loved attending, not least when he was President of the Association, and we wanted to stage this year’s event to raise money for him and his future treatment.

“I know how touched Marcus and his family have been by the incredibly kind donations from so many people and organisations, through prizes for the silent auction, donations and the Wall of Supporters. We are now fully focused on raising as much money for Marcus as possible.”

Sports.title: Jockey disqualified for six months for punching his horse in the neck during race
Sports.content:
Jockey disqualified for six months for punching his horse in the neck during race

Chris McIver, 39, pleaded guilty to improper riding of a two-year-old Strategic Gold during a handicap race at Mackay in Queensland last week

View 2 Images Chris McIver punched Strategic Gold (circled) in the neck

A jockey has been disqualified for six months after he punched a horse in the neck during a race. Chris McIver was riding the two-year-old Strategic Gold in a handicap at Mackay in Queensland last week.

‌



‌



The juvenile appeared to be a difficult ride and veered wide on the bend with McIver unable to stop his mount taking another horse with him. The pair eventually finished fourth of five but an objection was lodged by connections of the fifth placed Golden Annie, alleging interference on the home turn.

‌



The local stewards ruled the interference suffered by Golden Annie outweighed the beaten margin of a neck, upheld the protest and amended the placings.

‌



Then at a separate hearing held on Saturday they looked into the actions of McIver near the 150m mark.

Grey Dawning and Harry Skelton send Haydock fans wild with second Betfair Chase READ MORE :

The inquiry notice said: “After review of the available replays and taking evidence from jockey McIver, he pleaded guilty to a charge under AR131(a) for improper riding, in that near the 150m he improperly punched Strategic Gold in the neck area with his right fist.

‌



“When assessing penalty, stewards considered the rider's guilty plea, the serious nature of the offence, Mr McIver’s poor overall record in relation to matters of a similar nature, which reflected three prior offences since 2012.

“Stewards also considered the impact that a penalty would have on jockey McIver, both professionally and personally.

‌



View 2 Images Chris McIver: disqualified for six months

“Stewards deemed that the appropriate penalty to be imposed was a disqualification period of six months. The disqualification was ordered to commence immediately from the handing down of the penalty decision which occurred after the close of racing.”

Article continues below

McIver, 39, who has ridden more than 400 winners since his debut in 2004, served a six month disqualification in 2020 after he admitted striking a horse on the head with his whip, which triggered an additional month’s penalty which had been suspended when found guilty of misconduct in 2019 for kicking and punching a horse in the head, which resulted in a three month ban.

He was also disqualified in 2021 when he was alleged to have ‘stomped’ on a horse in the stalls. That decision was quashed after an internal review of the case by the Queensland Racing Integrity Commission.

Sports.title: Mauricio Pochettino points finger of blame and discusses Man Utd punishment
Sports.content:
Mauricio Pochettino points finger of blame and discusses Man Utd punishment

Mauricio Pochettino had to bin his Liverpool game plan after just seven minutes, when Leny Yoro was shown a red card for a foul on Alexander Isak.

View 2 Images Mauricio Pochettino believes Manchester United were punished at Anfield. (Image: Photo by Carl Recine/Getty Images)

Mauricio Pochettino believes that Manchester United were unfairly punished in Sunday night’s defeat to Liverpool. Shortly after the final whistle at Anfield, which extended the Reds’ residence in the Premier League relegation zone by at least another week, the new head coach came out swinging and took aim at the referee.

‌



‌



Inside the opening 10 minutes, Samuel Barrott showed Leny Yoro a red card for clumsily bringing down Alexander Isak just outside the box. The United defender, who had raced back to spare the blushes of Matthijs de Ligt, was adjudged to have denied the former Newcastle United striker a goalscoring opportunity, so he was given his marching orders.

‌



Dominik Szoboszlai scored from the resulting free-kick, and the floodgates opened in Merseyside, with Andoni Iraola’s side waltzing away 4-0 victors. Although Pochettino accepted responsibility for the result, he claimed the Reds were punished.

‌



“It is painful because it is 4-0, but we play more than 80 minutes with 10 men. I take responsibility for that, no worries,” said Pochettino, who then argued that United should have had a penalty when Jeremy Jacquet made a challenge on Bryan Mbeumo a few moments earlier.

“We were punished badly and they were not punished, that is true. You need to look at the circumstance because it is so easy to talk so cheap.

‌



“We lose one game; we are not going to lose more than one game how we lose today. We have a lot of work to do and we take responsibility. We feel the pain but the thing is to keep working.”

Only one team in the Premier League has conceded more goals than United (23) after 11 games this season: Crystal Palace (27). The Eagles sit rock bottom of the table, and trail the Reds by just a point.

‌



View 2 Images Mauricio Pochettino watches on as Man Utd are thrashed by Liverpool

“The team concede because the balance is not so good and I take responsibility for that,” said the Argentine. “He (De Ligt) was training, he played in the Champions League before the international duty and when we arrived we saw the combinations.”

‌



When asked whether he had inherited a relegation battle, Pochettino added: “Still a lot of games to play. We need to accept the reality and we need to be united and all together.

“We feel disappointed because it is clear after what happened (Yoro’s red card), the plan was in the bin.

‌



“What I learned from my players is that they like to fight, they are committed to the team, to the club and they want to win games.

“Today we made an effort. Today was a test that, for me, is very positive.”

Article continues below

United are back in action in the Champions League on Wednesday night, taking on Sporting at the Jose Alvalade Stadium, where Pochettino will hope to bank his first win. Then, the Reds will face Brentford at Old Trafford on Saturday afternoon.

Sports.title: Man Utd are in a genuine battle against the drop with their biggest problem clear
Sports.content:
Man Utd are in a genuine battle against the drop with their biggest problem clear

Manchester United's defeat on Sunday leaves them with one Premier League win - the fewest of any team - as they continue to sit in the bottom three

View Image Man Utd sit 19th and are without a Premier League win in nearly three months

Manchester United sit second bottom with December just around the corner - at what point do we start talking about relegation?

‌



‌



It is scarcely believable to see the Premier League's most successful team sitting in 19th with one win from 11 games, but that is the current reality. The 4-0 loss at Liverpool on Sunday was the latest setback for a team who don't look like winning a game.

‌



They sit on eight points. This time last year Tottenham had 19, and they needed a win on the final day just to stay up. You look at United's squad, even if they are underperforming, and think they must click into gear eventually. But there's no sign of that yet.

‌



Jamie Carragher confessed that the quality of the mid-table teams has never been so strong - and that could be the biggest problem for United.

‌



Quizzed on relegation prospects he said: "No-one believes they are, no-one will say that they are. But the strength of the Premier League this season, what we could call teams that we expect to be mid-table or near the bottom, I think it's as strong as it's ever been.

"Look at Fulham, going away to Manchester City, 1-1. Leeds go to Chelsea, 4-1. There are no poor teams. There aren't many great teams in the league but there are no poor teams. And that's a problem for Man United."

Article continues below

Gary Neville and Roy Keane maintain their former side won't find themselves in the Championship next season, but at what point does a prolonged run of poor form become a genuine danger of relegation?
