Sports.title: Herta replaced at Hitech to end F2 season early
Sports.content:
Colton Herta will end his torrid time in Formula 2 early by not returning for the final two rounds of the 2026 season following a “mutual agreement” with Hitech.

The nine-time IndyCar race winner made the transition to European single-seaters this year as part of his bid to gain an FIA Superlicence that is required to compete in Formula 1.

But F2 has not gone as planned for Herta, who is 19th in the standings with only 26 points from 12 rounds, achieving a best result of fifth at Barcelona from third on a reversed grid.

The 26-year-old American is not returning for the final race weekends in Qatar and Abu Dhabi and will be replaced by Roman Bilinski - who was already set to take Herta’s seat in 2027.

Jan Sumann, Hitech's F2 head of race engineering said: “We're delighted to welcome Roman to Hitech for the final two rounds of the season.

“These two weekends will give us an opportunity to start building important relationships before the winter.

“I would also like to thank Colton for his commitment and determination throughout his time with Hitech, despite a challenging season. We wish him the very best for the future.”

Roman Bilinski, Monza in F3 2025 Photo by: Formula Motorsport Ltd

Herta was not quoted in the team statement and it is not yet known what his plans for next year are because, despite a poor season, he was still in the frame for an F1 promotion.

That was via his role as Cadillac’s reserve driver and thanks to six FP1 appearances in 2026, he has now obtained a superlicence but days after doing so, Valtteri Bottas was confirmed for next year alongside Sergio Perez.

As for his replacement at Hitech, Bilinski also contested his rookie F2 campaign this year but didn’t fare much better, sitting 16th in the standings with 36 points for DAMS.

“I'm really excited to be joining Hitech for the final two rounds of the season. Having the opportunity to work with the team ahead of 2027 is a real bonus,” said the 22-year-old Polish-Briton, who finished 11th in F3 in 2025.

“It means we can start working together straight away, get to know each other and build a strong foundation ahead of next year. Of course, I’ll be hoping for some strong results to close out the current season.”

Sports.title: Why Bearman’s expected 2027 Haas F1 deal remains unsigned
Sports.content:
Ferrari protege Oliver Bearman remains the only driver on the F1 grid without a contract for 2027. It is a situation that would have been hard to imagine just a few weeks ago, given that his retention at Haas had been taken for granted since last summer.

The announcement of Rafael Camara as Bearman's 2027 team-mate, which came ahead of the Brazilian Grand Prix, was expected to be swiftly followed by that of his British team-mate. Instead, the silence has dragged on to the point of becoming a talking point, even prompting rumours of Bearman driving elsewhere next year. The paradox is that Bearman and Haas have strong reasons to reach an agreement.

Bearman has ruled out racing elsewhere in 2027, while Haas has long been expected to retain him, yet the negotiations have dragged on far longer than initially anticipated.

In recent weeks, there has been speculation about the reasons for the deadlock, some linked to the contractual relationship between Bearman and Ferrari and to the future prospects of the 21-year-old Briton.

According to information obtained by Autosport, however, the issue holding up the signing does not concern the driver’s long-term future, but rather the financial terms of the deal with Haas.

Ferrari has already exercised the option allowing it to retain Bearman within its driver programme. Given that Maranello has invested financial resources in the young Briton ever since he joined the Driver Academy in 2021, allowing Bearman to leave on a free transfer would be a big waste of all those efforts.

Rafael Camara will finish the 2026 season for Haas as he prepares for his full 2027 debut alongside Oliver Bearman. Photo by: James Sutton / LAT Images via Getty Images

Bearman could be in a position to leave Ferrari at the end of 2027 if he has not received a call-up to join the works team, but this scenario does not represent an obstacle to renewing with Haas, and there is no need to finalise his relationship with Ferrari in the short term – especially given that Lewis Hamilton is in the twilight of his career. The Scuderia has not ruled out any of its longer-term options.

The immediate negotiations therefore centre on two parties: Haas and Bearman’s entourage. The sticking point is the salary offered by the American team, a figure that the driver and his staff do not consider commensurate with their expectations.

This has led to a prolonged deadlock, despite both sides being aware of the need to reach an agreement. On the eve of the Las Vegas Grand Prix, Bearman made no secret of his disappointment at a situation that has now been dragging on for months. “There’s nothing new to say. To be honest, I’m rather disappointed to find myself here, at the twentieth round of the season, without a signed contract for next year. It’s a strange situation, but we’re getting there.”

The Briton admitted that the uncertainty is becoming difficult to cope with, especially after a season in which he believes he has proved his worth as the team's lead driver.

Bearman categorically ruled out the possibility of moving to another team in 2027, though. When asked if there was even the slightest chance of racing elsewhere, with no more seats up for real discussion, his answer was unequivocal: "No, zero chance."

He added: "My goal for 2027 is very clear. I think we have unfinished business here. Then looking further into the future, it's not really in my hands, let's say it like that."

Bearman has been open about his ambition to make it to Maranello, but he is aware that decisions regarding the Scuderia’s future do not depend solely on his performance.

"Of course I'm under contract with Ferrari. Ferrari have given me this incredible opportunity to step into F1 with them for the first time," he acknowledged. "I'm still a Ferrari junior driver and my ultimate dream is to race for Ferrari. First of all, they're the most iconic team and they're the first team that believed in me as a kid.

Oliver Bearman, Haas Photo by: Lars Baron / LAT Images via Getty Images

"It's still my ultimate dream, but there's no doubt that looking into the future, there may be some challenges there. There's no denying that, it's very clear. I don't really have much say in the matter. We just need to see how things develop over time."

The immediate contract situation is more straightforward. Ferrari has already clarified its contractual position and is not the party holding up Bearman’s confirmation. The ongoing negotiations concern only the terms of the agreement between the driver and Haas. Autosport understands the matter is expected to be resolved before the final weekend in Abu Dhabi, in all likelihood through an inevitable compromise on the financial front.

That doesn't make the lack of a deal by the end of November any less frustrating for Bearman. "It's not a good feeling to be sitting here with two races to go without things sorted out," he said. "Even though I know that we're pretty much there, the fact is that we're not. There's no excuse for being here without a contract signed, quite honestly."



Those comments show just how much this whole tug-of-war has weighed on the driver. Barring an unexpected breakdown in negotiations, Bearman is expected to remain with Haas in 2027 as well, forming one of the youngest driver pairings on the grid alongside Camara.

Sports.title: F1 plans two-team engine supply limit under 2030 V8 rules
Sports.content:
Formula 1 is planning a shift to just two power unit supplies per manufacturer in 2030, Autosport has learned, raising questions over the status of Mercedes' three current customers.

Over the Las Vegas weekend the FIA announced there was unanimous support to bring the next generation of power unit regulations forward to 2030. That includes a move to 2.1-litre V8 engines, including a turbocharger, a maximum of 200 kilowatts of electric power and the use of sustainable fuels.

That move satisfies the demand for cheaper and less complex engines, which FIA president Mohammed Ben Sulayem and F1 chief Stefano Domenicali had been pursuing in unison. Meanwhile, adding a turbo was a key requirement for the likes of Audi and also ensures engine noise remains at a suitable level for some of F1's urban venues.

What was also part of a wide-ranging document the FIA produced on the 2030 framework, but wasn't part of the public announcement, is an agreement between the six 2030 power unit manufacturers to supply just two teams each. This also includes their works team, leaving just one single engine supply available for external customer teams.

Autosport understands that one aim of the move is to reduce the political influence of manufacturers supplying a large share of the grid, in this case Mercedes and Ferrari, while the manufacturers in question had also been willing to downsize as supplying F1 engines is a loss-making operation, with supplies capped at just $18m per season.

Ferrari is currently supplying the works team, Haas and Cadillac, but the latter will be moving to in-house engines from 2030, meaning the question of Ferrari's supply is solving itself. Red Bull Powertrains will also be taking care of two teams, Red Bull Racing and Racing Bulls, while at present Audi, Aston Martin partner Honda and Cadillac's shareholder General Motors will all have their own works teams as their one and only confirmed customer.

Photo by: Manuel Eletto

The Mercedes question

That leaves the question of what will happen to Mercedes and the customers of Mercedes High Performance Powertrains. Alongside the works team in Brackley, the Brixworth operation is currently supplying McLaren, Williams as well as Alpine, whose parent company Renault recently abandoned and sold its in-house engine operation.

Per the 2030 framework, two of those three teams would be looking for a new engine supply if the FIA World Motor Sport Council approves the proposal in Shanghai next month. That seismic shift will set up months of political intrigue in the F1 paddock as teams scramble to secure what has been F1's most reliable and performant power unit supplier ever since F1 moved to hybrid engines in 2014, or conclude deals with currently less desirable options.

Autosport understands that both McLaren and Williams are fancying their chances of remaining with Mercedes. And while McLaren at least explored the idea of becoming its own power unit manufacturer when a move to a cheaper formula would make that more feasible than it is now, CEO Zak Brown indicated that ship has sailed for 2030 as he aims to remain a Mercedes customer.

"It's something we've looked at in the past, but we're very happy with HPP," Brown said in Las Vegas on Thursday. "I think we've proven that we can win championships with them, so we don't have any intention to have anything in the back of our car other than a Mercedes."

Mercedes' intentions about what its ideal customer team would look like are less clear right now. Having been beaten by McLaren in 2024 and 2025, CEO Toto Wolff maintained that a win for a customer is still a feather in the cap for HPP and the Mercedes brand as a whole, while a strong customer team also provides a valuable chassis benchmark for the works operation.

And while Brown hailed HPP as an "awesome partner", it's no secret that the relationship between HPP and McLaren has at least come under some strain at the start of this year amid a knowledge gap between the works team and its customer over how to exploit and deploy the complex new power units.

Photo by: Alex Pantling / Getty Images

Whether Mercedes will continue to lease engines to its most formidable rival or whether a deal with a midfield team is the preferred option will likely become the subject of plenty of intrigue in the coming months.

Why FIA engine is dead

What is certain is that the FIA's proposed third-party engine plan is now dead in the water. With F1 power units becoming less complex and expensive in 2030, FIA president Ben Sulayem had floated the idea of sourcing a supply of off-the-shelf, white-label engines to further alleviate concerns over team independence.

However, that plan never seemed economically viable for any prospective engine builder, and with all six PUMs at the table now unanimously agreeing to 2030's key infrastructure, a cap of two supplies would mean there are at least 12 power unit supplies available for 11 teams.

The FIA did include a safety net in case one of the six manufacturers decides to drop out, adding a clause under which a departing manufacturer’s F1 power unit intellectual property would transfer to the FIA, which could then assign it to a new manufacturer coming in.

As is the case today, there will also be an "obligation to supply", meaning the FIA could force one of the manufacturers to supply an additional, third team with an engine if that outfit can't arrange a deal to find one, which may well end up becoming a key clause.

What has also been agreed is the basis for the power unit cost cap for the 2030-2034 period. The cap will remain at today's figure of $190m for 2030 before falling by $7.5m per year, ending at $160m for the 2034 season.

Photo by: Alex Bierens de Haan / LAT Images via Getty Images

That sliding scale helps manufacturers with the initial development cost of the new power units. A development freeze of the current engines from 2028, as well as a ban on V8 dyno testing until the summer of that year, is expected to help F1's current manufacturers manage their resources between the two projects. Existing manufacturers will also receive more cost-cap headroom than newcomer General Motors, which can now abandon its V6 plans and just focus on the V8 programme in Charlotte. GM is understood to be signing up to a budget cap of $170m for the first couple of years.

Why early deal is so crucial for F1

There are still several important topics to be fleshed out further by the manufacturers, such as the exact nature of the electric push-to-pass system as it would need to work in conjunction with the chassis design to promote close racing.

But by defining the overarching framework and key engine architecture, which will be rubber-stamped by the FIA World Motor Sport Council, both the manufacturers and the FIA can now get to work on the next rules cycle on a reasonable timeline.

That should help the governing body come up with chassis regulations which are tuned to work well with the new power units and deliver a more pure and exciting set of rules, without facing the prospect of having to adapt to late U-turns by OEMs, which led to 2026's compromised and criticised formula to begin with.

Sports.title: Camara to finish F1 season with Haas, ending F2 title bid
Sports.content:
Haas rookie Rafael Camara will see out the season with Haas in Qatar and Abu Dhabi, effectively ending his F2 championship challenge.

Camara was confirmed in October as a full-time replacement for Esteban Ocon in 2027, and was fast-tracked into the seat after Ocon's relationship with the US-owned team deteriorated.

After test driver Ryo Hirakawa took over Ocon's car midway through the Mexico Grand Prix weekend, Camara made his F1 debut on home soil in Brazil and was also in the VF-26 at this weekend's Las Vegas Grand Prix.

The final two rounds presented a bigger decision to make, though, because the 21-year-old is leading the F2 championship by seven points over Red Bull junior Nikola Tsolov. Drivers are unable to take part in both F1 and F2 on the same weekend.

Haas has now decided to keep the Brazilian in the seat to finish the season, rather than bringing back Hirakawa, to give Camara as much experience as possible ahead of his 2027 rookie campaign.

"We’re excited to be able to finish the season with Rafa driving and build on his first two race starts with the team in Brazil and America," said Haas F1 Team boss Ayao Komatsu.

"I’m delighted that Rafa’s embraced every track session as a learning opportunity and embedded himself further within the team. We now get to finish the season together which is advantageous to us all ahead of a relatively short off-season and as our 2027 preparations get underway."

Rafael Camara, Haas Photo by: Lars Baron / LAT Images via Getty Images

Camara finished 20th after a difficult maiden race in Interlagos in the wet, and took 16th in Las Vegas.

While Tsolov now just needs seven points to match Camara, Camara’s absence also boosts third-placed Alex Dunne’s title chances, who trails the Brazilian by 18 points.

Sports.title: Bill Haney Warns Liam Paro Over VADA Testing Dispute
Sports.content:
Bill Haney brought up the possibility of a contract breach on Monday if Liam Paro walks away from his December 19 welterweight unification fight with Devin Haney over VADA testing. Speaking on Instagram Live, Bill mentioned lawyers and asked whether Paro’s side is looking for an exit from the Chase Center main event in San Francisco.

“I think it looks like you might be finding reasons to breach outside of the agreement,” said Bill Haney. He said lawyers handle those disputes and noted that the Haneys would face consequences too if they failed to meet what they signed up for. Bill stopped short of threatening a lawsuit, adding that Devin is already in camp and preparing to fight.

What Bill Says Happened In Negotiations

Bill claims Paro’s team never raised VADA testing during negotiations and only brought it up publicly after the contract was signed. Paro and his promoter, Matt Rose of No Limit Boxing, say VADA was agreed to during talks. Paro has publicly pressed Devin to enroll, though whether Paro himself has entered the pool remains unconfirmed.

Bill pointed to Devin’s bout against Brian Norman Jr. to show how he handles testing when it is part of a deal. VADA was written into that contract before Norman signed, and the disagreement then was over when Norman would enroll. With Paro, Bill said the bout came together on roughly four or five weeks’ notice, and he considers 12 weeks the minimum for VADA.

“Had it been a longer time where we would have had to negotiate, then I would have put it in the agreement,” said Bill.

The contract may say one thing. Devin still has nearly four weeks to volunteer for the program he spent years promoting. Bill said he stopped pushing Devin to enroll after leaving year-round testing because they took ridicule while few other fighters joined. That is a tough sell when the opponent is asking for the exact testing the Haneys used to champion.

What Paro Faces If He Walks

Paro is unlikely to pull out. A welterweight unification and the purse that comes with it would be difficult for him and No Limit Boxing to replace. If he stays in the fight, the Norman bout shows what he has to solve. Haney builds rounds behind his jab and quick combinations, then backs out behind an extended lead hand or ties up his opponent the moment the distance closes. He held Norman repeatedly. Paro has to punch as Haney reaches to clinch, before the referee breaks them and resets Paro at the end of the jab.

Bill says the testing already in place is enough for him. That gets harder to defend if Paro pulls the upset on December 19. You cannot turn down VADA when your opponent asks for it in November and then complain about the rules in January.

Sports.title: Devin Haney’s VADA Dispute Puts Liam Paro Fight at Risk
Sports.content:
Devin Haney’s December 19 welterweight unification against Liam Paro in San Francisco is running into conflicting reports over whether Haney has enrolled in Voluntary Anti-Doping Association testing. Chris Mannix reported Haney had not signed up, and Paro’s side was ready to walk.

“The Devin Haney-Liam Paro fight is in real jeopardy, sources say,” Mannix wrote on X. He said Paro wanted full VADA testing and summed up the camp’s position in four words. “No testing, no fight.”

The VADA Enrollment Deadline

Paro’s promoter, No Limit Boxing, told Nine it gave Haney’s team 24 hours to enroll. According to the promoter, VADA testing was agreed upon during the original talks. Paro later said he was told the Haneys wanted to rely on athletic commission testing alone.

Paro’s camp can take the IBF belt out of the December 19 main event by pulling him from the fight. Haney could still defend his WBO title against a replacement if the promoters found one, but that would cost him the chance to leave San Francisco with two belts.

The Missing VADA Start Date

VADA has yet to publicly confirm Haney’s enrollment or say when random testing will begin. Even if Haney has signed the paperwork, Paro’s camp still has to decide whether the testing arrangements are enough for him to fight on December 19.

We all heard Bill’s ridiculous excuse. What a farce.

The Haney’s, while Conte was around, argued that everyone should do VADA. Obviously as everyone knows, VADA’s testing substance panel is much more extensive than any commission. (We Verified this fact with VADA) VADA checks for blood doping, hGH, peptides and synthetic testosterone, and more. Even after everything that I went through, I have been willing to test for all that and more to prove i am clean . In fact, we hired the State of California Commission to do simultaneous testing in addition to VADA. — RYAN GARCIA (@RyanGarcia) November 23, 2026

A late start date shrinks how much of the final camp gets covered before both men step on the scale in San Francisco. Haney, 33-0 (15 KOs), is bringing his WBO welterweight belt into the bout against Paro, 27-1 (16 KOs), who holds the IBF title. Neither side has pulled out, though Paro’s team has made clear it will not box under commission testing alone. Until VADA puts Haney’s name on an official enrollment list, Paro’s side has no reason to back off its threat.

Paro’s camp might be doing Haney a favor if it walks away over VADA. Haney is also a promoter, and the Paro fight hasn’t generated much buzz for a pay-per-view main event. If he already has an opponent in mind who could sell more buys, Paro’s withdrawal would give him an opening to make that fight and keep December 19.

Sports.title: Deontay Wilder Gets Martin Bakole in Cardiff
Sports.content:
Martin Bakole has less than three weeks to prove he actually trained for his original December 11 bout before stepping in against Deontay Wilder. Turki Alalshikh named Bakole to replace injured cruiserweight champion Jai Opetaia in the co-main event of Tyson Fury against Anthony Joshua at Principality Stadium in Cardiff.

On paper, Bakole is not getting dragged off the couch this time. He was already scheduled to fight Solomon Adebayo on the same Netflix card. That sounds fine until you look at what Bakole weighed the last two times he stepped into the ring.

Bakole’s Weight Was Already Slipping

Bakole weighed 284 pounds when he walked down Jared Anderson in August 2024. He dropped the unbeaten American three times, doing much of his damage with uppercuts, and stopped him in the fifth. Six months later, Bakole took the Joseph Parker fight on 48 hours’ notice, weighed 310 pounds, and was stopped in the second round.

The late call helped explain the 310 pounds against Parker. Bakole had a full camp for Efe Ajagba in May 2025 and still came in at 299. He looked sluggish over 10 rounds and came away with a majority draw. Trainer Billy Nelson said the weigh-in caught him by surprise and brought in a nutritionist after the fight.

Bakole has not fought in the 19 months since that night against Ajagba. Coming into a routine undercard bout against Adebayo, nobody knows if he took the scale seriously or showed up around 305 pounds expecting an easy night. If his legs are heavy in Cardiff, Wilder will have all the space he needs to set his feet and fire the right hand.

Bakole Still Threatens Wilder’s Chin

Wilder, 41, holds a 45-4-1 record with 43 knockouts, though he had to grind through twelve rough rounds to edge Derek Chisora by split decision in April. His punch resistance is no longer what it was during his title reign.

Even at 300 pounds, Bakole has a heavy jab and can hurt Wilder with short uppercuts if he backs him to the ropes. If Bakole gets through the first three rounds and starts making Wilder fight with his back to the ropes, the extra weight may be less of a concern. The danger is getting there. If Bakole plods straight in, Wilder can drop him with a right hand before Bakole gets close enough to throw those uppercuts.

Sports.title: Ryan Garcia Calls Haney’s VADA Delay “Shady”
Sports.content:
Ryan Garcia called Devin Haney’s VADA testing delay “shady” on Monday, questioning why one of boxing’s loudest advocates for the program still has no publicly confirmed enrollment for his December 19 welterweight unification fight against Liam Paro.

Garcia pointed to Haney’s history with the Voluntary Anti-Doping Association and urged boxing reporters to cover the holdup. He was responding to a post from Paro, who claimed Haney’s camp wanted to rely solely on athletic commission drug testing. Paro’s claim about commission-only testing has yet to be independently confirmed.

It’s quite obvious Devin Haney is hiding he has advocating for Vada testing for years now. This hold up is shady and I’ve said it before and I’ll say it again you can’t trust the haneys The little brother knowing things before anyone knows And now this Where is all the boxing reporters BIASED Report on this. He has a long track record of using Vada. Fights 5 weeks away — RYAN GARCIA (@RyanGarcia) November 23, 2026

Haney said Friday that the Paro bout would be his 14th straight fight using VADA and that he had returned more than 65 clean tests. That statement came before Paro’s claim that Haney’s camp wanted commission testing alone.

Garcia has firsthand experience with the program he is now urging Haney to enter. VADA collected the samples in which Garcia tested positive for ostarine around their April 2024 fight. The New York State Athletic Commission changed Garcia’s decision win to a no contest and suspended him for a year. Haney spent two years preaching clean boxing after that night. Seeing his own enrollment missing inside four weeks of fight night gives Garcia an easy target.

Paro’s promoter, Matt Rose, told Fox Sports Australia that VADA testing was one of the first terms agreed during negotiations. Rose said his team gave Haney’s side 24 hours to enroll and that Paro was prepared to walk away. Standard commission testing on fight week does not match random out-of-competition blood and urine collection. Their WBO and IBF title fight is scheduled to headline a DAZN pay-per-view at Chase Center in San Francisco.

The Irony could not be more shocking. So Bill and Devin claim to be “clean” from PED’s, yet they are very knowledgeable about “cycling” etc. Very versed in this area. I didn’t even know what that ment. Now we learn that they “clean guys” are refusing to enroll in VADA testing. Suddenly, they have some issues with VADA, it turns out. Only change lately is that Victor Conte is not here. Can’t make this up. — RYAN GARCIA (@RyanGarcia) November 23, 2026

Haney says he intends to enroll with VADA for a 14th straight bout. Nothing has been filed yet. With December 19 less than four weeks off, every wasted day shrinks the window for out-of-competition testing in San Francisco.

Sports.title: Rumors Swirl Turki Alalshikh Could Walk After Fury vs Joshua Fight
Sports.content:
Johnny Nelson thinks boxing could go back to the “dark ages” if Turki Alalshikh steps away from the sport. Without Alalshikh putting up the massive purses to force big fights across the finish line, fans are going to struggle to see top matchups, even if plenty of spoiled stars have already been coasting for easy money on his cards.

Nelson believes Alalshikh will step away soon after the Tyson Fury vs. Anthony Joshua event.

“The rumor has it that Turki will be stepping away shortly after this at some point or another,” said Nelson to talkSPORT Boxing.

Big Purses And Flat Fights

Fans have gotten spoiled since 2024. Alalshikh has loaded cards with the biggest names in boxing, even when half of them turned in dull performances. Canelo Álvarez, Shakur Stevenson, Terence Crawford, Teofimo Lopez, Oleksandr Usyk, Devin Haney and Jai Opetaia all looked flat while collecting huge purses.

Maybe knowing the money is already in the bank takes away some of the urgency, or maybe they just had off nights, because it happened far too often with the best paid fighters on those shows. Only a handful of guys, like Ryan Garcia and Daniel Dubois, actually delivered real excitement for the money.

“We’ll not get the fights that we’ve been graced with,” said Nelson.

That is the real issue here. Once fighters get used to Alalshikh’s money, it will be hard to get top boxers to accept normal promoter purses again. They will turn their noses up at standard offers and sit on the shelf hoping he comes back.

The Purse Problem For Fighters

Look at Shakur Stevenson right now. He is already showing what happens when a fighter holds out for the big payday. The longer he waits around for the number he wants, the longer he goes without fighting a top opponent. You don’t get those prime years back, and nobody is going to bail him out once the Saudi money dries up.

The old promotional headaches will creep back in too. Eddie Hearn and Frank Warren both put on shows for DAZN, and they have done well for themselves working alongside Alalshikh over the last two years. Still, sharing a broadcaster settles nothing when one promoter holds a fighter the other needs.

Sports.title: Jermell Charlo Out Of December 5 Vergil Ortiz Fight
Sports.content:
Jermell Charlo will not replace Keith Thurman against Vergil Ortiz Jr. on December 5, according to Mike Coppinger. Good. Bringing a 36-year-old fighter out of mothballs with no tune-up after more than three years away would have been terrible optics. Charlo has not won a fight since May 2022, over four years ago. Is this really what Ortiz wants for his career at 28?

“Charlo indeed is not in the mix to fight Vergil Ortiz,” Coppinger wrote on X. Chris Mannix reported that Brian Mendoza and Eric Priest are the expected options after Thurman withdrew injured. Charlo is already set to face Brock Jarvis at 160 pounds on December 12 in Australia.

Poor Replacement Options For PPV

What about DAZN? They are charging fans $79.99 in the United States and £24.99 in the UK for the December 5 pay-per-view headlined by David Benavidez and Michal Cieslak. Ortiz was brought into the co-feature slot to liven things up, yet there is nothing sporting about feeding him either of these replacements.

Mendoza (23-5, 17 KOs) is no upgrade after dropping three of his last four fights. He caught lightning in a bottle with his seventh-round knockout of Sebastian Fundora in April 2023, though it has been all downhill since then with clear decision losses to Tim Tszyu, Serhii Bohachuk, and Yoenis Tellez.

Priest has spent six years fighting on small club cards without beating a single ranked contender, and Esneiker Correa even held him to a draw last November. Expecting fans to shell out $79.99 to watch Ortiz face a faded Mendoza or a club-level opponent like Priest makes zero sense for a pay-per-view show.

What Charlo Has Left At 160

Charlo has not stepped through the ropes since September 2023, when he jumped up two weight classes and lost a lopsided decision to Canelo Alvarez. Canelo dropped him in the seventh round and swept the cards by scores of 119-109 and 118-109 twice. Moving to 168 pounds was never going to be easy, yet Charlo spent the whole night in survival mode and gave Canelo zero reason to take his foot off the gas.

Coppinger noted that an Ortiz versus Charlo fight at 160 could happen in the first half of 2027 if both win next month. Beating Jarvis in Australia gets Charlo active again, though it still proves nothing against top middleweights.

Ortiz has already burned roughly 13 months since stopping Erickson Lubin in two rounds. His promotional dispute with Golden Boy helped kill talks for a fight against Jaron “Boots” Ennis, which would have answered every question about where Ortiz stands. Ortiz cannot afford to keep wasting his prime against short-notice fill-ins.

Sports.title: WBC Mandatory Challenger Souleymane Cissokho Wants To Face Ryan Garcia
Sports.content:
The WBC world welterweight champion Ryan Garcia has mentioned the possibility of a fight with either Floyd “Money” Mayweather or Teofimo Lopez, but the WBC mandatory challenger is wondering when he will receive his shot at the title.

In some cases, a fighter can enter the sport of boxing and gradually build his pro career brick by brick. Once that fighter has earned the right to walk through the door of opportunity, a boxer with name recognition cuts the line.

Back in May 2025, Souleymane Cissokho was set to defend his WBC Silver welterweight title against Egidijus Kavaliauskas. In addition to being a fight for the Silver belt, this matchup also served as a world title eliminator bout.

In a very competitive 12-round contest, Cissokho defeated Kavaliauskas by way of unanimous decision. With the victory, Souleymane Cissokho officially became the WBC number one ranked welterweight contender.

Eleven days later, the then 46-year-old Manny Pacquiao announced he was ending his four-year retirement to fight for the WBC world welterweight title. In a match that ended up being a draw, the champion Mario Barrios held on to the belt.

Seven months after the Pacquiao fight, Ryan Garcia leaped over Souleymane Cissokho, and he was locked in to challenge Barrios for the title. At the time, Garcia was coming off a loss he suffered against Rolando “Rolly” Romero.

On February 21, 2026, Ryan Garcia defeated Mario Barrios via unanimous decision. After Garcia became the new world champion, it seemed like the path was cleared for Cissokho to finally receive his shot at the world title.

Unfortunately for Cissokho, another named person cut in front of him as Conor Benn was penciled in to challenge Ryan Garcia. In their world title fight, Garcia stopped Benn in the 2nd round.

Once again, Souleymane Cissokho is at the front of the line as it relates to the opportunity to fight for the world title. Now it appears Cissokho will get skipped for a fourth time.

The WBC welterweight world champion Ryan Garcia and his promotional company CEO Oscar De La Hoya have been very vocal regarding the next title defense being against Floyd “Money” Mayweather or Teofimo Lopez.

The current No.1 contender Souleymane Cissokho was born in Dakar, Senegal, but moved to France when he was 4 years old. He started boxing at the age of 14 and would go on to represent France and win a Bronze medal in the 2016 Olympics.

Now the undefeated Souleymane Cissokho (18-0, 9 KOs) is waiting to receive the world title bout he rightfully earned. Unfortunately for him, Mauricio Sulaiman and the WBC are known for having number one contenders who don’t receive title shots.

Mauricio Sulaiman has the authority to order a mandatory world title fight. Hopefully, in 2027, Sulaiman will step up and make the proper decision in favor of the number one-ranked WBC welterweight contender Souleymane Cissokho.

Sports.title: Josh Kelly Plans To Retire After Ennis And Fundora
Sports.content:
IBF junior middleweight champion Josh Kelly has come up with one of boxing’s unlikeliest exit plans. He wants to beat Jaron “Boots” Ennis, take the last belt off Sebastian Fundora, and walk away as undisputed champion.

“Yeah. No, it’s Boots, Fundora, and then sail into the sunset,” said Kelly to Fight Hub TV. Asked if he would call it a career after that, he said, “Yeah, bro. Yeah, I don’t need to do much after that.”

Running Will Not Beat Boots

What Kelly never answered is whether he plans to retire if he loses to Ennis. The interviewer dropped the ball by skipping the most obvious follow-up question on the board. Getting carved up by Boots the way Kelly was in his sixth round stoppage loss to David Avanesyan in 2021, when his corner threw in the towel with him a bloody mess, would leave his career in rough shape.

Ennis is up first on February 27 in Atlanta. Anyone who watched Kelly win the IBF belt off Bakhram Murtazaliev saw a twelve round track meet, and he used the same running routine to get past his last opponent. Kelly thinks he can read Ennis’s style because he uses similar moves in the ring. He also claimed he saw a few habits from the Xander Zayas fight that he is keeping quiet until the opening bell.

“It’s whoever can adjust first is going to get the better of the fight,” said Kelly. He expects the fight to shift from round to round and even within a round.

Kelly liked being the underdog against Murtazaliev and says he fights looser when people expect him to lose. Atlanta is a totally different problem. Boots cuts off the ring, switches stances effortlessly, and punishes fighters who try to survive on their bicycle. A counter Kelly lands in the third round could easily turn into a trap Ennis springs in the fourth.

At this point, Fundora is not even worth discussing yet. Kelly said he has enough left to fight until 36 or 37 if he wants. “Why spoil that? Why come back after something like that?” said Kelly.

He will not have to worry about retiring early. His whole exit plan ends in Atlanta against Boots, so the Fundora fight will never happen.

Ghana News.title: Who should pay for student accommodation? – Universities demand national conversation
Ghana News.content:
Dr Cynthia Kpeglo-Freiku, Executive Secretary of Vice Chancellors Ghana. Photo credit: Abeiku Edqlics

The growing student accommodation crisis in Ghana’s public universities has sparked fresh calls for a national conversation about who should pay for decent student housing.

Dr Cynthia Kpeglo-Freiku, Executive Secretary of Vice Chancellors Ghana, says the debate must move beyond complaints about accommodation fees and focus on how government, universities, students, and private investors should share financial responsibility.

Speaking on Joy News’ PM Express on Monday, she argued that the accommodation challenges confronting students reflect wider economic hardships affecting public universities across the country.

“Well, there are a number of hardship situations on campuses. It's not just the housing and accommodation. Basically, I think that there is a general hardship in the country, and everybody is complaining. And so, the story is not very different in our universities.”

Her comments come amid concerns over student accommodation at the University of Ghana, which have raised broader questions about affordability and the responsibilities of university authorities.

But Dr Kpeglo-Freiku cautioned against treating the situation at the University of Ghana as an isolated problem.

“But I don't want us to limit our conversation to only the University of Ghana because I represent all the universities, so I can't speak for one university and what exactly is happening.”

She maintained that the controversy offers an opportunity to examine the pressures facing public tertiary institutions more broadly.

“So this University of Ghana matter, it is just a general or a wider reflection of what is happening generally in public higher education universities in the country,” she explained.

For the Executive Secretary, the central question is not simply whether students struggle to afford accommodation, but who should finance quality housing as universities expand.

“And the question we should really be asking ourselves is: who should be bearing the cost of providing quality student accommodation, and how should that responsibility be shared among government, among universities, among students, and even among private investors?”

She called for a national roundtable involving key stakeholders to examine the issue objectively and determine how to distribute the financial burden.

“This should be a roundtable discussion, devoid of emotion.”

Dr Kpeglo-Freiku also declined to comment on allegations that University of Ghana authorities were targeting students who had publicly expressed concerns.

“Whether management is hounding students that are being vocal and all that, I'm not able to speak to that.”

She insisted that attention should remain on the underlying challenges rather than the emotions surrounding the controversy.

“But I want us to address the core matter on the table, unemotionally. Let's look at the issues realistically and much more objectively.”

Her intervention spotlights a fundamental question facing Ghana’s public universities: how to expand access to quality student accommodation without placing the entire financial burden on one group.

Ghana News.title: Brentford hit Everton for four as Tarkowski sees red
Ghana News.content:
Keane Lewis-Potter scored twice as Brentford swept 10-man Everton aside to move sixth in the Premier League.

The Toffees were bidding to secure a third successive league win, which would send them fifth in the table.

But they were second best throughout, with the damage done in a woeful first half for David Moyes' side.

It had started as a celebratory moment for the Scot as he took charge of a record-breaking 593rd game with Everton, but the evening started to fall apart for the visitors in the 23rd minute when Lewis-Potter opened the scoring.

The full-back was picked out inside the box by Jaidon Anthony and he drove a shot at goal that took a deflection to leave Jordan Pickford stranded.

Just two minutes later and Brentford scored a second, through Lewis-Potter again. His initial shot was blocked but his second attempt took a big deflection off Thierno Barry to fly into the back of the net.

From then on it was wave after wave of Brentford attacks, and got worse for Everton five minutes before the break when James Tarkowski was sent off for the first time in his Premier League career.

The defender slid in to clear the ball but caught Yehor Yarmolyuk on the shin as he followed through.

Tarkowski was initially booked but referee Craig Pawson was sent to the screen by the video assistant referee (VAR) and he upgraded the card to a red after checking the replays.

Everton's best chance fell to Barry on the stroke of half-time, but Caoimhin Kelleher superbly kept out his bullet header.

The visitors improved after the break and it felt like Brentford needed a third goal to kill the game off.

That arrived in spectacular fashion midway through the second half when Vitaly Janelt hammered in an unstoppable strike from 30 yards.

Fabio Carvalho, making only his second Premier League appearance of the season, added a late fourth with his knee to wrap up a fine evening for Brentford.

Brentford analysis: Lewis-Potter the unlikely scorer

Brentford manager Keith Andrews had a conundrum before this game - how he would deal with the absence of suspended striker Igor Thiago.

He handed Callum Wilson a first Premier League start, but could hardly have anticipated it would be Lewis-Potter who would solve his goalscoring concerns.

The 25-year-old was deployed at left-back for Monday night's game but Everton struggled to pick up his attacking runs.

Both his goals involved some luck with deflections, but on both occasions he was given acres of space to get his initial shot off.

Lewis-Potter is something of an unsung hero for Brentford, with his ability to play anywhere down the left making him key to Andrews' side.

But he has not been known as much of a goalscorer, with his best tally before now three in a season. He now has four goals by November.

Lewis-Potter has not yet secured a senior England cap but performances like this will only increase the calls for him to receive international recognition.

Everton analysis: Misery for Moyes on record-breaking night

Moyes will be proud of his place in Everton's record books, having now managed more games for the club than anyone during his two spells.

But aside from that this was a night he will want to forget as almost everything that could go wrong did.

There was little Pickford could do about either of the deflected goals, while the Toffees may feel aggrieved by Tarkowski's red card - the first he has received in his career after being booked 74 times without a sending-off.

There did not appear to be intent from Tarkowski as he managed to clear the ball, but what went against him was the speed and intensity at which he flew in.

Regardless, his dismissal means Moyes cannot put this down as a bad night and move on, with Tarkowski now suspended for the Merseyside derby at home on Sunday (12:00 GMT).

Ghana News.title: Morocco and Senegal await AFCON final verdict after court case
Ghana News.content:
Everyone knows a football match should take 90 minutes, but the 2025 Africa Cup of Nations (AFCON) final has been playing out for 10 months.

Now, finally, Morocco or Senegal will be crowned winners. However, that moment of glory will come in a courtroom, not on the pitch.

On Tuesday afternoon, sport's highest legal authority, the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS), will render its judgement on Senegal's appeal against the decision to strip them of the title they thought they won in January against the hosts in Rabat.

The case was heard in early October, and the wait is almost over.

So how did we get here?

What happened in the Afcon final?

With 66,000 fans creating an electric atmosphere at Prince Moulay Abdellah Stadium, Morocco chased its first Afcon title since 1976.

But the final descended into chaos deep into second-half stoppage time.

With the match goalless, Senegal thought Ismaila Sarr had scored a dramatic winner, only to discover referee Jean Jacques Ndala had awarded Morocco a free-kick.

The controversy deepened in the 98th minute when, after a video assistant referee (VAR) review, Ndala awarded Morocco a penalty.

Tempers boiled over on the touchline and in the stands. Senegal coach Pape Thiaw led some of his players and staff down the tunnel, while supporters clashed with security as order briefly collapsed.

Play eventually resumed, and in the 124th minute, Morocco missed a golden chance to end their 50-year wait for continental glory when Brahim Diaz failed to convert a penalty, chipping it 'Panenka' style into goalkeeper Edouard Mendy's arms.

Pape Gueye's extra-time strike then secured a 1-0 win for Senegal, who lifted the trophy for a second time.

Or so they thought.

Why was the AFCON final result overturned?

The Royal Moroccan Football Federation (FMRF) quickly lodged a complaint with the Confederation of African Football (Caf), arguing that Senegal had breached competition regulations.

Article 82, contained within a chapter titled 'Withdrawals', states: "If, for any reason whatsoever, a team... refuses to play or leaves the ground before the regular end of the match without the authorisation of the referee", they shall be "considered [the loser] and shall be eliminated from the current competition".

In March a Caf appeals board agreed, ruling that Senegal had forfeited the match and awarding Morocco a 3-0 victory.

While CAF has overturned results during AFCON and World Cup qualifying, some people, including a former senior CAF official, argued that only the referee can abandon a match if a walk-off occurs.

The FMRF said it was seeking the proper application of tournament regulations, but Senegal's federation (FSF) described the ruling as "unfair, unprecedented and unacceptable" and appealed to Cas.

Some Senegal supporters were initially convicted of hooliganism offences after clashes during the final but eventually returned home after receiving a royal pardon

What is the Court of Arbitration for Sport?

Founded in 1984 and based in the Swiss city of Lausanne, Cas was set up as an independent legal body designed to settle disputes as global sport became more lucrative and, as a result, more litigious.

For governing bodies which recognise Cas' authority, it is deemed to be the supreme arbiter, meaning its ruling is final unless, in rare cases, Switzerland's highest court decides to set it aside based on a limited number of technicalities.

More than 900 cases are filed every year across more than 50 sports, covering issues such as employment contracts and transfers, doping, corruption, TV rights, and, in this case, the organisation of sporting events.

The FSF's appeal was heard in private on 8 October by a panel of three arbitrators chosen by Cas for their expertise in sports law.

The panel was led by Frenchman Gerald Simon, founder of the Sports Law Laboratory at the University of Burgundy and a Cas member for 23 years.

Italian international law professor Luigi Fumagalli and Hamburg-based attorney and professor of law at the University of Zurich, Ulrich Haas, completed the trio.

If the panel had failed to come to a consensus on the case, Cas president Simon will have made the final decision.

What could the long-term fallout be?

Although CAF's appeals board is independent, a reversal of its judgement would deliver another blow to the reputation of African football's governing body, which has been heavily criticised for the retrospective decision to hand Morocco the title.

CAF president Patrice Motsepe said in March that it will "adhere to" and "respect" whatever Cas decides, so, if things go in Senegal's favour, it could mean someone having to tinker with the AFCON rulebook.

The Senegal walk-off has, however, already changed football's rules.

"The referee may sanction with a red card any player who leaves the field of play in protest at ⁠a ​referee's decision," said IFAB, the game's lawmaking body, in April.

"This new rule will also apply ​to any team official who incites players to leave the field of play. A team that causes a match ​to be abandoned will, in principle, forfeit the match."

Thiaw lost his job following Senegal's last-32 World Cup exit this summer, while Walid Regragui, the man in the Morocco dugout in January, was dismissed in March.

Whatever the outcome of the case, animosity is likely to linger between the two federations.

The FMRF's senior hierarchy was furious with Senegal's behaviour, believing the pictures beamed around the world irrevocably tarnished the image of the first Afcon hosted by the kingdom since 1988 - a tournament into which a huge amount of time and money had been invested.

The FSF and the Senegalese government have leaned into a continent-wide feeling that Morocco holds too much influence in African football.

Other incidents also irked Senegal, such as laser pens aimed at players' eyes and ball boys moving goalkeeper Mendy's towel, which led to the barely believable sight of reserve keeper Yehvann Diouf being tackled to the ground by three ball boys when he tried to intervene.

With the next AFCON scheduled to take place in June and July next year, the chances of a high-profile rematch between Africa's best two teams are a tantalising thought.

While the chaos of this year's final may have sparked a new rivalry for fans to revel in, there is unanimous agreement that such encounters should be settled on the pitch, not in a courtroom.

Ghana News.title: Fury reveals schizophrenia diagnosis
Ghana News.content:
Tyson Fury says he was diagnosed with schizophrenia soon after his world title win over Wladimir Klitschko in 2015.

British heavyweight Fury, 38, says he heard voices in his head threatening to hurt him and his family.

In a documentary which will be released by Netflix on Friday, Fury and wife Paris describe how he was diagnosed after being admitted to hospital with a suspected heart attack in June 2016.

"Words can't explain the darkness I was in," Fury says.

"It was like a living version of the pits of hell. I thought I would end up in a padded room with the door locked, and that scared me so much.

"The anxiety was crippling me. I just could not overcome it and that's when I went and saw the psychiatrist down in London. She asked me a gazillion questions, and I ticked all the boxes. Depression, anxiety, bipolar disorder."

Doctors said Fury had suffered an anxiety attack.

Fury recalls hearing the radio talking to him, and begging Paris to get him out of the hospital because "the Illuminati" wanted him.

In the period after his victory over Klitschko, Fury gained weight and struggled with drug and alcohol addiction.

"It got that bad I was hearing voices in my mind," he says.

"I wouldn't be able to sit and have a conversation because I'd be hearing stuff in my mind.

"I didn't know where to turn and no-one knew what to do. I really needed help, or check into rehab or something.

"I never got a break from it for years. I wanted to be what I thought was normal again."

After Fury was released from hospital, a diagnosis of schizophrenia and bipolar disorder was confirmed, according to the documentary.

The NHS describes schizophrenia, external as a form of psychosis, and symptoms can include hallucinations, delusions and muddled thoughts and speech. It says the main symptom of bipolar disorder, external is extreme changes to your mood.

Fury describes a "turning point" in 2017 when he was on a night out for Halloween.

"I went out and I was embarrassed by how I looked," he says.

"I was a fat mess and I had a glow-in-the-dark skeleton suit with full face mask on.

"I looked around and could see all the young people and I thought, 'I had the world in my hands and I threw it all away, and now I'm a fat mess addicted to alcohol'."

He says that was the beginning of a comeback which led him to focus more on his family and to return to training.

It resulted in another world title when he beat Deontay Wilder in 2020.

Fury is preparing for the long-awaited all-British heavyweight fight against Anthony Joshua in Cardiff on 11 December.

The fight will be broadcast live on Netflix.

Ghana News.title: Rent Control considers easing six-month rent advance restriction
Ghana News.content:
Landlords in Ghana could be allowed to collect up to 12 months’ rent in advance under a proposed amendment to the country’s rent law, a move that has already drawn opposition from tenant advocates.

The proposal, being considered by the Rent Control Department, would double the current six-month limit stipulated under the Rent Act, 1963 (Act 220), for tenancies exceeding six months.

Acting Rent Commissioner, Frederick Opoku, disclosed this on JoyNews’ The Probe programme on Sunday, November 22, 2026, explaining that the proposal followed repeated concerns from property owners about the financial demands of developing and maintaining rental accommodation.

He said landlords had argued during stakeholder engagements that the existing restriction did not adequately reflect the cost of property investment and the resources required to keep buildings in good condition.

Mr Opoku stressed, however, that the proposed change was still at the drafting stage and had not received ministerial approval.

It would have to go through the necessary executive and legislative processes, including consideration by Cabinet and Parliament, before it could become law.

Under Section 25(5) of Act 220, a landlord is prohibited from demanding more than six months’ rent in advance where the tenancy is for a period exceeding six months.

The proposed revision would therefore represent a significant change to the existing arrangement, which has become a contentious issue in Ghana’s rental market.

Tenants raise concerns

The National Tenants Union has questioned the need to extend the advance payment period when, in its view, authorities have struggled to enforce the existing law.

A representative of the union, Reindolph Afrifa-Oware, said the immediate priority should be to ensure compliance with the current six-month limit rather than introduce a provision that could increase the financial pressure on tenants.

He said some landlords were already demanding one year’s rent in advance, despite the legal restriction, while tenants in parts of Kumasi were reportedly being asked to pay as much as two years’ rent upfront.

Mr Afrifa-Oware called for increased investment in the Rent Control Department to strengthen its capacity to monitor landlords, enforce tenancy regulations and protect renters from excessive advance payment demands.

He warned that allowing a longer period could worsen the difficulties facing tenants, particularly those who struggle to raise large sums before securing accommodation.

Landlords defend proposal

For his part, Emmanuel Preko-Boamah, representing the national secretariat of the Voice of Landlords Association in Ghana, said rent regulations must also recognise the financial obligations property owners face.

He argued that the cost of constructing, financing and maintaining residential properties should be taken into account in any review of the law.

Mr Preko-Boamah also appealed to the government to reduce or absorb some of the administrative charges landlords incur when accessing services from the Rent Control Department.

The debate highlights the competing concerns of property owners seeking to recover their investments and tenants struggling with the high upfront cost of securing accommodation.

For now, the proposed 12-month limit remains subject to further consideration and approval, while the existing six-month restriction under Act 220 remains the applicable legal requirement.

Ghana News.title: Raya to miss Dortmund game but injury ‘not serious’
Ghana News.content:
Arsenal goalkeeper David Raya's shoulder injury "doesn't look too serious", but he will miss Tuesday's Champions League against Borussia Dortmund, says Mikel Arteta.

Raya was helped off the pitch in the 70th minute of Arsenal's 2-2 draw at Newcastle on Saturday.

He hurt his left shoulder while claiming a cross and making contact with Newcastle forward William Osula.

"We need some more tests [on Tuesday] but it is quite encouraging," said Gunners boss Arteta.

"He is not fit [to face Dortmund] but it doesn't look too serious."

Arteta said that while the incident looked pretty innocuous the pain his keeper was in made him fear it was a serious injury.

"With the pain that he was showing immediately after the action we were all quite worried but it seems to be better than what we expected," said Arteta.

"When you look at the action it doesn't seem to be much but the extent of the pain that he had and how he was struggling, it was quite worrying.

"We expected something much worse because he could almost not handle the amount of pain he had in that moment.

"The first tests that we have done have shown something that is much more encouraging. He does not need to have surgery which was the worry as that would rule him out for months so let's see."

Arsenal face Borussia Dortmund, Manchester City, Brentford, Tottenham Hotspur and Real Madrid in their next tranche of matches.

And Raya is huge part of the way that Arsenal play because of his ability with the ball at his feet.

When asked if losing Raya for a long period of time would be the biggest blow to his team, Arteta said: "We have seen what David brings to the team but as well that is why we are very protective with Kepa [Arrizabalaga] and Illan [Meslier].

"Everybody needs to be ready because these things unfortunately happen and now we need to show everyone how well we are protected and the good keepers that we have in Kepa and Illan."

Ghana News.title: De Bruyne’s feelings for Man City will ‘never change’
Ghana News.content:
Kevin de Bruyne won six Premier League titles, the Champions League, two FA Cups and five League Cups during his time at Manchester City

Kevin de Bruyne says his feelings for Manchester City will "never change" even if the club are stripped of their titles after being found guilty of breaching the Premier League's financial rules.

De Bruyne, 35, enjoyed a trophy-laden decade at Etihad Stadium, lifting 16 trophies including the Treble in 2023 before leaving on a free transfer to join Napoli in 2025.

The Belgian returns to City for the second time on Tuesday when Napoli play them in the Champions League.

De Bruyne says he has "nothing but affection" for the club and that "will never change" even if City were forced to give up their domestic titles.

"Of course, it's a lot of things that's been going on, but I cannot change anything about that. I am proud of what I have done as a football player and, honestly, this is my club," he said.

"I love the owners; I have talked about a lot of stuff outside football - I have even spoken to [chairman] Khaldoon [Al Mubarak] about how to buy a club."

City deny any wrongdoing and are appealing the decision.

In September it was revealed that an independent commission found that City had arranged "sham contracts" with a number of commercial partners as part of a scheme to disguise secret funding of more than £830m.

'Everybody plays on the limits'

City await any sanctions that may be imposed following their guilty verdict, with possible punishments ranging from a hefty fine, points deductions, relegation from the Premier League and being stripped of titles.

Asserting its innocence, City said it had filed "a comprehensive body of irrefutable evidence [that] exists in support of all of its positions" on 2 October.

Sources have told BBC Sport that City were expected to claim that key sponsorship deals were funded by the Abu Dhabi government, rather than the club's owners, as part of an appeal.

Criticism of City has been intense, but De Bruyne said he can't "change anything" about people calling his former club a "disgrace".

"Of course, in life there are rules, but everybody plays on the limit, I would say, and for me, I played in between the white lines," he said.

"I don't think a lot of people will change in their mind how they view me as a player, or how we played, but everybody has their own opinion."

De Bruyne will receive a generous ovation when he returns to Etihad Stadium, having played more than 400 games for City and scoring 108 goals.

After his final home game for the club in May 2025, it was announced that a statue will be built in his honour outside the stadium.

Ghana News.title: Haruna backs GTEC’s nationwide audit of PhD programmes
Ghana News.content:
Education Minister Haruna Iddrisu has thrown his weight behind the Ghana Tertiary Education Commission’s (GTEC) nationwide assessment of PhD programmes, insisting that the exercise is necessary to safeguard academic standards and the credibility of doctoral qualifications awarded in the country.

He said Ghana’s priority should be to produce well-trained doctoral graduates rather than expand enrolment without ensuring that universities have the capacity to deliver quality training.

Mr Iddrisu made the remarks at the 2026 National Education Week and Evidence Summit in Accra on Monday, November 23, amid public criticism of GTEC Director-General, Professor Ahmed Abdulai Jinapor, over the audit and the suspension of new admissions to PhD programmes.

He explained that the assessment would provide a clearer picture of institutions running doctoral programmes, the disciplines they cover, the number of candidates they admit and the adequacy of their academic resources.

It would also help determine whether doctoral training in the country was producing the expertise needed to advance national development.

The Minister said concerns had been raised about some universities admitting large numbers of PhD candidates without sufficient qualified supervisors and the necessary resources to provide effective academic guidance.

He argued that such gaps could undermine the standard of research and the value of doctoral qualifications.

“I see he’s also come under some public criticism heavily with his audit of PhDs. What we need as a country is not quantity, but quality. To undertake an audit is only to appreciate who is being trained, where they are being trained, in which area are being trained, and how is that consistent with our national development objectives?” he said.

Mr Iddrisu further sought to allay concerns that the restrictions on new admissions amounted to an indefinite closure of doctoral programmes.

He said the current measures were linked to the assessment and should not be interpreted as a permanent ban on PhD admissions.

“It is not a ban into perpetuity. I’m sure when the audit is over, they will do what is needful and appreciate that,” he added.

The audit is part of GTEC’s broader quality assurance efforts to examine the capacity of tertiary institutions to run doctoral programmes and ensure that candidates receive the supervision and academic support required for advanced research.

The outcome is expected to inform decisions on the future operation and admission arrangements of PhD programmes across the country.

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

World.title: Russian authorities detain suspect over St. Petersburg cafe blast
World.content:
A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.
