World.title: Suspected Chinese spy balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing
World.content:
Washington —

The Chinese spy balloon that transited the US earlier this year was able to capture imagery and collect some signals intelligence from US military sites, a source familiar with the matter tells CNN.

The balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing in real time, the source said, and the US government still does not know for sure whether the Chinese government could wipe the balloon’s data as it received it. That raises questions about whether there is intelligence the balloon was able to gather that the US still doesn’t know about.

Still, the intelligence community has not been overly concerned about the information the balloon was able to gather, the person said, because it is not much more sophisticated than what Chinese satellites are able to glean as they orbit over similar locations.

A US intelligence official told CNN on Monday that “although analysis of the wreckage of the High Altitude Balloon remains ongoing, thus far, its flight over the United States does not appear to have provided critical new insights to the People’s Republic of China.”

The US also knew what the balloon’s path would be and was able to protect sensitive sites and censor some signals before the balloon was able to pick them up, officials have said.

As CNN has reported, the US intelligence community last year developed a method of tracking what it says is a fleet of these Chinese balloons operating across the globe, controlled by the Chinese military.

The FBI is still examining the balloon, but so far officials have been able to glean additional information about how the device worked, including the algorithms used for the balloon’s software and how it is powered and designed.

CNN has reached out to the National Security Council at the White House and the Pentagon for comment. NBC was first to report on the new intelligence.

Video Ad Feedback Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33 • Source: CNN Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33

The balloon first crossed into US airspace over Alaska in late January before passing through Canada and down into Montana, where it hovered for a few days, leading the US to believe it was trying to surveil sensitive military sites, like Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana. It was eventually shot down by the US off the East Coast on February 4, and the incident further escalated tensions between Washington and Beijing, including the postponement of a diplomatic visit by US Secretary of State Antony Blinken to China.

A senior State Department official said in February that, as the balloon floated across the US, it “was capable of conducting signals intelligence collection operations.”

Gen. Glen VanHerck, the commander of US Northern Command and NORAD, said at the time that the US “did not assess” that the balloon “presented a significant collection hazard beyond what already exists in actionable technical means from the Chinese.”

The surveillance program, which includes a number of similar balloons, is in part run out of the small Chinese province of Hainan, officials told CNN. The US does not know the precise size of the fleet of Chinese surveillance balloons, but sources tell CNN that the program has conducted at least two dozen missions over at least five continents in recent years.

Roughly half a dozen of those flights have been within US airspace, although not necessarily over US territory, according to one official familiar with the intelligence.

China has maintained that the balloon was actually just a weather balloon thrown off course, and the US has been assessing the possibility that it was not deliberately maneuvered into the continental US by the Chinese government, CNN has reported.

Still, China did maintain some ability to maneuver the balloon, officials believe. And once the balloon was over Montana, China appeared to take advantage of its position to loiter over sensitive sites and try to collect intelligence.

This story has been updated with additional reporting.

World.title: Beijing promised to 'fight back' over Taiwan leader's US visit. But this time it has more to lose
World.content:
Hong Kong —

An anticipated meeting between Taiwan’s President Tsai Ing-wen and US House Speaker Kevin McCarthy in California this week has sparked concerns of a repeat of the pressure campaign China launched last year when then-Speaker Nancy Pelosi visited Taipei.

At that time, Beijing encircled the island democracy with unprecedented military drills – firing multiple missiles into its surrounding waters and sending dozens of warplanes speeding across a sensitive median line dividing the Taiwan Strait.

It also cut off contact with the United States over a number of issues from military matters to combating climate change, in retaliation for what it viewed as a violation of its sovereignty.

This time, Beijing has already threatened to “resolutely fight back” if a Tsai-McCarthy meeting goes ahead.

Video Ad Feedback See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32 • Source: CNN See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32

It also slammed Washington for allowing Tsai to stopover in the US while en route to and from official visits in Central America, warning it could lead to “serious” confrontation between the two powers.

A defiant Tsai staked out her own ground, pledging as she took off on her 10-day trip not to let “external pressure” stop Taiwan from connecting with the world and like-minded democracies.

But the optics of the meeting, taking place in California and not Taiwan, and its timing – at a particularly thorny moment in China’s foreign relations and ahead of a presidential election in Taiwan that could reset the tone of its relationship with Beijing – may see Beijing tread more carefully this time, or at least not escalate further, analysts say.

“This puts the burden on China not to overreact, because any overreaction is only going to push China further away from the world,” said Yun Sun, director of the China Program at the Stimson Center think tank in Washington.

That doesn’t mean, however, that Beijing won’t be closely watching Tsai’s movements as it calibrates its response – and decides how much military might to flex over her meeting with an American lawmaker on American soil.

The opacity of China’s system – and the potential for competing interests within its vast bureaucracy – also make it difficult to accurately predict its response.

“Every time Taiwan does anything that China doesn’t like, the Chinese react with their own military coercion,” Sun said. But in the current situation, “they have to consider the consequences of overreaction,” she added.

House Speaker Kevin McCarthy talks to reporters at the Capitol in Washington on March 24, 2023. J. Scott Applewhite/AP

Rising pressure

The expected meeting, which McCarthy’s office announced earlier this week would take place on Wednesday, also comes at a precarious moment in US-China relations.

Washington and Beijing are struggling to stabilize their communication amid flaring tensions over issues from a downed suspected Chinese surveillance balloon to semiconductor supply chains – raising the stakes of potential damage to that relationship if Beijing lashes out as it did when Tsai met Pelosi.

Taiwan is still feeling the fallout of that response last August, with Chinese military forces now regularly making incursions over what had previously been an informal but largely respected border of control between Beijing and Taipei in the Taiwan Strait. Taiwan’s official Central News Agency also reported Monday that Tsai would meet with McCarthy, citing Tsai’s presidential office.

Video Ad Feedback See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05 • Source: CNN See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05

But a meeting between Tsai and the leader of the Republican majority in the US House of Representatives, who ranks second in line to the Presidency, would mark another symbolic moment for Taiwan and the US, which only maintain unofficial ties.

For Tsai, who is entering the final year of her two-term presidency, “it’s clearly a capstone event,” according to Wen-Ti Sung, a political scientist at the Australian National University’s Taiwan Studies Program. “She has this image as the Taiwanese president who has taken US-Taiwan relations to new heights, and who … has been able to give Taiwan almost unprecedented international visibility,” he said.

That increased visibility – and enhanced cooperation with the US – has followed China’s mounting pressure on the island, which sits fewer than 110 miles (177 kilometers) from the mainland coast.

China’s Communist Party claims the self-governing island democracy as its own despite never having controlled it, and has vowed to take the island, by force if necessary.

The party has undertaken a sweeping expansion of its military capabilities over the past decade under leader Xi Jinping – and ramped up its pervasive economic, diplomatic and military pressure on Taiwan.

That’s driven concerns, among some in Washington, that Beijing is preparing for an invasion, though China’s official language still suggests that scenario is not its preferred option for achieving the claimed goal of “reunification.”

It is those pressures – and how to support Taiwan against unilateral actions by Beijing – that are likely to be on the table when Tsai, McCarthy and a bipartisan group of US lawmakers sit down on Wednesday.

Congress has been a pillar of increasing American support for Taiwan in recent years. Lawmakers regularly visit the island and drive bipartisan legislation enhancing support and cooperation.

While the US switched its diplomatic relations to Beijing decades ago, it maintains unofficial ties with Taiwan and is bound by law to provide the democratic island with the means to defend itself.

Under Washington’s longstanding “One China” policy, the US acknowledges China’s position that Taiwan is part of China, but has never officially recognized Beijing’s claim to the island of 23 million.

Though McCarthy does not have Pelosi’s decades-long record of advocacy regarding China, the California Republican is now a leading voice pushing for closer scrutiny of Beijing, and meeting Tsai could help him to burnish that image.

Last month, McCarthy told reporters that meeting Tsai in the US would not impact whether he travels to Taiwan in the future – something he had earlier said he wanted to do.

Fighter jets of the Chinese People's Liberation Army Eastern Theater Command conduct joint combat training exercises around Taiwan on August 7, 2022 in this photo released by Xinhua News Agency. Gong Yulong/Xinhua/AP

Beijing watching

A meeting in California, on US soil, is widely seen as less likely to provoke Beijing than a McCarthy visit to Taiwan.

Pelosi’s trip – the first from a lawmaker of that rank to the island in 25 years – generated a fever pitch of nationalist and anti-US rhetoric in mainland China.

This time, so far, domestic conversation in China’s heavily controlled media sphere has been significantly muted.

But the stakes remain high – including for Beijing itself – over how it responds, analysts say.

As Taiwan prepares for a presidential election in January, a fierce response could push voters away from Taiwan’s main opposition party Kuomintang (KMT), widely seen as more friendly toward Beijing.

It could also jar with another high profile trip happening now: a tour of mainland China from former Taiwan president and senior KMT member Ma Ying-jeou, the first visit from a current or former Taiwan leader since the end of the Chinese Civil War in 1949.

Ma’s tour is a “once in a half a century opportunity to send a conciliatory message between the two sides, Beijing shouldn’t want to tank that,” said Sung, the political scientist.

China is also acutely aware that its actions toward Taiwan are under a significantly brighter global spotlight following the invasion of Ukraine by Russian President Vladimir Putin, a close diplomatic partner of Xi. Putin’s rhetoric over Ukraine has echoes of how Xi speaks of Taiwan.

Beijing has recently sought to position itself as an agent of peace in that conflict – especially as it aims to repair frayed ties with Europe.

This week, as Tsai is expected to meet with McCarthy, French President Emmanuel Macron and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen will head to China – an important opportunity that Xi may not want to overshadow with military posturing.

An aggressive response also risks stoking confrontation with the US, not yet six months after Xi and US President Joe Biden called to enhance communication during a face-to-face meeting in Bali.

“(A less overtly aggressive response) would imply that Beijing does not wish to escalate tension with the US to a level that can risk getting out of hand,” said Steve Tsang, director of the SOAS China Institute in London.

“A reset in US-China ties is not on the agenda, but an easing of tension is not beyond the realm of possibility.”

World.title: What Nvidia’s Jensen Huang’s return means for Washington and Wall Street?
World.content:
Share What Nvidia’s Jensen Huang’s return means for Washington and Wall Street? on social media

Nvidia founder Jensen Huang’s dramatic return to the helm of the world’s most valuable chipmaker, less than two weeks after his resignation, has sent the company’s stock soaring.

At the same time, the White House’s involvement in his reinstatement has raised questions about Silicon Valley’s growing sway in Washington, with United States President Donald Trump claiming to have been a linchpin in the decision.

What happened?

The saga began less than two weeks ago when Huang resigned amid reports of extramarital affairs, including with Alice Huang, a woman alleged to be a Chinese spy.

Beijing has denied that Alice Huang is a spy. She previously led Megaspeed, a company that had a business relationship with Nvidia, the Santa Clara, California-based tech giant.

Nvidia’s board had begun an investigation into the allegations, but Huang resigned before it reached a conclusion.

In his absence, Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress took over as interim chief executive while the board searched for a permanent successor.

However, Huang’s departure quickly prompted a backlash from influential figures in Silicon Valley. A petition calling for his reinstatement attracted more than 180,000 signatures, including that of SpaceX CEO Elon Musk.

Analysts also warned that losing Huang could significantly undermine Nvidia’s market value. Dan Ives, managing partner at Yorkville Ives, estimated that Huang’s departure could wipe as much as 30 percent off the company’s valuation.

By Monday, Nvidia brought Huang back to lead the company.



“The Board believes Jensen is the right person to lead NVIDIA, and that his reinstatement is in the best interests of our stockholders, employees, partners and customers,” said Harvey C Jones, chair of the board, in a news statement. That was an about-face from just a few days ago when the board ruled out bringing back Huang.

“I am honored to return to NVIDIA and lead one of the most consequential technology companies in the world at the beginning of a new industrial revolution,” Huang added.

How has the Trump administration been involved?

Trump said on Monday that he played a central role in Huang’s reinstatement, saying in social media posts and in an interview with CNBC that his intervention had been instrumental in the board’s decision.

Trump said he had participated in the board meeting, following efforts by influential Silicon Valley figures to persuade the president to intervene in the leadership crisis, which analysts say lacked a clear succession plan.

Trump told CNBC that the stock market reaction to Huang’s resignation from Nvidia “probably” factored into his decision to push for the CEO’s reinstatement, although his view of the long-term benefit of having Huang at the helm of the company was the bigger weight, the Reuters news agency reported.

“I think this move is unprecedented in the sense that a sitting president has exerted very public pressure on a corporate board to make a particular decision,” Aleksandar Tomic, associate dean for strategy, innovation and technology at Boston College, told Al Jazeera.

Corporate governance experts say greater transparency is needed about the extent of Trump’s involvement in Nvidia’s leadership decisions.

“A board can take input from [the] government; what it should not do is let any outside party choose the CEO without explaining to shareholders why,” Martin Mulyadi, professor of accounting at Shenandoah University’s College of Business, Engineering & Technology, told Al Jazeera.

The intervention comes amid divisions within the Trump administration over Nvidia’s business practices and its relationship with China.

The Department of Justice (DOJ) and Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) continue to investigate the company, and Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has emerged as one of its most vocal critics.

Bessent has questioned whether Nvidia facilitated chip sales to China to bolster its financial performance, alleging in an interview with Fox News that the AI chip giant had engaged in “seemingly illicit sales to goose their revenues and their earnings”.



He has also called for Nvidia to appoint a new chief executive from outside the company.

Meanwhile, Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick faces allegations that he delayed restrictions on Nvidia chip sales to China, raising questions about whether his decisions were influenced by the financial interests of his former firm, Cantor Fitzgerald, which is now controlled by his two sons.

Democratic lawmakers are seeking to determine whether the firm’s holdings or business relationships benefitted from the Commerce Department’s failure to impose those restrictions.

“The key issue is how much of Nvidia’s revenue may be coming from sales that would not pass increased scrutiny vis-a-vis export control violations. Given accusations within the government of lax monitoring and enforcement, it is also not clear that Nvidia had robust controls, and their inability to stick to the CEO decision makes it doubtful that they will be able to implement it in the future,” Tomic said.

What precedent does the decision set?

Trump’s involvement has also raised broader questions about the relationship between the federal government and corporate America, particularly the extent to which a president should influence decisions traditionally reserved for a company’s board of directors.

Tomic says that the level of direct pressure Trump placed on Nvidia’s board, including his participation in discussions about Huang’s reinstatement, is highly unusual for a sitting president.

The precedent could ultimately backfire on Republicans, Tomic warned, particularly as Democrats prepare to take control of both the House and Senate in January. Democrats have historically pushed for greater oversight of large corporations, and the incoming Congress could seek to exercise similar influence over corporate decision-making.

“I think that Nvidia will invite much stronger government scrutiny, especially with Congress and the new administration in 2028, as they have shown a complete lack of capacity for self-governance,” Tomic said.

Nvidia’s board’s decision to reinstate Huang could have lasting implications for corporate accountability, particularly in Silicon Valley, where investors frequently place enormous value on the leadership of company founders, Tomic added.

Huang’s reinstatement could reinforce the perception that prominent technology executives are indispensable to their companies, potentially making it more difficult to hold them accountable for personal or professional misconduct, he said.

“It is hard to imagine any other industry where this would happen. The attitude of immunity and idolatry of tech founders is grating on voters and is one of the reasons for the electoral outcome. This is an unforced error, as Huang could have stayed substantially involved at Nvidia in a much less public way,” Tomic added.

How have markets reacted?

Wall Street welcomed the news of Huang’s return, sending Nvidia shares soaring approximately 31 percent in early trading on Monday. The stock maintained much of those gains throughout the session.



The rally extended beyond Nvidia, helping lift broader US stock markets, with all three major indices finishing the trading day in positive territory.

The tech-heavy Nasdaq 100 rose nearly 7 percent, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average gained 3 percent and the S&P 500 climbed 4.7 percent.

Other major technology companies also benefitted from the rally. Shares of rival chipmaker Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) jumped 6.85 percent, while Microsoft gained 1.65 percent and Alphabet rose 5.8 percent.

Why does this decision matter for the broader markets?

Nvidia has taken an outsized role in the broader markets. As of October, the tech giant accounted for 8.1 percent of the Nasdaq 100 index.

According to an analysis by The Wall Street Journal, Nvidia has amassed investments worth more than $100bn, including more than $48bn in shares of eight publicly traded companies, citing SEC filings.

Among those holdings is a 10 percent stake in CoreWeave, a cloud-computing company that operates data centres. CoreWeave shares surged 22 percent following news of Huang’s reinstatement.

Nvidia has broader connections to other companies.

In late August, Amazon announced plans to deploy an additional two million Nvidia graphics processing units (GPUs) through its cloud-computing division, Amazon Web Services, in 2027 and 2028. That commitment followed a previously announced deployment of more than one million GPUs in March.

Nvidia has also deepened its financial ties to Anthropic, committing $10bn to buy shares in the AI company’s blockbuster initial public offering on US markets late last week.

World.title: Trump postpones US Army plan to detonate toxic explosives in Iowa
World.content:
NewsFeed Trump postpones US Army plan to detonate toxic explosives in Iowa

President Trump has further postponed the US Army’s planned detonation of nearly five tonnes of lead azide in Iowa after a court suspended its environmental permit, saying the operation will depend on reaching an agreement with the state’s incoming governor.

World.title: US escalates sanctions on Iran, targets ‘shadow banking’ networks
World.content:
US Treasury sanctions more than two dozen Iranian entities, citing efforts to disrupt Tehran’s global financial activities, amid ongoing diplomatic effort to end the US-Israel war on Iran.

The United States has launched another wave of sanctions against Iran under its Operation Economic Outcast, a move that comes shortly after US President Donald Trump threatened renewed military action next year.

The Department of the Treasury announced on Monday that it had targeted more than two dozen Iranian exchange houses, front companies, and key personnel with sanctions “in a sweeping effort to disrupt Iran’s global shadow banking networks”.

“Iran’s shadow banking system is the last financial lifeline of a bankrupt regime,” said US Secretary of the Treasury Scott Bessent.

The US Treasury claimed these entities help Iran “move billions of dollars through the international financial system to provide the regime access to foreign currency despite comprehensive sanctions”.

Bessent also vowed the “Treasury will continue dismantling these illicit networks until we have buried the head of the snake.”

The Central Bank of Iran oversees the designated entities, according to the statement.

The designated entities include an Iran-based company named “Rahbar Bazargani Nesim Baharan Qeshm Company (Nesim Baharan)”, which the Treasury claims worked closely with Iranian exchange houses and their front companies to facilitate transactions on behalf of Sarmayeh Bank’s Iranian clients, which include major Iranian petrochemical companies.

In addition, “Mina Fashki and Partners Exchange Company (Fashki Exchange) and Mellat Exchange Company” and a number of their owners and employees were designated.



The US claimed earlier this month that its sanctions campaign had pushed Iran’s rial to new lows and driven inflation to about 90 percent.

AP reported that Iran’s Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said Tehran still hoped diplomacy could end its nine-month war with the US, while President Trump said Iran wanted a deal, but one that was not acceptable to him.

Fox News said Trump told its chief foreign correspondent that he was “inclined to order military strikes against Iran after the new year if the two countries fail to reach an agreement”.

The remarks came as diplomatic efforts continued to end a conflict that has destabilised the Middle East, disrupted shipping, driven up global energy prices, and drawn in countries across the region.

World.title: Israel’s southern Syria incursion triggers fear and destruction
World.content:
NewsFeed Israel’s southern Syria incursion triggers fear and destruction

Families in Koya have been shot at in their homes, had their houses set on fire, and been forced to flee after Israeli military incursions in southern Syria. Al Jazeera’s Obaida Hitto speaks to residents affected by the expanding invasion.

World.title: US states sue SpaceX over Grok AI’s creation of child sexual abuse material
World.content:
The US states of Virginia and Oregon have sued Elon Musk’s SpaceX, saying the business harmed consumers by avoiding safeguards when it designed and launched an artificial intelligence chatbot capable of creating sexualised images.

The attorneys general of both states filed complaints in separate lawsuits on Monday.

Several states had announced investigations into Grok over similar claims in recent months, but Virginia and Oregon are the first states to sue.

The lawsuits filed in state courts accuse SpaceX of misleading consumers about Grok’s safety and failing to put adequate safeguards in place while promoting its “spicy mode”. The feature allows users to take an existing photograph of a person and generate a sexual or nude image or video, according to the lawsuits.

The company prioritised its business model over the safety of millions of people, Virginia Attorney General Jay Jones said in his state’s lawsuit.

“To push its lagging product, Grok, to tens of millions of new users, it stripped out industry-standard safeguards and marketed a ‘spicy mode’ built to produce nudity,” Jones said in the lawsuit. “For these Defendants, weak safeguards were not a failure but a feature.”

Virginia and Oregon accused SpaceX of violating their respective consumer protection laws. They are seeking damages, penalties and court orders forcing the company to stop violating state law.

SpaceX did not immediately respond to requests for comment. Grok is available to users of X, the social media platform that is a subsidiary of SpaceX.



In a statement posted on X on Monday that did not directly address the lawsuits, the platform’s safety team said it had taken action to block prompts that could generate sexualised or nude imagery and worked with law enforcement to pursue people who use the platform to make it.

“The people who tried to use Grok Imagine to generate this material did so by deliberately violating our Terms of Service and working aggressively to circumvent our safeguards,” the company posted.

Virginia’s lawsuit cites data from a study by the Center for Countering Digital Hate, which estimated that between December 2025 and January 2026, Grok generated and posted millions of sexualised images on X, including more than 20,000 depicting children.

Investigators from the attorney general’s office in Virginia found that Grok’s image moderation was inconsistent, and that the bot would advise users on how to circumvent the moderation measures by avoiding words that triggered it, according to the lawsuit.

Beginning in January, Grok told users that its image generation features were only for paying subscribers, which did not stop the images’ creation but allowed the company to profit from them, the lawsuit said.

SpaceX is facing more than a dozen lawsuits brought by individuals who say nonconsensual sexual images of them as minors or adults were generated by Grok.

World.title: US drug prices leave patients facing impossible choices
World.content:
Despite working and having health insurance, some of the country’s sickest patients have trouble affording the medicines they need.

Sarah Wisniewski and her sister were once contemplating an extraordinary arrangement to manage their shared multiple sclerosis (MS) diagnoses: alternating months taking a life-changing medication.

The drug, which Wisniewski says costs thousands of dollars a month without insurance coverage, was so expensive that the sisters considered rationing their treatment rather than going without it entirely.

“It’s a weird thing to have to think about,” the 45-year-old told Al Jazeera. “You go to college, you get insurance, you get a good job, you pay your bills, you do everything right and, still, you’re having to ration your medication.”

Wisniewski is one of more than four in 10 adults in the United States who did not take medication as prescribed last year because of the cost, estimates KFF, an independent health policy research organisation.

Her experience highlights the growing financial pressures facing some of the nation’s sickest patients, who have trouble affording costly prescription medications, despite having jobs and private health insurance.

‘Every spare dime’ needed for medications

Wisniewski was diagnosed with MS in 2017 after experiencing increasingly debilitating symptoms, including difficulties with her vision, mobility and breathing.

She became one of the nearly eight in 10 American adults who are living with at least one chronic condition, according to the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC).

In the summer of 2024, her neurologist prescribed Kesimpta, a medication that, she says, dramatically improved her condition. But her insurance company, Blue Cross Blue Shield, notified her it would not cover the treatment.



Wisniewski appealed three times before requesting a hearing in her state of Maryland. Only weeks before that hearing was due to take place did her insurer agree to cover the medication.

Without that intervention, Wisniewski said, she would have faced a monthly bill of approximately $10,000.

The impact of obtaining treatment has been significant on her life.

“I went from barely being able to walk … Now, I walk my dog every morning, a mile-and-a-half to two miles,” she said.

Wisniewski has also been able to maintain her federal contracting job, which she described as highly technical and demanding.

But the financial burden remains substantial. Even with the help of insurance, Wisniewski estimates she spends between $800 and $900 each month on medication.

“Almost every spare dime I get is going to just keeping me healthy, so I can make it to work the next day,” she said.

‘A uniquely American problem’

Unlike many countries, particularly wealthier ones, the US allows pharmaceutical companies significantly more latitude to set their own prices.

According to the Patients For Affordable Drugs Now patient-advocacy organisation, current laws give manufacturers “unilateral power to set launch prices in the US and the ability to raise prices at will”.

“I believe this is a uniquely American problem, ”Wisniewski said. “Other countries are … able to provide for their citizens these drugs, if not for free, at an affordable level.”

The monthly cost of her medication in Canada is 2,333 Canadian dollars ($1,623). It’s even lower in Australia at 41 Australian dollars ($27) or 6.60 Australian dollars ($4.37) with a concession card, which allows eligible residents in the country to receive discounts on healthcare and prescription medicines.

The Pharmaceutical Research and Manufacturers of America (PhRMA), a consortium that represents US drug companies, argues that a complicated network of third-party middlemen, known as pharmacy benefit managers (PBMs), and insurance companies are to blame for the country’s high drug prices.

“PBMs and insurers control benefits through processes like prior authorisation, embedded step therapy, and formulary controls that may allow PBMs and insurers to deny coverage or push patients to alternative treatments from the initially prescribed medicine,” PhRMA’s website said. The organisation did not reply to a request for comment.

A study by the nonpartisan RAND organisation, released in 2024, found that US prescription drug prices were substantially higher than those in other wealthy countries, particularly for name-brand medications.



Using 2022 data, RAND’s researchers found that US manufacturers’ gross prices across all prescription drugs were 278 percent higher than the average prices in 33 other high-income countries. For brand-name drugs, US prices were more than four times the comparison-country average.

But the consequences of the current US system can extend far beyond the cost of individual prescriptions.

Wisniewski said the money she spends maintaining access to medication is money she cannot put toward local businesses, transportation or investments in her community.

“I really think that a lot of people, at an abstract level, understand that this could happen to anybody at any point in time,” she said. “But I don’t think that it really hits home to folks that you are legitimately one bad phone call away from losing everything.”

What can be done?

After this month’s historic midterm elections in the US, where Democrats won control of both chambers in the US Congress by wide margins, there will be few areas of agreement with Democrats’ Republican counterparts – and President Donald Trump.

But targeted reforms that address the high cost of prescriptions could be an area where both parties find common ground.

A survey conducted by Fabrizio Ward in March 2025 found more than three in four voters – including 70 percent of Trump supporters – wanted Congress to take action on reducing drug prices.

The issue was the focus of a US Senate Judiciary Committee hearing on Tuesday of last week, when lawmakers and healthcare experts examined how pharmaceutical companies and insurers influence pricing and access to medication.

At that November 17 hearing, witnesses highlighted several factors contributing to high prescription drug costs, including pharmaceutical patent protections and the role of PBMs.

Merith Basey, chief executive officer of Patients For Affordable Drugs Now, argued that pharmaceutical companies exploit the patent system to delay competition from cheaper alternatives.

One of those practices, known as patent thicketing, involves companies securing multiple patents covering different aspects of a medication or its delivery device, potentially making it more difficult for competitors to introduce generic alternatives.

Basey told lawmakers the introduction of generic competition could substantially reduce prices, arguing a single generic competitor can lower a drug’s price by 39 percent, while six or more competitors can reduce prices by as much as 95 percent.

But other witnesses pointed to PBMs, claiming their involvement in distributing drugs can influence pricing.

The Senate panel has advanced a number of proposals to tackle the high cost of prescription drugs in the US. One of those is the bipartisan Eliminating Thickets to Improve Competition (ETHIC) Act, which would limit the practice of patent thickening, making it easier for generic drugs to enter the US market and lower costs.

“Big Pharma knows exactly what it’s doing in monopolising the US patent system: driving up drug costs for Americans while preventing generic-drug manufacturers from getting their foot in the market,” Republican Senator Josh Hawley of Missouri, one of the bill’s sponsors, said in a statement.



Wisniewski noted that while the ETHIC Act wouldn’t make her prescription “cheap”, it would be “astronomically better than what we have now”.

World.title: Iran flogs singer Parastoo Ahmadi for performing without headscarf
World.content:
Ahmadi and four production team members also face two-year bans on travel and artistic activity.

Iran has flogged a singer and her production team after they were convicted of “offending public decency”, according to local media.

The sentence of 74 lashes handed down to Parastoo Ahmadi and four members of her team was carried out in the city of Qom on Monday, the singer’s lawyer Mostafa Nili told the Emtedad news website.

A court in the city had sentenced the quintet in June. They were convicted of “producing and publishing obscene and immoral content online” over a video showing Ahmadi performing without wearing the mandatory hijab alongside male musicians.

The video was posted on YouTube in December 2024. In addition to the flogging, the five were banned for two years from taking part in artistic and musical activities and leaving Iran.

Western governments and human rights groups have condemned flogging as a form of torture that violates international law.

Iran rejects criticism of its human rights record and says Western countries should address abuses of their own.

Iran’s mandatory hijab rules became a focal point of protests in 2022 after Mahsa Amini, a Kurdish Iranian woman, died in custody following her arrest for allegedly violating the dress code.

More women have since defied the rules in Tehran and elsewhere in Iran, while authorities have enforced them more selectively.

World.title: Iran hits US bases and civilian sites in the Gulf after a lull
World.content:
Tehran has ramped up attacks in recent days as the US naval blockade and sanctions campaign hurt the country.

After a relative lull in its conflict with the United States, Iran is striking US assets in Gulf countries again. Civilian facilities have been damaged.

Is Iran just tightening its grip on the global economy?

Can Tehran force the White House to ease its economic blockade?

And could this revive a full-scale conflict?

Presenter: Rob Matheson

Guests:

Ali Akbar Dareini — Researcher at the Center for Strategic Studies

Barbara Slavin — Distinguished Fellow at the Stimson Center

Mehran Kamrava — Professor of Government at Georgetown University in Qatar

World.title: US to blacklist Asian AI firm Megaspeed after Nvidia scandal
World.content:
The US has said it intends to ban a Singaporean artificial intelligence (AI) company allegedly tied to the Nvidia scandal from doing business in America.

The Department of Commerce announced it planned to add Megaspeed Ltd to a list of entities that are blacklisted from buying or selling goods in the US.

The company is mainly a developer of data centres, but in recent weeks a former executive of Megaspeed was accused of working as spy for China while having a romantic relationship with Nvidia head Jensen Huang.

The relationship led to additional scrutiny by US officials and heightened concern that Megaspeed was funnelling Nvidia's advanced AI computer chips to China.

When exactly the ban against Megaspeed will go into effect was not specified in the commerce department announcement. The BBC has asked the agency for comment, along with the White House and Megaspeed.

Megaspeed was not well known within the US until last month when media reports emerged that a former Megaspeed executive, Alice Huang, had an affair with Jensen Huang.

Alice Huang (no relation) was thought by US intelligence to be working as an asset for Beijing, creating national security concerns within the US.

China has denied that she is a spy and warned the US not to use the scandal as a "pretext for imposing a technological blockade" on AI technology.

On 12 November, Jensen Huang resigned after allegations he had had another affair, this one with a Nvidia employee.

On Monday, Nvidia's board reinstated him after US President Donald Trump said he had "convinced" the company and "made the deal".

The commerce department has said it had been investigating Megaspeed for almost two years.

The department said it had suspected the company was violating US export controls by helping to get Nvidia's chips into the hands of companies within China.

China has been blocked from buying such technology since 2022.

Although based in Singapore, Megaspeed has significant business dealings in China.

Alibaba, for instance, the major Chinese online retailer, is its largest customer.

Megaspeed was a known buyer of billions of dollars of Nvidia computer chips, including through its subsidiary Speedmatrix, which has also been added to the Commerce blacklist.

Nvidia's computer chips, originally designed for use in gaming consols, in recent years have become crucial to the continued growth of the AI industry.

Without enough supply or access to computer chips that are capable of processing the huge amount of data needed to make things like AI chatbots and models run, AI companies will not be able to meet or grow demand from people using AI tools.

That has driven up the value of Nvidia on the stock market, as well as its influence in the AI industry and the White House.

Although tech stocks have in recent months been volatile and trending lower, when Jensen Huang resigned as CEO of Nvidia because of his affairs, the company's stock fell by more than 30%.

Anxiety about the company's influence and ability to operate within the AI ecosystem without its famed executive appeared to take down shares of other tech companies, too.

Huang was reinstated on Monday to his position as head of Nvidia, a move that US President Donald Trump said he told the company's board to take.

The company's stock rallied on his reinstatement, as did several other tech stocks, but shares of Nvidia did not climb to where the company had been before being immersed in scandal.

In the weeks ahead, Huang and the company he now runs again are facing multiple government agency investigations.

Huang and the chief legal officer of Nvidia are set to appear next for a closed-door briefing with the House Foreign Affairs Committee.

World.title: Russian warship hit by Ukrainian drones in Libya, Zelensky says
World.content:
A Russian warship was sunk by Ukrainian drones at a port in Libya on Sunday, President Volodymyr Zelensky has said.

There was an explosion on the warship at the Benghazi naval base in the early morning, while it was docking for fuel and supplies ahead of its return to Russia, local authorities said.

Zelensky added that Ukraine's attack hit a second Russian vessel, a cargo ship which he claimed was being used to transport weapons.

The local health ministry said it had received injured people from a commercial ship that was targeted off the coast of the port. It is not clear whether this is the same vessel as the one Ukraine has claimed responsibility for.

Following the strikes, the Kremlin warned of an "escalation of tensions in the region", but declined to comment directly on the attacks in Libya.

Libya's two governments - the UN-recognised government in the capital, Tripoli, and a rival administration in the east - have both condemned the attack.

The Tripoli foreign ministry said the country would not accept being drawn into the conflict.

It said foreign forces would not be allowed to use Libyan ports and civilian infrastructure for military purposes.

The eastern government, based in Benghazi, called it a violation of maritime safety and an attack on their sovereignty.

Seven naval drones were deployed to target and sink the corvette Merkury, one of Russia's newest ships, Zelensky said in a statement on Monday. He added that a Ka-27 combat helicopter was also destroyed.

The Ukrainian president said the second ship was the MV ANGARA, a Russian container carrier.

The attack came the day after a Russian cargo vessel was hit by a drone attack in the eastern Gulf of Finland. The Sparta II had been bound for Russia's Baltic exclave Kaliningrad when it was hit on Saturday morning.

Finnish defence forces said Ukraine was likely to be behind the attack. Kyiv has not commented.

Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov told reporters on Monday that the "expansion of terrorist activity in the Baltic" was a "dangerous trend" and has said "it is, of course, leading to an escalation of tensions in the region."

When questioned over the attacks in Libya, Peskov said information would be provided by the country's defence ministry and added: "We paid attention to Zelensky's statements about it".

Peskov declined to comment on the strikes on Russian ships in Libya and said that that information would be provided by Russia's Defence Ministry.

The UN mission in Libya expressed "serious concern" over the attacks on Sunday, calling for "an immediate, independent and transparent investigation".

"Libya cannot afford, and must not become a battleground for foreign conflicts," the UNSMIL wrote on X., external

Videos posted on social media and geolocated by BBC Verify show the ship that was struck in the morning engulfed in flames and smoke. Satellite imagery from Planet Labs PBC also shows a boat on fire at 05:47 GMT at the Benghazi port.

World.title: What strike on Russian ship in Libya says about spread of Ukraine war
World.content:
Anchored in a Mediterranean harbour nearly 2,000 miles from Moscow, the Captain of Russia's corvette Merkury might well have thought his ship was safe from attack. It wasn't.

The audacious and successful night-time attack in Benghazi, co-ordinated by Ukraine's SBU intelligence agency and its armed forces, has raised the obvious question: is the Ukraine war spreading well beyond its borders?

The answer is yes, in fact, it was already spreading. But this attack, which Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelensky called "an exemplary operation" will inevitably raise the stakes another notch.

Russia, which is currently engaged in a non-stop campaign to batter Ukraine's civilian population into submission with daily missile and drone strikes, has called it "a dangerous escalation".

It follows the suspected Ukrainian drone attack on a Russian dry-cargo ship in the Gulf of Finland at the weekend, which the Kremlin described as an act of terrorism.

Ukraine's long-range drones have also previously struck Russia's Baltic oil terminal at Ust-Luga.

Some of Ukraine's more audacious long-range drone attacks â what Zelensky likes to call "long-range sanctions" â have also struck targets thousands of kilometres beyond Ukraine's borders with Russia, deep inside Siberia.

The most notable of these was last year's Operation Spider's Web, which involved a specially adapted lorry that drove close to a Russian strategic nuclear bomber airbase and released a "swarm" of explosive drones that damaged or destroyed several expensive bombers.

And Ukraine has also been active further south in Africa where its forces have targeted Russian mercenaries from the Africa Corps, the successor to the infamous Wagner Group that was accused of carrying out numerous human rights abuses.

It's not just Russia that will be alarmed by this latest Ukrainian operation in Benghazi harbour. The United Nations mission in Libya has already expressed its "deep concern".

Libyan officials point out that their country is not a party to the Russia-Ukraine war, although the Merkury and an accompanying cargo ship that was also hit were berthed in the eastern part of Libya controlled by the pro-Moscow warlord and self-styled "Field Marshal" Khalifa Haftar.

World.title: Iranian authorities flog singer who performed without hijab, lawyers say
World.content:
A prominent singer who performed without the mandatory hijab and four members of her band and production team have been flogged by Iranian authorities, lawyers say.

Parastoo Ahmadi, three musicians and a producer were each given 74 lashes in the city of Qom, a member of their defence team told the BBC.

Ahmadi, 29, wore a sleeveless dress during a concert that was livestreamed in December 2024. Iran's laws ban public performances by women and require them to wear headscarves and modest clothing.

This June, a criminal court in Qom convicted Ahmadi and eight others of "offending public decency" through the publication of "obscene and indecent material", which they had denied.

In addition to being sentenced to 74 lashes, they were banned from audiovisual activities and from leaving the country for two years.

At the end of September, an appeals court in Qom rejected the defendants' appeal and confirmed the sentence, her lawyers said.

There was widespread condemnation of the sentences from other Iranian artists and human rights activists, who warned that flogging constituted cruel, inhuman and degrading punishment, and violated the international prohibition on torture.

On Monday, one of the defendants' lawyers told the BBC that Ahmadi and four of her male co-defendants had been flogged at the third branch of the Criminal Sentence Enforcement Office in Qom.

"We did everything in our power to have the verdict overturned, or at least to secure a reduction in the sentence or a suspension, but it didn't work out," he said.

"The other lawyers and I even tried to get the enforcement of the sentence postponed, but the enforcement branch insisted on carrying it out immediately."

Pro-reform daily Etemad cited another defence lawyer, Mostafa Nili, as identifying the four men flogged alongside Ahmadi as Soheil Faghih-Nasiri, Amin Taheri, Amirali Pirnia and Mohsen Lashkari.

"Parastoo Ahmadi's flogging for singing and dressing as she chooses is a flagrant violation of her fundamental rights and a chilling demonstration of the Iranian authorities' determination to suppress women's freedoms and to violently punish anyone who dares to challenge their discriminatory laws and policies," said Bahar Ghandehari, director of advocacy at the US-based Center for Human Rights in Iran (CHRI).

Under Iranian law, which is based on the country's interpretation of Sharia, women and girls above the age of puberty must cover their hair with a hijab and wear long, loose-fitting clothing to disguise their figures.

In 2022, protests swept across the Islamic Republic following the death in custody of Mahsa Amini, a 22-year-old Kurdish woman who was detained by morality police in Tehran in September that year for allegedly wearing her hijab "improperly".

Women burnt their headscarves or waved them in the air at the nationwide demonstrations against the clerical establishment, during which hundreds of people were killed in a crackdown by security forces.

Since then, many women and girls have stopped covering their hair in public altogether in open defiance of the dress code. Authorities have responded with periodic waves of arrests, warnings, business closures and other measures.

In January this year, thousands of people were killed and tens of thousands were arrested when security forces crushed another wave of mass anti-establishment protests, this time sparked by the country's economic crisis.

Since the start of Iran's war with the US and Israel in late February, authorities have intensified their use of the death penalty against protesters.

According to the Norway-based group Iran Human Rights, at least 39 men convicted over January's protests and two convicted over the 2022 unrest have been executed, along with 16 people allegedly affiliated with banned opposition groups and 17 others convicted of espionage or collaborating with foreign states.

Another 121 protesters detained in January, including six women and five juvenile offenders, have been sentenced to death and are at imminent risk of execution, it says.

World.title: What failure of COP31 reveals about a divided world
World.content:
Some may have found it ironic that the world's biggest conference on climate change should collapse over the very mention of fossil fuels - the main cause of global warming.

Yet that is what happened in Antalya, Turkey, on Sunday.

The failure tells us something about the state of climate diplomacy. But it may tell us even more about the increasingly divided world in which the negotiations take place.

Chris Bowen, the Australian minister who led the negotiations, spoke of a backdrop constituting "the most complicated and fraught geopolitical environment in living memory". The competing demands, he said, had become "unbridgeable red lines".

Murat Kurum, Turkey's environment minister and the summit's president, was blunter. Governments should not disappoint people desperate for climate action, he suggested, by getting "hung up on one word or phrase".

And Kurum had a point. Three years ago, at COP28 in Dubai, there was agreement to transition away from fossil fuels. The proposed Antalya Pact failed to mention them at all.

Was it really worth sacrificing the agreement over two words, then?

The countries that rejected it said the distinction was fundamental. They argued that there was a world of difference between promising to reduce greenhouse gas emissions and committing to move away from the fuels responsible for most of them. Without that explicit commitment, they feared the new agreement would weaken the one made in Dubai.

World.title: Israeli attacks have turned Gaza into 'toxic wasteland', Oxfam says
World.content:
Gaza has been turned into "a toxic wasteland", with more than 99% of the Palestinian territory showing indicators of environmental contamination from Israeli military attacks, a new report from the charity Oxfam says, external.

Heavy metals, explosive residues, asbestos from destroyed buildings, and dioxins and biological contaminants are threats to Palestinians now and potentially for decades to come, it says.

Oxfam International's executive director, Amitabh Behar, said the impact on Gaza "will have fundamentally degraded the environmental conditions necessary for human safety and survival".

In response, the Israeli embassy in the UK said the report "falls short of professional standards".

Behar also accused Israel of "environmental war crimes" as part of an "ongoing genocide in Gaza".

Israel has rejected genocide accusations in an ongoing case at the International Court of Justice as baseless and distorted. It maintains that its military campaign in Gaza is an act of self-defence against Hamas in response to the group's deadly attack on Israel on 7 October 2023, and that it takes steps to mitigate civilian harm.

World.title: India pledges $1.6bn to Nepal in reset of ties
World.content:
A Hindu-majority nation wedged between India and China, Nepal has long had to navigate competing interests from its two giant neighbours. Allegations of political interference and an unresolved border dispute have frequently complicated ties with India.

Nepal's former Prime Minister, KP Sharma Oli, who leads a communist party, was widely viewed as being closer to China. Shah, by contrast, emerged as a political outsider when he was elected earlier this year. The former rapper, then 35, led a party that was only four years old.

His new approach of dealing with India may explain why the border dispute was largely absent from the leaders' public remarks, although the joint statement acknowledged that outstanding issues remained.

According to Govind Pokharel, a former vice-chairman of Nepal's National Planning Commission, Shah's government may have chosen to set contentious issues aside in order to secure progress on more immediate development needs.

"Right now you can go home and convince the young Nepalis that it will be handled later," Pokhrel says, "but if they don't deal with these issues in the future, there will be criticism."

Veteran Indian diplomat Anil Trigunayat says both sides appear to have opted to leave the dispute to established mechanisms rather than engage in what he calls "cartographic aggressions".

There were other gains for Nepal as a result of the Delhi visit.

As a landlocked country heavily dependent on India for trade, Nepal secured access to two additional Indian ports, Kandla and Paradip. The two sides also agreed to improve road and rail connectivity.

The leaders jointly inaugurated a train service linking Ayodhya in India, revered by Hindus as the birthplace of Lord Ram, with Janakpur in Nepal, traditionally regarded as the birthplace of his wife Sita.

There was, however, disappointment on aviation.

Nepal has long sought greater access to Indian airspace in order to attract international traffic to its airports at Bhairahawa and Pokhara.

Some analysts believe the lack of an agreement reflects Indian concerns over Chinese involvement in the two airport projects.

"The airport in Pokhara can pose certain security challenges for India, so it is a more complicated issue to resolve," says Trigunayat.

India did, however, agree to make an existing air route linking Kathmandu, Bhairahawa and Lucknow bidirectional.

"Nepal invested a huge amount of money in those airports," says Pokharel. "It fell short of expectations, but the bidirectional route is a breakthrough."

Shah must now manage relations with China as he seeks to balance the interests of Nepal's two much larger neighbours.

For now he returns home with substantial financial commitments from India as Nepal continues the long task of rebuilding.

World.title: Search and rescue teams race against time to find survivors after Nigeria boat tragedy
World.content:
Nigerian search and rescue teams are racing against time to find survivors after a boat carrying mourners travelling to a funeral capsized on Friday.

Twenty-nine bodies have been recovered and 50 people rescued so far, a spokesperson for the National Emergency Management Agency (Nema) told the BBC.

The government has responded by ordering stricter enforcement of safety standards on the country's inland waterways.

Overcrowding, poor maintenance and failure to observe safety regulations have contributed to previous deadly accidents on Nigeria's rivers.

The boat was travelling from Ayama community when it developed mechanical problems, according to police spokesperson Musa Mohammed.

Passengers asked the boat operator to steer towards land, but he allegedly declined, leading to the accident.

Survivors have described the panic that followed as passengers struggled to swim and stay afloat while waiting for emergency rescue services.

"As I swam, people were dragging me to the bottom, and I bit one woman and saved myself," Charity Ebikaboaere told local media outlet Arise News.

"Our things, our money, phones, everything lost, but me and my siblings are alive," said another survivor, Tari Samuel.

World.title: 2027: Ebonyi PDP inaugurates campaign council
World.content:
The Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) in Ebonyi State on Monday inaugurated its campaign council ahead of the 2027 general elections.

The party announced the council’s constitution in a statement issued in Abakaliki and signed by its spokesperson in the state, Darlington Onwe.

According to the statement, the council comprises experienced political leaders, grassroots mobilisers, women, and youths drawn from the 13 local government areas and 171 political wards in the state.

The statement said the council would coordinate the party’s statewide campaign activities, strengthen voter engagement and mobilise support for the PDP across all elective positions in the general elections.

It described the council as part of efforts to advance the political ambition of the party’s governorship candidate, Ifeanyi-Chukwuma Odii.

The party urged all appointed members and supporters to demonstrate unity, discipline and commitment towards achieving its electoral objectives.

It also called on party faithful and stakeholders to work collectively towards rebuilding and repositioning the state.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The campaign slogan for the election is “Anyi G’Emeya,” Igbo words translated to mean “Yes, We Can.”

The Director-General of the campaign is Nwanne Ominyi, while Paul Okorie is the deputy director-general operations.

Others are: Chigozie Omege, deputy DG Ebonyi North Zone, Justus Ikechukwu-Okorie, deputy DG Ebonyi South Zone, Festus Okoha, deputy DG Ebonyi Central Zone and Mudi Erenede, director legal services.

Ikechukwu Nwobo is the campaign spokesperson, while Okorie C. Okorie is the director special duties & protocol, among others.

(NAN)

World.title: Killing of Delta NDC Supporters: Keyamo asks Oborevwori to urgently address the people
World.content:
Minister of Aviation and Aerospace Development, Festus Keyamo, has urged Governor Sheriff Oborevwori of Delta State to urgently address the people of the state over Monday’s killing of four Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) supporters by gunmen suspected to be political thugs.

The incident happened at Uduere Community, Ughelli North Local Government Area of Delta State where the NDC went on a campaign tour ahead of the 2027 general elections.

The Omo-Agege Campaign Organisation said in a statement on Monday evening that four people were killed in the attack, and that Ovie Omo-Agege, the NDC candidate for the Delta Central Senatorial District for the elections, was the target of an assassination attempt.

Mr Keyamo, in a statement on Monday night, condemned the killing and offered condolences to the bereaved families.

“I condemn in the strongest possible terms the killing of these persons, just as I also condemned the killing of a tricycle operator in broad daylight by identified supporters of a political party in Asaba on 7 November, 2026,” said Mr Keyamo who is from Delta State.

“I call on our leader and my elder brother, the Governor of Delta State and the Chief Security Officer of the State, Rt. Hon. Elder Sheriff Oborevwori, to urgently address Deltans and read the Riot Act against those who are threatening fire and brimstone.”

The minister called on security agencies to fish out perpetrators of the killings in the state.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

“Since 1999, Delta State has been a relatively peaceful state, politically. Our disagreements have never led to violence and killings. We are all brothers and sisters who went to the same primary, secondary and tertiary institutions, and we all know ourselves and our families so well. There is ABSOLUTELY NO NEED for a descent into violence.

“Those who have promoted the mantra of ‘Rig and Die’ in Delta State and elsewhere should have a rethink, publicly withdraw it, and apologise for overheating the political temperature in the State and country.

“As can be seen, anyone can be a victim. I have always maintained that it is only law enforcement agencies that are allowed to deal with offenders. It is wrong to tell your supporters to kill other citizens under whatever guise. It smacks of desperation,” the minister said.

READ ALSO: Police speak on deadly attack on NDC supporters in Delta

The Delta State Government has imposed a curfew on Ughelli North Local Government Area over the killing, while the police have deployed operatives to the area.

Meanwhile, Omo-Agege campaign mentioned a local government official whom it alleged led the attack. It challenged Governor Sheriff Oborevwori to condemn the attack and order immediate investigation and arrest of those responsible for it.

World.title: Police speak on deadly attack on NDC supporters in Delta
World.content:
The police command in Delta State said it has deployed its operatives to the area where gunmen suspected to be political thugs killed some members of the Nigeria Democratic Party (NDC) who were on a campaign tour on Monday.

The incident happened at Uduere Community, Ughelli North Local Government Area of Delta State.

The Omo-Agege Campaign Organisation said in a statement on Monday evening that four people were killed in the attack, and that Ovie Omo-Agege, the NDC candidate for the Delta Central Senatorial District for the 2027 elections, was the target of an assassination attempt.

Mr Omo-Agege is a former deputy president of the Nigeria Senate.

“The Commissioner of Police, Delta State Command, Samuel E. Erale, has directed intensified security operations in the affected area to prevent further violence and maintain law and order,” Bright Edafe, the police spokesperson in the state, said in a statement on Monday night.

“The commissioner of police has ordered a full-scale investigation and assures residents of the state that anyone found culpable will face the full weight of the law, irrespective of political affiliation or status, and urges members of the public to provide credible information to assist ongoing investigations.”

The police also urged residents to comply with the curfew imposed by the Delta State Government on Ughelli North over the incident.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

“The commissioner of police warns political actors and their supporters against thuggery, intimidation and the unlawful use of firearms, stressing that political differences must never be allowed to degenerate into violence or loss of lives.”

Mr Edafe, a superintendent of police, said the police commissioner condoled with the bereaved family and wished the injured a speedy recovery.

The Omo-Agege campaign mentioned a local government official whom it alleged led the attack. It challenged Governor Sheriff Oborevwori of Delta to condemn the attack and order immediate investigation and arrest of those responsible for it.

It also called on the police and the State Security Service to investigate the incident.

‘Campaigning is not a crime’

“We state it clearly: Delta State is not a war zone. Campaigning is not a crime. Seeking the votes of the people should not be a death sentence,” Sunny Areh, a media adviser to Mr Omo-Agege, said in the statement on behalf of the campaign.

“We call on INEC, civil society organisations, the international community, and all lovers of democracy to take note: Deltans are being shot and killed for exercising their democratic right to campaign.

“To the families of Moses Anaughe and Akima Efemena Umukoro: We mourn with you. Your loved ones did not die in vain. Their blood cries out for justice, and we will not rest until justice is done.

“To our supporters: Do not retaliate. Do not take the law into your hands. We refuse to be intimidated. We refuse to be silenced. Our ward-to-ward tour of Delta Central will continue.”

World.title: 2027: Tinubu meets with Igbo leaders, traders in Lagos
World.content:
President Bola Tinubu on Monday thanked the Igbo communities and business leaders in Lagos for their resolve to support his re-election on 16 January 2027

He assured them of his administration’s commitment to inclusive governance, national unity and equity for all Nigerians.

President Tinubu gave the assurance while addressing youths, elders and leaders of Ndigbo during a town hall meeting organised by the Ndigbo National Dialogue and Development Initiatives at the Wole Soyinka Centre for Culture and the Creative Arts, Iganmu, Lagos State.

He called on Ndigbo to strengthen their unity, deepen their participation in national politics, and work with other ethnic groups to build a peaceful, prosperous, and united Nigeria.

To reaffirm his commitment to national unity, President Tinubu joined the gathering to sing the national anthem a second time.

“I didn’t believe you would turn out this many; I am very, very happy. May God bless you, and God will continue to guide and bless our country. It is a great honour for me to be here before you as your president.

“I can commit to one thing: the unity of Nigeria. Though tribes and tongues may differ, in brotherhood we stand. None of us told God when we were born where we would be born or what language we would speak. Whether you are Igbo or Hausa, you have no control over yourself. God created you, created that opportunity. We are all Nigerians.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

“Let’s see ourselves as individuals living in the same house, geographically called Nigeria,” the president told the gathering.

The president said his administration recognises the significant contributions of the Igbo communities to Nigeria’s economic growth, assuring them that no section of the country would be left behind under the Renewed Hope Agenda.

President Tinubu appreciated the leadership of all the market leaders in Lagos for leaving their businesses to be at the gathering.

” To all of you, I am grateful for one thing: that you are here this afternoon. You left your businesses, left money-making to come and listen to the president, and I must say thank you,” he said.

The president expressed his determination to consolidate his administration’s economic gains.

He said national development requires collective commitment, mutual understanding, and cooperation, urging the Igbo community to embrace dialogue and constructive engagement to address challenges and advance their interests within the Nigerian federation.

President Tinubu told the gathering that all the South East governors are with him on the journey to make Nigeria a better place and are working for his re-election. He mentioned Chidi Anyeagbu, owner of Chisco Motors; Dave Umahi, Doris Uzoka-Anite, and Nkeiruka Onyejeocha, who were at the gathering, as people he has close connections with.

President Tinubu explained some of the reasons behind his policies, such as ensuring the tertiary schools are no longer paralysed by union strikes.

“To eliminate the crisis in the universities, to build good roads and the engineers that will maintain our cars, our children must be in school. Just because they are poor doesn’t mean they must not go to university or develop.

“We are doing that with NELFUND. The university is stable today because we are doing well. We are putting money in agriculture and trading, and anyone in the trade business can apply to the Bank of Industry and get a loan; anyone in agriculture can take a small farmers’ loan.

“We have to maintain this country for the sake of every one of us. The critical line in our national anthem is what I’m standing here for. I begged for it, and I am ready to serve.

“And I served the first term. The constitution says I can ask for a second term. I want a second term. As you are here today, you make me happy, you make me excited, and I will go home happy and eat (Akpu),” the president said.

President Tinubu also called on Ndigbo residents in Lagos to participate actively and vote for him, APC governorship candidate Obafemi Hamzat, and other APC candidates in the 2027 general elections.

He commended the organisers of the town hall meeting for providing a platform for constructive engagement between the Federal Government and the Igbo community,

On his part, the host Governor, Babajide Sanwo-Olu, rallied members of the Ndigbo to support President Bola Tinubu’s re-election bid, assuring the president of massive votes from the state in the 16 January 2027 presidential election.

Mr Sanwo-Olu described the turnout of Igbo leaders, traders, and business owners as proof that Lagos residents were united behind the president, despite the meeting being held on a Monday, when many participants had to leave their businesses to attend.

The governor urged the community to sustain the unity and support, saying Lagos would deliver an unprecedented number of votes for Tinubu.

He also praised Mr Tinubu as a detribalised Nigerian and nationalist, saying his administration had promoted development across the six geopolitical zones and strengthened national unity.

Mr Sanwo-Olu further commended the president for what he described as economic stability, increased investment and opportunities for young people, while thanking him for his contributions to Lagos State.

Describing the gathering as a reflection of the “One Lagos” spirit, the governor said the presence of people from different ethnic backgrounds demonstrated that residents could work together in support of a common political cause.

In her remarks, the Convener of the meeting and Minister of State for Budget and Economic Planning, Doris Uzoka-Anite, declared the Igbo community’s commitment in Lagos State to supporting President Tinubu’s re-election bid, saying the community has resolved to unite behind his leadership.

She said the Ndigbo had commenced grassroots mobilisation across Lagos State, with structures established at the polling-unit level ahead of the 2027 presidential election.

Also speaking, the former Minister of State for Labour and Employment, Nkeiruka Onyejeocha, assured President Bola Tinubu of the Ndigbo’s support for his 2027 re-election bid, saying the gathering of Igbo leaders and stakeholders in Lagos demonstrated their unity and commitment to the president.

She said the community had recognised the importance of building political alliances with other geopolitical zones to achieve its future presidential ambition.

She assured the president that Ndigbo acknowledged the difficult circumstances under which his administration began and appreciated some of the government’s decisions.

She commended the president for removing the fuel subsidy, adding that the decision had improved sub-national fiscal capacity to meet salary obligations in their respective states.

The former minister also praised the administration for fulfilling its commitment to reviewing workers’ salaries every three years and introducing a national minimum wage of ₦70,000.

The leader of the Ndigbo Traders Association in Lagos, Tony Nwakeze, pledged members’ support for President Bola Tinubu’s re-election bid, while appealing for access to loans at a 5 per cent interest rate to help traders transition from importation to local manufacturing.

Mr Nwakeze said traders from Alaba, Trade Fair and Ladipo markets were seeking financial support to empower young people and expand their businesses.

He also assured the president that traders were prepared to organise themselves and adopt a cross-guarantee arrangement to ensure repayment of any loans granted to their members.

He also pledged that the market leadership would honour agreements reached with the government, stressing that traders had learnt from previous misunderstandings and were committed to sustaining a cordial relationship with the Lagos State Government.

He thanked the president for attending the meeting and promised that traders across Lagos markets would support him and honour every agreement reached with the government.

“We, the market people, will stand with you, support you and honour every agreement we enter into today,” he said.

Bayo Onanuga

Special Adviser to the President

(Information & Strategy)

November 23, 2026

World.title: Ex-NNPC cooperative chief ordered to appear in court over alleged N582m fraud
World.content:
The Federal Capital Territory (FCT) High Court in Gwarinpa, Abuja, on Monday ordered the former President of the NNPC Staff Multi-Purpose Cooperative Society, Olalekan Ogunbayo, to appear in court on 15 December for his arraignment over an alleged N582 million fraud.

A statement by the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC) said the trial judge, Leslie Wike, warned that Mr Ogunbayo risked a warrant of arrest if he failed to appear on the next adjourned date.

The EFCC filed an eight-count charge against Mr Ogunbayo and Abolade Nurudeen over the alleged criminal misappropriation of N582 million, conspiracy and corruption.

The money was generated from the sale of a property belonging to the NNPC Staff Multi-Purpose Cooperative Society, according to the EFCC.

However, Mr Ogunbayo was absent when the case came up for arraignment on Monday. EFCC lawyer R.U. Adagba informed the court.

Attempts to reach Mr Ogunbayo

This is the second time Mr Ogunbayo has failed to appear for his arraignment. He was also absent when the case came up on 26 October.

Ms Adagba told the court that the EFCC had made several attempts to reach the defendant, including sending him written invitations.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

She also said Mr Ogunbayo was aware of the charge against him, having personally deposed to an affidavit in support of a bail application before the court on 13 October.

Defence arguments

In his defence, Mr Adoo acknowledged that he had undertaken to produce his client in court but argued that he had not been served with a copy of the charge.

Mr Adoo also disclosed that the Inspector-General of Police and the Code of Conduct Bureau had invited Mr Ogunbayo over the same matter.

Responding, Ms Adagba argued that the court had not made any order authorising the service of the charge on Mr Ogunbayo’s lawyer on his behalf.

She maintained that the defendant was aware of the criminal proceedings because he had filed an affidavit in support of his bail application.

After hearing both sides, the judge directed that Mr Ogunbayo be served through his lawyer, Mr Adoo. He warned that the defendant risked a warrant of arrest if he failed to appear in court.

The judge subsequently adjourned the case until 15 December for arraignment.

Failed arraignments

The failure of defendants to appear in court for arraignment is one of the factors contributing to delays in the administration of justice.

Mr Ogunbayo is not the first defendant to miss an arraignment. The former Minister of Humanitarian Affairs, Disaster Management and Social Development, Sadiya Umar-Farouq, has also failed to appear in court for her arraignment over alleged fraud involving $1.3 million and N746.6 million.

Ms Umar-Farouq’s lawyers attributed her absence to health reasons.

Her repeated failure to appear prompted the judge to order her arrest.

Adeniyi Adeyemi, accused of creating and operating a purported government agency, has also failed to appear in court for arraignment.

Several attempts to arraign him since last year were unsuccessful for various reasons, including applications by his lawyers, his absence from court and the judge’s official engagements elsewhere.

He was eventually arraigned in September before the Federal High Court. However, the charges were later withdrawn and transferred to the FCT High Court in Maitama.

World.title: Yelwata Massacre: Farmer tells court how gunmen killed his wife, three sons
World.content:
A farmer on Monday told the Federal High Court in Abuja how he lost his wife and three sons in the June 2025 Yelwata massacre in Benue State.

The witness, Ukeyima David, from Guma Local Government Area, testified as the third prosecution witness in the trial of nine men accused of involvement in the attack.

“They hacked me with a machete and killed my wife and three sons,” Mr David told the court, presided over by Judge Joyce Abdulmalik.

“My youngest child, Kingsley, was nine months old.”

He said his wife, Judith, and three sons, Samson, Michael and Kingsley, were killed during the attack.

Mr David also showed the court a scar on his back from a machete injury he said he sustained while fleeing the attackers.

The defendants include Ardo Lawal Mohammed Dono, Ardo Muhammadu Saidu and Alhaji Haruna Abdullahi.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Others are Yakubu Adamu, Musa Mohammed, Abubakar Adamu, Shaibu Ibrahim, Sale Mohammed and Bako Jibrin.

They are facing 57 terrorism-related counts over the 13 June 2025 attack on Yelwata, which reportedly killed more than 150 people.

They pleaded not guilty when they were arraigned by the Nigerian government in February.
