The main trial resumed after Judge Abdulmalik dismissed the defendants’ objections to the admissibility of their statements, allowing the substantive proceedings to continue.

Farmer recounts night of attack

When prosecution lawyer Mariam Okorie asked Mr David to testify, he said the attack began at about 10:45 p.m. on 13 June 2025, while his family was asleep.

He also said he heard gunshots and later realised that armed men had surrounded Yelwata Market.

According to him, the attackers first approached the new market, where police officers and soldiers were stationed at a checkpoint. They later moved towards the old market because of the security presence.

“My children were asking me what we should do, and I assured them that security was around,” he said.

But the gunmen began killing residents as gunshots rang out across the community. Residents, he said, were unsure where to run for safety.

Mr David said he noticed that the attackers were preparing to pour fuel on his roof and set his house ablaze. He struggled to push his children outside as people shouted for help from different directions.

He said the attackers struck him with a machete as soon as he stepped outside.

After showing the injury to the court, he said he fled from the old market towards the new market, where security personnel were stationed. The attackers pursued him, threatening that his “days are numbered”.

He eventually reached a police station and reported that his family had been killed.

However, the officers told him they could not confront the attackers because they were outnumbered.

According to Mr David, the attack lasted about four hours. When it ended, security personnel took him back to the area, where he found his wife and children dead.

He said one of his sons had been hacked with a machete, while Michael had been cut near the door. His youngest son, Kingsley, “was burnt to ashes”.

Other residents were also killed in different buildings during the attack, he added.

Mr David said residents had stopped sleeping in their homes before the massacre after receiving warnings that attackers were coming to Yelwata. They instead spread tarpaulins and slept in beer parlours and shops.

He said security personnel had also advised residents to remain indoors and lock their doors whenever the attackers arrived. He attributed the attackers’ eventual discovery of their hiding places to this advice.

During cross-examination by defence lawyers, Mr David agreed that the attackers came through the market, which operates during the day.

He maintained that the attack began at about 10:45 p.m. and that the shooting continued until 2 a.m.

The witness admitted that he could not identify the attackers during the incident. He said recurring disputes between Fulani herders and Tiv residents had led people to suspect that the attackers were Fulani.

Asked whether he had death certificates or photographs of his family members to establish their deaths, Mr David said he had none.

He explained that he fled his home with nothing and that the attackers burnt the house. His family members were later buried alongside other victims in mass graves.

He also said he could not return to his hometown to bury them because Fulani herders had displaced him from his village about five years earlier.

Mr David, however, identified the third defendant, Alhaji Haruna Abdullahi, as someone who regularly visited Yelwata to settle disputes between Fulani and Tiv residents. He maintained, however, that he could not identify anyone during the attack.

Witness recounts tensions before massacre

The prosecution subsequently called its fourth witness, Achin Tor Mathias, a native of Yelwata and publicity secretary of the Yelwata Youth Vanguard Forum.

Mr Mathias told the court that residents had lived peacefully before a series of incidents that preceded the June 2025 attack.

He traced the tensions to 20 April 2025, when a Tiv man and a Fulani man had a disagreement at Mbagwen, another community in Guma Local Government Area.

World.title: Gunmen kill four as Omo-Agege escapes alleged assassination attempt
World.content:
HeadThere has been a reported assassination attempt on Ovie Omo-Agege, the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) candidate for the Delta Central Senatorial District for the 2027 elections.

The Omo-Agege Organisation said in a statement on Monday evening that four people were killed on Monday afternoon when armed men opened fire on the candidate’s entourage during a campaign tour at Uduere, Ughelli North Local Government Area of Delta.

“We are pained to report that four people, including two of our aides—Moses Anaughe and Akima Efemena Umukoro—were shot dead,” Sunny Areh, a media adviser to Mr Omo-Agege, said in the statement.

“Four others—Chief Evance Ivwurie, Chuks Erhire, Tobore Agba (who was shot in the neck) and Ayodo Wanogho—were shot at very close range and wounded critically. They are currently receiving medical attention.”

The statement quoted unnamed witnesses as saying that the assailants were shouting that they wanted Mr Omo-Agege during the attack.

“This was not a clash. This was not a misunderstanding. This was, according to witnesses, a targeted attempt to assassinate Senator Ovie Omo-Agege.”

The campaign mentioned a local government official whom it alleged led the attack. It challenged Governor Sheriff Oborevwori to condemn the attack and order an immediate investigation and the arrest of those responsible.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

It also called on the police and the State Security Service to investigate the incident.

“We state it clearly: Delta State is not a war zone. Campaigning is not a crime. Seeking the votes of the people should not be a death sentence.

“We call on INEC, civil society organisations, the international community, and all lovers of democracy to take note: Deltans are being shot and killed for exercising their democratic right to campaign.

“To the families of Moses Anaughe and Akima Efemena Umukoro: We mourn with you. Your loved ones did not die in vain. Their blood cries out for justice, and we will not rest until justice is done.

“To our supporters: Do not retaliate. Do not take the law into your hands. We refuse to be intimidated. We refuse to be silenced. Our ward-to-ward tour of Delta Central will continue.”

PREMIUM TIMES could not immediately get the police reaction to the incident. Bright Edafe, the police spokesperson in Delta, did not respond to calls from our reporter on Monday night.

Meanwhile, the Delta State Government has imposed a curfew in the entire Ughelli North Local Government Area because of the incident.

In a statement issued by the Secretary to the Delta State Government, Kingsley Eze Emu, on Monday, the state government acknowledged that there were “alleged gunshots and attendant deaths in some parts of Ughelli North.”

“The State Government hereby declares an immediate curfew from 6p.m. to 6a.m. every day starting from today until further notice. This is to bring the situation under control.”

World.title: FIFA names USA, Mexico, Costa Rica, Jamaica hosts of expanded 2031 Women’s World Cup
World.content:
FIFA has confirmed the United States, Mexico, Costa Rica and Jamaica as co-hosts of the 2031 Women’s World Cup, while England, Northern Ireland, Scotland and Wales will jointly stage the 2035 edition.

The decisions were taken at an Extraordinary FIFA Congress held virtually on Monday 23 November, with the four nations appointed by acclamation following bidding processes launched by the FIFA Council in March 2025.

The 2031 tournament will mark a major milestone for women’s football, becoming the first edition to feature 48 teams and the first to be staged across four FIFA member associations.

The appointments also come almost 35 years after the opening match of the inaugural Women’s World Cup, which was contested by 12 teams in 1991.

Speaking ahead of confirming the two host arrangements, FIFA President Gianni Infantino described the decisions as a significant moment in the governing body’s ambition to take women’s football to a wider global audience.

“Our objective, of course, is making women’s football truly global, and to build the future together with all Member Associations and with all stakeholders. Today, we decide here on the hosts of the FIFA Women’s World Cup 2031 and 2035. This is a proud moment for you; this is a proud moment for us, for all of us,” Mr Infantino said.

The FIFA president stressed that the impact of the two tournaments must extend beyond the pitch, calling for greater opportunities for women and girls at every level of the game.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

He said the focus should include increasing the number of female players, inspiring more girls to take up football and creating pathways for women to become coaches, referees, administrators and leaders.

“More women players, more girls inspired, more women coaches, more women referees, more women administrators, more women leaders. Our priorities for the women’s game are very, very simple: we have to expand the game globally, we have to close the gaps that still, of course, exist and we have to build the future together,” he added.

In his closing remarks, Mr Infantino reiterated the need for investment, infrastructure and development opportunities to ensure football reaches more people around the world.

“Football belongs to everyone, everywhere in the world, and we have to create opportunities; we have to create development; we have to create infrastructure. We also need resources to make this happen. And together, we will have a real impact,” he said.

World.title: FG seeks stronger food policies to curb malnutrition, NCDs
World.content:
By Chidinma Chukwu, Abuja

The Federal Government has called for stronger implementation of healthy food policies to address malnutrition, micronutrient deficiencies and the rising burden of diet-related non-communicable diseases (NCDs) in the country.

The Minister of State for Health and Social Welfare, Dr. Iziaq Adekunle Salako, made the call on Monday while delivering the keynote address at the maiden National Healthy Food Week and Learning Conference 2026 in Abuja.

The conference, themed, “Our Food, Our Health, Our Future,” was organised to promote healthier food systems and strengthen efforts to address nutrition-related health challenges.

Represented by the ministry’s Permanent Secretary, Ms. Daju Kachollom, Salako said tackling the country’s nutrition and health challenges required stronger collaboration among government institutions, regulatory agencies, food manufacturers, health professionals, researchers, development partners, the media and consumers.

He noted that food choices and the quality of food available in markets, schools, hospitals, workplaces and homes had significant implications for public health, workforce productivity, child development and national prosperity.

The minister said the Federal Government had introduced several policies and regulatory measures to improve food safety and nutritional standards, including the Revised National Policy on Food Safety and Quality and its Implementation Plan (2023).

He said the policy framework promoted food safety, food fortification, sodium reduction, elimination of industrially produced trans fats and healthier food procurement practices in public institutions.

Salako also highlighted the National Guidelines for Sodium Reduction, the National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control’s (NAFDAC) Read the Label Campaign and the development of front-of-pack nutrition labelling as measures to help consumers make informed food choices and encourage manufacturers to improve the nutritional quality of their products.

On public food procurement, he said government institutions provided millions of meals annually through schools, hospitals, correctional centres, emergency shelters and National Youth Service Corps (NYSC) camps, making public procurement an important instrument for improving the country’s food environment.

He urged relevant authorities to ensure effective implementation of the Bureau of Public Procurement’s National Guidelines for Public Procurement of Food and Related Services through adequate monitoring, accountability and capacity building.

The minister also identified fiscal measures, including the sugar-sweetened beverage tax, as important tools for discouraging excessive consumption of sugary drinks and generating revenue for public health interventions.

He advocated transparent allocation of part of the revenue to nutrition education, healthier food environments and the prevention of diet-related diseases.

On micronutrient deficiencies, Salako emphasised the need to strengthen large-scale food fortification, noting that its effectiveness depended on regulatory compliance, quality assurance, adequate laboratory capacity and market surveillance.

He also encouraged Nigerians to consume more locally available nutritious foods, including legumes, fruits, vegetables, nuts, whole grains and traditional nutrient-rich foods.

While acknowledging progress in developing healthy food policies and regulatory frameworks, the minister said the priority should now be to ensure their effective implementation on a wider scale.

He identified state and local governments, primary healthcare facilities, community organisations, traditional and religious institutions, women’s groups, youth networks and the media as critical partners in translating policies into measurable health outcomes.

Salako warned that unhealthy food environments could worsen the burden of hypertension, diabetes, obesity, cardiovascular diseases, stroke and kidney disease, with serious implications for healthcare costs and national productivity.

He called for the National Healthy Food Week and Learning Conference to become a sustainable platform for accountability, partnership, innovation and continuous improvement of Nigeria’s food systems.

He stressed that every Nigerian should have access to safe, nutritious, affordable and health-promoting food.

In a goodwill message, the Interim Country Director of Resolve to Save Lives (RTSL), Dr. Jenom Danjuma, reaffirmed the organisation’s commitment to supporting government efforts to promote healthy diets and strengthen food policies to reduce the burden of NCDs.

Danjuma identified excessive sodium, industrially produced trans fats and added sugars, particularly from sugar-sweetened beverages, as major dietary risk factors contributing to premature deaths from hypertension, cardiovascular diseases and type 2 diabetes.

He called for evidence-based policies and sustained collaboration among stakeholders to promote healthier food environments and make nutritious food more accessible to Nigerians.

He said the four-day conference would provide an opportunity for stakeholders to assess progress in implementing healthy food policies, share experiences, identify challenges and develop practical strategies to accelerate action.

Similarly, the Executive Director of the Network for Health Equity and Development (NHED), Dr. Jerome Mafeni, said access to safe, nutritious and affordable food should be treated as a public health priority rather than solely an individual responsibility.

Mafeni said food choices were influenced not only by personal preferences but also by availability, production standards, affordability and access to reliable consumer information.

He argued that the effectiveness of healthy food policies should be measured by their impact on what was produced, marketed and made available to consumers rather than by the mere adoption of policy documents.

He urged stakeholders to move beyond discussions and agree on practical commitments, stronger institutional coordination and sustained accountability, adding that the conference’s success would depend on the actions taken and their impact on Nigerians.

Also speaking, the World Health Organisation (WHO) Representative, Dr. Pavel Ursu, represented by Pindar Wakawa, called for stronger measures to promote healthy diets and address the growing burden of diet-related NCDs in Nigeria.

Ursu described the conference as a timely national platform for advancing healthy food policies, noting that healthy diets were among the most effective investments countries could make to prevent diseases, improve productivity, strengthen human capital and accelerate socioeconomic development.

He expressed concern that diet-related NCDs accounted for approximately 27 per cent of all deaths in Nigeria, identifying cardiovascular diseases, hypertension, diabetes and chronic respiratory diseases as major public health concerns partly driven by excessive consumption of salt, sugar and unhealthy fats.

The WHO representative also disclosed that nearly one in three Nigerian adults was living with hypertension, a major risk factor for heart disease, stroke and kidney failure.

He called for sustained collaboration among government institutions, development partners, civil society organisations and the private sector to ensure that healthy food was accessible, affordable and available to all Nigerians.

World.title: 2027: NUC proposes 4-week break for universities
World.content:
By Omeiza Ajayi

The National Universities Commission NUC has proposed that universities adopt a three-to-four-week break to accommodate the 2027 general election, saying the entire election cycle will last no more than four weeks.

Executive Secretary of the NUC, Prof. Abdullahi Yusufu Ribadu, made the proposal on Monday in Abuja during a courtesy visit by the Chairman of the Independent National Electoral Commission INEC, Prof. Joash Amupitan SAN.

According to a statement from INEC on Monday night, Amupitan was accompanied by National Commissioners and senior officials of the commission.

The Presidential and National Assembly elections hold on Saturday, 16 January 2027. The Governorship and State Houses of Assembly elections follow on Saturday, 6 February 2027.

He noted that the academic community had for over a decade served as the backbone of collation and declaration of results, with Vice-Chancellors serving as Collation and Returning Officers across the Federation.

The INEC Chairman said the commission had introduced operational, technological and security reforms to make the work of its university partners safer and less contentious.

He said polling unit results on Form EC8A would undergo automated arithmetic consistency and over-voting checks before transmission to the INEC Result Viewing Portal (IReV).

According to him, the commission has procured 57,000 new Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS) devices and lowered the voter-to-device ratio to 850 per machine.

Amupitan added that INEC would conduct a nationwide mock accreditation and result transmission exercise across the 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory (FCT) on Saturday, 28 November 2026.

On security, he said the Inter-Agency Consultative Committee on Election Security (ICCES) had been decentralised to every Local Government Area and Registration Area, with dedicated security cordons and escort protocols around collation centres.

He drew attention to Sections 96 and 97 of the Electoral Act 2026, which criminalise violence, abusive rhetoric and threats against electoral personnel, and Section 148, which empowers the commission to prosecute offenders directly.

“No Returning Officer or Collation Officer will be left to stand alone against lawlessness,” Amupitan said.

He then asked the NUC for support in four areas: the timely nomination of academic staff of verified non-partisan standing, the alignment of academic calendars with the election dates, collaboration on voter education and counter-disinformation on campuses, and the welfare and recognition of academics deployed for election duty.

Responding, Ribadu congratulated Amupitan on his appointment, describing him as a lawyer and academic of international repute and “a round peg in a round hole.”

,

The NUC Executive Secretary said the commission would engage Vice-Chancellors on the nomination of academic staff, including through an online meeting. He said it would also transmit a circular to the universities once INEC forwards a formal letter on the matter.

“Since we want to have credible elections, we also have to have credible personnel,” Ribadu said. He added that all ad hoc personnel should take an oath of neutrality.

On the academic calendar, he said the entire election cycle would last no more than four weeks, and suggested that universities could adopt a three-to-four-week break to accommodate it.

“We will discuss with the Vice-Chancellors and have their calendars tweaked in such a way that it will not affect the elections, nor will it affect the studies of the students,” Ribadu said.

He said students could also support voter education through campus clubs.

Ribadu expressed confidence that INEC would deliver a transparent, free and fair election that would serve as an example to other African countries.

He proposed expanded collaboration between the two institutions, including student internships at INEC offices, a possible programme in electoral studies, and joint research on artificial intelligence, robotics and data analytics.

World.title: Trump backs Nvidia CEO’s return amid US lawmakers’ spy allegations, security concerns
World.content:
Photo by Kevin Dietsch / GETTY IMAGES NORTH AMERICA / Getty Images via AFP.

US President Donald Trump praised Nvidia’s decision Monday to reinstate Jensen Huang as chief executive, as Democratic leaders vowed investigations and prominent Republicans questioned whether his return posed a national security risk.

Trump also posted a doctored version of the famous photograph of him raising his fist after surviving a 2024 assassination attempt, replacing himself with Huang, who brandished a red bra beneath an Nvidia flag.

The image appeared to allude to the scandal that forced Huang, co-founder of the AI chip giant, to resign less than two weeks earlier following revelations of extramarital affairs, including with a woman suspected of being a Chinese spy.

“The NVIDIA Board of Directors has made the correct and proper decision to return Jensen Huang to the position of CEO,” Trump wrote on Truth Social, adding that the government had no reason to believe his return posed a national security risk.

In a telephone interview with CNBC, Trump suggested the scandal could prove to be “a net positive” by highlighting Nvidia’s technological advances.

“I don’t think he’s going to be diminished at all,” he said, predicting Huang would return at “an almost higher level.”

He said the attorney general had confirmed that US authorities possessed no evidence Huang had engaged in unlawful conduct, but urged Nvidia to continue investigating its compliance with restrictions on advanced chip sales to China.

Senate Democratic leader Chuck Schumer and House speaker-designate Hakeem Jeffries vowed sweeping investigations into Nvidia, Trump and his senior officials, with Jeffries singling out Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick.

“We will not allow America’s national security to be sold out by the Trump administration for personal financial gain,” Jeffries said.

– ‘What changed?’ –

Huang is already scheduled to face questioning behind closed doors by three House committees on December 1 over his relationship with the suspected Chinese intelligence operative and concerns about Nvidia’s chip exports.

And the Republican-led Senate Banking Committee has announced that his appearance scheduled for December 3 will be livestreamed.

“We still don’t know what information Chinese intelligence may have obtained from him,” said House Intelligence Committee Democrat Raja Krishnamoorthi, demanding a full public congressional hearing.

Senator Elizabeth Warren called the decision “reckless” and demanded details of what input senior administration officials had provided in support of Huang’s return.

Republican Senator John Curtis raised similar questions, noting that Nvidia’s board had reversed its opposition to reinstating Huang while an independent investigation remained unfinished.

“Who in our government weighed in? What did they tell the board?” he wrote on X. “I’d like to know what changed.”

Senator Pete Ricketts, also a Republican, said Huang’s behavior did not warrant reinstatement and insisted the move did not excuse him from testifying before Congress.

Former Republican House speaker Newt Gingrich called for scrutiny of what he described as a national security issue “of enormous proportions.”

Outgoing Republican congressman Don Bacon alleged Huang had been “compromised and exploited by a Chinese spy,” demanding answers about who had authorized advanced chip sales to China.

And Republican Senator John Cornyn offered a terse response to Trump’s assurances.

“No national security risk? Based on what?” he wrote on X.

Trump declined earlier Monday to comment on a New York Times report that the woman at the center of the scandal had been in contact with an official from China’s principal intelligence agency during her affair with Huang.

World.title: Nigeria’s rice revolution collapses as 90 mills shutdown
World.content:
File: Rice mill collapses in Kebbi.

*Paddy production volume crashes *From 75% self-sufficiency country goes into massive imports *Farmers abandon rice, move to other crops *Operators blame policy reversals, others *Why rice value chain now struggling —FG

By Emma Ujah, Abuja Bureau Chief, Jeff Agbodo (Abakiliki), Aliyu Usman (Birnin Kebbi) and Sukanmi Akanni (Lagos)

Nigeria’s much-celebrated rice revolution is facing a major reversal, with more than 90 out of the country’s 260 integrated rice mills shutting down completely over acute paddy scarcity, rising production costs and the influx of cheaper imported rice.

This comes as the National Rice Development Strategy II, launched in 2021 to accelerate investments and self sufficiency in rice production expires next month.

The programme was part of the Buhari administration’s agricultural transformation agenda, which sought to reduce dependence on food imports and conserve foreign exchange.

Nigeria had announced 75 per cent self-sufficiency in rice production in February 2023 and projected to become a net exporter of the commodity by 2026.

The progress was showcased in January 2023 when the Federal Government, the Central Bank of Nigeria, CBN, and Rice Farmers Association of Nigeria, RIFAN, unveiled what they described as the world’s largest rice pyramids in Abuja.

The pyramids, comprising one million bags of paddy, were presented as evidence of Nigeria’s growing capacity to produce enough rice for domestic consumption and eventually export the commodity.

Nigeria’s annual rice import bill, estimated at about $1 billion in 2015, was said to have fallen to approximately $18.5 million by 2021.

But the year 2025 marked the beginning of the reversal of fortune with Paddy production, which had risen to 8.5 million tonnes in 2021, recording a sharp decline to about 4.8 million tonnes, while mill capacity utilisation dropped below 30 per cent.

Industry operators told Financial Vanguard that leading integrated mills, including Umza in Kano and Stallion in Lagos, are operating below 50 per cent of their installed capacity.

Speaking to the unfolding crisis the National Chairman of the Rice Millers Association of Nigeria, RIMAN, and Chairman, Board of Trustees of the Competitive African Rice Forum for Sustainable Development, CARF-FSD, Nigeria Chapter, Mr. Peter Dama, noted the rice policy inconsistency especially the suspension of the Anchor Borrowers’ Programme (ABP), which drove the country’s rice production surge between 2015 and 2023.

The industry operators listed inadequate agricultural financing, insecurity, escalating input costs and weak supply chains as key in the derailing of the growth over the past three years.

More recently they said that 2026 has witnessed a deliberate opening of the country’s borders allowing massive importation of cheaper foreign rice especially through Seme border with Benin Republic.

They lamented that Nigerians have invested heavily in building rice mills but the government has failed to sustain the agricultural production policy needed to keep them running.

Paradox of idle capacity, imports

Perhaps the most disturbing aspect of the current crisis is the contradiction between Nigeria’s enormous milling capacity and the shortage of locally produced paddy.

According to Dama, the country has installed rice milling capacity of approximately 7.5 million tonnes annually but currently produces only 4.1 million tonnes of paddy.

This leaves a huge gap between the capacity of the industry and the raw materials available to sustain its operations.

The operators noted cost over-run as the main factor stoking the crises as a tonne of paddy that sold for about N180,000 in 2021 now costs between N600,000 and N650,000.

Fertiliser prices, according to them, have increased from about N8,000 to N45,000, while petrol has risen from N250 to N1,400 per litre.

The input cost, according to them, has made the local rice now uncompetitive against the imported brands.

Dama said, ‘‘locally milled rice at current paddy prices costs higher than imported finished rice through Lagos ports.

‘‘This is a fundamental competitiveness problem that cannot be resolved merely by announcing restrictions on rice imports’’.

Consequently, some farmers are abandoning rice for alternative crops such as sesame and sorghum, further worsening the shortage of paddy.

The crises, according to the operators, goes beyond the fortunes of rice mill owners to include farmers, transporters, distributors, workers and millions of households that depend on rice as a staple food.

Why rice value chain now struggling — FG

A top official of the Federal Ministry of Agriculture, who spoke on condition of anonymity, said that the main challenge facing the rice value chain is policy inconsistency.

He said three other factors combined to create the current gap in rice production and the consumption needs of the Nigerian society.

According to him the growing population, rural-urban migration and the changing eating pattern of Nigerians combined to put pressure on rice, which is a staple food in almost every part of the country.

He said Nigeria remains the largest producer but also the largest importer of rice due to the inability of production to meet demand.

He revealed that the nation’s current self-sufficiency in rice production has dropped to 69 percent.

He however lamented that the cost of inputs such as fertilisers, seeds and agro-chemicals have challenged farmers lately, especially since the end of the Presidential Fertiliser Initiative (PFI) initiative when Urea was imported from Morocco and sold to fertilizer blenders at subsidized rate, who in turn sold fertilisers to farmers at subsidised rates.

According to him, fertiliser blenders now buy urea at market prices and that combined with the geopolitical crisis in the Middle East, especially the blockade of the Strait of Homuz, where 30 percent of fertiliser raw material pass, the fertiliser market has become more challenged, making the products more expensive and out of reach for many small-holder farmers.

He added that with very expensive inputs, paddy produced is sold to millers at high prices.

He confessed that millers who also face high operational costs due largely to dependence on diesel, rather than electricity come up with milled rice that cannot compete with the imported rice.

According to him, governments of the countries of origin of imported rice subsidise rice production for export and that as such, locally milled rice is struggling to compete with the imported rice.

He suggested that if rice production is to significantly increase in the country, the government must consider a way of subsidizing agricultural inputs, as is the case with other countries of the world.

Collapse of ABP

At the heart of the crisis, according to the operators, is the collapse of the Anchor Borrowers’ Programme, ABP, introduced by the Central Bank of Nigeria under former Governor Godwin Emefiele.

The programme was one of the most ambitious attempts to address Nigeria’s food import dependence by linking smallholder farmers with processors and providing them with affordable agricultural financing.

Between 2015 and 2021, it reportedly helped increase paddy production from 2.5 million tonnes to 8.5 million tonnes.

Official rice imports, according to figures supplied by industry stakeholders, fell from 2.4 million tonnes to less than 400,000 tonnes during the period.

The programme’s strength was its integrated approach to agricultural production.

Rather than simply giving farmers cash, it provided seeds, fertiliser and herbicides on credit, with repayment made in paddy after harvest.

It also linked farmers to rice millers who guaranteed markets for their produce.

Interest rates were pegged at nine per cent, significantly below the commercial lending rates of about 28 per cent cited by industry stakeholders.

This arrangement addressed two major constraints confronting farmers: access to inputs and guaranteed markets.

It also provided millers with a more predictable supply of paddy.

However, the programme became controversial over allegations of politicisation, poor loan recovery and the inclusion of beneficiaries who were not genuine farmers.

Although more than N1.1 trillion was reportedly disbursed, loan recovery was said to have fallen below 30 per cent.

Consequently, a new CBN leadership discontinued the programme in 2023 without an effective replacement arrangement.

That decision created a financing vacuum in the rice value chain.

Dama estimates that more than 40 per cent of smallholder farmers who participated in the programme have since moved into other crops.

The Ministry of Agriculture’s dry-season wheat and rice initiatives, according to him, have not been sufficient to reach the majority of genuine farmers, while the Bank of Agriculture lacks the resources to provide financing on the scale required.

Dama further argued that ‘‘it is not necessarily that the ABP should be restored in its original form. Its weaknesses, particularly poor loan recovery and political interference, must be addressed.

‘‘But dismantling a programme without putting a functional alternative in place has exposed the industry to precisely the production challenges it was designed to overcome’’.

Cotonou smuggling challenge

Commenting on the influx of cheaper imported rice, which local millers say is undermining their ability to compete, Dama described the situation as an open secret, alleging that more than 2.5 million tonnes of foreign rice entered Nigeria through the Benin Republic’s Cotonou port and porous land borders so far in 2026.

He claimed that imported rice sells for between N52,000 and N60,000 per 50kg bag, compared with N75,000 to N80,000 for locally produced rice.

The price difference makes foreign rice attractive to consumers, particularly households struggling with the rising cost of living.

More troubling, according to him, is his allegation that some lower quality imported rice is repackaged and sold as Nigerian rice in major markets across Lagos, Abuja, Kano and Ibadan.

If the allegation is established, it points to a serious enforcement failure, with implications for consumer confidence, local investment and government revenue.

The tariff differential between Nigeria and Benin Republic is also contributing to the problem.

According to Dama, Nigeria imposes a 70 per cent duty, compared with 35 per cent in Benin, creating an incentive for traders to route rice imports through the neighbouring country.

He therefore called for the implementation of the ECOWAS Rice Roadmap 2025-2035, which provides for a common external tariff of 35 per cent for paddy and 50 per cent for milled rice across the 15 member states.

‘‘A harmonised regional tariff, combined with technology-driven border surveillance, could reduce the incentive for smuggling’’, Dama said.

Lagos Lake Rice disappears

The disappearance of Lake Rice from Lagos markets offers another illustration of the difficulty of sustaining agricultural partnerships beyond their initial political appeal.

In 2016, Lagos and Kebbi states entered into a Memorandum of Understanding to promote rice production in Kebbi and processing and distribution in Lagos.

The arrangement was designed to transport paddy from Kebbi to Lagos, where it would be milled, packaged and sold to consumers.

The initiative was intended to connect farmers in the North with a major consumer market in the South. But the arrangement eventually collapsed.

Investigations by Vanguard indicated that personal interests undermined the original agreement.

Lagos State Governor Babajide Sanwo-Olu’s Special Adviser on Agriculture and Food Systems, Dr Oluwarotimi Fashola, said the initiative was discontinued because the original understanding between the two states was not followed. According to him, the agreement was for Kebbi to supply paddy to Lagos for milling and packaging, rather than for finished rice supplied by a private consulting firm to be repackaged and distributed as Lake Rice.

The industry stakeholders said the collapse of the arrangement underscores the importance of transparency, accountability and strict adherence to agreed terms in public-private agricultural partnerships.

They also said it illustrates how potentially beneficial agricultural arrangements can fail when institutional interests and implementation shortcomings undermine their original objectives.

Women farmers and the financing gap

The consequences of the collapse of agricultural financing are also being felt by women farmers, particularly in Kebbi State.

The Chairperson of Kebbi State Female Farmers Associations, Hajia Hadiza Kola, identified inadequate funding as a major obstacle to expanding agricultural production following the end of the Anchor Borrowers’ Programme.

She said women faced additional social challenges because farming was traditionally regarded in parts of the state as an occupation largely reserved for men.

Some women also struggle to obtain the support of their husbands to participate in commercial farming.

Nevertheless, advocacy activities across towns and villages have encouraged hundreds of women to register with female farmers’ associations and take up farming, including through home gardening.

Their experience highlights the importance of making agricultural financing accessible to women and other groups that may be excluded from conventional farming arrangements.

Without affordable credit, the potential contribution of women to Nigeria’s food production drive will remain constrained.

Other failed rice project

Amidst the failures recorded in rice projects across Northern parts there are other fortune reversals of the Nigerian rice value-chain in other regions that grow the commodity.

The government of Chief Martin Elechi in Ebonyi State established modern rice cluster mills in three senatorial districts, located at Izzi, Ikwo and Oso Edda around 2013.

The mills started with very big expectation to complement the existing Abakaliki rice mill with morden machines. The mill started simultaneously churning out foreign-like polished rice and with good packaging with the brand name EbonyRice. But the mills have turned to ghosts of themselves as at 2025.

A former worker at the mill Mr. Onyeka Ndukwe Nkama, told Vanguard that Governor Elechi’s administration handed over the mills to Chief David Umahi who handed over a dying project to the present administration.

The modern mills started closing down one after the other starting from the mill at Oso Edda to Ikwo and now the Izzi mill has finally shutdown.

Nkama stated: “The managers had complained of lack of enough Paddy to feed the mills, they said that Ebonyi Rice farmers could not produce enough rice to run three mills. At some time, they were sourcing rice Paddy from the northern part of the country to feed the mills but to no avail.

“So, after some time some parts of the machines started rusting and could not perform effectively. So, gradually the mills started packing up. I learnt that the mill at Izzi that worked last but I’m not sure whether it still processing rice. For some time now all the workers at the mills had left to look for other jobs.” Chief Charles Ugwu established a private rice mill at Ikwo which produced high quality rice branded as Ebony Gold and Ebony Silver. The mill has also shut down due to similar Paddy problems.

Emma Ujah, Abuja Bureau Chief, Jeff Agbodo (Abakiliki), Aliyu Usman (Birnin Kebbi) & Sukanmi Akanni (Lagos) contributed to this report.

Vanguard News

World.title: Gov. Mutfwang loses brother
World.content:
Plateau State Governor, Caleb Mutfwang

By Golok Nanmwa

Plateau State Governor, Caleb Manasseh Mutfwang, has lost his elder brother, Arc. Morris Manasseh Mutfwang, who died Sunday night following a protracted illness, family sources have disclosed.

The Plateau State Government confirmed the death on Monday, as the State Executive Council and the Plateau State Inter-Religious Council paid separate condolence visits to the Governor’s family at the Government House, Jos.

The Deputy Governor, Ngo Josephine Piyo, who led members of the State Executive Council on a condolence visit to the Governor’s Residence at the Old Government House, Jos, described the deceased as “a distinguished personality, a devoted family man, a lover of peace and a patriotic Nigerian who made meaningful contributions to public service.”

She said the Council received the news of his passing “with profound shock and sadness,” noting that his death was “not only a painful loss to the Mutfwang family but also a significant loss to Plateau State and the nation, given his contributions to society and his exemplary life.”

Piyo prayed for the peaceful repose of his soul and asked Almighty God to grant the Governor, the bereaved family and all those mourning his demise “the strength, grace and fortitude to bear the tragic loss.”

In a separate visit, the Plateau State Inter-Religious Council also condoled with the Governor and his family over the death of Arc. Morris Manasseh Mutfwang.

The delegation, led by the Emir of Wase, Alhaji (Dr.) Muhammadu Sambo Haruna, who spoke on behalf of the Council’s Co-Chairman, Rev. Prof. Pandam Yamsat, described the deceased’s passing as “a painful loss to the family and the state.”

Haruna acknowledged the inevitability of death as part of the human experience, urging the bereaved family to “find solace in the sovereignty and wisdom of Almighty God.”

He also prayed that God would grant the family “the comfort, strength and resilience needed to navigate this difficult period.”

Responding on behalf of the family during the separate condolence visits, Mr. Jonathan Mutfwang expressed “profound appreciation to both delegations for their thoughtful gesture, solidarity and prayers.”

He noted that their presence had brought “considerable comfort and encouragement to the bereaved family at this difficult time.”

Jonathan also prayed for God’s continued protection, blessings and preservation upon members of the delegations.

The family disclosed that the burial of the late Arc. Morris Manasseh Mutfwang has been scheduled for Thursday, November 26, 2026.

The condolence visits were disclosed in a statement signed by the Director of Press and Public Affairs to the Governor, Gyang Bere, PhD, and made available to newsmen in Jos on Monday.

World.title: South-East governors are with me, working for my re-election — Tinubu
World.content:
By Johnbosco Agbakwuru

Ahead of the January 16 presidential election, President Bola Tinubu on Monday told the Igbo community in Lagos and their leaders that all the South-East governors are with him on the journey to make Nigeria a better place and are working for his re-election.

The President said he was excited and that he would go home happy and eat because of their endorsement of his second term.

He thanked the Igbo communities and business leaders in Lagos for their resolve to support his re-election on January 16, 2027.

He assured them of his administration’s commitment to inclusive governance, national unity and equity for all Nigerians.

President Tinubu gave the assurance while addressing youths, elders and leaders of Ndigbo during a town hall meeting organised

by the Ndigbo National Dialogue and Development Initiatives at the Wole Soyinka Centre for Culture and the Creative Arts, Iganmu, Lagos State.

He called on Ndigbo to strengthen their unity, deepen their participation in national politics, and work with other ethnic groups to build a peaceful, prosperous and united Nigeria.

To reaffirm his commitment to national unity, President Tinubu joined the gathering to sing the national anthem a second time.

“I didn’t believe you would turn out this many; I am very, very happy. May God bless you, and may God continue to guide and bless our country. It is a great honour for me to be here before you as your president.

“I can commit to one thing: the unity of Nigeria. Though tribes and tongues may differ, in brotherhood we stand. None of us told God where we would be born or what language we would speak when we were born. Whether you are Igbo or Hausa, you have no

control over yourself. God created you and created that opportunity. We are all Nigerians.

“Let’s see ourselves as individuals living in the same house, geographically called Nigeria,” the President told the gathering.

The President said his administration recognises the significant contributions of the Igbo communities to Nigeria’s economic growth, assuring them that no section of the country would be left behind under the Renewed Hope Agenda.

President Tinubu appreciated the leadership of all the market leaders in Lagos for leaving their businesses to be at the gathering.

“To all of you, I am grateful for one thing: that you are here this afternoon. You left your businesses and money-making opportunities to come and listen to the president, and I must say thank you,” he said.

The President expressed his determination to consolidate his administration’s economic gains.

He said national development requires collective commitment, mutual understanding and cooperation, urging the Igbo community to embrace dialogue and constructive engagement to address challenges and advance their interests within the Nigerian federation.

A statement by the presidential spokesman, Bayo Onanuga said: “President Tinubu told the gathering that all the South-East

governors are with him on the journey to make Nigeria a better place and are working for his re-election.”

He mentioned Chief Chidi Anyeagbu, owner of Chisco Motors; Dave Umahi; Doris Uzoka-Anite; and Nkeiruka Onyejeocha, who were at the gathering, as people with whom he has close connections.

President Tinubu explained some of the reasons behind his policies, such as ensuring that tertiary institutions are no longer paralysed by union strikes.

“To eliminate the crisis in the universities, to build good roads and train the engineers who will maintain our cars, our children must be in school. Just because they are poor doesn’t mean they must not go to university or develop.

“We are doing that with NELFUND. The university is stable today because we are doing well. We are putting money into agriculture and trading, and anyone in the trade business can apply to the Bank of Industry and get a loan; anyone in agriculture can take a small farmers’ loan.

“We have to maintain this country for the sake of every one of us. The critical line in our national anthem is what I’m standing here for. I begged for it, and I am ready to serve.

“And I served the first term. The constitution says I can ask for a second term. I want a second term. As you are here today, you make me happy, you make me excited, and I will go home happy and eat akpu,” he said.

President Tinubu also called on Ndigbo residents in Lagos to participate actively and vote for him, APC governorship candidate Obafemi Hamzat, and other APC candidates in the 2027 general elections.

He commended the organisers of the town hall meeting for providing a platform for constructive engagement between the Federal Government and the Igbo community.

On his part, the host governor, Babajide Sanwo-Olu, rallied members of the Ndigbo to support President Bola Tinubu’s re-election bid, assuring the President of massive votes from the state in the January 16, 2027, presidential election.

Sanwo-Olu described the turnout of Igbo leaders, traders and business owners as proof that Lagos residents were united behind the President, despite the meeting being held on a Monday, when many participants had to leave their businesses to attend.

The governor urged the community to sustain the unity and support, saying Lagos would deliver an unprecedented number of votes for Tinubu.

He also praised Tinubu as a detribalised Nigerian and nationalist, saying his administration had promoted development across the six geopolitical zones and strengthened national unity.

Sanwo-Olu further commended the President for what he described as economic stability, increased investment and opportunities for young people, while thanking him for his contributions to Lagos State.

Describing the gathering as a reflection of the “One Lagos” spirit, the governor said the presence of people from different ethnic backgrounds demonstrated that residents could work together in support of a common political cause.

In her remarks, the convener of the meeting and Minister of State for Budget and Economic Planning, Dr Doris Uzoka-Anite, declared the Igbo community’s commitment in Lagos State to supporting President Tinubu’s re-election bid, saying the community had resolved to unite behind his leadership.

She said the Ndigbo had commenced grassroots mobilisation across Lagos State, with structures established at the polling-unit level ahead of the 2027 presidential election.

Also speaking, the former Minister of State for Labour and Employment, Hon. Nkeiruka Onyejeocha, assured President Bola Tinubu of the Ndigbo’s support for his 2027 re-election bid, saying the gathering of Igbo leaders and stakeholders in Lagos demonstrated their unity and commitment to the President.

She said the community had recognised the importance of building political alliances with other geopolitical zones to achieve its future presidential ambition.

The leader of the Ndigbo Traders Association in Lagos, Prince Tony Nwakeze, pledged the members’ support for President Bola Tinubu’s re-election bid, while appealing for access to loans at a 5 per cent interest rate to help traders transition from importation to local manufacturing.

Nwakeze said traders from Alaba, Trade Fair and Ladipo markets were seeking financial support to empower young people and expand their businesses.

He also assured the President that traders were prepared to organise themselves and adopt a cross-guarantee arrangement to ensure repayment of any loans granted to their members.

He also pledged that the market leadership would honour agreements reached with the government, stressing that traders had learnt from previous misunderstandings and were committed to sustaining a cordial relationship with the Lagos State Government.

He thanked the President for attending the meeting and promised that traders across Lagos markets would support him and honour every agreement reached with the government.

“We, the market people, will stand with you, support you and honour every agreement we enter into today,” he said.

World.title: Delta govt imposes curfew in Ughelli North after campaign rally violence
World.content:
The Delta State Government has imposed a dusk-to-dawn curfew in Ughelli North Local Government Area following reported violence at a campaign rally of the National Democratic Congress (NDC) in Uduere Community, which allegedly left some people dead and several others injured.

The curfew, which takes effect from 6:00 p.m. to 6:00 a.m. daily, will remain in force until further notice.

The Delta State Police Command disclosed this in a statement issued on Monday by its Police Public Relations Officer, SP Bright Edafe.

According to the statement, the police have commenced investigations to establish the circumstances surrounding the incident and identify those responsible.

The Command urged residents to comply strictly with the curfew and cooperate with security personnel to maintain peace and public safety.

The statement reads, “The Command therefore urges residents of Ughelli North Local Government Area to comply strictly with the curfew imposed by the Delta State Government, restricting movement between 1800hrs to 0600hrs until further notice. Residents are advised to remain calm and cooperate with security personnel in the interest of public safety.

“The Commissioner of Police, Delta State Command, CP Samuel E. Erale, psc, mnips, has directed intensified security operations in the affected area to prevent further violence and maintain law and order. The CP has ordered a full-scale investigation and assures residents of the state that anyone found culpable will face the full weight of the law, irrespective of political affiliation or status, and urges members of the public to provide credible information to assist ongoing investigations.”

Erale also extended his condolences to the families of those who died and wished the injured a speedy recovery.

He reaffirmed the Command’s commitment to protecting lives and property while ensuring a peaceful environment for lawful

political activities.

The police commissioner further warned political actors and their supporters against thuggery, intimidation and the unlawful use of firearms.

He stressed that political differences must never be allowed to degenerate into violence or loss of lives.

Vanguard News

World.title: 89 fall ill after unknown substance released at UK Arena concert
World.content:
Thousands of concertgoers were evacuated from the UK’s largest indoor arena after the release of an “unknown substance”, with dozens reporting suffering side effects, police said Monday.

Some 12,000 people were attending the Sunday night show by US rapper Don Toliver at the Co-op Live arena in Manchester, northwest England.

“A total of 89 people displayed symptoms believed to be linked to exposure,” Manchester police said, adding one woman was taken to hospital for treatment.

“Enquiries remain ongoing to establish the nature of the substance, where it came from and any associated risk,” Assistant Chief Constable Tom Harding said in a statement.

Toliver said he had postponed his Monday night London show following the incident, which led to one person being taken to hospital.

Emergency services were called after “reports of people in the crowd suffering effects from an unknown substance”, Manchester police said, declaring a major incident at the scene.

The venue, which bills itself as the country’s largest live entertainment arena, said it was working with police to “identify the cause of the incident”.

The regional ambulance service said it assessed more than 50 people, including some reporting “eye and respiratory symptoms”.

Toliver, who was nominated for five Grammy Awards last week, is currently on the second leg of his “Nitrous” world tour.

He announced he was rescheduling his show at London’s O2 arena due to an “unfortunate incident last night (in) Manchester”.

“My heart and prayers are with everyone that was injured last night,” Toliver said on Instagram, without providing more details.

Concertgoers told the BBC that people were “choking” and coughing, recalling “distressing scenes” of people leaving the venue in a panic.

Some criticised the lack of security checks at the venue, especially in a city still scarred by the 2017 Manchester Arena bombing, which killed 22 people at an Ariana Grande concert.

World.title: NDC: Tinubu’s Lagos Record Was Industrialised Taxation, Not Economic Transformation
World.content:
Follow THISDAYLIVE on Google Add us as a preferred source to see more of our stories in Google 

* Party accuses president of replicating alleged opaque fiscal practices at national level

Sunday Aborisade in Abuja

The Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) has criticised President Bola Tinubu’s record as governor of Lagos State, describing his administration’s fiscal policies as a system of industrialised taxation rather than economic transformation.

The party, which accused the president of failing to translate Lagos State’s substantial revenue earnings into commensurate infrastructure and social development, said his record in the state should not be presented as a model for national economic transformation ahead of the January 2027 presidential election.

The NDC National Campaign Council, in a statement issued Monday and signed by its Deputy Spokesperson, Sony Neme, challenged promoters of Tinubu’s presidential ambition to explain how the enormous revenue generated by Lagos during his administration was utilised.

It argued that the economic foundations of Lagos, including the Apapa and Tin Can Island seaports, Murtala Muhammed International Airport and the Third Mainland Bridge, predated Tinubu’s administration, noting that most of the infrastructure was developed by the Federal Government before 1991.

According to the party, Lagos’ economic growth was largely driven by its inherited infrastructure and the entrepreneurial activities of Nigerians from across the country, rather than the policies of any particular governor since 1999.

“Peel away the carefully manufactured folklore, and citizens across the country have every right to ask: where is Lagos money?” the statement queried.

The opposition party alleged that what emerged under successive administrations in Lagos after 1999 was an aggressive revenue-generation system rather than the industrialisation and broad-based economic development being projected by the president’s supporters.

It maintained that despite the substantial amounts generated through Internally Generated Revenue (IGR) and Value Added Tax (VAT), alongside considerable borrowing, the state continued to grapple with infrastructure deficiencies and inadequate social services.

The NDC also raised questions about the reported outsourcing of Lagos State’s tax collection to Alpha-Beta Consulting, allegedly at a 10 per cent commission.

It cited court filings in 2020 which allegedly raised questions about more than N20 billion in unauthorised transfers, as well as past Senate testimony by former Chairman of the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC), Nuhu Ribadu, in which he reportedly described corruption allegations involving the former Lagos governor as being of an “international dimension”.

However, the party did not provide further details of the judicial proceedings or establish the outcome of the allegations in its statement.

It further contrasted the development of luxury projects such as Eko Atlantic City with the challenges confronting several mainland communities, including recurrent flooding, inadequate healthcare facilities and the unfulfilled promise of the Fourth Mainland Bridge.

The NDC argued that Lagos, as Nigeria’s commercial nerve centre, should be benchmarked against major African cities such as Cairo, Kigali, Algiers, Rabat, Nairobi and Cape Town, rather than assessed solely against other Nigerian cities.

The campaign council expressed concern that the president was allegedly reproducing at the national level the fiscal management approach it attributed to his administration in Lagos.

It listed mounting public debt, increased taxation and what it described as inadequate transparency as some of the challenges confronting Nigerians under the Tinubu administration.

The party argued that these policies had imposed additional burdens on citizens without corresponding improvements in their living conditions and infrastructure.

“Even more concerning, President Tinubu has now transported this exact opaque style of fiscal management to the national level, where mounting debt, heavy taxation, and lack of transparency continue to burden citizens without commensurate development,” it stated.

The NDC, therefore, called on Nigerians to scrutinise the president’s governance record in Lagos and at the national level as the country approaches the January 2027 general election.

It urged voters to consider the party’s presidential ticket of Peter Obi and Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso, whom it said represented its proposed alternative of transparent and people-centred governance.

World.title: Bayelsa Boat Mishap: Youth Group Mourns Victims, Advocates Safety Measures
World.content:
Follow THISDAYLIVE on Google Add us as a preferred source to see more of our stories in Google 

Blessing Ibunge in Port Harcourt

The Niger Delta Ethnic Nationalities Youth Leaders Forum (NDENYLF) has expressed grief over the boat mishap in Southern Ijaw Local Government Area of Bayelsa State, calling for intensified rescue operations and stronger enforcement of maritime safety regulations.

The Forum, in a statement Monday by its spokesman, Legborsi Yamaabana, described the incident as a painful loss to the Ijaw nation and the wider Niger Delta, while commiserating with the affected families and communities.

The incident reportedly occurred on Friday, November 20, 2026, when a passenger boat travelling from Ayama to Ukubie for a burial ceremony capsized around 11 a.m. near the river junction between Oweikorogha and Otuan/Angiama communities in Southern Ijaw.

Reports said several passengers were feared dead or missing following the incident, while the Bayelsa State Police Command, through its spokesperson, DSP Musa Mohammed, reportedly confirmed the recovery of four bodies as rescue efforts continued.

Yamaabana said the Forum’s thoughts were with families awaiting information about their relatives, stressing that the tragedy had affected the entire Niger Delta.

“This is a very sad day for the Ijaw nation and the entire Niger Delta. Our hearts are heavy, particularly when we consider the families who left their homes expecting their loved ones to return, only to be confronted with this devastating uncertainty and loss,” he said.

He added that NDENYLF stood in solidarity with the affected communities and prayed for the safe recovery of anyone who might still be missing.

The Forum commended emergency responders, community volunteers and other persons involved in the rescue operation, urging the Bayelsa State Government and relevant agencies to sustain the search for survivors and provide timely information and support to the affected families.

NDENYLF also called on maritime regulatory and safety authorities to investigate the circumstances surrounding the mishap and strengthen enforcement of passenger safety measures, including the use of life jackets and compliance with applicable passenger-carrying requirements.

Yamaabana said the safety of water transportation was particularly important in the Niger Delta, where waterways remain critical to the movement and livelihoods of millions of residents.

“Moments such as this demand compassion, unity and collective responsibility. When tragedy strikes one constituent nationality, the pain is felt across the entire region,” he said.

The Forum urged traditional rulers, political leaders, community organisations and other stakeholders across the Niger Delta to support the bereaved families and affected communities.

World.title: Foundation to Provide 500 Free Medical Outreach to Immortalise Late Gobir in Ilorin
World.content:
Follow THISDAYLIVE on Google Add us as a preferred source to see more of our stories in Google 

Hammed Shittu in Ilorin

The Gobir Trust Foundation has concluded plans to provide free medical outreach to over 500 indigenes of Ilorin, Kwara State capital, as part of a move to remember the 30th year anniversary of the death of the scion of Gobir family, Ambassador Abubakar Garba Gobir.

Late Gobir died in 1996 after retiring from public service where he served as Nigeria’s Ambassador to Togo, India, Burma (now Myanmar), Thailand, Sri Lanka, Sweden, Norway, Finland and Denmark.

His family however deemed it fit to unveil a foundation tagged Gobir Trust Foundation so as to continue with the legacy of the late diplomat.

A statement issued in Ilorin on Monday by the organisers said that the unveiling of the foundation would assist the family in remembering late Gobir not only for the offices he held, but also for the values he represented and the legacy of service he left behind.

The statement said a two-day programme, scheduled for Friday, November 27, and Saturday, November 28, 2026, will feature special prayers, the inauguration of the newly completed Sarkin Gobir Mosque, the public unveiling of the Gobir Trust Foundation and a free medical outreach targeting 500 beneficiaries.

The activities will take place at the Sarkin Gobir Compound, Ilorin, exactly three decades after the ambassador’s passing.

Beyond the remembrance of the distinguished father and patriarch, the foundation stated that the anniversary offers an opportunity to reflect on the contributions of a generation of Nigerian public servants whose commitment to education, professionalism and national development helped shape the institutions of modern Nigeria.

The foundation therefore pledged to continue with the legacies of the late diplomat to the people of Ilorin Emirate.

World.title: APC Flays Fake INEC Letter, Describes It As Desperate, Reckless
World.content:
Follow THISDAYLIVE on Google Add us as a preferred source to see more of our stories in Google 

Adedayo Akinwale in Abuja

The All Progressives Congress (APC) has condemned in the strongest possible terms a purported letter circulating on social media, allegedly written by the National Chairman of the party, Prof. Nentawe Yilwatda, to the Chairman of the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) directing the commission to ensure the victory of President Bola Tinubu in the 2027 presidential election.

Yilwatda, in a statement issued Monday by his Special Adviser on Media and Information Strategy, Abimbola Tooki, described the letter titled, ‘Preparations for the 2027 Presidential Election and Ensuring the Victory of President Bola Ahmed Tinubu’ as desperate and reckless.

The chairman noted that the unsigned letter, dated November 22, 2026, contained an outrageous and entirely fabricated claim that the APC leadership expects INEC to deploy its institutional mechanisms, administrative frameworks and operational capacities to ensure the declaration of President Tinubu as the winner of the 2027 presidential election.

The party categorically stated that the purported letter did not emanate from Yilwatda, was not authored by him, and has absolutely nothing to do with the national chairman or his office.

Yilwatda noted: “It is a fraudulent document, a malicious fabrication and a reckless attempt to impugn the integrity of the national chairman, the APC and the democratic process.”

The chairman maintained that the writer of the shameful document has demonstrated a disturbing level of irresponsibility, dishonesty and desperation by attempting to manufacture a scandal around the APC leadership and the nation’s electoral institution.

He added: “The decision to circulate such an explosive allegation under the guise of an official communication, without a signature, authentication or any credible indication of its origin, exposes the hollowness, deceit and cowardice of its author.

“The absence of a signature is particularly telling. It is a glaring indication of the writer’s lack of credibility, accountability and seriousness, and reinforces the suspicion that the document was deliberately concocted to mislead the public, provoke needless controversy and damage the reputation of the party’s national chairman.

“Beyond its fraudulent content, the purported letter is a gross departure from the established internal procedures, communication protocols and administrative processes of the APC.”

Yilwatda stressed that it is inconceivable that a communication of such grave significance would be issued by the national chairman outside the established channels and procedures of the party.

He said: “The document is therefore not only false but also fundamentally inconsistent with the institutional processes and standards of the APC.

“The APC will not allow faceless individuals, political mischief-makers and purveyors of fabricated information to drag its leadership into disrepute through the circulation of fictitious documents.

“We condemn the author of this despicable letter in the strongest possible terms and challenge those responsible to come out of hiding, take ownership of their actions and provide verifiable evidence for their claims, rather than hiding behind anonymity to spread falsehoods and create distrust in democratic institutions.”

For the avoidance of doubt, Yilwatda said the APC remained firmly committed to a peaceful, transparent, free and fair electoral process in the forthcoming 2027 general election.

He stressed that the ruling party believes in the sanctity of the ballot, the independence of INEC and the right of Nigerians to freely choose their leaders without intimidation, manipulation or interference.

“President Bola Ahmed Tinubu himself has consistently demonstrated his commitment to democratic principles. At campaign rallies and public engagements across the country, the president has repeatedly urged Nigerians, particularly eligible voters, to obtain their Permanent Voter Cards (PVCs) and exercise their civic responsibility,” Yilwatda said.

He emphasised that this was a clear demonstration of his confidence in the democratic process and his belief that electoral legitimacy must come from the will of the people, freely expressed through the ballot.

The chairman said the APC is a party that respects democratic institutions, upholds constitutional order and believes that electoral victory must be earned through the support and mandate of Nigerians.

“No fabricated letter, malicious insinuation or desperate attempt at political blackmail will distract us from our commitment to democratic values, peaceful elections and the continued engagement of Nigerians in the electoral process,” Yilwatda insisted.

He urged the public, the media and all Nigerians to disregard the purported letter in its entirety and refrain from giving credence to a document that is unsigned, unauthenticated and wholly disowned by the national chairman.

The chairman said the APC would continue to campaign on its record, its vision and its commitment to the Nigerian people.

Yilwatda assured Nigerians that the party would approach the 2027 elections with confidence, discipline and respect for the democratic process, saying the party remained convinced that the ultimate decision rests with the Nigerian electorate.

He said the APC would not be intimidated by fabricated documents, nor would it be drawn into the sinister agenda of faceless individuals seeking to undermine its leadership and democratic institutions.

World.title: N’Delta: Coastal Communities Seek Increased Investment in Blue Economy
World.content:
Follow THISDAYLIVE on Google Add us as a preferred source to see more of our stories in Google 

Blessing Ibunge in Port Harcourt

Stakeholders from creek communities across Nigeria have called for special development plan for coastal settlements and increased investment in the blue economy to unlock the economic potential of the Niger Delta.

The demand formed part of the resolutions contained in a 30-point communiqué issued after the 2026 Creek to Creek Movement Summit held in Port Harcourt, Rivers State.

The summit, organised by the Creek-to-Creek Movement to unite creek communities, empower youths and women and promote sustainable development, was themed ‘Unity, Prosperity and Renewed Hope Across the Creeks.’

The communiqué, signed by the Founder/Director-General of the movement, Chief Mike Ayapaye, and Deputy Director-General, Okiemute Onovughakpo, stressed that creek communities were not merely remote settlements but critical components of Nigeria’s economic development.

“Nigeria cannot fully realise its economic potential while neglecting the creeks which help to sustain it,” the communiqué stated.

The stakeholders argued that the creeks and waterways connect coastal communities to the Atlantic economy and should therefore occupy a strategic position in the Federal Government’s blue economy agenda.

They called for increased investment in commercial fisheries, aquaculture, fish processing, marine transportation, port services, shipbuilding and repairs, coastal tourism, renewable energy and marine research.

The summit also advocated a shift from subsistence fishing to modern deep-sea commercial fisheries through access to technology, cold storage, processing facilities, financing and markets.

On infrastructure, the stakeholders commended state governors for efforts to improve water transportation and urged the Federal Government to ensure the completion of the 750-kilometre Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway as originally planned, alongside the 415-kilometre East-West Road.

The movement further called for environmental restoration to be treated as an economic priority, with stronger pollution prevention, remediation, mangrove restoration, improved waste management, coastal protection and climate adaptation.

It also urged the private sector to invest deliberately in peaceful and prosperous host communities while encouraging successful sons and daughters of the creeks to channel investments back into their communities.

The summit noted that development of the region should extend beyond oil and gas to include modular refineries, power generation, mini-LNG, LPG, CNG, petrochemicals and fertiliser industries.

Recalling the 1957 Willinks Commission, the stakeholders said its recommendation for special treatment of the Niger Delta remained relevant nearly seven decades later.

Earlier, Ayapaye said the movement was founded on the belief that every creek community deserved to be recognised and included in national development.

“Creek to Creek means that when one creek rises, all creeks must rise too. When one child succeeds, it becomes a victory for all of us,” he said.

The summit also resolved to establish a Niger Delta Investment and Development Fund to mobilise and invest resources from government, the private sector, communities, corporate organisations and development partners under appropriate regulatory oversight.

World.title: Coalition Urges Tinubu to Sack NPA MD Over Alleged Poor Governance, Mounting Controversies
World.content:
Follow THISDAYLIVE on Google Add us as a preferred source to see more of our stories in Google 

A Coalition of Maritime and Energy Consultants in Nigerian has called on President Bola Ahmed Tinubu to remove the Managing Director of the Nigerian Ports Authority (NPA), Dr. Abubakar Dantsoho, accusing him of poor governance, administrative shortcomings and failure to adequately reposition the nation’s ports since assuming office in July 2024.

The coalition argued that the president’s determination to transform Nigeria’s maritime sector and establish the country as a leading maritime and logistics hub requires competent, transparent and result-oriented leadership at the NPA, insisting that retaining Dantsoho could undermine the administration’s ambitious reform agenda.

The spokesperson, who signed a press statement on behalf of various groups, Mr. Danjuma Yakubu, alleged that the NPA under the current management had become associated with a succession of controversies, procurement questions, institutional accountability concerns and operational challenges, rather than the decisive transformation expected from an agency central to Nigeria’s economic development.

The group specifically cited the controversy surrounding the reported $25 million emergency dredging contract for the Warri-Escravos Channel in 2025, which attracted questions over the procurement process, the emergency justification and the extent of compliance with established public procurement requirements.

Although the NPA subsequently defended the contract, insisting that due process was followed under the Public Procurement Act, the coalition maintained that the controversy reinforced the need for greater transparency.

It also referenced “media investigations questioning the NPA’s multi-billion-naira budgetary allocations, particularly expenditures relating to dredging, consultancy services, environmental sanitation, conferences and other administrative activities”.

According to the coalition, “The scale of such allocations demands independent scrutiny, comprehensive disclosure and demonstrable evidence of value for public money.

“Another major concern is the unresolved controversy surrounding expired port concession agreements and terminal leases. Recent investigations have revealed that several terminal operators continue to operate under agreements that expired years ago, with some dating back to 2016 and 2021. The absence of published terminal-by-terminal performance audits and clear timelines for concluding the reviews has further heightened concerns about transparency and regulatory certainty.

“Such prolonged uncertainty over concession agreements could discourage fresh investments, delay terminal modernisation, weaken competition and deprive the government of potential revenue. It questioned why a critical institution such as the NPA should continue to operate within an environment where fundamental contractual and regulatory issues remain unresolved.”

It also.stated that there were also reports of procurement-related disputes and alleged administrative lapses involving the Authority, including questions raised by contractors and other stakeholders.

The coalition said reported controversies, alongside parliamentary oversight concerns, reinforced the need for an independent assessment of the management’s stewardship.

On operational efficiency, it said it is very ridiculous that Nigerian Ports continue to suffer from congestion, high charges, prolonged cargo clearance and inadequate infrastructure, despite the passage of considerable time since Dantsoho’s appointment.

The coalition stated that industry reports have put cargo dwell time at Apapa and Tin Can Island ports at between 18 and 21 days, compared with a global benchmark of approximately four days, while port charges have been reported to be 30 to 40 per cent higher than those of competing regional ports.

“Also, our coalition is in great worries over the concerns raised by the Presidential Enabling Business Environment Council over the economic losses associated with persistent port inefficiencies. The continued challenges undermine the government’s efforts to improve the business environment, reduce the cost of doing business and attract foreign investment,” the statement read further.

The coalition maintained that the combination of procurement controversies, concession uncertainties, administrative concerns and operational inefficiencies raises serious questions about the capacity of the current NPA leadership to deliver the institutional transformation required at this critical moment in the country’s maritime development.
