It recalled that President Tinubu had demonstrated renewed commitment to expanding Nigeria’s maritime infrastructure, including the November 2026 approval of the Ibom Deep Seaport in Akwa Ibom State and the development of the Bakassi Deep Seaport in Cross River State.

The president also approved the full operationalisation of the Tsamiya Inland Dry Port in Kebbi State, while the Federal Government has approved the modernisation of Onne, Rivers, Delta and Calabar ports, in addition to the Apapa and Tin Can Island modernisation programme.

According to the coalition, “These initiatives represent significant opportunities for economic diversification, employment generation, regional trade expansion and increased government revenue.”

It, however, warned that: “Infrastructure investments alone would not deliver the desired results without a competent NPA management capable of coordinating the projects, attracting investors, enforcing concession agreements and ensuring efficient port operations.”

It therefore urged President Tinubu to look beyond political considerations and appoint a more capable maritime professional with proven administrative competence, integrity and a clear understanding of contemporary port management.

“Such an individual must be prepared to confront entrenched inefficiencies, enforce accountability, accelerate digital transformation and establish an investor-friendly environment across the nation’s maritime corridors,” the coalition suggested.

The group stressed that President Tinubu’s Renewed Hope Agenda must not be jeopardised by avoidable leadership shortcomings in strategic government institutions, warning that the “NPA cannot afford to become the weakest link in an administration that has publicly demonstrated its ambition to reposition Nigeria’s maritime economy”.

It consequently appealed to the president to “consider an immediate leadership change at the Nigerian Ports Authority”, insisting that “the country needs a new direction, fresh energy and accountable leadership capable of translating the president’s maritime vision into measurable results”.

The coalition maintained that the removal of Dantsoho would send a strong message that the Tinubu administration would not compromise institutional performance and public accountability in its quest for lasting reforms.

World.title: IPOB Suspects Voluntarily Confessed to Killing DSS Officer, Legal Aid Lawyer Tells Court
World.content:
Follow THISDAYLIVE on Google Add us as a preferred source to see more of our stories in Google 

A Deputy Director of the Legal Aid Council of Nigeria (LACON) on Monday told the Federal High Court in Abuja that four suspected members of the outlawed Indigenous People of Biafra (IPOB), standing trial for the alleged kidnapping and killing of a Department of State Services (DSS) operative, Ekpeyong Owoh, voluntarily confessed to the crime.

The lawyer, Mmaduabuchi, who is attached to LACON’s Anambra State office, stated this while testifying as the second prosecution witness (PW-2) in the ongoing trial-within-trial before Justice Joyce Abdulmalik.

She told the court that she witnessed the statement-taking sessions of the four defendants at the DSS office in Awka, Anambra State, including the audio-visual recordings, and maintained that they voluntarily confessed to committing terrorism.

Led in evidence by the Director of Public Prosecutions of the Federation, Rotimi Oyedepo, SAN, the witness said her presence during the sessions was in compliance with the law and that she did not participate in the interrogation of the defendants.

“I only went there because I was supposed to be there to witness the taking of their statements in compliance with the provisions of the constitution,” she said.

She dismissed suggestions that the defendants might have been tortured into making the statements, insisting that her professional responsibility would not permit her to witness such treatment.

“I think it will not be reasonable that I will say that I will be there to witness how they were being tortured as a Deputy Director of Legal Aid Council of Nigeria,” she said.

According to her, all four defendants made their statements voluntarily, adding that their fundamental rights were not violated during the process.

“That was why I was there. They voluntarily made their statements.

“They were asked whether they don’t want to make statements or they want to and if they did not want to, they would have said no, and nothing will happen.

“And if they said no and they were forced, that is when I will protect them,” she explained.

Under cross-examination by counsel to the first and second defendants, K.C. Ekwe, the witness said she had been in legal practice for 21 years.

“I have been practising for 21 years now. I was called in 2003,” she said.

When asked about the official opening hours of the DSS office, she replied: “I don’t work with DSS. I work with Legal Aid Council. So it is somebody who works with DSS that will know that.”

The deputy director reiterated that the council’s responsibility was to defend vulnerable persons in society and protect their rights.

“This work I am doing, I don’t choose to do it. It is the provisions of the law,” she added.

Also responding to questions from Geoffrey Oputa, counsel to the third and fourth defendants, on the circumstances surrounding the statement-taking sessions, the witness said she could not recall the exact dates because of the numerous cases handled by the council daily.

She, however, maintained that the defendants appeared calm and showed no signs of having been beaten or tortured.

“They were okay. They were not looking beaten. They were sound even the DSS that interviewed them joked with them.

“With the kind of job I do, I will not be there while they were being tortured,” she said.

Following the conclusion of her testimony, Justice Abdulmalik discharged the witness from the box.

The trial-within-trial was ordered after the defendants, through their lawyers, challenged the admissibility of their alleged confessional statements, insisting that they were not made voluntarily.

The Federal Government had opened its case on November 11, when a DSS investigator, identified as “AAA” for security reasons, testified as the first prosecution witness and tendered the defendants’ alleged confessional statements and audio-visual recordings.

The four defendants — Michael Okafor, also known as Onyechimeleze; Chinedu Chukwudozie, alias Kante; Chibunna Olisa; and Chigozie Olisa, also known as Ability — are facing a six-count charge bordering on terrorism and kidnapping.

They were arraigned before Justice Abdulmalik on September 28 and pleaded not guilty to the charges.

The prosecution alleged that the defendants conspired to commit acts of terrorism and kidnapped Owoh in 2022 while he was travelling from Port Harcourt, Rivers State, to Awka, Anambra State.

They were further accused of taking the DSS operative hostage and killing him.

The prosecution also accused them of belonging to the proscribed IPOB and its armed wing, the Eastern Security Network (ESN), as well as unlawfully possessing firearms, including an AK-47 rifle and a pump-action gun, in connection with the alleged offences.

Justice Abdulmalik adjourned the matter until December 7 and 8 for the defendants to open and conclude their defence, following an agreement by counsel.

The judge warned that any defence witness who failed to appear on the adjourned dates would have their testimony foreclosed.

World.title: Military Air Interdictions Eliminate 37 Terrorists, Destroy Logistics Assets in North-East
World.content:
Follow THISDAYLIVE on Google Add us as a preferred source to see more of our stories in Google 

Linus Aleke in Abuja

The sustained operational pressure exerted by air assets of the Joint Task Force North-East, Operation Hadin Kai (OPHK), on terrorist elements through a series of intelligence-led precision air strikes across the theatre has resulted in the killing of 37 terrorists and the destruction of their logistics assets, the Nigerian military has said.

The military also disclosed that, between 16 and 23 November 2026, OPHK air assets conducted six precision air strikes across five locations, neutralising 37 terrorists, as confirmed by Battle Damage Assessments (BDA), and destroying four terrorist vehicles.

According to a statement by the Acting Media Information Officer of the Joint Task Force North-East, Operation Hadin Kai, Captain Mohammed Goni, the operations also destroyed a terrorist building and a staging target, disrupted suspected improvised explosive device (IED) activities and further degraded terrorist capabilities, with reports of injuries and the flight of surviving elements from targeted locations.

Captain Goni said the successive air interdiction missions, conducted on the basis of credible intelligence and persistent Intelligence, Surveillance and Reconnaissance (ISR), targeted terrorist movements, hideouts and logistics assets across Monguno Local Government Area (LGA), Kerenoa and Fage in Marte LGA, and the Tumbuma Baba general area of Kukawa LGA.

He gave details of the operations as follows: “On 16 November 2026, following verified intelligence indicating that approximately 40 terrorists were moving north-east of Monguno to attack our troops, a pre-emptive strike was carried out. BDA indicated that 10 terrorists were neutralised, while several others sustained injuries.

“In another operation on 17 November 2026, an ISR asset conducting surveillance over Arina Chiki identified a terrorist staging area where elements were reportedly planning an attack on our defensive positions. A precision air strike was subsequently conducted. BDA confirmed the destruction of the targeted building, with no further movement observed within the structure.

“On 20 November 2026, an Intelligence, Surveillance, Target Acquisition and Reconnaissance (ISTAR) asset conducting surveillance over Kerenoa sighted two terrorist vehicles parked near a tree. The targets were engaged with a precision strike, and subsequent BDA confirmed the destruction of both vehicles.

“Similarly, on 20 November 2026, an ISTAR asset operating over the Fage general area sighted a terrorist vehicle at an identified IED assembly location, where preparations were reportedly under way to lay an ambush along a troop movement route. The vehicle was immediately engaged in a precision strike and successfully destroyed, thereby disrupting terrorist IED-related activities in the area.

“Furthermore, on 23 November 2026, an ISTAR asset conducting surveillance over the Tumbuma Baba general area identified a terrorist vehicle following verified intelligence about terrorist activities in the location. A precision strike was subsequently conducted, with BDA confirming the destruction of the vehicle. Two suspected terrorists were also observed emerging from a nearby life-support structure.

“In a follow-up offensive operation within the Tumbuma area, a persistent ISR asset tracked the two suspected terrorists to a gathering of six other terrorists taking cover under a tree. After additional terrorists joined the gathering, a precision strike was conducted against the identified terrorist position. BDA confirmed the neutralisation of all eight terrorists, with no further movement observed at the location.”

These successes, the spokesperson said, underscored the effectiveness of intelligence-led air operations and sustained ISR in degrading terrorist capabilities and disrupting their movements and logistics across the theatre.

Captain Goni said Operation Hadin Kai commended the professionalism of its air and intelligence components and reaffirmed its commitment to sustained offensive operations in synergy with ground forces to defeat terrorism, restore lasting peace and create a secure environment for socio-economic activities to thrive across the North-East.

The Task Force also urged members of the public to continue providing credible and timely information in support of ongoing operations.

World.title: Residential burglaries up 92% in South Africa’s ostrich capital
World.content:
Oudtshoorn, the Klein Karoo’s largest town, experienced the biggest rise in residential burglaries in the country.

This is according to the South African Police Service’s (SAPS) second-quarter crime statistics.

While this is the largest increase in the nation, it is also part of a worrying trend of rising crime in Oudtshoorn.



Crime is taking over Oudtshoorn

Between July and September, residential burglaries rose 92.2% in Oudtshoorn, known as the ostrich capital of the world.

This type of crime went from being recorded fewer than 5 times a week to being recorded at least 9 times a week.

The police precinct, which has a population of 94 059, recorded only 51 fewer residential burglaries than Mankweng, a town that has more than double its population.

Mankweng, which recorded the most residential burglaries in South Africa, has a population of 220 099.

But the crime spree in Oudtshoorn isn’t limited to residential burglaries.

According to SAPS, thefts rose 64.9%. Commercial crime rose 22%.



Overall, property-related crime rose 35.5%, having overtaken its 2022 peak.

Contact crime is up 13.2%.

Even arson, malicious damage to property, and kidnapping are up.

Police Action on the Decline

Police action has also dropped significantly, over the three months between July and September.

In a separate category, SAPS records crimes that require police action to be detected.

This can happen because of investigations, raids, roadblocks, and other police-initiated action.

During July to September 2025, police recorded 344 drug-related crimes.

However, SAPS’ most recent data shows these crimes dropped 9.3% this year.

Overall, crime detected by the police in Oudtshoorn is down 4.8%, and it’s the lowest it’s been in three years.

Instead, most crime in the police precinct is the result of community reporting.

According to the most recent data, community-reported serious crime is up 26.4%.

World.title: Good news for South Africa as urgently needed medicine reaches Durban port
World.content:
SA has made progress in moving urgently needed medical supplies through one of its busiest ports. Image: SAnews.gov.za

South Africa has made progress in clearing urgently needed medicine shipments delayed at Durban’s port, as efforts intensify to address pharmaceutical supply shortages.

Transnet confirmed on Monday, 23 November, that 18 of the 41 containers carrying critical pharmaceutical products intended for the Department of Health have been cleared and delivered.

The shipments form part of efforts to address medicine shortages linked to delays and congestion at the country’s ports.



More medicine shipments expected in December

According to Transnet, seven additional containers are expected to arrive in South Africa between 23 November and 2 December 2026.

However, there are still outstanding shipments. The shipping line has yet to nominate the 16 containers headed for Durban Gateway Terminal for berthing.

Transnet said it was working closely with Durban Gateway Terminal (DGT) to monitor and prioritise the movement of the affected pharmaceutical products.

The company is also considering berthing and discharging needed pharmaceutical cargo urgently at alternative terminals where necessary.

Why are medicine shipments delayed?

The delays are linked to traffic and logistical challenges at the Port of Durban, which have affected the movement of essential cargo.

The Department of Health provided Transnet with a list of pharmaceutical containers that need urgent evacuation from the port system.



Transnet and DGT subsequently worked together to prioritise these shipments as part of measures announced on 18 November.

The delays have raised concerns about the availability of essential medicines, particularly as medical facilities rely on consistent deliveries to maintain their supplies.

Transnet said it would continue working with the Department of Health, shipping lines and terminal operators to speed up the movement of critical medical supplies.

The latest update does not confirm which specific medicines are contained in the shipments or when all the outstanding products will reach medical facilities.

World.title: Jobs at risk as Continental weighs Gqeberha factory closure
World.content:
A worker handles industrial tyres in a warehouse. This is an illustrative photograph, not the Continental Gqeberha factory. Photo: Quang Nguyen Vinh / Pexels.

Continental is considering closing its tyre factory in Gqeberha, putting about 950 jobs at risk.

The proposal raises fresh concerns about manufacturing in the Eastern Cape, where other major tyre producers have already closed plants.

Continental confirmed the proposal in its 20 November statement. It has started consultations with employees under Section 189A of the Labour Relations Act.



The company has not made a final decision. The announcement therefore does not mean that 950 workers have already lost their jobs.

Why is Continental considering closure?

Continental says low factory utilisation and difficult market conditions have damaged the plant’s long-term prospects.

The company has explored ways to improve competitiveness. However, those efforts have not secured the recovery it needs.

If the proposal proceeds, Continental aims to end local tyre production in early 2027.

The Gqeberha facility has a history dating back to 1947. For decades, it has provided industrial employment and supported the region’s automotive economy.

Continental operates its only African tyre manufacturing plant in Gqeberha. Its possible closure would therefore have implications beyond the Eastern Cape.



However, the company says its South African sales business will continue. The BestDrive retail network would also remain operational.

In other words, a factory shutdown would not mean Continental was leaving South Africa entirely.

Another blow to Eastern Cape manufacturing

The proposal follows Goodyear’s factory closure in nearby Kariega in 2025. That decision raised concerns about job losses and the future of local manufacturing.

In 2020, Bridgestone announced plans to close its Port Elizabeth bias tyre manufacturing plant.

These developments have intensified concerns about the region’s ability to retain specialised manufacturing jobs.

The Nelson Mandela Bay Business Chamber has warned about the impact of losing another major factory.

The economic consequences could extend beyond Continental employees. Local suppliers and service providers may also feel the effects if production ends.

However, the scale of any wider losses remains uncertain. Consultations must take place before the company reaches its final decision.

What happens to Continental’s 950 workers?

Section 189A requires consultations when an employer considers certain large-scale retrenchments.

During this process, the parties can examine alternatives to job losses. They may also discuss ways to reduce the impact on affected employees.

Continental says approximately 950 workers could be affected. That figure refers to jobs at risk, not confirmed dismissals.

The company has invited discussions about alternatives to ending production. It has not announced the outcome of those discussions.

The consultation process will determine whether the plant has a viable future. For workers and their families, the uncertainty is already significant.

Can Continental’s Gqeberha factory and its 950 jobs be saved?

World.title: SASSA reminder: Children’s grant payment dates for December 2026
World.content:
The South African Social Security Agency (SASSA) has confirmed the final children’s grant payment date of 2026, with caregivers set to receive their money at the end of the first week of December.

SASSA pays older persons grants on Wednesday 2 December, disability grants on Thursday 3 December and children’s grants on Friday 4 December.

The early payment gives parents and guardians access to funds ahead of the festive season and the back-to-school rush in January.



The 4 December date applies to Child Support, Foster Child, and Care Dependency grants. All other grants, such as the care dependency and foster child grants, are paid with the Children’s Grants on 4 December.

November’s schedule shifted because of the elections, but that change did not carry over. SASSA said the shifted November dates applied only to that month, and that payments from December to March 2027 stay as previously announced.

Grant amounts for December

The December cycle will use the grant amounts introduced in April 2026 following the Budget Speech. The child support grant pays R580, the foster child grant pays R1 290, and the care dependency grant pays R2 400.

Caregivers do not need to queue on payment day. Money paid into a bank account stays there until you draw it, so you do not have to withdraw it on payment day.

Beneficiaries whose grants are under review should watch for notices, as their payment date may differ from the published schedule.

Budget for the wait until January

The early December payment means a longer wait for the next grant, just as school expenses start to pile up. The longer gap before the January payment cycle means careful financial planning is essential.



Caregivers who need to update their payment details should do so promptly. Banking detail changes must reach SASSA before the 19th of the month to take effect for that month’s payment.

SASSA has also urged beneficiaries to disclose changes in their finances, warning that anyone who no longer qualifies could be forced to repay the money.

The agency has also warned grant recipients not to rely on unverified messages about payment date changes.

Win R2 000 in the South African SASSA grant survey

If you receive a SASSA grant and want to share your story, we want to hear from you.

Take part in our survey and stand a chance to win R2 000. Your responses help us tell the stories that matter.

World.title: What Sundowns coach said to Chiefs player’s ear
World.content:
As witnessed by millions of fans on television, the Sundowns coach was spotted chatting to Ndlovu on the touchline.

It happened seconds before the midfielder replaced Lebohang Maboe in the 83rd minute of the Carling Knockout semi-final at Loftus Versfeld.

THE INCIDENT THAT STILL HAUNTS MAMELODI SUNDOWNS COACH MIGUEL CARDOSO

According to the Portguese coach, the conversation was not so ordinary.



Cardoso had a particular incident in mind, involving Sundowns defender Keanu Cupido, who was undergoing another operation following an injury suffered in a previous meeting between the clubs.

The Portuguese coach wanted to remind Ndlovu that he did not need to resort to dangerous challenges to make his presence felt on the pitch.

WHAT HE TOLD THE KAIZER CHIEFS MIDFIELDER

“I think the word I used was not the best one, but the intention of what I said was proper. Yesterday, Keanu (Cupido) was (in) surgery for the second time. I just wanted (him) to remember that he is a fantastic player.

“He can play the game without needing that kind of things,” Cardoso told media after his side’s 2-1 defeat to Kaizer Chiefs.

Cupido’s injury dates back to last season when Ndlovu made a challenge that resulted in the defender dislocating his shoulder.

The defender subsequently featured in the CAF Champions League final against AS FAR despite the injury, with Sundowns having limited defensive options because of Grant Kekana’s suspension.



However, Cupido has not featured since that continental final.

Cardoso was clearly conscious of the history between the two players and wanted to avoid another situation that could leave someone seriously injured.

The Sundowns coach was also keen to dismiss suggestions that there had been a confrontation with Ndlovu.

“The expression I used was strong, but I did not treat him bad. There was no conflict. I just wanted him to enter and understand the guys are playing fair,” Cardoso said.

He also referenced an exchange with Pule Mmodi after the match, explaining that he had no issue with the Chiefs winger’s challenges on Thabang Matuludi.

“It was a beautiful match in terms of fair play. Even in the end, you saw me speaking with (Pule) Mmodi. Mmodi had two actions on the line and immediately I said ‘it was fair. There is no intention for you to touch on Thabang (Matuludi)’.

“It was a reminder, nothing more,” the Sundowns boss added.

World.title: Table Mountain cable car prices: What it costs this festive season
World.content:
See the 2026/27 Table Mountain cable car prices, including online, ticket office, Fast Track and pensioner fares. Image: City Pass

A trip up Table Mountain remains one of Cape Town’s – and the world’s – must-do experiences, but it’s worth knowing A family trip to the top of Table Mountain can cost more than R1 400 in cable car tickets alone, with visitors paying significantly more if they purchase their tickets at the lower cable station rather than online.

The Table Mountain Aerial Cableway’s 2026/27 rates are applicable from 1 July 2026 to 30 June 2027.

For a family of four, consisting of two adults and two children aged between four and 17, an online return ticket costs R1 410.



However, buying the same tickets at the ticket office will cost R1 600 – a difference of R190.

READ | The eye-watering price of a private Table Mountain cable car ride

Table Mountain cable car prices 2026/27

Visitors can save money by purchasing their tickets online before arriving at the lower cable station.

The standard return ticket prices are:

Ticket category Online return Ticket office return Adults R475 R530 Children (4–17) R230 R270 Children under 4 Free Free

For a family of four, the online calculation is:

Two adults: R950

Two children: R460

Total: R1 410

At the ticket office, the same family will pay R1 600.



That means booking online saves the family R190.

What if you only need a one-way ticket?

Visitors planning to hike up or down Table Mountain can purchase one-way cable car tickets.

The current fares are:

Ticket category Online one-way Ticket office one-way Adults R300 R330 Children (4–17) R165 R180

A family of two adults and two children will pay R930 for one-way tickets online, compared with R1 020 at the ticket office.

Children under four travel free.

Fast Track tickets available

For visitors wanting to avoid potentially lengthy queues, the Table Mountain Aerial Cableway also offers a Fast Track ticket option.

These tickets cost:

Return: R1 200 per person

One-way: R750 per person

Adults and children pay the same price.

Fast Track tickets allow visitors to skip the queue and can be purchased through Webtickets.

Pensioner discounts

Visitors aged over 60 also qualify for discounted fares.

Pensioner tickets cost:

One-way: R70

Return: R130

These prices apply to purchases both online and at the ticket office.

Where to buy Table Mountain tickets

Visitors are encouraged to purchase tickets through recognised sales partners to avoid fraudulent or unofficial ticket sellers.

These include:

Webtickets

Cape Town Tourism

City Sightseeing South Africa

Booking online in advance is particularly advisable during school holidays, long weekends and peak tourism periods (like the upcoming festive seson).

Visitors should also check the weather before setting off.

Strong winds and adverse weather conditions can result in temporary suspensions of cableway operations, potentially affecting travel plans.

For those planning a visit to one of Cape Town’s most recognisable attractions, buying tickets ahead of time could save money and help avoid unnecessary queues.

When last did you take the cable car up Table Mountain?

World.title: Dead humpback whale removed from Hout Bay shoreline
World.content:
NSRI crews and City of Cape Town teams recovered a dead humpback whale from Flora Bay in Hout Bay. Marine scientists are investigating its death. Image: Facebook / SeaRescue

The carcass of a humpback whale has been successfully recovered from a rocky shoreline in Hout Bay following a coordinated operation involving the National Sea Rescue Institute (NSRI) and the City of Cape Town.

The whale was discovered washed ashore at Flora Bay, prompting concerns about potential environmental risks associated with its decomposing carcass.

READ | The story of the bronze leopard of Hout Bay



The NSRI Hout Bay station was notified of the discovery on the evening of Saturday, 21 November.

Station commander Spencer Oldham said the rescue organisation immediately coordinated with the City’s marine animal stranding network to plan the recovery.

An assessment was scheduled for daybreak on Sunday, 22 November, to determine the safest way to remove the whale from the shoreline.

Major recovery operation in Hout Bay

NSRI Hout Bay crews arrived at Flora Bay on Sunday morning alongside members of the marine animal stranding network.

The operation presented several challenges, with the whale trapped among sharp rocks and in shallow surf.

Oldham said recovery efforts would begin closer to high tide to improve the chances of successfully moving the carcass away from the shoreline.



NSRI rescue swimmers, a rescue vehicle and two rescue craft, the Spirit of Ubuntu and Spirit of Gabi, were deployed.

In a carefully coordinated operation, NSRI swimmers carried a tow rope through the surf to the Spirit of Gabi, which transported the line to the Spirit of Ubuntu.

The teams then worked together to tow the whale away from the rocks and through the challenging surf conditions.

The operation was successfully completed, with the carcass reaching the Hout Bay Harbour slipway at approximately 14:08 on Sunday.

The City of Cape Town’s waste management team subsequently took responsibility for the carcass and its appropriate disposal.

Scientists investigating cause of death

The recovery operation also provided an opportunity for marine scientists from the Department of Environment to collect samples from the whale.

The samples will form part of an investigation into the animal’s cause of death.

The City of Cape Town’s Coastal Management team praised the NSRI for its assistance.

Gregg Oelofse from the City’s Coastal Management department thanked the rescue organisation for its role in ensuring the whale was recovered safely and effectively.

The incident once again highlighted the importance of cooperation between rescue organisations, municipal authorities and environmental specialists when dealing with marine animal strandings along the Cape coastline.

World.title: WATCH | Sworn-in Joburg councillors react to first council meeting
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - The City of Johannesburg's 270 councillors have officially been sworn in during the first council sitting on Monday.

However, the meeting remains incomplete, with the election of the city’s Executive Mayor, Speaker and other office bearers postponed to Friday as coalition talks between political parties continue.

The postponement, according to City Manager Floyd Brink, was supported by 21 political parties.

It follows a request from the DA, which argued that the continuation of the meeting would prejudice those negotiations and the prospects of electing stable political leadership.

READ | Election of Joburg mayor postponed

Reacting to this was ANC regional secretary Sasabona Manganye, who deemed the delay unfortunate given the service delivery issues that persist within the city.

But even so, he supported the postponement to allow parties more time to finalise their coalition agreements.

World.title: MKP's 24-year-old Joburg councillor eyes student debt and jobs as key priorities
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - At just 24 years old, sworn-in MKP councillor Siphesihle Sibande, says tackling student debt and youth unemployment will be among his key priorities in the City of Johannesburg.

He was among the 270 councillors who were sworn in on Monday during the city's first council meeting.

Speaking to eNCA, Sibande acknowledged that the task ahead will be ‘hefty’, given the city's financial woes; however, he said he is ready to take on the task at hand.

“The organisation has entrusted young people insofar as the government's helm is concerned. So, I think it is quite a big responsibility. But I'm representing the aspirations of young people, the students, the marginalised and the poor,” he said.

The MKP has secured 15 seats in Johannesburg.

Leading in the city with a high number of seats is the DA, which secured 91 seats, followed by the ANC with 64 seats, and rounding out the top three was ActionSA with 42 seats.

However, a majority in the city Council needs 136 seats to govern. This leaves the parties with no other choice but to turn to other political parties for support.

To date, coalition talks are still ongoing with political parties, with parties left this week to reach agreements.

These talks have seen the election of the Johannesburg Executive mayor, Speaker and other office bearers being postponed to Friday.

READ | Election of Joburg mayor postponed

World.title: Number Of The Day | R372 Billion | 23 November 2026
World.content:
Coca-Cola's R372bn JSE Debut Raises a Bigger Question: Where Are South Africa's Next Corporate Giants?

A stock exchange can become more valuable without necessarily becoming healthier. That is the uncomfortable contradiction confronting the Johannesburg Stock Exchange as Coca-Cola HBC joins its main board with a market valuation approaching R372 billion. The arrival of another global heavyweight is significant for South Africa's financial markets, but it also highlights a persistent structural challenge: while the country's exchange continues attracting some of the world's biggest businesses, it is struggling to retain a broad base of smaller listed companies.

Coca-Cola HBC's secondary listing on 23 November 2026 gives South African investors access to shares in one of the world's largest Coca-Cola bottling partners. Its arrival comes ahead of a planned $2.6 billion acquisition of a 75% stake in Coca-Cola Beverages Africa, a transaction expected to make the enlarged group the world's second-largest Coca-Cola bottler by volume. Together, these developments represent a substantial expansion of the company's African business and reinforce Johannesburg's relevance as an international investment destination.

Yet the more revealing measure of the JSE's health may not be the value of the companies entering the market, but the number and variety of businesses capable of remaining there.

Why Fewer Listed Companies Should Concern South Africa

In the 23 November edition of eNCA's Number of the Day, Francis Herd draws attention to a striking imbalance. The JSE had recorded 13 delistings during the year, according to figures provided to the programme, while only three new listings had taken place. He also reports that departing companies represented approximately R44 billion in lost market capitalisation. These figures provide context for the importance of a listing as large as Coca-Cola HBC's, but they also expose the limitations of measuring an exchange's success purely through its overall value.

Not every delisting represents a vote of no confidence in South Africa. Companies disappear from stock exchanges for several reasons, including mergers, acquisitions, changes in ownership and decisions to operate privately. For some smaller businesses, the regulatory obligations, reporting requirements and administrative costs associated with a public listing can become increasingly difficult to justify. The benefits of access to capital must be weighed against the expense and complexity of remaining listed, particularly when a company no longer needs to raise substantial funding from public shareholders.

The problem becomes more consequential when these departures narrow the range of businesses available to investors. Large multinational companies provide scale, liquidity and international recognition, but a public market dominated by established giants may offer fewer opportunities to invest in emerging domestic enterprises. A functioning stock exchange should provide different businesses with access to capital at different stages of their development, rather than serving primarily as a trading venue for companies that have already achieved considerable global success.

This matters beyond the financial sector. The ability of growing companies to raise capital influences how businesses fund expansion, invest in productive capacity and pursue new markets. Public listings are not appropriate for every company, but they remain an important financing option. If the route to the stock exchange becomes unattractive to a generation of promising businesses, South Africa risks weakening one of the mechanisms through which smaller enterprises can become larger economic players.

The Opportunity Behind Coca-Cola's African Expansion

Coca-Cola HBC's arrival also demonstrates why international corporate investment remains important. The company's proposed acquisition of Coca-Cola Beverages Africa would extend its operations across a wider African consumer market, strengthening its position in production, distribution and the broader beverage supply chain. The enlarged business is expected to serve markets representing approximately 1.2 billion consumers, illustrating the commercial scale that multinational companies increasingly see across the continent.

There is, however, an important distinction between market capitalisation, corporate acquisitions and direct investment in productive activity. Coca-Cola HBC's R372 billion valuation represents the market value of its shares, not R372 billion newly invested in South Africa. Similarly, the acquisition of an existing business is different from spending money on additional factories, distribution infrastructure or employment. The wider Coca-Cola system has separately announced plans to invest R17.6 billion in South Africa through 2030, offering a more direct indication of intended operational expansion.

South Africa needs both forms of economic participation. International companies can bring scale, investment capacity and access to regional markets, while domestic businesses need an environment that enables them to grow into competitive enterprises themselves. The challenge is ensuring that the success of large incoming companies does not obscure the structural conditions affecting smaller businesses already operating in the country.

Coca-Cola HBC's listing is therefore worth celebrating, but it should also sharpen the conversation about the JSE's future. Attracting another enormous multinational demonstrates that Johannesburg remains relevant to global capital. Building an exchange where ambitious South African companies can raise money, expand and remain publicly listed would demonstrate something more enduring: that the market is not merely a destination for established corporate giants, but a place where the next generation can emerge.

World.title: Election of Joburg mayor postponed
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - The City of Johannesburg has a newly constituted council, but who will lead it for the next five years remains unanswered for now.

This is because the election of the city council office bearers has been postponed to Friday amid ongoing coalition talks between parties.

Johannesburg Speaker of Council, Executive Mayor and other office bearers were supposed to be elected during Monday's first council sittings, where 270 newly elected councillors gathered.

READ | WATCH | City of Joburg inaugural council sitting

However, proceedings were limited to just the swearing-in of newly elected councillors following a request by the DA for the postponement.

Addressing the council, City Manager Floyd Brink said all 21 parties were in support of the postponement and that confirmed that a new notice for the meeting will be issued to parties before the end of the day.

“The meeting will take place on Friday, and it will be in line with Rule 55, Subsection 1, which reads that notice of the time and place of every ordinary meeting of the Council must be served on every Council, either personally and/or electronically, or by leaving the notice at his or her usual place of residence or place of business at least three calendar days before such a meeting takes place,” he said.

At the start of the first sitting of the city’s municipal council in the morning, Brink indicated that they had received a letter from Helen Zille of the DA requesting the postponement of the meeting.

He said the letter cited coalition negotiations between parties which are yet to be concluded.

Brink said among other reasons indicated in the letter for a postponement is that the continuation of the meeting would prejudice those negotiations and the prospects of electing stable political leadership.

READ | ActionSA places coalition ball in ANC's court

Brink said a few minutes later he received another letter with a similar request from other members of the DA.

World.content:
eTHEKWINI - eThekwini Municipality in KwaZulu-Natal has placed emergency teams on standby due to severe weather warnings.

A level four thunderstorm warning has been issued for Monday and Tuesday.

Several communities are expected to be affected, including KwaMashu, Inanda, uMlazi, Chatsworth, Phoenix and Pinetown.

READ | Severe weather has Joburg EMS on high alert

The weather service has warned of possible flooding and disruptions to essential services.

Residents are urged to avoid unnecessary travel and move to higher ground if water levels rise.

World.title: Corruption accused Mapisa-Nqakula to know her fate in December
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - Former defence minister Nosiviwe Mapisa-Nqakula will know her fate on 3 December.

That's when the High Court in Pretoria will deliver judgment in her corruption and money laundering trial.

Closing arguments have been delivered in the high-profile case.

READ | New witness expected in Mapisa-Nqakula corruption trial

The state accuses Mapisa-Nqakula of taking bribes from contractor Nombasa Ntsondwa-Ndlovu when she was defence minister.

The prosecution points to R4.5-million in alleged dodgy payments between 2016 and 2019.

Mapisa-Nqakula has denied all charges.

World.title: Netcare’s Tech investment pays off
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - Netcare is ending its financial year on a strong note.

The private hospital group has grown its profits, with technology and better cost management helping to improve its performance.

This is despite pressure on consumers and medical aid members.

READ | Rising costs push South Africans towards health insurance

Netcare says its investment in digital systems is paying off, helping hospitals work more efficiently and save money.

The group says these digital initiatives have already generated more savings than the cost of implementing them.

The results come as CEO Richard Friedland prepares to step down at the end of December, after three decades at the helm. His successor, Melanie Da Costa, takes over in January.

World.title: Continental shutdown puts nearly 1000 jobs at risk
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - Continental is the latest tyre manufacturer is considering halting production at its Gqeberha plant.

The potential plant closure planned for early 2027 could see approximately 950 employees being affected.

This is another blow to the Eastern Cape's manufacturing sector, following the closure of Goodyear and Bridgestone plants.

The move comes as the local tyre industry battles sustained competitive and operational challenges.

READ | Why finding a job is becoming increasingly difficult in SA

In a statement released on 20 November, the manufacturing company said Intensifying price competition from low-cost imports has placed significant pressure on the African tyre market.

"These challenges have been compounded by rising energy costs, supply chains disruptions and an increasingly fragile infrastructure – all of which have increased manufacturing costs and made it harder to plan ahead. " As a result, production capacity at the Gqeberha tire plant has been significantly underutilized in recent years, despite various turnaround efforts aimed at improving its operational performance," the statement read.

If the plant closes permanently, South Africa will be left with just two major tyre manufacturers.

Local demand for locally manufactured tyres has already fallen from more than 60% in 2016 to below 40% in 2024.

That's a major concern for the Eastern Cape, where the automotive and related manufacturing sector contributes around 22% of the provincial economy and supports some 40-thousand jobs.

World.title: Ruto backs Didmus Barasa for Bungoma governor in 2027
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Kimilili MP Didmus Barasa with President Ruto at a political rally in Mt Elgon during the President’s development tour in the Western region. [PCS]

President William Ruto has thrown his weight behind Kimilili MP Didmus Barasa in the race to succeed Bungoma Governor Kenneth Lusaka in 2027, setting the stage for a contest over the county's political leadership.

During his ongoing tour of Western Kenya, the President rallied support for Barasa, signalling his preference for the legislator in the battle for control of Bungoma County after the next General Election.

Barasa has expressed confidence in securing the United Democratic Alliance (UDA) party nomination, citing his development record and grassroots mobilisation in Kimilili as the foundation of his gubernatorial bid.

The MP has urged Bungoma leaders aligned with Kenya Kwanza to unite behind his candidature, arguing that a common political front would strengthen the region's bargaining power within the national government.

He said he intends to replicate his development model in Kimilili across the county's 45 wards, prioritising healthcare, education and youth empowerment.

“I want to take the development model we have implemented in Kimilili and extend it to all the 45 wards in Bungoma. Our people deserve better healthcare, improved education infrastructure, functional vocational training centres and quality early childhood education facilities,” he said.

The legislator pledged to strengthen county hospitals, improve the availability of medicines and expand access to healthcare services at the grassroots.

He also promised to invest in vocational training centres to equip young people with practical skills for employment and entrepreneurship, while improving Early Childhood Development and Education (ECDE).

Barasa identified agriculture, trade, infrastructure and youth entrepreneurship as key sectors requiring investment to unlock Bungoma's economic potential. He said his proposed administration would prioritise accountability, efficient use of public resources and improved service delivery.

His bid has received backing from a section of county leaders, including Senator Wafula Wakoli of Ford Kenya and Webuye East MP Martin Pepela.

However, Ruto's apparent preference for Barasa has attracted opposition from Sirisia MP John Waluke, who has questioned the endorsement and instead declared support for Westlands MP Tim Wanyonyi, who is associated with the Linda Mwananchi Movement (LMM).

Waluke argued that Bungoma residents should determine their next governor without external political influence.

“Bungoma belongs to its people, and the people must decide who will lead them in 2027. We cannot allow the gubernatorial contest to be determined through political endorsements from outside. Residents must be given the freedom to choose a leader who represents their interests,” he said.

The contest is also unfolding amid political differences between Barasa and National Assembly Speaker Moses Wetang'ula, adding to the competing interests shaping Bungoma's succession politics.

World.title: Shun leaders inciting you to cause chaos, PS Omollo tells youth
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Internal Security Principal Secretary Raymond Omollo. [File,Standard]

Internal Security Principal Secretary Raymond Omollo has warned young people against political violence, saying the destruction of public property costs lives and diverts resources meant for development.

The warning comes amid concerns over political violence in Embu following the September 12 incident at Nembure Stadium, where a meeting attended by Deputy President Kithure Kindiki was disrupted, leaving one person dead, six vehicles torched and three others vandalised.

Speaking during a Mass at St Thomas More Kairuri Parish in Embu County, Omollo challenged young people to question leaders who ask them to disrupt meetings, block roads or destroy property.

“Before you leave home to disrupt a meeting, ask that leader whether they would allow their own child to do what they are asking you to do,” he said.

“Ask them what they are doing to help you access education, training and employment.”

Omollo said young people should also question what political leaders were doing to improve their access to education, technical training and employment.

He said the Government was working to expand opportunities for young people through education, technical training and employment.

The PS welcomed efforts in the technical and vocational education and training (TVET) sector to equip young people in Embu with skills to pursue their ambitions.

At the same time, Omollo commended county leadership for working with the national government to combat illicit alcohol and drug abuse.

Omollo said proposed legislative changes targeting the sector had passed the first reading in Parliament and urged residents to participate in the next stages of the legislative process.

On security, the PS acknowledged calls for more police vehicles, saying the Government was investing in personnel, vehicles and equipment.

However, he challenged residents to help protect public investments, citing reports that 10 police vehicles had been burned in Embu.

“We use our taxes to buy police vehicles, build markets and construct roads. We cannot pay for development and then allow a few individuals to destroy what belongs to all of us,” he said.

Omollo warned that anyone suspected of destroying property would be taken to court in accordance with the law, where the judiciary would determine their cases.

He maintained that political differences should not be used to justify vandalism, endanger lives or disrupt public services.

“The Constitution protects the right to express ourselves peacefully and unarmed. Political differences cannot be an excuse to vandalise property, endanger lives or disrupt the services our communities depend on,” he said.

Those present included Public Service, Human Capital Development and Special Programmes Cabinet Secretary Geoffrey Ruku, Embu Governor Cecily Mbarire, Senator Alexander Munyi and Deputy Governor Kinyua Mugo, among others.

World.title: Narok Senator under fire after threatening to shoot auctioneers in Sh1.2m dispute
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Narok Senator Ledama ole Kina is at the centre of a national uproar after a viral video captured him threatening to shoot individuals during a volatile confrontation involving auctioneers and a former Senate office employee.

The dramatic standoff erupted when court-backed agents attempted to seize a milk delivery truck over an unresolved legal dispute and has since ignited intense public debate regarding political accountability and the rule of law.

The controversy surrounds long court battle after Zakayo Rotiken, who served sacked as Narok North Constituency Coordinator between 2017 and 2020, was sacked.

According to records, the claimant was illegally dismissed amidst unpaid salary arrears.

On October 31, 2023, the Employment and Labour Relations Court ruled in Rotiken's favour , a decision that was subsequently upheld when the Senator lost his appeal.

With accrued interest, the court decree now stands at Sh 1.2 million.

Consequently, when the debt remained unsatisfied, licensed auctioneers moved in to execute lawful warrants which in turn provoked a furious reaction from Senator Ole Kina, who fiercely framed the entire episode as a political witch-hunt.

The lawmaker argued that Rotiken was hired by the Narok Senate office rather than his personal capacity, maintaining that any resultant liabilities ought to be handled by the Parliamentary Service Commission (PSC) rather than attaching his private property.

Defending his harsh words in the widely circulated footage, the senator dismissed the agents as trespassers and asserted action against them.

"Anybody who trespasses will get a bullet in their head or leg because that is trespass," said Ole Kina.

“Nitakupiga Risasi!” Senator Ledama Ole Kina embroiled in confrontation with alleged auctioneers over unpaid car loan https://t.co/k4OSXpNsdi November 21, 2026

The claimant's legal team condemned the threats made against statutory court officers emphasizing that a court judgment is an enforceable command rather than a mere suggestion, calling upon the Inspector General of Police of Police and the Director of Criminal Investigatons to urgently investigate the alleged death threats.

Rotiken noted that he merely sought justice through proper judicial channels and should not be penalized or intimidated for pursuing his lawful entitlements.

"When I was illegally dismissed with unpaid salary arrears, I did not resort to violence or politics—I went to the Employment and Labour Relations Court. Nobody is above the law, and I appeal to the police to protect the officers doing their job so that justice can finally be served," he said.

Ultimately, as pressure mounts on security agencies to look into the firearm threats, the unfolding saga highlights a tense intersection between public office obligations and the absolute sanctity of judicial decrees.

While the senator maintains that his assets were unjustly targeted by political rivals, legal experts and the public continue to demand that the rule of law must prevail without exception.

World.title: Ruto defends IEBC, challenges rivals to present alternative policies
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

President William Ruto during his tour of the Western region. [PCS]

President William Ruto has launched a scathing attack on opposition leaders over their demands on the Independent Electoral and Boundaries Commission (IEBC), accusing them of attempting to interfere with the electoral agency because they fear losing the 2027 General Election.

The President challenged opposition leaders to allow IEBC to prepare independently for next year's elections, saying they should instead focus on identifying their presidential candidate, developing a manifesto and presenting alternative policies to Kenyans.

Ruto accused his competitors of attempting to play the roles of both contestants and referees by seeking to influence decisions on the procurement of election materials and equipment.

He spoke a day after opposition leaders walked out of a meeting convened by IEBC, alleging bias by the commission.

“Please give IEBC a chance to arrange the elections next year. The people of Kenya will decide. You go and first look for your candidate, find your policies, agenda and plans and sell them to the wananchi. We shall meet at the ballot,” said Ruto.

Speaking during his development tour of Western Kenya, Ruto questioned why opposition politicians were concentrating on determining how IEBC should procure election materials instead of preparing to face voters.

“How can somebody who is in a competition want to decide where the pitch will be, who the referee will be and where the ball will be placed? Leave IEBC alone. Those who will vote are the citizens, and they are the ones who will decide,” he said.

The President accused his opponents of lacking a clear political agenda and capacity to deliver, claiming their campaigns were centred on slogans and personal attacks against him.

He challenged them to explain what they would do differently in agriculture, education, healthcare, infrastructure and employment rather than mobilising Kenyans around the slogan 'Kasongo Must Go'.

“The reason why my competitors cannot develop a plan is that they have no capacity. The reason why they have no agenda is that they have no knowledge. The reason why they cannot develop anything is that they know they have no capacity to deliver on anything that they will say,” he said.

His remarks were echoed by Kakamega Governor Fernandes Barasa and National Assembly Speaker Moses Wetang'ula, who rallied Western Kenya leaders behind his re-election bid and defended IEBC against what they termed unnecessary political pressure. President William Ruto during his tour of the Western region. [ Benjamin Sakwa, Standard]

Speaking in Butere, Barasa said the region's political leadership, including Prime Cabinet Secretary Musalia Mudavadi, Cabinet Secretary Wycliffe Oparanya, Wetang'ula and trade unionist Francis Atwoli, was united behind Ruto's development agenda.

“IEBC will conduct the elections according to the law. Opposition leaders should leave IEBC alone and allow it to do its work,” he said.

Wetang'ula maintained that IEBC was independent of both the government and the opposition and should be allowed to conduct its work without interference.

“IEBC is independent of the government and independent of the Opposition. You stand there to do your work fairly, truthfully and equally,” he said.

He added: “Just as Arsenal supporters cannot dictate what uniform the referee should wear, the referee's responsibility is to ensure the game is played fairly and the winner emerges through a legitimate process.”

The exchanges underline the growing political contest over the management of the 2027 elections, with the government side accusing the opposition of undermining the electoral agency before campaigns gather momentum.

Beyond the political exchanges, Ruto used his Western Kenya tour to highlight development projects, saying his administration was committed to correcting years of neglect and unequal distribution of national resources.

He also announced plans for a second phase of the Nyota programme targeting an additional 200,000 young people, each expected to receive Sh50,000 to establish or expand businesses.

The government is also targeting 100,000 college graduates for internships from January, with each expected to receive a monthly stipend of Sh20,000.

Ruto's tour comes amid growing competition for Western Kenya's support ahead of the 2027 General Election, with emerging opposition alliances seeking to challenge his influence.

World.title: Ruto sustains attacks on Gachagua, dares Opposition to name 2027 flagbearer
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

President William Ruto launches Matisi-Bokoli-Milani-Teremi road in Webuye West on November 19, 2026. [Benjamin Sakwa, Standard]

President William Ruto has challenged Opposition leaders to name their presidential candidate and unveil a clear political agenda, accusing them of wasting time hopping from one hotel to another and holding meetings in private residences in search of a flagbearer and campaign manifesto.

The President said the Opposition was yet to settle on a flagbearer or agree on a common agenda despite the clock ticking towards the 2027 General Election.

He dismissed the rival camps' political engagements as endless consultations and manoeuvres, arguing that their leaders were more preoccupied with political meetings than developing policies to convince Kenyans.

Speaking in Bungoma during his development tour of Western Kenya, Ruto challenged his opponents to stop what he termed political confusion and present an alternative development agenda, insisting he was ready to face them in the 2027 contest.

"These people do not have a candidate. They are struggling, moving from one hotel to another and from one person's house to another, trying to find an agenda and a manifesto before they can start campaigning. Time is running out, yet they are still struggling to agree on an agenda," he said.

Ruto also launched a fresh attack on former Deputy President Rigathi Gachagua, accusing him of promoting tribalism and hatred while questioning his remarks about relocating to Texas, United States.

The President mockingly referred to Gachagua as "Mr Chuki wa Texas", questioning why he would allegedly acquire a house in the US while engaging in politics that could divide Kenyans and fuel hostility.

"Mr Chuki wa Texas has gone to buy a house in Texas. He wants to know whether he will flee our country after spreading tribalism and hatred, dividing people and turning them against each other, before boarding a plane to Texas and leaving others to deal with the consequences," Ruto said.

He accused the former Deputy President of attempting to turn communities against one another for political gain, warning that he would not allow anyone to undermine national unity through ethnic mobilisation.

Ruto said he was ready to confront his political opponents directly but insisted that political competition should not become an avenue for spreading hatred and inciting Kenyans against one another.

The President also questioned Gachagua's allies over their reported visit to the Independent Electoral and Boundaries Commission (IEBC) offices in Kizirani, accusing the Opposition of picking unnecessary fights with the electoral agency ahead of the 2027 General Election.

He suggested that politicians who begin questioning the electoral commission before elections could be preparing grounds to reject the results should they lose.

"Whenever you see someone picking a fight with IEBC, that person is already looking for an excuse to fail. Now they are coming up with all sorts of excuses, asking whether it is IEBC that votes. Is IEBC responsible for the votes?" He posed.

Ruto urged politicians to stop harassing the electoral agency, maintaining that the power to elect leaders rests with Kenyans and not the commission.

"I want to tell Kenyans to stop harassing IEBC. IEBC does not have votes. The votes belong to the people of Kenya," he said.

The President maintained that his administration was focused on delivering development, challenging the Opposition to explain its alternative plans on electricity connectivity, education, healthcare and infrastructure.

He questioned what the Opposition considered its development agenda, dismissing what he described as recycled political slogans and simplistic promises.

The President particularly took issue with promises centred on providing porridge to Kenyans, questioning whether such pledges could constitute a credible national development agenda.

He urged voters to interrogate the policies and development track records of politicians seeking their support instead of being swayed by political rhetoric and personal attacks.

The latest attack marks an escalation in political exchanges between Ruto and his rivals as competing camps intensify mobilisation ahead of the 2027 General Election.

It also comes amid efforts by Gachagua and other Opposition figures to consolidate their political formations and build a formidable challenge to Ruto's re-election bid, with Western Kenya emerging as a key battleground.

World.title: Ruto lists measures to lower cost of living, put more money in Kenyans' pockets
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

President William Ruto during his State Of The Nation Address at Parliament, Nairobi. November 18th, 2026. [Elvis Ogina, Standard]

President William Ruto has outlined a raft of government interventions aimed at reducing the cost of living, increasing household incomes and creating more employment opportunities for Kenyans.

Addressing Parliament during the 2026 State of the Nation Address on Wednesday, Ruto said his administration had prioritised lowering the cost of essential goods and services while increasing earnings across key sectors of the economy.

“Our economic proposition was simple: Reduce the cost for families and increase the income from what they do,” he said.

On food prices, the President cited the government’s fertiliser subsidy programme, which has reduced the price of a 50-kilogramme bag of fertiliser from Sh7,500 in 2022 to Sh2,000 this year.

He said the government had distributed 38.5 million bags of subsidised fertiliser to farmers, contributing to an increase in maize production from 44.3 million bags in 2022 to 71 million bags last year.

Consequently, maize imports declined from 9.9 million bags to 3.3 million bags, while the average price of a two-kilogramme packet of sifted maize flour dropped from a high of Sh230 in September 2022 to Sh152 in September this year.

Ruto also highlighted gains in the tea, coffee, dairy and sugar industries, saying government interventions had helped improve production and increase farmers' earnings.

He said the Cherry Advance Revolving Fund had disbursed Sh15.07 billion to 684,000 coffee farmers, while tea export earnings increased from Sh163 billion in 2022 to Sh187 billion in 2025.

In the dairy sector, milk production rose from 4.5 billion litres to 5.52 billion litres, while average earnings for farmers increased from Sh32 to Sh60 per litre last month.

Sugar production, he added, increased by 60 per cent between January and October, with cane crushing rising by 57 per cent. The industry is projected to produce more than 900,000 tonnes by the end of the year, with Sh1.2 billion in bonuses expected to be paid to sugarcane farmers.

On healthcare, Ruto said the Social Health Authority (SHA) was designed to ease the financial burden of medical expenses on households through a shared health financing system.

In education, he said the government had employed 100,000 teachers and was preparing to recruit an additional 20,000 to address staffing shortages and reduce the burden on parents who pay teachers hired through Boards of Management.

He added that 23,000 classrooms had been constructed, while 1,600 laboratories were being built and equipped.

The President said the annual education allocation had increased from Sh521 billion in the 2022/23 financial year to Sh784 billion in the current financial year.

"These investments improve the quality of education while progressively reducing the need for Kenyans to finance education," he said.

On affordable housing, Ruto said more than 313,000 homes were at different stages of construction across the 47 counties, with over 1.37 million Kenyans registered on the Boma Yangu platform and more than 18,000 homes already allocated.

He said households could work towards homeownership through monthly payments starting at Sh4,000, which he argued would help ease the burden of rent.

The housing programme, according to the President, had also generated more than 1.1 million employment opportunities and reserved orders worth over Sh61 billion for Jua Kali artisans.

On employment, Ruto said 350,000 Kenyans had secured jobs through the digital economy programme, while another 707,000 had obtained employment abroad through international labour mobility initiatives.

He also cited the Hustler Fund, saying more than seven million Kenyans had established credit records through the programme, with cumulative borrowing reaching Sh94 billion.

Under the NYOTA programme, more than 133,000 young entrepreneurs had received training, mentorship and Sh50,000 each in start-up capital, he said.

The President further announced proposed tax measures aimed at increasing disposable incomes, including exempting workers earning Sh32,333 or less per month from Pay As You Earn (PAYE).

Other proposals include scrapping stamp duty on land transactions valued at Sh1 million or less and removing the 25 per cent import duty on mobile phones.

On pending bills, Ruto said the government had approved the settlement of 28,726 verified claims amounting to Sh27.8 billion, covering debts of Sh50 million and below dating back to 2005.

He added that Sh18 billion owed to public universities and another Sh16 billion owed to public and private hospitals under the former National Hospital Insurance Fund (NHIF) had been approved for payment and were undergoing Treasury processing.

“These are not isolated interventions, but parts of one comprehensive undertaking,” Ruto said.

He maintained that the government's economic strategy was anchored on reducing household expenditure, increasing incomes and expanding opportunities for Kenyans.

World.title: After 22 years of waiting, woman welcomes quadruplet boys
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Samuel Langat speaks to journalists outside St Clare's Kaplong Mission hospital in Sotik Subcounty, Bomet county after his wife Lily Langat gave to quadruplets at the hospital. [Kiprono Kurgat, Standard]

After 22 years of waiting to become a mother, a woman has welcomed quadruplet boys in a rare and joyful birth that has brought immense happiness to her family.

Lily Langat delivered the quadruplets through a Caesarean section at St Clare’s Kaplong Mission Hospital in Sotik Sub-County on November 14, 2026.

The four boys arrived after more than two decades of waiting for a child in what the family described as a double blessing.

The 43-year-old mother could not hide her joy, saying the arrival of the four babies was an answer to years of prayer.

“I am very grateful to God for giving me four babies at once. This is a great blessing to my family. I thank the hospital staff for ensuring I got to see these bundles of joy,” she said.

“I have been praying and waiting upon God to give me double for the trouble. I have been childless for a long time, and God could not have given me a better gift than this,” she added.

She said she had been looking forward to the moment after doctors informed her early in the pregnancy that she could be carrying quadruplets.

Hospital staff celebrated the successful delivery, describing it as a rare occurrence at the facility.

A nurse who spoke with The Standard said the mother and her four newborns were in stable condition.

“We were delighted to deliver the babies. The mother faced some difficulties because of the combined weight of the four babies, but both she and the newborns are now stable,” she said.

The nurse said the babies had been placed in the nursery for observation and were doing well.

“This is a rare case in this hospital. We have had twins before, but this is different. None of the babies has developed complications so far, and we expect them to be discharged once they are fully stable,” she said.

She added that the mother was also recovering well and was expected to be discharged once doctors were satisfied with the condition of the newborns.

Lily's husband, Samuel Langat, appealed to well-wishers to support the family as they prepare to raise the four children.

“Raising four babies at once is no easy task. I am calling on well-wishers to lend a helping hand as we begin this extraordinary journey,” he said.

“Our four precious miracles have arrived safely, and while our hearts are overflowing with gratitude, the reality of caring for four newborns at once has brought challenges,” he added.

Naturally conceived quadruplets are extremely rare, although the likelihood varies depending on several factors, including maternal age and fertility treatment.

The birth marks a remarkable new beginning for the Langat family after 22 years of waiting for a child.

World.title: Libyan Army denies withdrawal of Egyptian military experts from Benghazi
World.content:
The General Command of the Libyan Arab Armed Forces has denied reports about the withdrawal of Egyptian military experts from the city of Benghazi, affirming that cooperation between both sides continues as normal.

In a statement issued on Sunday, the General Command noted that it monitored reports circulating in certain media outlets and on social media platforms concerning an alleged rift with Egypt, dismissing such claims as entirely unfounded.

The command emphasized that Egyptian-Libyan relations remain firmer than ever, representing a deep-rooted and enduring partnership built upon strong historical ties, mutual trust, and shared interests.

This partnership is reflected in close cooperation across military and security sectors, as well as extensive collaboration on reconstruction, development, and infrastructure projects, it said.

The General Command affirmed that this partnership reflects the depth and significance of the relationship between both nations, as well as its role in safeguarding their shared national security and enhancing regional security and stability.

It reiterated its pride in the ties with Egypt and its commitment to further strengthening them across various fields.

Furthermore, it urged media outlets to ensure accuracy, rely on official sources, and refrain from circulating unverified reports concerning the relationship between the two countries.

Egypt remains committed to Libya’s stability

Egyptian Minister of State for Information Diaa Rashwan previously denied claims circulated by certain media outlets and social media platforms suggesting that Egypt had withdrawn its military experts from Benghazi, allegedly due to disagreements with the General Command of the Libyan National Army (LNA).

In a statement issued by the Ministry of State for Information, Rashwan affirmed that Egypt remains committed to supporting Libya’s stability, territorial integrity, and the preservation of its national institutions.

He emphasized that communication and coordination with the LNA’s General Command continue as usual, showing a shared commitment to upholding security and stability in both Libya and the broader region.

The minister urged media outlets to exercise accuracy and avoid being swayed by unsubstantiated claims—allegations intended to sow doubt in the deep-rooted and multifaceted relationship Egypt and Libya share.

Edited translation from Al-Masry Al-Youm

World.title: Prime Minister issues new decision regarding private sector participation in Egyptian government projects
World.content:
Prime Minister Mostafa Madbouly has issued a new decision concerning the disclosure and regulation of investor access to data on infrastructure, service, and public utility projects intended for implementation through public-private partnerships (PPP).

The decision was published in the Official Gazette on Sunday and enters into force on Monday.

What does the decision entail?

Its first article mandates that administrative entities must submit a statement detailing any infrastructure, service, or public utility projects, for which they seek private sector participation, to both Central Agency for Public Mobilization and Statistics (CAPMAS) and the Central PPP Unit at the Finance Ministry, no later than January 1s following the date this decision takes effect

These administrative entities include ministries, government departments, local administration units, public service and economic authorities, as well as wholly state-owned companies (or those owned by public legal entities).

For each project, the statement must include its name, implementation location, sector, investment cost, duration, the scheduled date for its tender, the scheduled date for contracting, the applicable law, regulation, or rules, and the chosen contracting method along with the justifications for it.

The aforementioned entities and companies shall update this statement and submit it to the two bodies referred to in the first paragraph of this article on a quarterly basis—specifically, at the end of every three-month period, calculated from the aforementioned January 1st.

Projects intended to be tendered by any of the aforementioned entities or companies are exempt from the provisions of this article if national security considerations dictate that their details should not be disclosed or published.

Article Two

Article Two of the resolution stipulates that the Central PPP Unit shall categorize, classify, and enter the data submitted to it—pursuant to the provisions of Article One of this resolution—into its own database.

The unit shall update this data periodically, based on the quarterly information it receives, by incorporating new projects, recording any amendments to previously submitted data, and identifying projects for which contracts have been signed or which have been abandoned.

The Central PPP Unit shall publish this data on its website, including information regarding projects intended for contracting, and make this data accessible for review by investors and the entities concerned with such projects.

Edited translation from Al-Masry Al-Youm

World.title: French police officers convicted of racist assault on Black music producer
World.content:
Paris AP —

The lawyer for a Black man who was beaten up by three French police officers hailed a “historic ruling” on Saturday after a court acknowledged the racist nature of the violence and sentenced them to between one and two years in prison.

The assault on Michel Zecler, a music producer, took place six years ago during the coronavirus pandemic and was caught on camera. It showed the officers repeatedly punching him, using a truncheon and tear gas against him for no apparent reason.

Zecler told The Associated Press after the incident that the officers hurled repeated insults at him, including a very strong racist epithet.

“What is very important is that the racist nature of the violence he suffered has been recognized,” Zecler’s lawyer, Serge Money, told France Info. “As a legal professional, one can only be satisfied. This is a first.”

Money said that from the very beginning of the proceedings, Zecler maintained that he had been racially insulted, whereas the defendants’ accounts were somewhat inconsistent.

“Ultimately, they were convicted of lying, as the falsification of written records was established,” he said. The verdict was issued late Friday in Paris.

Music producer Michel Zecler (L) stands next to his lawyer Serge Money (R) addressing media during a lunch break at the Palais de Justice, the main law court of Paris on the Ile de la Cite, central Paris. Thomas Samson/AFP/Getty Images

Videos published showed the violent arrest of Zecler in the 17th arrondissement of the French capital. The three officers intended to stop him for not wearing a face mask during the restrictions imposed because of the pandemic.

The video images, obtained by the AP, both from a security camera inside the studio and filmed by neighbors outside, showed officers following Zecler inside his music studio, where they could be seen repeatedly punching him and beating him with a truncheon.

“I want to understand why I have been assaulted by people who were wearing a police uniform,” Zecler told AP at the time. “I want justice actually, because I believe in the justice of my country.”

Zecler suffered injuries to his head, forearms and legs.

French law enforcement agencies have long faced complaints of excessive force. After Zecler was taken into custody for violence against public authority, then-Justice Minister Eric Dupond-Moretti said in a television interview that he was scandalized by the images. He admitted that some officers were racists, but denied systemic racism within the force.

Money said that without the video, Zecler would have ended up in prison. He added that the officers apologized.

“This ruling should set a precedent for all those who have not been believed,” he said. “There has to be a first, a starting point. It is now up to the justice system to make use of this ruling.
