World.title: Zelensky says intelligence shows Russia planning new strikes on Ukraine
World.content:
Ukraine’s President Volodymyr Zelensky said on Monday that intelligence showed Russia planned new strikes on Ukraine, and he urged the United States ​and other countries to take note as supplies of air defense systems depended on their decisions.

Russian forces have been subjecting Kyiv and other cities to virtually continuous air attacks since September. An attack on a central district of the capital on Monday injured five, while a strike on a town in the surrounding region killed 11 on Sunday.

“Our intelligence has information about preparations ‌by the Russians for ‌new strikes,” Zelensky said in his ​nightly ‌video address, ⁠without ​giving a ⁠time frame for any new attacks.

Zelensky has long called for increased supplies of air defense weapons and said on Monday that ensuring a ready supply meant denying Moscow the opportunity of “showing contempt for diplomacy and human life.”

“It is important that such signals are also heeded in the United States and in other countries whose decisions ⁠affect the supply of ballistic-missile defense systems to protect ‌our cities and infrastructure,” he said.

Zelensky ‌expressed satisfaction at support he said he noted ​at a meeting on Monday ‌of NATO’s parliamentary assembly, adding that this showed that Ukraine ‌merited a place in the alliance.

“The key point is that there is an understanding that Ukraine fully deserves a place in NATO and that Ukraine is not only capable of joining the Alliance but can genuinely strengthen NATO,” ‌he said.

“We are already in effect part of NATO – through the way we cooperate and through ⁠the values ⁠and political principles that unite us.”

Russia has consistently rejected any notion of Ukraine joining the Alliance and restated its position last week after the resumption of three-way talks with Ukraine and the United States of resolving the 4-1/2-year-old conflict.

Zelensky said earlier this month that US negotiators had floated the idea of Ukraine’s potential withdrawal from its eastern region of Donbas in exchange for joining NATO.

French President Emmanuel Macron said last week after a meeting of countries supporting Ukraine: “I think we must reopen the question of Ukraine’s membership ​to NATO.”

The Kremlin declined ​to comment on Zelensky’s account of the idea he said US negotiators had raised.

World.title: Israeli forces carry out major military operation in Al-Amari refugee camp
World.content:
LONDON: Israeli forces conducted a large-scale military operation in Al-Amari refugee camp, south of Ramallah, on Monday.

The raids, which began in the early hours of the morning, spread to the nearby city of Al-Bireh in the evening, amid reports of heavy gunfire and use of tear gas canisters. No injuries or detentions were immediately reported.

Israeli soldiers converted Al-Amari Youth Center at the refugee camp into a detention and field interrogation facility, the Palestinian Wafa news agency reported. They deployed military vehicles in the center’s courtyard in the early stages of the operation, while others were stationed at the entrance to the camp and soldiers took up positions on the roofs of some houses. They searched dozens of homes, vandalized the contents, detained dozens of people and interrogated them, Wafa said.

The refugee camp, home to about 7,800 people, is adjacent to Al-Quds Road, which connects Jerusalem with Ramallah.

Its youth center serves as a sports and social club. According to figures from the Palestinian Football Association, Israeli forces have killed 1,017 athletes since Oct. 7, 2023, and destroyed about 265 Palestinian sports facilities in the occupied West Bank and Gaza Strip.

World.title: Moscow accuses Estonia of hostile actions on ‘verge of triggering open war’
World.content:
MOSCOW: ​Russia’s Foreign Ministry on Monday accused Estonia, a NATO and European Union member state, of a range of hostile actions “on the verge of triggering open war,” ratcheting up its rhetoric after Estonia announced the closure of their land border.

Estonia plans to close border crossings with Russia from December 1 for at least six months after accusing Russian security services of staging an attempted arson attack on an Estonian defense company. Russia denied involvement in the attack.

The Russian ministry set out its accusations in a statement after summoning Estonia’s charge d’affaires ‌in Moscow to ‌issue a formal protest over Tallinn’s decision to close the ​border.

“The ‌Estonian ⁠diplomat was ​once ⁠again told that such provocative and extremely dangerous actions are on the verge of triggering open war with Russia,” the Russian ministry said.

Among a list of accusations, it said Estonia had allowed Ukraine to use its airspace “on the quiet” to attack Russian targets.

It also accused Estonia of trying to obstruct the movement of Russian cargo ships in the Baltic Sea, banning the transit of Russian and Belarusian grain, seeking a ban on the Russian language and threatening to ⁠close the Russian Orthodox Church.

“The Russian side reserves the right to ‌take comprehensive political and diplomatic measures aimed at protecting ‌Russia’s national interests and the legitimate rights of its citizens,” the ​ministry said.

In a statement, Estonia’s Foreign Ministry ‌did not respond to all of the allegations but denied that it allows its territory ‌to be used for Ukrainian military operations.

“While we generally do not comment on or engage with Russian propaganda narratives, in this case we can reiterate that Estonia has never allowed, and will never allow, its territory to be used for military operations by another country,” it said.

“Other countries ‌in our region have also made this position clear,” the ministry said.

In a post on X late Monday evening, Estonia’s foreign minister ⁠Margus Tsahkna wrote that “Russia ⁠is flooding the airwaves with baseless accusations against Estonia to distract from its own actions undermining European security.”

Russia has long accused Estonia and other NATO states in the Baltic region of allowing Ukrainian drones to use their airspace. Ukrainian drones have frequently entered NATO airspace, which Kyiv says is a result of Russian signal jamming.

NATO countries have repeatedly denied intentionally allowing drones to use their airspace, and blamed Russia for the incursions, for having launched the war with Ukraine in 2022.

NATO Secretary-General Mark Rutte, speaking in Berlin, mentioned the situation in Estonia along with an incursion last week by Russian missiles into Poland as events that the alliance was monitoring, and said it had options available to respond.

“We see ​situations in Poland and Estonia, etc.,” ​Rutte said. “When it comes to the military domain, we will always make assessments of our deterrence and defense and make updates where necessary.”

World.title: US flew drone over Mexican territory to help capture drug lord in Sinaloa
World.content:
MEXICO CITY: The United States flew a surveillance drone over Mexican territory to help the government track down and capture a top drug lord over the weekend in Sinaloa, Mexican security officials said Monday.

The recent detention of Fausto Isidro Meza Flores, known as “El Chapo Isidro” illustrates increasing law enforcement cooperation between the neighboring countries, but US involvement in Mexican security operations has long been a touchy subject.

US President Donald Trump has pressured Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum to crack down on cartels, while Mexico has repeatedly underscored its sovereignty. On Monday, Sheinbaum emphasized that US forces were not allowed to operate on the ground in Mexico and the governments were only sharing intelligence.

“This case in particular demonstrates the capacity of the armed forces” of Mexico to make major detentions, Sheinbaum said.

The US has sought to line up allies across Latin America to allow them to operate in their territories, with mixed responses from across the region.

The weekend detention of the capo, who was one of the FBI’s most wanted fugitives, triggered a burst of violence in the northern state of Sinaloa that left 20 people dead in the city of Guasave. Among them were four soldiers and 16 suspected criminals, Mexican officials said Monday.

Defense Secretary Gen. Ricardo Trevilla Trejo said Monday that the capture of Meza Flores and 16 members of his criminal group was the result of “very important intelligence sharing” with US authorities over the past three months to pinpoint Meza Flores’ location in Guasave.

In the week leading up to Meza Flores’ capture, that included authorizing the US to fly intelligence drones over Mexican territory, to assist Mexican law enforcement to later surround the capo and go in for the capture, Trevilla Trejo and other Mexican officials said. They emphasized that the intelligence mission was carried out in compliance with Mexican law.

On Monday, Mexico’s prosecutors’ office announced that it had formally charged Meza Flores and two other alleged cartel members with illegal possession of firearms and possession of methamphetamine with the intent to sell, adding that the three were flown to Mexico City over the weekend following their capture.

Authorities also highlighted that the US has an existing extradition request for Meza Flores for drug trafficking charges, leaving open the possibility that the cartel boss may be sent north to face justice.

His capture was celebrated by Mexican and US law enforcement as a major blow to criminal groups in the region.

The US government highlighted its intelligence support in the operation, but did not immediately provide more details about the use of the surveillance drone when asked on Monday.

Meza Flores led the Beltran Leyva organization and later became the leader of his own group, the Meza Flores Transnational Criminal Organization. He was also a key ally of a Sinaloa Cartel faction known as “Los Mayos,” which is locked in a brutal territorial war against another cartel faction in the Mexican state.

The capture of Meza Flores was the latest in a string of targeted operations against cartel kingpins by Mexican authorities, the largest of which was the February killing of Jalisco New Generation Cartel leader Nemesio Oseguera Cervantes, known as ” El Mencho.”

While the captures show that the government is doubling down on its fight on crime, many experts were quick to emphasize that the strategy could backfire.

In previous anti-crime offensives in Mexico and other parts of Latin America, knocking out cartel leaders without debilitating the entire criminal structure around them has largely only fueled bloody power struggles between cartel factions. That has been the case in recent years in Sinaloa.

World.title: Could divided Libya become a new front in the Russia-Ukraine war?
World.content:
LONDON: The distance from the Libyan port of Benghazi to the front line in war-torn Ukraine is more than 2,400 kilometers. But dramatic strikes on two Russian ships in the Mediterranean on Sunday served as a reminder that in the age of drone warfare, the front line is wherever combatants decide it is.

Ukraine’s security service, the SBU, said seven domestically made naval drones had been launched from a mothership in an operation the president, Volodymyr Zelensky, described as “exemplary.”

Ukraine said the drones hit the dry-cargo ship MV Angara, which it believed Russia was using to transport weapons, and sank the corvette Merkury, one of the Russian Navy’s newest warships, in the eastern Libyan port of Benghazi.

It was not the first time Ukraine had targeted Russian-linked vessels in the region. In December 2025, a Ukrainian security official said aerial drones hit and damaged the Qendil, a sanctioned oil tanker linked to Russia. Ship-tracking data later placed it off the coast of Libya.

In March, the Russian tanker Arctic Metagaz, which was carrying liquefied natural gas, caught fire in the Mediterranean. Moscow blamed Ukrainian naval drones. The tanker drifted for weeks before Libya’s coast guard began towing it.

The attacks show how the war in Ukraine is spreading beyond that country’s borders, raising fears that Libya was becoming a new battleground for foreign powers.

Addressing the NATO Parliamentary Assembly in Berlin by video on Monday, Zelensky said Russia could feel Ukraine’s response, from the oil refineries of western Siberia “to the coast of Libya, where its warships are sinking.”

Before (above) and after: satellite images show the Russian corvette at Benghazi naval base. Zelenskyy said Russia could feel Ukraine's response “to the coast of Libya, where its warships are sinking.” (Reuters file)

Western Libya is controlled by an internationally recognized government in Tripoli. The east of the country, where Benghazi is located, is controlled by forces loyal to military commander Khalifa Haftar, who has ties to Russia.

The eastern authorities said the Merkury had docked at Benghazi to refuel and take on supplies under a cooperation agreement with Russia.

The operation was the latest long-range assault by Kyiv’s forces, and followed an attack last week on the Kerch Bridge linking Russia to occupied Crimea.

Dmitry Peskov, spokesperson for the Kremlin, declined to comment directly on Sunday’s strikes and referred questions to the Russian Defense Ministry.

He issued a warning to Ukraine: “These actions result in highly painful consequences for the Kyiv regime. I would like to recall a statement made by Putin in Shenzhen, in which he affirmed that this practice, this course of action by our military will continue.”

Libya’s government in Tripoli condemned the Ukrainian operation and said it would not accept being drawn into the war.

Responding to Zelensky’s remarks, the Libyan Foreign Ministry said: “The continuation of the war between Russia and Ukraine gives neither side the right to conduct military operations on Libyan territory or in its territorial waters.”

Foreign forces would not be allowed to use Libyan ports or civilian infrastructure for military purposes, it added.

The Tripoli government also said it was alarmed by “risks posed by involving civilian ports and facilities in activities linked to external conflicts.”

The UN Support Mission in Libya expressed “serious concern” over the attacks and called for “an immediate, independent and transparent investigation.”

In a message posted on social media platform X, it added: “Libya cannot afford, and must not become, a battleground for foreign conflicts.”

The strikes underscored the ways in which the rival governments in Libya had left the country exposed to competition among outside powers. Whether Ukraine intends to open a new front in the Mediterranean or Africa remained unclear.

“Ukrainians are bringing war to Libya and the Sahel. It’s not a risk, it has happened,” Karim Mezran, director of the North Africa Initiative at the Atlantic Council’s Rafik Hariri Center, told Arab News.

“There are lots of Ukrainian special troops, or irregular troops, not tied to the Ukrainian government acting among some of the militias in Libya. And now they came out in the open.”

Russia's President Vladimir Putin (R) and Libya's eastern military strongman Khalifa Haftar. Karim Mezran said the attacks carried political weight and could strain Moscow’s alliance with Haftar. (AFP file)

He said widening the fight to Russian assets in Africa made little strategic sense for Ukraine, which was already stretched and risked retaliation. The aim, he suggested, was to dismantle the economic empire Russia had built in Libya.

That empire included oil and gas projects, mines, infrastructure and reconstruction contracts, he explained, as well as an arrangement under which Moscow relied on Haftar’s eastern-based Libyan National Army for access to airfields, ports and operational hubs.

Moscow had long backed Haftar and used eastern Libya as a staging post for its presence in North Africa and the Sahel. The location offered access to oil, military facilities and a deep-water Mediterranean port on NATO’s southern flank.

In April, a report by the Associated Press cited Libyan officials as saying that Ukrainian drone specialists were operating at military sites in Misrata, Tripoli and Zawiya in western Libya.

In September, Libyan authorities denied a CNN report that they had allowed Ukraine to use a military base to launch drones against Russia’s “shadow fleet” in the Mediterranean. The report linked those operations to the attack on the Arctic Metagaz.

“They have places with hangars where they have put these drones,” Mezran said, adding that Ukrainians themselves had named two bases.

He said the attack on Sunday would be “the first of many” that he warned could further destabilize a country already split between Haftar’s forces in the east and the internationally recognized Government of National Unity in Tripoli.

A Libyan Navy vessel is docked at the military port in Benghazi. The location offers access to oil, military facilities and a deep-water Mediterranean port on NATO’s southern flank. (Reuters file)

“Because the Russians are in the game in the Sahel, then there will be spillover against Haftar’s men,” Mezran said, suggesting that Ukraine might be providing military support to militias opposed to Haftar.

The attacks carried political weight and could strain Moscow’s alliance with Haftar, he added, and the incident “exposed the whole Russian structure, the money, the alliances with Haftar. In communication terms, it’s a masterpiece. Now the Russians have to reevaluate the relationship.”

An open confrontation between Russia and Ukraine on Libyan soil appeared unlikely. A more plausible risk was that Libya would become an arena for indirect competition as both sides looked for ways to raise the cost of a largely stalled war and strengthen their positions in any future talks.

The strikes on the Russian vessels on Sunday, far from the front line, could fit that pattern, though Ukraine has not said so. The consequences could be significant for Moscow, which uses eastern Libya’s ports and airfields as a foothold on Europe’s southern flank.

They could also complicate matters for Haftar, who is involved in a US-led push to unify the rival administrations in Libya. That effort was already struggling before the strikes and Mezran doubted it would succeed.

“I think the Boulos plan is dead,” he said. “I don’t believe the Libyans will ever go for it anyway.”

Libya has been divided since the NATO-backed uprising that toppled and killed Muammar Qaddafi in 2011. A civil war followed and a UN-brokered ceasefire halted the main fighting in October 2020.

Fire burns after an explosion aboard a Russian ship docked at Benghazi port, Libya, November 22, 2026. (Social media/via Reuters)

Now the country is split between the internationally recognized Government of National Unity, led by Prime Minister Abdul Hamid Dbeibah, and the eastern administration aligned with Haftar’s Libyan National Army.

The US-led initiative, spearheaded by Massad Boulos, senior adviser to US President Donald Trump on Arab and African affairs, aims to unify Libya’s rival administrations and pave the way for national elections.

According to diplomatic briefings, Dbeibah would remain as prime minister under the proposal, which would also give Haftar’s son, Saddam Haftar, a role on a presidential executive council. Critics have described the framework as a “forced marriage” that could entrench the power of the two families.

The UN is pursuing a parallel plan, presented in August 2025 and welcomed by the Security Council in Resolution 2835. Its political road map aims to unify state institutions and pave the way for presidential and parliamentary elections through broad Libyan participation.

The effort gained momentum with an agreement in August 2026 on steps to reconstitute the electoral commission and resolve disputes over election rules. Implementation has been held up by disagreements over appointments, however.

“This is a game of ignorance,” Mezran said. “I don’t know who to listen to anymore.”

He recalled a conversation with Hanna Serwaa Tetteh, the UN’s special representative for Libya, who, he said, told him: “I cannot do anything. I need the Security Council. And the Security Council doesn’t support me.”

Mezran said Tetteh was ready to pursue broader talks and added: “We need a dialogue, a quick dialogue.” What the country required, he added, was “a moment of inclusion. Otherwise, they will keep going to war.”

World.title: Soudah Waterfall becomes Saudi Arabia’s second Ramsar wetland
World.content:
RIYADH: Hidden among the misty highlands of Aseer, where monsoon clouds drift across terraced mountainsides, one of Saudi Arabia’s most distinctive natural landmarks has gained international recognition.

Soudah Waterfall, a year-round cascade tucked into the Kingdom’s highest mountain region, has been added to the Ramsar List of Wetlands of International Importance, becoming only the second site in Saudi Arabia to receive the designation.

The announcement, made by the National Center for Wildlife and Soudah Development, highlights growing efforts to safeguard some of the Kingdom’s most ecologically significant landscapes as environmental conservation takes on a larger role under Vision 2030.

Perched more than 2,400 meters above sea level in the Soudah highlands, the waterfall is a rarity in Saudi Arabia, where permanent mountain waterways are uncommon. Known locally as Wadi Al-Aziza, the site spans around 30 hectares and is centered on a dramatic 600-meter rocky gorge fed by perennial springs and pools.

The landscape is shaped by moisture carried inland by seasonal southwestern monsoon winds, creating pockets of greenery and wet habitats that stand in striking contrast to the region’s better-known arid environments.

That unique setting has helped turn the area into a biodiversity hotspot. Scientists regard the site as particularly important because it lies where the Paleotropical and Afrotropical floristic zones overlap, creating conditions that support a rich mix of plant and animal life, including rare and endemic species.

But the significance of Soudah Waterfall extends beyond its ecological value.

The surrounding mountains bear traces of centuries of human history, including traditional agricultural terraces carved into the slopes and the historic Abo Sarrah Palaces, which date back more than 1,000 years and stand just a short distance from the gorge.

Together, they tell the story of a long relationship between local communities and the landscape, where generations developed farming practices adapted to the rugged terrain while helping preserve natural resources.

The Ramsar designation places the site among wetlands recognized internationally for their environmental importance. Wetlands play a critical role in supporting wildlife, regulating water systems and storing carbon, while also helping communities sustain agriculture, fisheries and tourism.

As part of efforts to protect the newly listed site, the National Center for Wildlife has developed a 10-year conservation strategy in cooperation with Soudah Development and other stakeholders. The plan includes habitat restoration, sustainable water-resource management, invasive species control, climate adaptation measures, scientific monitoring and community engagement programs.

The designation comes at a time when wetlands worldwide are facing mounting pressure. According to figures cited by the center, around 411 million hectares of wetlands have disappeared globally since 1970, while more than a quarter of species that depend on wetland ecosystems are at risk of extinction.

Against that backdrop, conservationists say protecting places such as Soudah Waterfall is becoming increasingly important, not only for biodiversity but also for preserving cultural landscapes shaped by people and nature over centuries.

For visitors to the mist-covered peaks of Aseer, the designation offers fresh recognition of what locals have long known: that amid the Kingdom’s mountains lies a rare oasis where flowing water, wildlife and history converge.

World.title: The rise of community activities in Saudi Arabia
World.content:
RIYADH: For years, social connections in Saudi Arabia were often built through family networks, school friendships or the workplace. Increasingly, however, people are finding one another in different places: around pottery wheels, at book discussions, during hiking trips and through communities built around shared interests.

Across the Kingdom, hobby clubs, creative workshops and community-led gatherings are creating new opportunities for people to meet, connect and form friendships beyond their existing circles.

For many participants, the attraction is not simply the activity itself, but the relationships that grow around it.

That shift has given rise to platforms such as Private CRCL, an app designed to help people discover communities and experiences aligned with their interests.

For Fida Alkaud, co-founder and CEO of Private CRCL, the trend reflects a broader change in how people choose to socialize.

“I definitely think there’s a shift towards being more intentional and having an interest-led social culture in Saudi (Arabia),” she told Arab News.

The idea for the platform emerged after Alkaud noticed that many communities already existed across the Kingdom but were often difficult for newcomers to find.

“There wasn’t really a trusted digital platform that is connecting them in the way they should be, but I wanted to create that,” she said.

The communities range from creative workshops and cultural gatherings to sports and outdoor activities, offering people a chance to meet others who share similar passions and interests.

For Alkaud, what keeps people coming back is often the sense of belonging that develops over time.

“People aren’t necessarily just coming to do the activity. They’re looking for the people, and they’re looking more importantly for the sense of belonging that comes with being part of a community, that comes with being part of something bigger,” she said.

The growth of those communities comes as Saudi Arabia’s organized hobbies sector continues to expand.

Through the national Hawi platform, established under the Quality of Life Program, people can create and join clubs, organize activities and events, access dedicated spaces and connect with others who share their interests.

Yet beyond the growth in platforms and organized activities, participants say the appeal remains deeply personal.

Najla Alnafisi, a Riyadh resident who regularly attends creative workshops and community events, said the friendships and shared experiences are often what leave the greatest impression.

“I think it’s really about the people and the experience you share with them, more than the activity itself,” Alnafisi told Arab News.

She has noticed a growing number of opportunities for people to meet through common interests rather than circumstance.

“There has been a really nice shift in the way people connect in Saudi Arabia. We’re seeing more spaces where people can meet through shared interests,” she said.

For many, these communities provide something increasingly valuable in modern life: a chance to slow down, explore new interests and build meaningful connections with people they may never have met otherwise.

As interest-based communities continue to grow across the Kingdom, hobbies are becoming more than a way to fill spare time. They are creating spaces where people can discover new passions, broaden their social circles and find a sense of belonging.

In that sense, the activity itself may be only the beginning. What many participants ultimately find is a community.

World.title: US to blacklist Megaspeed chip firm linked to Nvidia scandal, source says
World.content:
WASHINGTON: The United ‌States on Monday is set to add Singapore-based chip firm Megaspeed, which is closely tied to an espionage investigation involving Nvidia, to its trade blacklist, a source told Reuters.

The expected addition of the company follows revelations that Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang had a relationship with Alice Huang, a Chinese businesswoman and Megaspeed’s controlling shareholder who is reportedly alleged to ‌be a ‌spy for Beijing. US companies cannot ‌ship goods, software and technology to companies on the list without a license, which is likely to be denied.

The New York Times reported last month that US authorities had concluded Alice Huang was a Chinese intelligence asset who passed information to Beijing while developing a close relationship ‌with the Nvidia ‌CEO.

Reuters could not independently verify the intelligence allegation. China ‌has said the spy accusations are “groundless.”

Nvidia ‌lists Megaspeed as an official cloud partner in its directory. Megaspeed attracted public attention in October 2025, when the New York Times reported it was ‌under US investigation over whether it was helping Chinese customers obtain advanced Nvidia chips subject to Washington’s export controls. The last time the Commerce Department placed any new entities on the list was October 2025.

As Reuters exclusively reported in June, the US has held off adding China’s AI startup DeepSeek, memory chipmaker CXMT and more than 100 other companies flagged as national security risks to the trade blacklist, as the Trump administration tried to avoid escalating tensions with Beijing.

World.title: Iraq, Egypt agree to lift entry visa requirements
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq and Egypt have reached an agreement to cancel entry visa requirements between the two countries.

Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi announced the decision on Monday during a joint press conference with Egyptian President Abdel Fattah el-Sisi at Ittihadiya Palace in the Egyptian capital, Cairo.

The visa waiver aims to facilitate the movement of citizens and boost tourism, trade, and political ties between both countries.

The announcement came alongside the fourth session of the Iraq-Egypt Higher Joint Committee, where officials discussed agreements covering energy, oil supplies, transportation, investment, and regional security.

While the agreement has been officially announced by the state-run Iraqi News Agency (INA), it is still unclear when the exemption will go into effect, how long visitors may stay, and whether security checks would still be required.

Travelers should check with their respective foreign ministries or airlines before booking immediate visa-free travel.

World.title: Iraqi Airways to sell two 1982 Boeing 747s parked in Tunisia since 1991
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Airways published on Wednesday an official direct-sale notice for two 1982 Boeing 747 aircraft that have been parked at Nefta International Airport in Tozeur, Tunisia, since January 1991.

Both airplanes were built in 1982. One is originally configured as a VIP government transport used during Saddam Hussein’s rule, and the other is a convertible passenger-and-cargo airliner.

The two aircraft are equipped with Pratt & Whitney JT9D-7F engines.

Each aircraft is valued at $900,000, or $1.8 million for the pair, an 82 percent increase over an unsuccessful 2023 auction attempt priced at $494,000 per jet.

Shortlisted bidders must provide a 20 percent deposit per aircraft. The buyer must also pay a two percent service fee,  publication costs, ownership transfer, customs clearance, transport, taxes, and any parking fees accumulated after handover.

Both planes are sold strictly “as is” on the ramp in Tozeur with no technical warranty or guarantee of airworthiness.

Companies or individuals can submit offers for one or both aircraft to a sales committee at the Iraqi Embassy in Tunisia between December 21, 2026, and January 5, 2027. Selected buyers have five days to pay the full balance, and any final sale requires the approval of the Iraqi minister of transport.

The two jets were flown to southern Tunisia in January 1991 to shield them from coalition airstrikes ahead of the Gulf War.

International sanctions, legal disputes, and decades of unpaid storage fees kept them grounded.

Iraq previously settled roughly $5.4 million in accumulated parking debts with Tunisian authorities in 2020, and unlike the 2023 sale attempt, the current notice removes earlier restrictions that required the airplanes to be scrapped or barred political use.

World.title: Iraqi PM, Egyptian president co-chair expanded meeting in Cairo
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi and Egyptian President Abdel Fattah el-Sisi co-chaired an expanded meeting between the delegations of the two countries on Monday at the Ittihadiya Palace in Cairo.

The two sides discussed mechanisms to strengthen and develop bilateral relations, particularly in the economic, trade, and investment areas to fulfill the aspirations of the people in both countries.

The two leaders also addressed coordination on regional and international issues of mutual concern, according to a statement released by the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO).

The Egyptian president and Iraqi prime minister held a joint press conference where al-Zaidi highlighted the distinguished economic relations between the two countries and the mutual commitment to promote these ties in different sectors.

According to al-Zaidi, a series of measures have been adopted to bolster cooperation between Iraq and Egypt.

Iraq is open to the Arab world, seeking strong relations that are based on cooperation and mutual interests, according to the Iraqi prime minister.

Al-Zaidi underlined that Iraq and Egypt have similar political positions and a shared strategy for creating regional security, reducing tensions, and resolving conflicts through communication to maintain regional and international stability.

Al-Zaidi’s visit to Egypt coincides with the fourth session of the Joint Higher Committee between the two countries.

The Egyptian president commended Iraq’s positions that support peace, as well as its efforts to prioritize dialogue and avoid escalation to achieve stability in the region.

World.title: Iraqi PM, Egyptian president discuss bilateral ties, regional issues
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi and Egyptian President Abdel Fattah el-Sisi met at Cairo’s al-Ittihadiya Palace on Monday to expand economic cooperation and coordinate diplomatic efforts on regional security.

The discussions coincide with the fourth session of the joint higher committee, which al-Zaidi is co-chairing alongside Egyptian Prime Minister Mostafa Madbouly.

The trip marks al-Zaidi’s first official visit to Egypt since taking office in May 2026.

Baghdad and Cairo are negotiating a potential supply of 10 million barrels of Iraqi crude to Egypt, alongside alternative export paths that bypass the Strait of Hormuz.

In addition to discussions for establishing an Iraqi Rafidain Bank branch in Cairo, the two countries are negotiating new agreements pertaining to commerce, transportation, and finance.

In 2024, the volume of trade exchange between Iraq and Egypt totaled $1.1 billion.

While both parties talked about increasing the participation of Egyptian companies in Iraq’s infrastructure development, al-Zaidi proposed additional initiatives to attract investment.

To handle wider regional issues, such as security risks involving Iran, Yemen, and Red Sea commerce routes, al-Zaidi and el-Sisi emphasized the importance of dialogue.

Al-Zaidi is expected to meet with Arab League Secretary-General Nabil Fahmy while in Cairo and speak to representatives of member states to promote joint Arab action.

World.title: Ninth Erbil International Food, Packaging, and Plastics Exhibition opens with 286 companies
World.content:
Erbil (IrraqiNews.com) – The ninth edition of the Erbil International Food, Packaging, and Plastics Exhibition opened on Monday, November 23, 2026, bringing together 286 local and international companies from 20 countries.

Speaking at the opening ceremony attended by the Iraqi News Agency (INA), Erbil Governor Omed Khoshnaw stated that the Erbil International Fair serves as a premier hub for showcasing domestic goods and attracting foreign enterprises, ranking first among trade exhibitions across Iraq.

Khoshnaw noted that strong domestic and international corporate participation reflects ongoing stability and economic growth in Erbil and the broader Kurdistan Region, emphasizing that supporting local manufacturing remains a central pillar of the Kurdistan Regional Government’s strategic agenda alongside steady annual growth in registered production firms coordinated with the Investment Board and relevant ministries.

Exhibition spokesperson Hoshmand Mohammed told INA that the ninth edition features broad international representation across specialized food processing, packaging, and plastics sectors.

He added that the event provides a vital commercial platform to introduce Iraqi-made products to global firms while giving domestic businesses and citizens direct access to the latest international food technologies and product lines, noting that the exhibition opens daily to visitors from across all Iraqi governorates starting at 11:00 AM.

World.title: Iraq considers exporting 10 million barrels of oil to Egypt
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq is currently studying a proposal to supply Egypt with approximately 10 million barrels of crude oil.

The potential shipment is a primary topic during Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi’s official visit to Cairo, which coincides with the fourth session of the Iraqi-Egyptian Joint Higher Committee.

According to Iraqi Deputy Minister of Trade Sattar al-Jabiri, the 10-million-barrel supply is still being considered. There have been no confirmed or declared delivery dates, shipment timetables, or payment arrangements.

Finding other export routes to avoid the Strait of Hormuz, where shipping has experienced increased security hazards, is one of the important topics of the discussions taking place in Cairo.

In addition to oil, al-Zaidi and Egyptian President Abdel Fattah el-Sisi are overseeing bilateral memoranda of understanding (MoUs) pertaining to commerce, transportation, and the possible reactivation of Iraq’s Rafidain Bank branch in Cairo.

The fourth session of the Joint Higher Committee aims to build on cooperation agreements signed previously, while both nations continue advancing regional integration through the Egypt-Iraq-Jordan trilateral cooperation mechanism.

Additionally, al-Zaidi’s official trip to Egypt aims to promote bilateral ties and expand Egyptian corporate participation in Iraqi infrastructure.

World.title: Iraqi Atomic Energy Commission outlines 10-year roadmap for peaceful nuclear reactor
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Iraqi Atomic Energy Commission announced on Monday, November 23, 2026, that constructing a peaceful nuclear reactor will take roughly seven to ten years, confirming that authorities are preparing to launch immediate preparatory steps—including specialized workforce training, laboratory construction, and radiopharmaceutical projects—ahead of full-scale reactor operations.

In statements to the official newspaper, Murtadha Adhab, Iraq’s National Liaison Officer with the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA), emphasized that peaceful nuclear applications span agriculture, industry, education, and broader sectoral development.

He highlighted the practical role of radioactive materials in sterilizing medical supplies and preserving agricultural seeds over extended storage periods to prevent spoilage.

Rather than delaying progress until a reactor is fully built, Adhab explained that the commission is actively coordinating with relevant state institutions to bring near-term strategic projects into execution.

Foremost among these is a radiopharmacy initiative focused on producing medical radioisotopes. Under the commission’s phased roadmap, initial efforts will prioritize qualifying technical personnel, establishing specialized laboratories, and initiating radioisotope fractionation processes before transitioning to full domestic isotope production once the reactor comes online.

Adhab underscored that Iraq’s nuclear reactor and all associated atomic energy programs are strictly dedicated to peaceful purposes. He noted that this commitment is firmly enshrined in the Iraqi Constitution and governed by domestic legislation as well as the international treaties and IAEA safeguards agreements ratified by Baghdad.

World.title: US dollar drops noticeably to 168,000 dinars across Baghdad, Erbil, and Basra markets
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The exchange rate of the U.S. dollar against the Iraqi dinar recorded a notable drop across major domestic parallel markets on Monday morning, November 23, 2026, breaking well below the 170,000-dinar threshold as purchasing bids harmonized at 168,000 IQD per $100 across Baghdad, Erbil, and Basra.

According to morning trading figures, physical banknote rates across Iraq’s three primary commercial hubs opened as follows.

In Baghdad, currency exchange counters posted retail selling rates at 168,500 IQD against buying offers of 168,000 IQD per $100.

In Erbil, currency desks quoted slightly lower retail selling rates at 168,300 IQD alongside matching buying bids of 168,000 IQD per $100.

In Basra, foreign exchange offices mirrored Baghdad’s pricing, listing retail selling rates at 168,500 IQD and purchasing offers at 168,000 IQD per $100.

Despite the noticeable retreat toward the 168,000-dinar mark, parallel cash rates still maintain a spread of 16,300 to 16,500 dinars above the Central Bank of Iraq’s (CBI) official rate of 152,000 IQD per $100 (1,520 IQD per dollar).

World.title: PM Modi meets Nepal's Balen Shah, offers Rs 15,000 crore economic package
World.content:

NEW DELHI: India and Nepal looked to usher in a new chapter in ties, setting aside recent friction, as PM Modi announced a $1.63 billion (Rs 15,000 crore) economic package, the largest ever for the Himalayan nation, after a meeting with his counterpart, Balendra Shah. The Nepal PM responded by declaring that India-Nepal ties stand as firm as the Himalayas and as vast as the ocean.India and Nepal also signed eight MoUs as the leaders laid foundation stones for multiple cross-border infrastructure and energy initiatives, while virtually flagging off the Saryu-Kamala Express, a new rail service connecting Ayodhya to Janakpur in Nepal, to boost religious tourism and people-to-people exchanges.A 10-point joint vision document, which will shape the roadmap for cooperation across various sectors, emphasised updating the bilateral legal framework - including through a review of the 1950 Treaty of Peace and Friendship - to ensure a forward-looking relationship. Both sides reaffirmed their commitment in the document to resolving all outstanding matters, including boundary disputes, through "constructive dialogue"."The bond between India and Nepal is not merely one of neighbourhood, but of belonging and unshakeable trust. Our joys are shared, and so are our challenges. We are partners in each other's progress, and a pillar of support for one another in difficult times," said Modi after what was his first meeting in person with Shah.The talks saw focus on border infrastructure as the two inaugurated the Dharchula road bridge connecting Uttarakhand and Nepal, and laid the foundation stone for the Banbasa Integrated Check Post. Modi said India remained committed to accelerating road and rail links via UP and Bihar, while providing Nepal access to India's Kandla and Paradip ports to facilitate smooth transit trade.The contentious boundary matter was also discussed in the meeting with the two directing the foreign secretaries to work on the outstanding-related issues.In his remarks, Modi leveraged deep religious and spiritual links as an anchor for bilateral ties, referencing Ram, Sita and the Buddha, and saying India and Nepal had the blessings of all three. He said India and Nepal will also work together to enhance connectivity between Buddhist and Shiv-Shakti sacred sites in both countries, including Lumbini and Bodh Gaya.Expressing condolences for the loss of life caused by the devastating floods in Nepal in Aug, Modi said India's development cooperation package worth 24,000 crore Nepalese rupees ($1.63 billion) will give fresh momentum to Nepal's reconstruction and long-term development. The package includes Rs 3,500 crore as a grant and the remaining in the form of a line of credit for energy projects.Modi called the vision document a blueprint to collectively realise their respective resolutions of a Viksit Bharat and Samunnat Nepal (Developed India and Prosperous Nepal). He said together they were going to write a golden chapter in India-Nepal ties.Shah, who invited Modi to visit Nepal, said the leaders held forward-looking discussions and that "mutual respect, steadfast trust, and unbroken goodwill" are bedrock of the ties. Nepal PM called for expanding air connectivity and the leaders agreed to convert the Kathmandu-Bhairahawa-Lucknow air route into a two-way route, allowing planes to fly back and forth along the same path instead of just one direction.Energy cooperation figured prominently in the talks, with the duo laying foundation stone for Lower Arun Hydroelectric Project and reiterating commitment to timely completion of Arun-3 project. They inaugurated Motihari-Amlekhgunj Pipeline Phase-2 and laid the foundation stone for the new Jhapa Petroleum Terminal, expanding fuel supply security for Nepal."For many years, India has been a reliable supplier of petro products and other essential commodities for Nepal. In keeping with the spirit of our Neighbourhood First Policy, despite serious challenges related to oil supply this year, we maintained the supply of fuel, fertilisers, and other essential items to Nepal," said Modi.PM said Nepal's rivers hold potential for clean energy and India's vast energy market can turn this potential into a strong foundation for Nepal's economic prosperity.In his remarks, Shah stressed the "incomparable bond" shared by the people of India and Nepal. "The ties between Nepal and India stand as firm as the Himalayas and as vast as the ocean. As a dependable and trusted neighbour, India has consistently stood as a first responder during difficult hours," he added.

World.title: Bisleri controversy puts industry in hot water
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Even as Bisleri on Monday said its mineral water is "safe for consumption, following stringent 90-odd quality checks", the

action against the popular brand has put the spotlight on compliance and raised the bar across the nearly $4 billion packaged water industry.

With Bisleri International accounting for an estimated 60% of the packaged water market, the action may have wider implications across the sector on quality controls, manufacturing processes and labelling practices, industry experts told TOI.

The development comes after the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) Sunday initiated prosecution against the country's most widely recognised packaged water brand after a sample was found non-compliant with prescribed safety standards.



On Monday, the scrutiny seems to have extended beyond Bisleri, with testing and investigations covering other players in the industry. The market led by players such as Bisleri, Coca-Cola's Kinley, PepsiCo's Aquafina and Tata Consumer Products' Himalayan, continues to project a positive long-term growth trajectory, underpinned by population growth, rising per-capita consumption and increasing penetration of branded packaged water across consumer segments.





Bisleri could face a short-term impact, but the larger outcome should be a more accountable industry and better consumer protection, notes Lloyd Mathias, independent director, who had stints in senior leadership roles in FMCG and telecom companies. "The tightening of compliance norms is a long overdue move and will ultimately benefit consumers. The packaged water industry has operated with considerable flexibility (on standards), with definitions around purity, mineral content and even the addition of minerals or vitamins often remaining fluid.

These need to be clearly and strictly defined, as they are in developed markets, with transparent labelling so consumers know exactly what they are drinking. Companies have also been relatively casual about the labelling (on the pack)," he said.

Further, the compliance on the sector has increased over the last two years since it moved under the ambit of FSSAI as a "high-risk food" category in Nov 2024, following the removal of BIS.

Typically, enforcement and monitoring in the industry has been weak, allowing even substandard and fake brands to operate. "Greater regulatory oversight is a positive step towards ensuring consistent quality and consumer safety," said an industry expert. Many see it similar to 2003, when CSE's findings on pesticide residue in soft drinks, triggered a wider review of food safety standards and testing.

World.title: NIA court frees 4 held for 2020 Srinagar terror attack that killed 2 soldiers
World.content:
Special NIA judge Manjeet Rai ordered their release forthwith if they were not required in any other case.

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

SRINAGAR: The killing of two Army soldiers in a Nov 2020 terrorist attack on the outskirts of Srinagar was established, but the prosecution failed to prove that the four arrested men had helped the terrorists, a special NIA court said Monday while acquitting them under UAPA.Special NIA judge Manjeet Rai acquitted Nasir Ahmad Dar, Zahid Ahmad Allai, Usman Ahmad Sheikh and Humayun Ahmad Sheikh of charges under sections 13, 18, 19 and 39 of UAPA. He ordered their release forthwith if they were not required in any other case.The court said there was no evidence that the accused conspired with, sheltered or supported the terrorists, communicated with them or were present near the attack site. No arms, explosives or other material were found in their possession, making the statutory presumption under section 43E of UAPA inapplicable.The prosecution case rested entirely on circumstantial evidence, with no eyewitness linking the four men to the attack. Citing Supreme Courtâs 1984 judgement in Sharad Birdhichand Sarda vs State of Maharashtra, NIA court reiterated that every circumstance in a case based on circumstantial evidence must be fully established and the chain must point exclusively to the accusedâs guilt.The court said prosecution had established that the attack killed two soldiers and a service rifle was lost, but the gravity of the crime could not substitute for legal proof.âThe loss of lives is a grave one and the anxiety of the prosecuting agency to bring every person responsible to book is understandable. But the law requires that guilt be proved by legal evidence and the gravity of the crime only heightens the need for such proof,â it said.The four men are residents of Zainakote, where the attacked happened near the HMT factory on Nov 26, 2020, when terrorists fired at an Army road opening party, killing constable Rattan Singh and sepoy Des Raj. The attackers took away a service rifle.Police registered an FIR, naming seven accused. The four men were arrested after questioning several alleged âovergroundâ operatives of terrorist groups. They remained in judicial custody throughout the trial and appeared before the court through video conferencing.The other three, identified as Abrar Nadeem alias Khitaab, Muslim alias Hanzala alias Babar and Asrar alias Mahmood alias Abdullah, were described as Pakistani terrorists in the chargesheet. They were killed in separate shootouts in Sopore of Baramulla district and Malura outside Srinagar in June 2021, and proceedings against them were abated. The snatched rifle was later found in a separate case in Sopore.

World.title: Can't do much for Tamil Nadu man in Russia army: Govt to SC
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The Centre on Monday told the

that it does not have much locus in ensuring the return of an Indian national who renounced his citizenship to take up Russia's and joined its army.

Although Solicitor General (SG) Tushar Mehta said that govt would explore its options for the repatriation of Abinesh - a

native who had gone to Moscow for studies but took up Russian citizenship there after surrendering his Indian passport - he added that Russian authorities are right in refusing information about the individual who is now enrolled in their armed forces.

The apex court asked the Union govt to explore the possibility of Abinesh's return.



Hearing his father's petition, a bench led by CJI Surya Kant said little is known about Abinesh's agreement with the intermediary who had arranged for his studies in Moscow. It asked the Centre if it could help now that the Russian authorities are claiming that he had renounced Indian citizenship and acquired Russian citizenship.

The Solicitor General told the court that he would take instructions from the ministry concerned on what kind of humanitarian intervention could be made in this case.





Months after Abinesh left for Russia for studies in April, the Indian Embassy in Moscow responded to his family, saying, "The Embassy has taken up the matter with the Ministry of Defence of the Russian Federation and requested it to release him. It may be mentioned that he has joined the Russian Army as a Russian citizen. As per the attached documents, he has willingly relinquished Indian citizenship. He has a Russian passport; the Embassy will update you as soon as a response is received from the Russian authorities.

World.title: SCO: Pakistan set to invite India for culture ministers' meeting
World.content:
After participating in the SCO inaugural civilisational dialogue in New Delhi,

is now all set to deliver an invitation to India for a meeting of the culture ministers it will host under its presidency of the Eurasian bloc early next year.

It will be interesting to see how India responds as no Indian minister has visited Pakistan since the Pahalgam terrorist attack.

Significantly, Islamabad is also preparing to host the SCO heads of state council summit - where India is usually represented by PM Narendra Modi -next year in late August, after initially considering having it on August 14 â Pakistan's Independence Day. An August 14 summit is unlikely to have seen participation by India at any level.



The only significant visit to Pakistan from India after the April 2025 Pahalgam attack was by MEA additional secretary Alok Dimri for a meeting of the SCO national coordinators in September â shortly after Pakistan assumed presidency â to firm up the calendar of events under Islamabad's stewardship.

After what is officially called Meeting of Ministers of Culture (SCO-MMC), Pakistan will also host more high-profile meetings of the SCO defence and foreign ministers in the run up to the Islamabad summit in August.





The meeting for cultural cooperation among SCO member-states in Pakistan is a relatively low-stakes event for India that keeps political commitments minimal, unlike the foreign and defence high-level gatherings which might raise the political temperature at home.

The last minister to visit Pakistan was S Jaishankar for a meeting of the SCO foreign ministers' meeting in October 2024, well before Pahalgam.

Amid criticism by the Opposition for hosting Pakistan minister Musadik Malik for the Modi-proposed civilisational dialogue last week, India reiterated there was no dilution of its position on the

that was "put in abeyance" after the Pahalgam attack. India has stressed that SCO cooperation should not be mistaken for bilateral thaw.

The visit by Malik passed off smoothly without any bilateral friction as he adhered to the protocol of addressing multilateral SCO themes, rather than raising sensitive bilateral issues.

While the key question remains whether Modi will travel to Islamabad for the SCO summit, Indian officials say such a visit is highly improbable at this stage. Any bilateral thaw that might result in Modi's visit requires, as far as India is concerned, a fundamental shift in Pakistan's position on cross-border terrorism.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

India is seeking tangible progress on its security concerns and doesn't want to create any optics of normalisation when these concerns remain unaddressed.

The possibility of a senior minister, most likely Jaishankar, representing India is not ruled out. It would allow India to sustain its active engagement with the SCO, while not being seen as softening its Pakistan policy. Officials point to the fact that there's already a precedent for that. In 2024, it was Jaishankar who attended the heads of summit in Kazakhstan, filling in for the PM.

World.title: Sandpapergate scandal: AB de Villiers makes new claim about Australian ball-tampering
World.content:
Former South African batsman AB de Villiers has alleged Australia engaged in ball-tampering from the first match of their 2018 "Sandpapergate" tour of South Africa.

Also read | You cannot sandpaper the truth selectively or partially

de Villiers alleged in a post on his YouTube channel that the ball-tampering, which culminated in Cameron Bancroft being caught using sandpaper in the third Test in Cape Town, actually began in the first Test in Durban.

He also said the Australian bowlers, who have denied any involvement, must have known what was going on.

A fierce debate about the eight-year-old events was triggered in Australia this month when Usman Khawaja claimed the whole team knew about the plot to alter the flight of the ball.

Bancroft, who was banned along with captain Steve Smith and David Warner after the incident, said in a recent article that sandpaper was first used in the second Test in Port Elizabeth.

But de Villiers said: "It started in Durban, by the way, not in PE. I'm very happy for people to quote me on that.

"I see everyone is sort of admitting that in Port Elizabeth it also happened. I can very much tell you Durban was no different, in the first Test. Go look at the footage. Absolutely no doubt in my mind."

He added: "We lost that first Test match in Durban with the ball reversing at a very, very interesting time. Way too early for anyone to reverse a ball at Kingsmead. Trust me, I've played a lot of cricket there."

de Villiers added: "So whatever they did there, whether it was sandpaper or [a] nail, I don't care. The fact of the matter is they were caught and everyone knew. Just stand up and say 'we were wrong'. A lot is at stake now because they lied.

"The bowlers in particular knew because the ball doesn't just reverse. It's not your first Test match for Australia. So just stand up and say, 'guys, we were wrong'."

de Villiers was a central figure in a bad-tempered series. He was run out in Durban and Australian bowler Nathan Lyon appeared to drop the ball on him — one of several incidents that inflamed tensions during the series.

The then South African captain Faf du Plessis revealed in his autobiography that he had persuaded the normally mild-mannered De Villiers to lead an aggressive response in the second Test to what Du Plessis saw as bullying tactics by Australia.

"I spoke to AB and said that the only way we were going to win the series was if he was willing to lead the fight against the Aussies with me. 'You and I will fight fire with fire. The rest of the team will follow, but only if the two of us lead the charge'."

Du Plessis wrote that his former schoolmate took up the challenge, not only by aggressively "sledging" Smith but by scoring an outstanding century, which helped South Africa win the match and go on to win the series.

Cricket Australia on Saturday (November 21) threw its "unanimous support" behind Pat Cummins to remain the current Test captain, rejecting any suggestion his integrity had been compromised by the lingering "Sandpapergate" scandal.

Cummins has been under huge pressure since Khawaja claimed the whole team knew about the ball-tampering plot but he strenuously denied being aware of what was going on in a press conference last week.

World.title: Federal appeals court gives President Donald Trump path to erasing hush money conviction
World.content:
A federal appeals court on Monday (November 23, 2026) gave U.S. President Donald Trump a new pathway to erasing his hush money criminal conviction, moving the case to a federal court where he could seek to have it dismissed on immunity grounds.

Also read | Donald Trump sentenced to ‘unconditional discharge’ in hush money case

A three-judge panel of the 2nd US Circuit Court of Appeals reversed a lower court decision that had kept the case in state court in New York, where Mr. Trump was tried and convicted on 34 felony counts of falsifying business records to obscure a $130,000 payment to adult film performer Stormy Daniels.

The panel ordered a lower court to promptly issue a decision on whether the case should remain in federal court. If that happens, Mr. Trump could then argue that the verdict should be discarded because of Presidential immunity.

The decision also set in motion a halt to proceedings in Mr. Trump's simultaneous state court appeal. Trump denies wrongdoing and was given no punishment in the case, which made him the first U.S. President convicted of a crime.

In a two-page order, the 2nd Circuit panel said it disagreed with the late US District Judge Alvin Hellerstein's earlier denial of Mr. Trump's request to move the historic case from state court to federal court, a process known as removal.

World.title: Manik Saha says party probing presence of masked men in BJP election rally
World.content:
Tripura Chief Minister Dr. Manik Saha on Monday (November 23, 2026) reacted to the presence of several masked youths in a BJP election rally in Agartala on Saturday (November 21). He said he had come to know this from newspaper reports and subsequently took up the matter with the party leadership.

“I don’t support this. In fact, our party does not approve such behaviour from our ranks. The party is inquiring into the matter and will follow up,” he told reporters.

Elections to 21 Urban Local Bodies including Agartala Municipal Corporation (AMC) are due on November 27. The ruling BJP has already won five of them unopposed as candidates from other parties and independents did not submit nomination papers.

The appearance of several masked men at the BJP’s election rally in Agartala stirred controversy, with CPI(M) and Congress registering complaints to the state election commission. The Congress also lodged a complaint at the West Agartala Police Station.

Secretary of the State Election Commission on Monday (November 23) said they received complaints about the issues and forwarded them to the police headquarters for necessary action. He said the commission would ensure free and peaceful elections.

BJP sources said veteran minister and city campaign in-charge Ratan Lal Nath organised the procession. They said the masked youths were actually party supporters from Mohanpur, north of Agartala, home Assembly constituency of minister Nath.

CPI(M) and Congress, however, claimed the masked men were actually anti-socials who were likely to be engaged in creating trouble and rig the elections. They also complained of the silence of the police in initiating action despite registering complaints.

World.title: Close to realising PM Narendra Modi’s dream for Kashmir, says Kiren Rijiju
World.content:
Terming the work of J&K Waqf Board as “the best-performing” in the country, Union Minister of Parliamentary Affairs and Minority Affairs Kiren Rijiju on Monday (November 23, 2026) said the region is close to achieve the dream Prime Minister Narendra Modi has for it.

Also read | Kiren Rijiju reiterates Centre’s resolve to restore Statehood to Jammu and Kashmir in due course

Recalling his past tours of Kashmir as Minister of State (MOS) Home and as Law Minister, Mr. Rijiju said, “I remember there were no large programmes as we visited frontier districts to meet soldiers and discuss how to realise the dream of PM Modi. I must say we are very close to realising the dream PM Modi had for Kashmir. He set a goal not only for a peaceful region but also to take J&K to new heights,” said Mr. Rijiju, while speaking at the Waqf Day-2026 at the Sher-e-Kashmir University of Agricultural Sciences and Technology in Srinagar.

Mr. Rijiju said Kashmir was moving ahead at a very “fast pace”. “Seeing the situation today, I can say India’s and J&K’s future is bright. People of Kashmir are large hearted. Today, sportsmen across the country wait to participate in the winter games at Gulmarg every year. The concept, besides adventure and water sports, was introduced in 2019,” said Mr. Rijiju.

Earlier in the day, the Union minister inaugurated the construction of Bibi Halima College of Nursing & Medical Technology (BHCNMT), at Kathi Darwaza, Rainawari, Srinagar. He said the alumni of the educational institute included 16 Kashmir University Gold Medalists, the highest among nursing colleges and over 10 international NCLEX qualifiers in the USA and Canada. “Its graduates also constitute around 30% of nursing officers at SKIMS and over 25% of the nursing workforce at Government Medical College-associated hospitals,” he added.

Praising the arrangements and management at the Nursing College and also the works done at the Hazratnal shrine, Mr. Rijiju said, “The space created at Hazratbal for female pilgrims to offer prayers is beautiful and aesthetically pleasing. I congratulate the Chairperson of the Waqf Board, Darakhshan Andrabi, in this regard. It’s the best performing board in the country.”

The Union Minister also highlighted the need to properly utilise and manage over nine lakh Waqf properties across the country. “It could bring significant socio-economic changes in the Muslim community. Poor and disadvantaged members of the Muslim community could benefit considerably if Waqf assets were utilised for their welfare, of which the J&K Waqf Board’s functioning is an example,” said Mr. Rijiju.

He also congratulated Ms. Andrabi and her entire team for “undertaking development initiatives and improving facilities at important religious and public institutions”.

Praising PM Modi for his vision. Mr. Andrabi said, “I became the first woman chairperson in 2022 and the board was constituted. There was no official structure then and the same was put in place. It is paying dividends.”

National Conference (NC) leader and Member of Parliament (MP) Mian Altaf highlighted the role of Mr. Rijiju pertaining to Kashmir. “He [Rijiju] frequently visits Kashmir and has always loved people. He always tried to contribute to Kashmir as he held different ministries. We all dream to have a better Kashmir, even what it was 30 years ago. My sister Ms. Andrabi is doing work that deserves applaud too,” said Mr. Altaf.

World.title: Will bank manager accept Kayalvizhi Alagiri’s apology, asks Madras High Court
World.content:
The Madras High Court on Monday (November 23, 2026) wanted to know whether a bank manager would be willing to accept an apology from former Union Minister M.K. Alagiri’s daughter Kayalvizhi Alagiri and agree for closure of a criminal case registered against her for allegedly slapping him supposedly due to anger management issues on July 20, 2026.

Justice V. Lakshminarayanan directed the Inspector of Shastri Nagar police station in Adyar, Chennai to make sure that Harsheen Singh, a branch manager with State Bank of India, appears before the court on Tuesday (November 24, 2026) if he is willing to accept the apology and give a quietus to the issue than continuing the prosecution.

The direction was issued during the hearing of a writ petition (criminal) filed by Ms. Alagiri seeking a direction to the police to register a First Information Report (FIR) against the bank manager on the basis of a counter complaint lodged by her on July 25, 2026 accusing him of having subjected her to verbal abuse, aggressive intimidation and public humiliation.

Government Advocate (criminal side) S. Yogaraja Sekar told the judge that Ms. Alagiri was the owner of a commercial building in which the bank branch was functioning. There was a dispute between the landlady and the tenant over the non-functioning of an elevator in the building and a quarrel over that issue had led to a physical assault against the bank manager on July 20, 2026.

The police had intially registered a First Information Report (FIR) against Ms. Alagiri under various provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita for abusing and assaulting the bank manager. It also completed the investigation and filed a charge sheet before a Metropolitan Magistrate in Chennai. The Magistrate was slated to take up the case for hearing next on December 22, 2026, the law officer said.

In so far as the counter complaint lodged by the landlady against the bank manager was concerned, the Government Advocate said, the police had conducted a preliminary inquiry but did not find any material to substantiate any of the allegations levelled by her. Therefore, the investigating officer had dropped further action and closed her complaint, he added.

On his part, the petitioner’s counsel S.L. Sudarsanam said, his client would apologise, if necessary and in order to give a quietus to the entire issue.

World.title: Rajasthan women’s varsity signs MoU with BRICS nations for global leadership centre
World.content:
Banasthali Vidyapith, a residential women’s university situated in Rajasthan’s Tonk district, on Monday (November 23, 2026) signed a memorandum of understanding with the BRICS nations for establishment of a centre for global women’s leadership. The new centre will work for women’s educational empowerment and leadership development on a global scale.

The MoU was signed on the conclusion of a five-day BRICS women leaders’ summit, organised on the university campus, which focused on promoting women’s leadership, cultural exchanges, and mutual cooperation and innovative research across the 11 BRICS member countries.

Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla, who inaugurated the summit, called upon women leaders to harness their collective leadership, experience and innovative capabilities to address global challenges and shape a “more peaceful, stable and prosperous” world. He also laid emphasis on cooperation among BRICS nations.

Banasthali Vidyapith organised the summit in partnership with Eurasian Women’s Forum, Russia’s Federation Council, Senezh Management Group of Russia and BRICS Youth Alliance. Vice-Chancellor Ina Aditya Shastri said the participants would act as torchbearers for women’s leadership development in their respective countries.

Extensive discussions were held during the summit on developing women’s leadership in the fields of politics, higher education, science and technology, entrepreneurship, administration, and social development. The speakers agreed to formulate future action plans to address the challenges of inequality in opportunities, limited access to financial resources and socio-cultural barriers.

Senezh Management Workshop’s First Vice-Rector Sergey Vladimirovich Bocharov said the BRICS countries had much to learn from India and Banasthali Vidyapith’s model of women’s leadership. He said the new centre would help expand women’s role in civil society and strengthen their decision-making capacity.

World.title: Proposal for extending scholarship to Sri Lankan students to pursue medical education in Tamil Nadu
World.content:
The Sri Lankan Deputy High Commission (SLDHC) in Chennai is proposing to strengthen cooperation in medical education in Tamil Nadu, including the possibility of extending scholarships to Sri Lankan students. Sri Lankan Deputy High Commissioner in Chennai Ganesanathan Geathiswaran met Health Minister K.G. Arunraj in this regard recently.

“During the meeting, discussion focused on further strengthening cooperation in the field of medical education, including the possibility of extending scholarships to Sri Lankan students to pursue medical studies in Tamil Nadu under a proposed 50/50 scholarship between the government of Tamil Nadu and the university concerned,” SLDHC said in a social media post.

Mr. Geathiswaran meeting with the Minister last week also explored the potential for establishing student exchange programmes for medical students and postgraduate trainees, including opportunities for clinical rotations, academic exchanges and professional engagement between medical institutions in Sri Lanka and Tamil Nadu, it said.

World.title: No Winter Session of Parliament? Skipped only four times in history
World.content:
The Winter Session of Parliament has been skipped only four times in India’s parliamentary history, and each instance was linked to exceptional circumstances, including the Emergency, the premature dissolution of the Lok Sabha, the assassination of Prime Minister Indira Gandhi, and the COVID-19 pandemic.

With the Monsoon Session yet to be prorogued, setting a record for Parliament remaining unprorogued for more than 100 days, speculation has grown over the possibility of a short special session to consider the delimitation Bill.
