World.title: Savarkar kin sends legal notice to Sonia Gandhi over book
World.content:
Satyaki Savarkar, grandnephew of Vinayak Damodar Savarkar, has sent a legal notice to Congress leader Sonia Gandhi seeking an apology and clarification about statements concerning Savarkar published in her book titled Belonging: A Journey of Love.

The notice sent by Satyaki through his lawyer advocate Sangram Kolhatkar states statements about Savarkar appearing on pages 201 and 443 of the book are “factually inaccurate, historically misleading, distorted and prejudicial to the reputation and legacy of Swatantryaveer Vinayak Damodar Savarkar”.

“My client specifically objects to the statement appearing on Page No. 201, wherein Swatantryaveer Vinayak Damodar Savarkar has been referred to in the context of persons allegedly collaborating with British colonial authorities. The manner in which the said statement has been framed creates an impression that Swatantryaveer Savarkar was associated with or responsible for acts of informing upon or collaborating with the British authorities against Indian freedom fighters. My client categorically disputes such an implication and states that the same is unsupported by the historical context in which Savarkar’s imprisonment, petitions and political activities must be examined.” the notice stated.

World.title: Money laundering probe: ED summons AAP’s Moga, Dharamkot MLAs, 8 others
World.content:
The Enforcement Directorate (ED) has summoned two AAP MLAs, Devinderjeet Singh Laddi Dhose from Dharamkot and Amandeep Kaur Arora from Moga, and eight others in connection with its probe into a money laundering case against her.

Eight persons include some serving and retired Punjab government officials and Arora’s family members.

The ED summoned the Moga MLA and her husband Rakesh Arora to depose at its Chandigarh Zonal-1 Office for questioning on November 26 and 25, respectively.

On November 4, the ED had searched seven properties of the Moga MLA in connection with fraudulent acquisition of government and institutionalised properties and misappropriation of public funds. In a statement issued subsequently, the ED alleged that she and her husband facilitated the siphoning of compensation funds the government gave to locals in Moga district whose land was acquired for constructing a highway.

The ED probe stems from the alleged fraudulent mutation of government land acquired for National Highway No 754A acquired in Andraman village of Dharamkot and “wrongful” disbursement of compensation worth at least Rs 1.06 crore for which an FIR was also registered by Moga police at the Dharamkot police station on June 16, 2024. The ED, in a statement, had said that it was also probing “several other properties that were transferred to Moga MLA’s relatives by manipulating revenue records”.

According ED sources, the Moga MLA is the principal beneficiary of alleged fraudulent acquisition and transfer of Government, Municipal Corporation, Market Committee and Church Trust properties through relatives and associates. Her husband has been summoned for his alleged involvement in fraudulent property transactions, handling of unaccounted funds and financial affairs of Aashirwaad Hospital.

The Dharamkot MLA has been summoned on November 27 for his “beneficial interest” in approximately 2-3 acres at Baggipura, Ludhiana, and alleged involvement in irregularities concerning crematorium land compensation at Dharamkot.



The Moga MLA’s father Jaspal Singh has been summoned on November 27 for allegedly holding seven marlas of the Punjab government land at Civil Lines in Moga on behalf of the MLA and her husband.

Her brother Valjinder Singh has been summoned on November 30 for his alleged involvement in benami property transactions, handling of cash and acquisition of Market Committee land.

Moga MLA’s maternal uncle Harminder Singh has been summoned on December 2 for allegedly acting as a benamidar in acquisition of Market Committee land and facilitating payments towards other properties.

Lakhwinder Singh, Partner/Director, M/s Aashirwaad Hospital & De-addiction Centre, the private facility run by her husband, has also been summoned for his alleged involvement in the management of the hospital, unaccounted cash collections, financial transactions and procurement/dispensing of psychotropic medicines.



The officials who have been summoned include Nirvair Singh, patwari, for his alleged involvement in manipulation of revenue records, fraudulent mutations, property transfers and withdrawal of compensation funds; Gurdev Singh Dham, former DRO, Moga, for alleged irregularities in assessment and disbursement of compensation under NH-754A, including compensation of approximately Rs 1 crore; and Lakhwinder Singh Gill, former tehsildar, Moga, for his alleged involvement in registration of sale deeds concerning Government, Municipal Corporation and Church Trust lands despite judicial orders and objections.

Incidentally, the Moga MLA has been summoned on November 26, the day AAP will sound its poll bugle for the 2027 Punjab Assembly elections at the “Khushaal Punjab” rally to be held at the border of Matwani and Nathuwal Jadid villages in Moga, with the party’s national convener Arvind Kejriwal in attendance.

Speaking to The Indian Express, Dr Amandeep Kaur Arora said, “I will file an application before the ED for changing the date or the time, given I have to attend the party’s first election rally on November 26, which is being held in my constituency.”

Responding to the ED summons, the AAP said, in a statement, “The Enforcement Directorate summoning the Moga MLA on November 26, the same day the Aam Aadmi Party is celebrating its Foundation Day with a historic Maharally for a Khushhaal Punjab in Moga, raises serious questions about the timing and intent of the action.”



“This is a politically motivated attempt to target the Aam Aadmi Party and its leaders and disrupt the party’s historic rally. The BJP-led central government is misusing central agencies to target political opponents. AAP will not be intimidated by such tactics,” the ruling party said.

Dr Amandeep Kaur Arora, who is also the president of the AAP Women’s Wing in Punjab, has been renominated by the party from the Moga seat for the Punjab Assembly elections expected early next year.

After the raids, the Moga MLA had accused the BJP of indulging in a political vendetta, alleging that the 42-hour-long ED raids at her residence included repeated pressure to join the BJP in exchange for a ministerial position. “Despite extensive searches at my residences and hospital, the ED could not recover a single penny and returned empty-handed,” she had said.

World.title: ‘Stopped by Modi government’: CJP’s Saurav Das alleges he was barred from flying to London
World.content:
Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) spokesperson Saurav Das on Monday alleged that he was stopped from flying to London from Delhi’s Indira Gandhi International Airport, where he was scheduled to deliver a lecture at the University of Oxford.

Das claimed that the Narendra Modi-led government prevented him from boarding his flight. He raised the allegation in a post on X but did not disclose the specific reasons given to him by the authorities for stopping his travel.

“I have been stopped by this cowardly Modi Govt at the Delhi Airport from flying to London to deliver a lecture at the University of Oxford,” Das wrote on X.

World.title: Why Javokhir Sindarov winning the World Championship matters to Uzbekistan
World.content:
Just over a decade ago, Javokhir Sindarov’s family had a tough decision to make. They had two sons, Javokhir and Islombek, both prodigiously talented at chess, but the family could only use its limited resources to fund the career of one.

They chose Javokhir. On Tuesday, that chosen one will begin a fight against India’s D Gukesh to become the 19th world champion in chess history.

The Sindarov family was not the only one that had to make similar decisions. Nodirbek Abdusattorov also remembers the struggle he faced in his early years . Back in those days, support from the Uzbekistan Chess Federation was hard to come by. He too had an older brother and a sister who had talent, but they had to give up the sport.

“When I started playing chess, we didn’t have too much support for chess in Uzbekistan even though we had some decent talents already. These were not super prodigies, but there was a talented bunch of boys with potential that could have become grandmasters by the age of 14 or 15. But they never really got enough support to travel and to play in events,” recalls Abdusattorov, the current world no.5. “I also struggled a lot when I was trying to hunt for my norms. Support was primarily from my father. But once I got the grandmaster title, it became way easier to get a sponsor and attention.”

Both Sindarov and Abdusattorov had other federations trying to lure them, with the latter being courted both by Russia and the United States.



But now is a different time in Uzbek chess. When players from the country win a big event — like the Olympiad golds in 2022 and 2026; or Sindarov clinching the FIDE World Cup in 2025 or the Candidates this year — the whole country erupts in celebration.

ALSO READ | Gukesh vs Sindarov: Vishy’s Children vs Kasimdzhanov’s Kids

When Sindarov won the World Cup in Goa last year, he was given a three-bedroom apartment, cash prize worth $10,000 and the title of ‘Honored Athlete of the Republic of Uzbekistan’. His welcoming party at the tarmac in Tashkent included the country’s Prime Minister Abdulla Aripov while President Shavkat Mirziyoyev announced his victory in the middle of an event to a stadium full of Olympic athletes.

The change started a few years ago, and with each big result, the support only increased.



Awards and rewards

The government’s support also flowed into chess because so much of the country’s national sporting identity hinges on the sport. It’s the one discipline where Uzbekistan can be the world No. 1. The closest any other sport comes in terms of success was amateur boxing at the Olympics, besides a few medals in weightlifting.

“I can safely say that chess is now one of the mainstream sports in Uzbekistan. If we judge by results, I think it’s number one already. We don’t have any other sports that can compare with chess in terms of results. When you have good performances, it motivates the government to spend more and to support,” says Abdusattorov.

There are already plans to build a sports complex in New Tashkent with a 500-seat hall for chess players. Sindarov has started his own chess academy. Abdusattorov plans to start one soon. Other Uzbek grandmasters who were part of their Olympiad successes have started chess clubs in their hometowns where they frequently play simuls against others and meet upstarts in the sport.



Abdusattorov has spoken about how Sindarov’s triumphs over the past year have given him a second wind as a player. Now, he hopes that Sindarov can install himself as the next world champion, so the impact gets bigger.

“If Javokhir becomes world champion, it will shake the chess community in Uzbekistan and spark a new boom. Investment from private sponsors and government support will keep rising. The next generation will get inspired by our results and get better support too,” he predicts.

World.title: ‘To fit into this outfit’: Ananya Panday’s lymphatic drainage comment sparks curiosity about the wellness treatment
World.content:
“I have done a lymphatic drainage to fit into this outfit,” said Ananya Panday during her appearance on the final season of Koffee with Karan. The actor’s remark brings attention to a wellness treatment often associated with reducing facial puffiness, water retention and bloating. But can a single session really make you slimmer or help you fit into an outfit? Speaking with indianexpress.com, Dr Rituja Ugalmugle, Consultant, Internal Medicine, Wockhardt Hospitals, Mumbai Central, explains how lymphatic drainage works and what it can realistically achieve.

The lymphatic system helps maintain fluid balance by collecting excess fluid, proteins and cellular waste from body tissues and returning them to the bloodstream.

Manual lymphatic drainage is a specialised massage technique involving gentle, rhythmic movements along lymphatic pathways to encourage fluid movement.



“It can help reduce swelling in people with fluid accumulation or impaired lymphatic drainage. In otherwise healthy individuals, it may offer a temporary improvement in facial puffiness caused by fluid retention,” says Dr Ugalmugle.

However, she clarifies that not all bloating responds to this treatment. Abdominal bloating caused by gas, constipation or digestive issues will not meaningfully improve with lymphatic drainage. It also does not break down fat cells or reduce body fat.

DISCLAIMER: This article is based on information from the public domain and/or the experts we spoke to. Always consult your health practitioner before starting any routine.

View this post on Instagram A post shared by Dr Devayani Barve (@doctorbarve)

Can one session help you fit into an outfit?

“Some individuals may notice a temporary reduction in facial puffiness or fluid-related swelling after a single session. The visible difference depends on whether the puffiness is actually caused by fluid accumulation,” explains Dr Ugalmugle.

However, the duration of these effects is not well established through clinical research. There is also no convincing scientific evidence that routine lymphatic drainage produces sustained reductions in body measurements, abdominal circumference or weight.



“So, while someone may notice a subtle difference before an event, it should not be considered a body-contouring or weight-loss treatment,” she adds.

Is lymphatic drainage safe for everyone?

“It should be avoided in people with suspected deep vein thrombosis or acute cellulitis. Those with decompensated heart failure or unexplained swelling need medical assessment before undergoing the procedure,” says Dr Ugalmugle.

Incorrect techniques or excessive pressure can also cause discomfort, bruising and skin irritation. Frequent sessions without a medical requirement do not necessarily offer additional benefits.

Persistent or unexplained swelling should never be dismissed as a cosmetic concern. Consult a doctor to identify any underlying medical condition rather than relying on repeated massage sessions.
